items.statement: Order book to revenue ratio expected to be two to three times.
items.quote: And 70,000 order book generally we are expecting to have a order book to revenue ratio of two to three times.

items.statement: Fuses supply planned at around 500 crores per year.

items.statement: Targeting 80% to 90% indigenization of fuses in two to two and a half years.
items.period: two to two and a half years
items.quote: More than 50% already is there, but we are targeting 80% to 90% in another two, two and a half years.

items.statement: Expects SG&A to be 27.5% to 28% of sales for the full fiscal.
items.quote: We expect our SG&A to be in the range of 27.5% to 28% for the full fiscal.

items.statement: Expects R&D investment to be 8.5 to 9% of sales for the full fiscal.
items.quote: Overall, R&D continues to be a cornerstone of our growth strategy and we expect the investment to be in range of 8.5 to 9% for the full fiscal.

items.statement: Expects normal effective tax rate of 24% to 25% for the fiscal.
items.quote: We expect our normal ETR to be in the range of 24% to 25% for the fiscal.

items.statement: US business expected to grow single digit, excluding lenalidomide, to compensate for price erosion.
items.quote: We have the capability - and I'm excluding even lenalidomide in this kind of discussion - to grow in single digit, meaning, to compensate for any price erosion on a year-to-year basis.

items.statement: India baseline business expected to grow double digits this year, excluding acquisitions.
items.quote: The baseline of India, without acquisitions, will be double digits this year.

items.statement: Abatacept filing expected end of calendar 2025, launch end of calendar 2026.
items.period: end of calendar 2025, end of calendar 2026
items.quote: Abatacept filing should be in the end of calendar '25. And launch should be in the end of calendar '26, assuming approval on time.

items.statement: Denosumab launch expected next year.
items.quote: So, denosumab is next year.

items.statement: Investing in Bachupally biologics facility to reach 50 kilolitre capacity, taking two more years.
items.quote: We are still investing in our Bachupally facility. The intent is to become something like 50 kilolitre in that facility. This probably will take us additional two years to reach that level.

items.statement: Aurigene CDMO biologics facility investment is a few hundred crores.
items.quote: The level of investment is a few hundreds of crores, I don't remember exactly how much.

items.statement: Freight cost impact around Rs. 50 crores or Rs. 60 crores due to Middle East conflict.
items.quote: It should be around Rs. 50 crores or Rs. 60 crores or something like that.

items.statement: North America activity should continue to grow throughout the year.
items.quote: Right now, it looks like that the North America activity should continue to grow throughout the year.

items.statement: US growth driven by base business, not new products.
items.quote: So most of it is from the base business. Most of it is the products that we had before and the contribution of the three products helped the growth, but the lion’s share of the growth came from products that we had before.

items.statement: USFDA issued Form 483 with observations at Duvvada and Srikakulam facilities; will resolve within timelines.
items.quote: In May, the USFDA completed a routine GMP inspection at two of our formulations manufacturing facilities in Duvvada, Vizag and issued a Form 483 with two observations. In June, the USFDA completed a GMP inspection at our API manufacturing facility in Srikakulam, Andhra Pradesh and issued a Form 483 with four observations.

items.statement: Has about US$2.5 billion for inorganic investments without impacting ratings.
items.quote: First, we believe that we have about US$2.5 billion that we can invest inorganically. That depends, of course, on the time, but we have enough financial capacity without even changing dramatically ratings or anything like that.

items.statement: Nestlé JV operations to go live on August 1st.
items.quote: Progressing very nicely and we hope that in the beginning of August we can announce ‘Day 1’, likely, August 1st, but we will announce when it will come.

items.statement: Telecom equipment segment revenue expected to reach approximately Rs.2000 crores in FY25.
items.quote: We expect the revenue from this segment during FY25 to reach approximately Rs.2000 crores from just Rs.143 crores in FY24.

items.statement: Overall revenue growth expected 25% to 30% this year.
items.quote: This year, for example, you will see a reasonable increase in the revenue of the C ompany from 25% to 30%, which has been possible despite of this slowdown in optical fiber cable business because revenue from other segments is increasing substantially

items.statement: Expect 20% to 30% annual growth; in three years telecom equipment, fiber optic cables, and EPC each around INR3,000 crores.
items.quote: We expect that every year we should be able to grow by some 20% to 30%. In three years' timeframe our telecom equipment business should be around INR3,000 crores. Similar number would be the fiber optic cables. Similar number would be the EPC business.

items.statement: Passive connectivity solutions revenue expected Rs.250 crores in current financial year, growing to Rs.750 crores in 2-3 years.

items.statement: Net margin generally around 8% to 10% for telecom products, with PLI benefit.
items.quote: And generally, the margin, net margin is around 8% to 10%, as you know. Added to that would be some benefit from PLI also.

items.statement: Overall turnkey contract margin expected around 10% PBT.
items.quote: But on a longer term if you ask me that what's going to be the overall margin on turnkey contract I will keep it around 10%.

items.statement: Total order book stands at ~INR 6776 crores as on Q1 FY25.
items.quote: Our total order book now stands at ~ INR 6776 crores as on Q1 of FY25.

items.statement: Optical fiber cable demand expected to restore from Q3/Q4 FY25 onwards.
items.quote: We anticipate that Optical Fiber Cables demand will be restored from Q3/Q4 FY25 onwards, both in India and key global markets.

items.statement: Global optical fiber cable market expected to grow again from last quarter of FY25.
items.quote: It is expected that globally Optical Fiber Cable market will start witnessing growth again from the last quarter of financial year 2024-25.

items.statement: Global optical fiber cable market slowdown due to geopolitical situation, high inventory, delayed government programs.
items.quote: Geopolitical situation throughout the world and its impact on important aspects of business i.e. cost of raising capital, cost of logistics, large inventory built with operators and delay in major government funded programs have resulted in this temporary slowdown.

items.statement: Revenue mix changed towards products; private customers 51%, international 9.82%.
items.quote: The revenue from Private customers and International Business stands at 51% and 9.82% respectively.

items.quote: The total is about INR650 crores we are eligible for. We will start getting it from the current financial year itself because our is not PLI, but DLI.

items.quote: In a landmark verdict on 14th June, 2024, the European Commission has decided not to impose anti-dumping duty on optical fiber cables manufactured by HFCL and its subsidiary HTL, whereas provisional anti-dumping duty has already been imposed on all other Indian Optical Fiber Cable Manufacturers.

items.statement: Maintains 10% to 15% volume growth for FY25.
items.quote: See, we maintain a 10% to 15% volu me growth, which we had forecast in the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Expects 10% to 15% CAGR growth.
items.quote: No, no, this year as well. CAGR also, we expect a 10% to 15% growth. Yes.

items.statement: Firm capex plan expected next quarter.
items.quote: So in the next quarter, we should be in a position to come up with a firm plan.

items.quote: see, typically, a 100,000 metric ton capacity plant will cost you anywhere between INR 300 crores and INR 400 crores. Okay.

items.quote: And therefore, coming up with incremental capacity can take place within 6 to 8 months.

items.statement: New capacity lead time 18-24 months.
items.quote: So it's anywhere between 18 to 24 months. This is including land, building, equipment.

items.quote: And yes, you will have some impact because of the VCM delta reducing.

items.statement: Excess cash after expansion to be returned to shareholders.
items.quote: And whatever is not needed for expansion will be given back to the shareholders.

items.quote: So, we are targeting to grow this segment by 12 % to 14% in FY'25. This will be a mix of volume as well as price growth.

items.statement: Grain prices elevated and increasing post Q1 FY25; implementing operational efficiencies and cost control.
items.quote: The price of crucial inputs like grain and packing materials remains elevated. The grain price is increasing further post Q1 FY25.

items.quote: With the increased contributions from our IM FL products, we anticipate a gradual rise in revenue contributions from our IMFL proprietary brands.

items.statement: Expect ethanol volumes to be in similar range quarter-on-quarter.

items.quote: So, we don't foresee to increase further equity from here onwards. So, we will be able to do the expansion through our debt s orry through our internal accruals and a small debt if required that two also we don't foresee there is a big number which is coming in debt.

items.quote: Further, the raw malt, which like ENA, which is selling at around, let's say, INR60, INR65, the raw malt can be sold at around INR200 per litre.

items.statement: IMFL proprietary revenue split: 40% MP, 60% Kerala, miniscule from other states.
items.quote: So, IMFL proprietary, 40% will be MP, 60% will be Kerala and a miniscule number will be coming from other states, which should increase in coming quarters.

items.statement: Expects Valia nitrile latex capacity utilization to be 50-70% for next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Expects overall margins to be in 13-17% range over next 4-5 years.
items.quote: So, this is how I think things will go, will happen as long as we keep growing and growing at a reasonable margin.

items.statement: Plans to overhaul R&D center and build new R&D building, value to be announced later.
items.quote: One is the complete overhaul of our R&D center so that will require some CAPEX and we're planning to build a new R&D building and invest in our R&D.

items.statement: Will announce additional investment for styrene butadiene latex in next 3-6 months.
items.quote: the second investment is which we will announce again in the next 3 to 6 months is additional investment for our styrene butadiene latex products because we expect that capacity to be utilized by end of next year.

items.statement: No decision taken on expanding Valia nitrile latex capacity from 50,000 to 80,000 tonnes.
items.quote: No, 100%, we have not taken any decision. Given the margins where we are, I think we'll wait for some time.

items.quote: We may actually use that space where we had left some space for the additional capacity for Nitrile Latex. We actually use it to manufacture current styrene butadiene and other current latex products. That decision will be taken in the next 3 to 6 months.

items.statement: Glove segment pulling down margins; other segments also have lower margins due to capacity additions.
items.quote: Of course, the glove segment is pulling it down. A couple of other segments also, we have built capacity, some of our competitors have built capacity that is in the short term.

items.statement: Nitrile latex project is EBITDA neutral, with some quarters negative and some positive.
items.quote: It is about EBITDA neutral, I would say, some quarter negative, some quarters positive, but overall EBITDA sort of zero EBITDA neutral, yes. EBITDA breakeven rather.

items.statement: Glove industry showing green shoots; Q2 expected better than Q1.
items.quote: We do expect, I mean we're seeing some green shoots. I mentioned it last quarter also we saw initially some green shoots in Q1 was slightly better than Q4 of last year, but Q2 is expected to be even better.

items.statement: Export volumes grew 12% YoY in Q1.
items.quote: On the international front, export volume grew by 12% year-on-year.

items.statement: Overall volume growth of 14% YoY in Q1.
items.quote: I think we're up, Sachin, by about 14% this quarter. So, Q1 against Q1 of last year, volume growth is up by 14%.

items.statement: Freight and container availability issues impacted exports, absorbing some costs.
items.quote: We've seen that impact the margins as well to some extent because we've had to absorb some of those paid costs. Of course, we try and pass it along as well, but it takes time sometimes, so yes.

items.statement: NBR margins lower due to China slowdown and Russian NBR entering Asia.
items.quote: The Russia NBR, which used to largely go to Europe because of the sanctions are now finding its way towards Asia. So, I think there's a little bit of a glut of NBR in the Asian region causing the margins to be muted.

items.statement: Flooding at plant caused damage, but plant resumed in less than a week; assessing damage.
items.quote: So, we had to keep the plant closed for safety reasons for a few days. Of course, there was a lot of damage. We are still in the middle of assessing the exact damage.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 25% to 30% CAGR for next 4 years.
items.quote: We look forward to achieve revenue growth of 25% to 30% CAGR for t he next 4 years

items.statement: ROCE of 25% to 30% despite proposed investments.
items.quote: We are also confident of hitting 25% to 30% of ROCE despite these proposed investments supported by working capital efficiencies.

items.statement: Kisan sales target INR450-500 crores in current financial year.
items.quote: Going forward, we want to take this sales for Kisan to INR450 crores to INR 500 crores in the current financial year

items.statement: Kisan sales target INR600-650 crores next year and INR750-800 crores by FY27 with 10% EBITDA margin.
items.value: INR600 crores to INR650 crores, INR750 crores to INR800 crores
items.quote: Then in the follow ing year, take it to around INR600 crores to INR650 crores and eventually around INR750 crores to INR800 crores by FY '27, with 10% of EBITDA margin

items.statement: Kisan EBITDA margin to sustain 7-8% for full year, then 10-12% in next 2 years.
items.quote: So Kisan, see I mean, in Q1, you saw 7%, 8% of EBITDA margin, right? We plan to sustain these levels for full year. And going forward, in the next 2 years, we plan to take this company at 10% to 12% EBITDA level.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR100-150 crores for next 2-3 years, funded by internal cash flows and equity infusion.
items.quote: Next 2, 3 years, we will be doing around INR100 crores to INR150 crores on annualized basis, which will be mainly funded from the internal cash flows and plus the balance equity infusion, whi ch is due from the promoter and employees as part of the preferential allotment

items.statement: Apollo EBITDA margin to remain around 10% for next 2 years, then inch up to 12-13%.
items.quote: So Apollo should move towards a 12% to 13% EBITDA margin, but as of now, we will remain around 10% for the next 2 years becau se of a lot of capex, which is coming

items.statement: Revenue target of more than INR2,600 crores by FY27.
items.quote: And FY '25, FY '26, FY '27, we believe that we should be more than INR2,600 crores of revenue by FY '27, right?

items.statement: O-PVC segment contribution to overall revenue around 5% this year, 8-10% next year.
items.quote: So this year, on overall revenue, my contribution from this segment should be around 5%, right? And next year, when all the 3 lines will be operational for full 12 months, the contribution should be 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Apollo Pipes revenue expected around 25% increase for FY25.
items.quote: So revenue, we should expect around 25% increase for Apollo Pipes on an overall basis, and Kisan will be additional.

items.statement: Balance capex for Varanasi, window profile, and brownfield expansion around INR250 crores.
items.quote: So the balance capex for Varanasi, right, and for window profile, plus some brownfield expansion is around INR250 crores, right?

items.statement: South India plant investment minimum INR200 crores.
items.quote: See, any big plant, it should look at investment of around INR200 crores minimum.

items.statement: Next year capex projected at INR150 crores.
items.quote: So next year, we are projecting INR150 crores, right? There could be some residual capex for Varanasi, some for O-PVC, some for window profiles, plus we will start looking out for opportunities in Southern India, yes.

items.statement: PVC prices near bottom, expected upward from next month due to antidumping news.
items.quote: So it should be on the near to bottom price, and should be on upward from next month onwards of -- for PVC prices.

items.statement: Channel inventory at minimum level, expected to build up in coming quarters.
items.quote: And right now, t hey are at, you can say, minimum level of inventories. And we hope that in the coming quarters, again, when the prices starts build up, then we will start building up their inventories

items.statement: Consolidated revenue target INR1,650-1,750 crores for FY25.
items.quote: So the number could be from INR1,650 crores to INR1,750 crores, right? Base, you can take INR1,650 crores.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected to remain 48-51% for next 4-6 quarters.
items.quote: Because of this as we discussed in the earlier quarters, our cost-to-income ratio will be in the same range of 48% to 51% for the next 4 to 6 quarters.

items.statement: ROA expected to remain at current level of 1.5% plus.
items.quote: And ROA is expected to remain at our current level of 1.5% plus.

items.statement: Advances growth to reach industry level as soon as possible.
items.quote: We are putting our best efforts to reach the industry level growth as soon as possible.

items.statement: Double digit growth target for FY25 remains.
items.quote: Double digit target remains, right, for the end of FY25? N. Kamakodi: Yes, that is what. Already we have reached that and we are working to ensure the growth rate further accelerates from where we are

items.statement: Operating profit to show corresponding increase after 2-3 more quarters.
items.quote: As you have seen, because of the other upfront expenditure and all what we are taking, we have to wait for maybe 2-3 more quarters to see the operating profit showing corresponding increase compared to the business growth.

items.statement: Breakeven next year, profit addition beyond that.
items.quote: So, it will be reaching breakeven only next year and probably adding to the profit kitty by next, like say, beyond that.

items.statement: Slippages expected around Rs. 800 crores for FY25.
items.quote: So, effectively the slippage came down from 1300 to 1000 to this year we expect about maybe about Rs. 800 crores or something like that, maybe even slightly below that is what our calculations currently demonstrate.

items.statement: Recoveries run rate anticipated at Rs. 200-250 crores.
items.quote: The recovery numbers are almost Rs. 1,000 crore plus, the stable numbers which we have started seeing, about Rs. 200 crores to Rs. 250 crore.

items.statement: Credit cost moderation expected compared to last year.
items.quote: So, as explained in the previous quarters also, this year also, there has to be a considerably reasonable credit cost moderation compared to last year.

items.statement: Favorable credit cost environment may prolong for at least six to seven quarters.
items.quote: And in this cycle, maybe for at least another not less than six to seven quarters or so, there is every possibility that current favorable credit cost environment may prolong.

items.statement: ROA expansion beyond 1.5% possible once new growth engines deliver.
items.quote: We expect once we start seeing the delivery or productivity from the new growth engines which we are trying to add, definitely, there could be expansion in the ROA beyond 1.5% whatever we are there.

items.statement: Long-term strategy to grow few percentage points above industry growth rate.
items.quote: So, we take steady path, growing maybe few percentage points over and above that of the industry growth rate is what we have demonstrated over a period of time, and it has proved good City Union Bank July 26, 2024 for us in terms of the long term stability of the institution, which we think we will be following that proven path as we had seen in the past

items.statement: LCR to stabilize around 115-125% after latest circular.
items.quote: So, after some amount of aberrations, ups and downs, things should be stabilizing around 115 to 125 for all of us and for us also.

items.statement: Cost of funds has almost peaked.
items.quote: It has almost peaked, and we expected the reduction and the interest rate cycle will start, but now enough indications are that they are not going to be as quick as it was expected. So, by and large, it has almost peaked.

items.statement: Digital lending project expenditure: BCG fees Rs. 25-30 crore, software Rs. 10-15 crore.
items.value: Rs. 25 to Rs. 30 crore; Rs. 10 to Rs. 15 crore

items.statement: Priority on secured retail lending; unsecured retail not a priority, may expand in 3-5 years.

items.statement: Expects not to lose money at cash level this year in core business.
items.quote: I'm very hopeful given now how the Print business and I'm now talking about only the core business, how that is poised, we will definitely not lose money this year. I mean at a cash level I am talking.

items.statement: Ad revenue expected to perform better in Q2 and Q3 if pricing sticks.
items.quote: So, if our pricing sticks and the program goes as per plan, you will see ad revenue performing better and better in the second quarter and the third quarter because that is the plan which is already under motion.

items.statement: Digital losses to reduce significantly this year vs last year, but no profitability this year.
items.quote: Having said that, we have said that as revenue scale s up and our scale builds, the loss would have significantly reduced for this year as compared to last year. But we will not be looking at profitability, at least this year for sure

items.statement: Working aggressively to increase ad pricing; early success seen in Q1.
items.quote: At this p oint in time, we are working very aggressively to work on the ad pricing. Although the volumes are already back, the pricing is something which is under pressure

items.statement: Newsprint cost at INR 48,000 per ton; Q2 expected at similar level with marginal increase.
items.quote: And on newsprint, we are at on consolidated basis at about INR 48,000 per ton. We are seeing some pressure on pricing given all the disruptions in the market from a global supply chain logistics perspective.

items.statement: Government revenue declined 25-30% due to model code of conduct.
items.quote: And as far as this quarter is concerned, i f you just equate the government revenues, which obviously came down by about 25% to 30% because of the model code of conduct, you can see that the resultant revenue will already be

items.statement: Industry volumes in relevant markets down 12%, led by government segment.
items.quote: So, in the relevant markets for us, we have seen industry volumes come down by 12%. So, in the market that we are in, both English and Hindi, the market volumes have also come down by 12% percent, largely all led by the government piece.

items.statement: Government ads contribute 20-25% of ad revenue.
items.quote: About 20 to 25% is broadly the government contribution.

items.statement: OTTplay revenue recognized pro rata; INR 9 crore in HMVL is quarterly portion of annual subscriptions.
items.quote: So that means this INR 9 crore revenue that we have reported on OTTplay in HMVL, that is a quarter of the annual subscription, right?

items.statement: Content rights restrict OTTplay to India; cannot air outside Republic of India.
items.quote: No. So, the current content rights do not allow us to take it beyond the country’s border. So, this is a Pan India product at this point in time and we cannot air this content outside the Republic of India.

items.statement: Radio industry awaiting NOTEF guidelines; will be beneficial once notified.
items.quote: Well, I think that's an industry issue, and we've been along with the industry, making representations to the ministry. So, we are hoping that they will be notified pretty soon.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth expected 11.5% to 13.5% in constant currency.
items.quote: For the Fiscal Year ‘25, we now expect our revenue to grow in the range of 11.5% to 13.5% in constant currency terms. This is ahead of our initial guidance of 10% to 13%.

items.statement: FY25 EBIT margin expected 11% to 12%.
items.quote: For operating margins, we continue to expect our FY25 EBIT margin to be in the range of 11% to 12%. This is inclusive of the impact of upfront investments that we are making in the business.

items.statement: Expect US$1 billion revenue run rate by Q4 FY26.
items.quote: We also remain optimistic of achieving a US$1 billion revenue run rate by Q4 of FY26.

items.statement: Post investment phase, EBIT margins to improve 50-75 bps annually over medium-term.
items.quote: Post the investment phase, we expect our EBIT margins to improve by 50 to 75 basis points each year over the medium-term as we have stated earlier.

items.statement: Aim to converge to 14%-15% EBIT margin over next three to four years.
items.quote: So, the way we are designing the business is that we should converge to the 14%-15% over the next three to four years and that’s where we are keeping our current line of sight too.

items.statement: Wage revision advanced to Q2, may pose margin headwinds but stay within guided band.
items.quote: We have also advanced our annual wage revision cycle from Q3 to Q2. While this will pose some headwinds in our margin in Q2, we remain confident of staying within our guided band for FY25.

items.statement: Expect sequentially improving growth trajectory in BFS through rest of FY25.
items.quote: Overall, we expect a sequentially improving growth trajectory in this vertical through the rest of FY25.

items.statement: Expect strong growth in healthcare vertical, driven by payer segment.
items.quote: Overall, we expect g rowth to remain strong in the vertical, driven by the payer segment

items.statement: Expect good growth in CMT vertical despite onshore-to-offshore shift headwind.
items.quote: Overall, while movement of specific processes from onshore to offshore in our top client could remain an optical headwind in the near term, we expect good growth in the overall vertical given continued ramp ups in other clients as well as the healthy deal pipeline.

items.statement: Diverse vertical revenue decline expected to recover in Q2.
items.quote: We expect the same to recover in Q2.

items.statement: Europe expected to see stronger second-half; US broad-based growth across verticals.
items.quote: We expect Europe to see a stronger second-half in the US we expect a more broad-based growth across verticals.

items.statement: Signed three large deals in Q1, expected to ramp up in phases.
items.quote: We signed three strategically large deals in Q1, another first for Firstsource . As you are aware, we consider a deal with ACV of over US$5 million as a large deal. We expect these deals to ramp up in a phased manner over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Added two new seating capacities in Chennai and Philippines; investing in Hyderabad and Mexico.
items.quote: We continue to invest in expanding our execution infrastructure. In Q1, we have added two new seating capacity in Chennai and Philippines. We are also investing in additional capacities in Hyderabad and Mexico.

items.statement: Offshore mix increased from 25% to 35% over last four quarters; expect continued shift.
items.quote: If I go back t o Q1 of FY’24 to where we are today, we were at about a 25 -75 mix and we are now at about a 35 -65 mix. What you will see is just the renewed focus on continuing to try and balance that mix out towards the greater offshore concentration and that’s something that all of us in the leadership team are driving very clearly.

items.statement: AI expected to cannibalize lower-end BPS services but new opportunities larger.
items.quote: What I do expect is that AI will certainly cannibalize some of the lower end of the BPS services but it’s not material enough. New business opportunities using AI is far bigger and at the same time what I am also seeing is data, AI /ML operations, tech led trust and safety will be a new frontier to expand our business using AI.

items.statement: Net debt expected to become zero within 6 to 8 quarters with normal cash generation.
items.quote: But I will not be able to give you exact timeline when it will be, but if you really model it, most likely that is equal to around $110 million to $115 million, it should be probably within 6 to 8 quarters, when the normal cash generation should make it net debt zero.

items.statement: Transaction charges impact from new regulation is Rs. 40 crores annualized, to be passed on to customers.
items.quote: So on the F&O side, we are reviewing and analyzing the SEBI discussion paper, they have still not confirmed how the contract size and all will work. As of now, the transaction charges impact is not much on overall revenue. T he impact is around Rs. 40 crores on an annualized

items.statement: Transaction charges impact is Rs. 10 crores per quarter, to be reviewed for recovery from customers.
items.quote: So if I look at the overall transaction charges, which is going to impact because of the new regulation coming up October 1. As previously discussed, it's an impact of Rs. 10 crores a quarter for us, which is comparatively very small on the overall revenue.

items.statement: Digital spending is around Rs. 150 crores annually.
items.quote: So overall, on the digital side, we are spending in a big way , around Rs. 150 crores annually. We have spent on the overall business model from a tech to the digital side to build the overall back -end and the front end systems and these are continuously being built up on.

items.statement: Dividend payout to be maintained at about 20% of operating profit, subject to working capital and business growth needs.
items.quote: Our dividend payout has been about 20% of the operating profit average over the last decade, and we will continue to maintain this payout subject to working capita l and business growth needs.

items.statement: Operating profit growth of 34% over 10 years, optimistic about future years.
items.quote: To sum up, the 10-year track record of the group has been an operating profit growth of 34%, which we are quite optimistic about in the years to come.

items.statement: AI to be developed in-house, with a senior resource joining next month.
items.quote: So on the artificial intelligence side, we are having our team alre ady in place, and we have hired a senior resource, who will be joining us next month to enhance the overall scope on the artificial intelligence. We'll be building it up in-house, and also may have some tie-ups with some vendors but majorly it will be in-house developed, the overall artificial intelligence.

items.statement: Building algo and high-frequency trading strategies for retail clients on digital and option side.
items.quote: Coming to the second question, we already have some tie-ups for the algo's trade and high-frequency trades for our customers and we are also building it up more aggressively going forward. So we are coming up with some strategies for our retail clients, which can be used for trading on the digital side and the option side.

items.statement: STT rate increases have not materially impacted F&O volumes historically.
items.quote: So in fact, that has been the case even in the past. If you look at continuously the STT rates have gone up, but I think volumes have only grown in the market. So we don't see this to be any material impact on the volumes.

items.quote: However, we believe that advertising expenses on entertainment category are anticipated to recover later in the year, driven by festive season and improving rural demand.

items.statement: Expects rural demand to revive and grow steadily, and festive demand spend to fructify around festive season starting September-October.
items.quote: So, while we have never had a practice of giving forward earni ngs guidance, but what we are seeing definitely we expect that in the festive season, and thanks to a decent monsoon, we are expecting the rural demand also to revive and kind of steadily grow back, and festive demand spend

items.statement: Expects B2B deals in pipeline to fructify over the next three quarters.
items.quote: I mean, I cannot say Q2, but I am saying over the next three q uarters you would see those deals fructifying

items.statement: Expects second half to be better.
items.quote: So, basically the second half will be better for us?

items.statement: Budget for new initiatives this year is about Rs. 60 odd crores.
items.quote: The budget for this year, I think we had shared it the Q1, I d on't remember, but I believe it was about around Rs. 60 odd crores

items.statement: Additional accelerated inventory charge-off this quarter was around Rs. 30-32 crores.
items.quote: However, the broad indication I can give is the additional accelerated charge-off during this quarter was in the range of around Rs. 30-32 crores.

items.statement: Targets bringing down debt by about Rs. 100 crores from March 2024 level in two years, funded by internal accruals.
items.quote: And we have targeted that in two years we will bring down the debt by about Rs. 100 crores from the March level where we were at March ’24.

items.statement: Debt reduced from Rs. 338 crores to about Rs. 324 crores, a reduction of roughly Rs. 13-14 crores.
items.quote: So, June, from Rs. 338 crores we have come down to about Rs. 324 crores, which is a reduction of roughly about Rs. 13 crores to Rs. 14 crores.

items.statement: Inventory reduced from Rs. 682 crores as of March 2024 to Rs. 640 crores as of June 30, 2024, a reduction of about Rs. 42 crores.
items.quote: Our inventory has come down from Rs. 682 crores as of March 2024 to Rs. 640 crores as of 30th June, 2024, which is a reduction of about Rs. 42 crores.

items.statement: Digital platform deals are between one and three years; television movie licenses are for five years.
items.quote: Typically, digital platform deals are between one and three ye ars, not more than that, because space is evolving and growing in different speeds. So, what is relevant today may not be the relevant price or commercial model two years down the line. Television is a much more stable platform, so we typically license our move. And that's again a trade practice, industry licenses movies for five years

items.statement: In last three years, generated about Rs. 50-60 crores free cash flow net of new business investments.
items.quote: If we look at net of that, each of the last about three years, we have been generating probably about Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores free cash flow.

items.statement: Gaming and metaverse industry in infancy; no immediate major monetization potential, investing just enough to be future-ready.
items.quote: Right now, we do not see any immediate, in the immediate future we do not see any ma jor monetization potential there. However, there could be a lot of possibilities opening up in the future. What we are doing is investing just enough to be future‐ready

items.statement: Capacity guidance for FY25 maintained at early double digits.
items.quote: And for the seasonally weak second quarter, we are expecting to add around high single digits capacity as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 passenger unit revenue (PRASK) expected stable year-over-year.
items.quote: Further, on the revenue side basis the early trends of July, we are estimating a stable revenue environment on a passenger unit revenue which is PRASK basis in the second quarter of financial year 2025 as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Firm orderbook of 975+ aircraft enables receiving more than one aircraft per week.
items.quote: With our firm pending orderbook of 975 plus aircraft that will enable us to receive more than one aircraft per week and the mitigation measures we remain firm on our capacity guidance of early double digits for the financial year 2025 .

items.statement: Goal to become a 600+ aircraft airline by end of decade.
items.quote: We continue to utilize part of our free cash towards future growth and our goal to become a 600 plus aircraft airline by the end of the decade.

items.statement: Will induct 6 more aircraft from Qatar Airways on wet or damp lease subject to approvals.
items.quote: In addition to this, subject to regulatory approvals we will induct 6 more aircraft from Qatar Airlines for the Doha route on wet or damp lease in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Will continue to add more aircraft on finance leases to diversify financing sources.
items.quote: Going forward, we will continue to further diversify our sources and will add more aircraft on finance leases.

items.statement: Aircraft groundings expected to start reducing towards start of next year.
items.quote: We are working with Pratt & Whitney towards constant supply of spare engines and basis the current estimates we expect the groundings to start reducing towards the start of the next year.

items.statement: Compensation from Pratt & Whitney will not fully cover all costs; will be less than overall cost.
items.quote: No, it's not going to be neutral, like I said, it's always going to be less than what the overall cost is going to be.

items.statement: Solid demand seen in July; no change in capacity guidance or planning.
items.quote: Looking at the overall outlook for July, we see a solid demand. And therefore, we have no change in our capacity guidance.

items.statement: Average fare stable around Rs.5,000 to Rs.6,000 range for last couple of quarters.
items.quote: If you look to our yields, we see an average fare still in that range around Rs.5,000 to Rs.6,000 range, which is a very stable setting actually for the last couple of quarters.

items.statement: Increased costs in fuel, navigation, and airport fees will need to be reflected in prices.
items.quote: And clearly, some of the increased cost in fuel and navigation and airport fees will have to find their way back in the cost.

items.statement: International share of ASK is around 27% and expected to grow.
items.quote: Therefore, today, the international share of IndiGo is around 27% of the ASK. We have announced earlier that that percentage is expected to grow, and we'll continue to build on that.

items.statement: International routes are more accretive than domestic.
items.quote: But definitely, international is definitely more accretive than what the domestic is for us.

items.statement: Compensation accrual in Q1 included catch-up from prior quarters; going forward no catch-up.
items.quote: So, this particular quarter, because of finalization of the agreement, there's catch-up. Going forward, there's no catch-up that is needed to be done.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA of Rs. 10 to 12 per SCM for the year.
items.quote: Overall I think it is a comfortable position whatever guidance we have been giving in the past Rs. 10 to 12 per SCM EBITDA, we are hopeful that we will be able to achieve that for the year.

items.statement: Volume CAGR guidance remains slightly more than 6-7%.
items.quote: Our CAGR volume guidance remains the same, I mean, slightly more than 6% - 7%.

items.statement: UEPL volume growth expected more than 10% year-on-year for at least few years.
items.quote: So, we think that the volume base is small, but the growth rate will be more than 10% on year-on-year basis for at least few years to come in Unison, or maybe slightly more than that.

items.statement: CAPEX incurred around Rs. 250 crores in Q1.
items.quote: During the quarter, we have incurred CAPEX in the range of around Rs. 250 crores.

items.statement: Plan to add more than 50 CNG stations in MGL and 25 in Unison this financial year.
items.value: more than 50 stations in MGL, 25 in Unison
items.quote: we have set up a shift target around more than 50 stations we expect to add this financial year in MGL alone, and maybe another 25 stations will be added in Unison Enviro.

items.statement: Endeavor to maintain blended cost for priority sector in current range.
items.quote: And our endeavor will be that blended cost for priority sector remains in this range.

items.statement: Took a price increase of Rs. 1.5 in July.
items.quote: We have also taken a price increase, as you may be aware, in the month of July of Rs. 1.5, so our endeavor is to maintain margin in line with the gas cost available to us.

items.statement: Expect better volume growth in Q2 and Q3 due to seasonality.
items.quote: If you consider that there is a seasonality in Q1 always, so we expect that there will be better growth in Q2 and Q3.

items.statement: Industrial and commercial segments expected to get double digit growth this year.
items.quote: Industrial and commercial, we repeat that we will most probably be getting double digit growth in industrial and commercial segments this year also.

items.statement: Overall, expect more than 7% volume growth year-on-year.
items.quote: So, overall, we expect that more than 7% growth at least we will hit year-on-year.

items.statement: APM allocation may reduce slightly or stabilize; monitoring exchange rate.
items.quote: Last few quarters it has been reduced but let us see that the trend may get stabilized or may reduce slightly.

items.statement: CNG two-wheeler launch seen as volume growth opportunity.
items.quote: It has opened up new set of customers for CGD companies, and MGL sees it as another volume growth opportunity considering the large number of two wheelers in the country.

items.statement: UEPL expected to cross 1 mmscmd in six to seven years.
items.quote: And we think our guidance was that six, seven years we will cross 1 mmscmd, maybe 1.3 mmscmd.

items.statement: Targets disbursements of over INR60,000 crores this year, with 20% done in Q1.
items.quote: And this year, the target is around 60,000 plus kind of disbursement, out of which 20% disbursement has been done in this quarter.

items.statement: Confident to grow deposits by 25% this year.
items.quote: Overall, we remain confident to grow our deposits by 25% this year, but we will continue to revisit our deposit strategy quarterly based on ma rket liquidity conditions and the rate of interest dynamics.

items.statement: Expects credit cost for the year to be in the range of 1.10%-1.15%.
items.quote: As we guided in our March call that overall, we believe that the kind of market we deal in, the kind of yield we deal in the assets, normalized credit cost would be in the range of 1.10 %- 1.15%.

items.statement: Aims to defend ROA of 1.6% for the year.
items.quote: So we really want to stick to our earlier guidance that we should defend our last year ROA, which is 1.6%.

items.statement: Guides full-year NIM corridor of 5.7% to 5.8%.
items.quote: I think for now, our guidance remains that our margins -- full year margins for this financial year will be in the corridor of last year's, which was about 5.5 %, so maybe add about 10, -15 basis points on that, but allow us to come back on that. I think anything around about -- I'll be happy with anything between 5.7% to 5.8%.

items.statement: Plans to raise around INR25,000 crores of deposits in the next 9 months.
items.quote: So I believe that we will be able to build around INR25,000 crores of deposits in the next 9 months.

items.statement: Expects cost to income ratio for the year to be around 61%-62%.
items.quote: So I believe over the year, it will be around 61%-62%. That's my sense.

items.statement: Guides credit cost for credit card business at 6.5% to 7% for the full year.
items.quote: The quarter was a bit seasonal, but I think for the full year, we have guided for anywhere between 6.5% to 7% that should remain.

items.statement: Plans to issue around 5 lakh credit cards for the full year.
items.quote: Yes. No, I think for the full year, we remain on -- very similar to last year number, around 5 lakhs cards. So it will pick up as we go along the year.

items.statement: Expects cost of funds to increase by around 35 basis points for the year.
items.quote: So that's the sense that we want to really be guiding you that maybe around 35 bps, our cost can go up.

items.statement: Aims to achieve approximately INR2,000 crores in acquisition from Samriddhi branches.
items.quote: We aim to achieve approximately INR2,000 crores in acquisition from these branches which are aligning with AU productivity and should reach similar run rates by quarter 3.

items.statement: Plans to take 3% annualized credit cost on microfinance portfolio.
items.quote: And the second one was that we will have a credit cost of 3% annualized beginning first. And we have started that process now, right . We have taken it -- we haven't waited for the year, but we have started doing it from the first quarter itself.

items.statement: Expects branches launched until FY20 to breakeven in FY25.
items.quote: Our focus on branch profitability will leverage the comprehensive product suit we offer to cross-sell and upsell to liability customers aiming for branches launched until FY'20 to breakeven in FY'25.

items.statement: No capital raise envisaged in this financial year.
items.quote: No, no, no capital raise resolution is a very routine, enabling one. So we don't envisage any kind of capital raise in this financial year

items.statement: Expects other income to sustain at 1.7% of assets.
items.quote: For the overall fees, I think we delivered about 1.7% of assets this particular quarter. And if the last full year as well, we were around 1.7% kind of level. So we do hope that we can sustain that number, if not grow.

items.statement: Targets 15 to 18 SME IPOs this year, with profit at least 5x bigger than last year.
items.quote: So this year, we have already helped two companies to get listed on BSE SME and target is 15 more companies should be coming in the rest of the 9 years. And when I'm saying 15, that means we are already working on the DRHP, and some has been filed and some are to be filed in the next 2 months. So 15 plus 2, 17 -- 15 to 18 companies we are targeting this year.

items.statement: Targets MTF book of INR250 crores by end of this financial year.
items.quote: And we started MTF -- for the retail, we started MTF last year, and I proudly say when we are talking, we have MTF book of INR150 crores right now, and we are targeting INR250 crores of MTF book by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Targets NBFC loan book of around INR500 crores by 2027.
items.quote: So right now, once we will build like secured book, definitely we will get support from the banks and organically and inorganically, we are targeting at least INR500 crores book by 2027.

items.statement: MTF book should be around INR700 crores by 2027.
items.quote: I will -- next time, I will also give the projections about the insti business, merchant banking, MTF should not be less than INR500 crores, it's a concern again, by 2027, I guess should be around 700 crores.

items.statement: Expects to maintain 28% net profit margin for the year; 25% was the lowest.
items.quote: But I think as the year will progress, we'll see that we're able to manage this 28% margin overall in the year. So that's kind of margin we're expected. We're not expecting anything in 40s or 45 because in that case, you have to stop new verticals, you have to stop incurring big costs.

items.statement: Long-term profit margin range is 30% plus or minus 3%.
items.quote: Yes. So even in our previous con calls, we had always maintained that 30% plus, minus 3% is approximately the long-term range that we are looking at for the profit margin percentage.

items.statement: Plans to apply for AIF and PMS licenses this year, start operations next financial year.
items.quote: So we are planning to apply for AIF very soon and PMS license with the SEBI. Once we get the license, we hope next financial we start the operations also.

items.statement: STT increase and capital gains tax changes pose short-term challenges but expected to be absorbed in 2-3 months.
items.quote: Yes, it is a challenge. It will definitely take some time to get absorbed. But I think in next -- once it is applicable, then in 2 to 3 months, things will change as per the new cost structure.

items.statement: Bullish on uTrade Algo product, expects it to be a game changer in next 3 years.
items.quote: And this product will be widely accepted in coming years like the next 3 years, we are very bullish on this product and it can change the entire course of the company in the coming years.

items.statement: Plans to start wealth management division next year, applying for licenses this year.
items.quote: So wealth is one we are announcing that we'll start next year. We are applying for the licenses this year.

items.statement: GNPA for NBFC subsidiary this quarter around 3%.
items.quote: The GNPA for this quarter should be around 3% approximately, give or take, yes, around 3%, give or take, yes.

items.statement: Total loan book currently around INR200 crores, reduced from INR250 crores last quarter.
items.quote: So the total loan book is around INR200 crores currently. It has reduced from last quarter, which was around INR250-odd crores due to a certain impact in Punjab and Haryana territory.

items.statement: Capex plan of around INR15 billion for next 7 quarters for announced projects, largely funded through internal accruals.
items.quote: The company continues to invest in its growth and has a capex plan of around INR15 billion for the next 7 quarters for the announced projects, which will be largely funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: Expect 90% of office portfolio leased out by end of calendar year.
items.quote: We continue to expect 90% of the office portfolio leased out by end of the calendar year.

items.statement: Expect better flow-throughs and higher margins for the rest of the year.

items.statement: Expect to add 130 rooms to Bangalore in December.

items.statement: Expect occupancies and rates to grow sharply starting October.

items.statement: Expect to complete Four Points renovation in around 10 months.

items.statement: Expect to add 1,000 rooms pipeline over next 3 years.

items.statement: Expect to grow margins.

items.statement: Expects MDF margins around 16.4% for current year.

items.statement: New MDF plant to start production in Q3FY25.

items.statement: Margins have bottomed out and will be better in Q2.
items.quote: I think the margins have bottomed out. Definitely, since we are seeing volume improvement in Quarter 2, I think margins will definitely be better in Quarter 2 as compared to Quarter 1.

items.statement: Plywood segment to be EBITDA positive by end of year.

items.statement: New plant EBITDA positive at 55% capacity utilization.

items.statement: No major further reduction in market pricing expected.

items.statement: Possibility of passing on timber cost increases in coming months.

items.statement: No price increase assumption for Q2FY25 yet.

items.quote: We are also hopeful that in the next month, month and a half, we will see some price improvement in plywood as well. We have already sent out a notice to the market for the same. And we are hopeful that within a month's time that w ill get implemented.

items.statement: Imports not expected to increase significantly for next 2 quarters.

So, I don't think imports will go up significantly at least for the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Demand in developed markets remains robust.

items.statement: Value-added products were 47% of domestic volumes in Q1.

items.statement: Organized segment competition is a bigger concern than unorganized.

items.statement: Confirmed revenue and high-probability extensions to contribute 10%+ growth.
items.quote: So, 10% of growth will come just from all the confirmed work and the high potential extensions that we have.

items.statement: Debt to EBITDA expected to stay within 3-3.5x and net debt to EBITDA 2-2.25x despite expansions.
items.quote: In spite of these all expansion, which are going to happen over the next 5, 6 years, we don't see our debt to EBITDA crossing anywhere between 3 to 3.5 and a net debt to EBITDA about 2 to 2.25.

items.statement: Udaipur to reach 75% utilization by Q4 FY26.
items.quote: FY26, quarter 4, I think we'll achieve that.

items.statement: Expects demand to improve and prices to inch up in Q2.
items.quote: I think this is general market trend and price which I see, right? So, that is what is there and second quarter definitely once demand goes up, prices are going to go up, right?

items.statement: Premium product share at close to 30% in Q1.
items.quote: In terms of premiumization, our premium product was at 30%, close to 30%, which is a good moment and that has impacted our bottom line to an extent.

items.statement: Merger with Udaipur Cement Works expected to create stronger balance sheet and synergies, but savings not quantified.
items.quote: But more importantly that merger will help to make a stronger balance sheet with all the capaci ties consolidated into a single entity. And cash flow also in a single entity will help us to grow faster organic or inorganic

items.statement: Northeast project approvals expected by end of year; civil work to start in Q4.
items.quote: What we believe that, we are in July, so by end of this year, we are going to have approvals in place. And somewhere quarter 4 of this year, we'll start the civil work.

items.statement: Conveyor belt approvals expected in a couple of months.
items.quote: So, we are still awaiting approvals. That is in the final stages. And we are expected to get that maybe in another couple of months’ time.

items.statement: Expects CV industry to be flattish at worst, with possible growth for the full year.
items.quote: We think at worst, industry would be flattish, but we can also expect some kind of growth in the overall CV industry as well for the whole year.

items.statement: Expects next three quarters to continue the momentum.
items.quote: It does seem the next three quarters should continue the momentum.

items.statement: Expects Power Solutions business to register healthy growth on a full year basis.
items.quote: On a full year basis, we expect this business also to register healthy growth.

items.statement: Aims to double defense business in the next 2 to 2.5 years.
items.quote: So, now our intention is to double the defense business again in the next 2 to 2.5 years.

items.statement: Plans to double defense top line again in the next two years or so.
items.quote: And now going forward, based on a very strong pipeline of orders and visibility of orders that can come in, we hope to double that number again in the next two years or so.

items.statement: Retained earlier capex estimate of around 750 crores.
items.quote: On the CAPEX side, I would say that we have retained our earlier estimates as Shenu had indicated earlier. It could be around 750 crores.

items.statement: May invest another 500 to 750 crores in associate companies, primarily Switch and OHM.
items.quote: It could be around another 500 to 750 crores of the investments in the associate companies , primarily, Switch and OHM.

items.statement: Expects to do better on margin front due to operating leverage and cost headroom.

items.statement: Not taken any price increase in Q1 or Q2 so far.

items.quote: We will be launching four more LC V products in the next few quarters within the year.

items.statement: DFC impact is medium-term, no major significant impact in next couple of years.
items.quote: A lot remains to be seen, but we don’t think there will be a major significant impact in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Rights issue expected to close on 19th August; proceeds to repay short-term debt for acquisitions.
items.quote: We announced the rights issue. We expect to close on 19th August. And as announced, we will use the proceeds to repa y short-term debt finan cing raised for acquisitions.

items.statement: Committed to move growth businesses from 20% to 30% of portfolio; 30% will grow at 30%.
items.quote: We had committed last quarter when we finished the acquisitions that we will move our growth businesses from being 20% of the portfolio to 30% of the portfolio. W e had also committed saying 20% of the portfolio was growing 30% and that 30% will grow at 30%.

items.statement: Committed to complete Organic India integration in 100 days.
items.quote: While the Capital Foods integration is largely complete, the transactions for Organic India was completed on 16th April and we have made a commitment of completing it in 100 days.

items.statement: Plan to aggressively expand vending machine installed base from 1700 machines.
items.quote: We now have an installed base about 1700 odd machines and the plan is to aggressively expand that going forward.

items.statement: Expect gross margins for acquisitions to return to stated levels and climb higher.
items.quote: Ultimately, we do expect gross margins to come back to the numbers that we stated which is significantly accretive to our current portfolio. In fact, if anything, the gross margin should climb higher and not stay where they are.

items.statement: Confident to deliver business case for Capital Foods and Organic India acquisitions.
items.quote: So, right now, we are working on what we have. And we remain quite confident that we will be able to deliver the business case.

items.statement: Amortization charge for acquisitions is about Rs. 55 crores per quarter, likely static.
items.quote: So, on the acquisition as I mentioned while discussing the financials, that is a charge of about Rs. 55 crores per quarter and that is likely to remain static quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: No intention to move energy drinks into PET bottles; cups are key differentiator.
items.quote: And there is no intention currently of moving into PET bottles. Cups is my single biggest differentiator, helps me manage the price point, helps me build the imagery and therefore currently we will stick to it.

items.statement: Will provide more specific volume and pricing data going forward.
items.quote: But point taken, we will try to be more specific as we go forward.

items.statement: Will consider aligning segment reporting with management commentary for transparency.

name: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Ltd

items.statement: Management expects volume growth of about 20%, possibly 25%, for the year.
items.quote: As indicated in my last call also, we expect a margin growth of about close to 20%, definitely. It could inch closer to the 25% also in fact.

items.statement: Management expects margins to remain at current levels for FY25.
items.quote: Yes, thank you, definitely as it has been indicated by us, the management and by all of us on the call, these margins are there to stay and we are very confident of our margin levels as we talk about at least for the year 24-25 that we are in.

items.statement: Management expects margins to continue in FY26 if global outlook remains favorable.
items.quote: But broadly if the global outlook and, the global foray is going to be as it is, you can expect the margins to continue even in the year FY25-26.

items.statement: Camphor sales along with Isoborneol and Isobornyl acetate have looked up well.
items.quote: Camphor sales along with Isoborneol and Isobornyl acetate has really looked up very well and of course as informed in my previous investor call, the company is one more step in the process of obtaining the U.S. FDA and we definitely are poised to get the U.S. FDA by this year-end or so.

items.statement: Camphor prices increased 7-8% in last 1-1.5 months and expected to continue.
items.quote: Last one, one and a half month, we have seen close to about maybe 7% to 8% or so in fact.

items.statement: Finished goods prices in spot market are trending up due to raw material price increases and shortages.
items.quote: We feel, with regard to certain specific things happening around on the spot market, we are seeing definitely a trend that the prices on the finished goods are going up.

items.statement: Operating efficiencies and yield improvements have increased margins and will sustain them.
items.quote: Long and short, what we're trying to say is that in terms of operating efficiencies, we have come a long way by virtue of which the margins are definitely gone up and they will continue to be at those levels where the prices could go up, prices could go down, but this would continue.

items.statement: Menthol project to increase ROCE by 200-300 bps over 3 years.
items.quote: And you will find that over the next 3 to 4 years, of course it takes 18 months to implement the project. items.statement: Utilization is upwards of 85% and expected to reach near 100% for new products.
items.quote: It's been upwards of 85%. That's what I'm saying that Galaxmusk and Camphor have really done very well, and we expect in this quarter that it could be almost at 100% capacity as we talk about.

items.statement: Freight costs negotiated down and some passed on to customers.
items.quote: So, we have been able to, to some extent negotiate and bring down the prices with most of the sea freight and freight forwarders. And hence, you will see a saving happening around on my other expenses front.

items.statement: Latin America sales improving with better payment terms and dollar availability.
items.quote: Latin America definitely is looking up as we speak in fact. And some of the countries have also made some sort of an understanding with regard to the dollar availability and they have made some sort of a schedule as to how the government is ready to pass o n this dollar on various number of days.

items.statement: Privi Fine Sciences acquisition awaiting shareholder approval; integration planned post-approval.
items.quote: After the shareholder approval is received, we already have a plan to integrate everything. So that going forward we are able to optimize on the cost also.

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 147 days, targeting 130-135 days.
items.quote: Second, with regard to the working capital cycle, yes, there has been an improvement from the 150 to 170 days. We are close to in this quarter from in a moved down from 155 in the previous quarter to this quarter of about 147 days on a consol basis. And we expect to move around as indicated in the last call also. We expect, we could be at on 135, though it would be great if we are able to do 130.

items.statement: NIMs have been trending downwards and will probably be range-bound.
items.quote: Clearly, from a NIM perspective, we were at a peak NIM about year and half ago and they have been trending downwards and which has got everything to do with the rate cycle which RBI have. So, in line with that, o ur NIMs have been operating and they will be probably in range-bound

items.quote: And , therefore, if you look at the NII growth year-on-year for this quarter, the NIM for this quarter is at 4.36 %, whereas the NIM for the same quarter last year was 4.78 %.

items.quote: For example, if we look at, as I said, over the last four or five quarters, the NIM has gone down by 40 basis points.

items.quote: We continu e to work on increasing prices, refini ng credit parameters and optimising sourcing cost.

items.quote: As we have been saying, I mean the capacity utilisation across corporate is now ranging in the 75% to 80%.

items.quote: And corporate CAPEX has been in a way a lot of it is getting funded through internal accruals.

items.quote: So, the portfolio between personal loan and credit card is about 14% of our portfolio.

items.quote: The portfolio has increased by about 24% year -on-year and 1.5% sequentially and this number was significantly higher as you are aware in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Credit costs are still 50 bps of the average loan.
items.quote: So, if you look at it, the credit costs are still 50 bps of the average loan.

items.quote: And the provisioning coverage remains at about 80%.

items.quote: The additions to KCC has been about ₹721 crore.

items.statement: Credit cost to advances would be about 50 bps, adjusting for AIF provision release and KCC seasonality.
items.quote: Adjusting for the AIF provision release and the seasonality of KCC provisioning which comes in only in Q1 and Q3, the credit cost to advances would be about 50 bps, which is the adjusted credit cost level we had spoken of in the earnings calls for the previous two quarters as well.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to further normalise gradually, but will be better than historical levels.
items.quote: This, I would expect it to further normalise gradually, but what the long period average will be, in the kind of portfolio construct and the systemic construct that we have now, is difficult to say at this point, but I would say that it will be better than historical levels for sure.

items.statement: Personal loan growth expected to be closer to 20% or lower by year-end.
items.quote: On PL, we had taken a number of actions last year and I think the growth rate has come off; if you look at the year-on-year growth, it has come from 40% to 24% and I am guessing by the time we end this year it will be closer to 20% kind of number or lower.

items.statement: Deposit rates tight; wholesale rates not down, retail hikes seen; will calibrate based on market.
items.quote: As you said, the deposit rates continue to be tight, the wholesale deposit rates have not really come down during the first quarter as they usually do and of late there has been one or two hikes in the retail deposit rate also, although in one case it is at a longer tenor.

items.statement: Competition on corporate lending side; will calibrate both deposits and loans.
items.quote: On the lending side also, I think there is a price competition the other way and we are seeing fair amount of competition particularly on the corporate side. So, we will keep calibrating both.

items.statement: Domestic LDR to remain in low-to-mid 80s, no big change expected.
items.quote: As far as the LDR is concerned, I think this low-to-mid 80s is the level of domestic LDR that we have historically operated at and I don't see any big change in that, it may vary one quarter here up or down, but broadly it should be at that level.

items.statement: Revised LCR guidelines may impact deposit and loan markets; impact to be assessed.
items.quote: As far as both deposit growth and loan growth are concerned, of course, over the next couple of quarters, we will also have to take into account the impli cations of the revised guidelines on 15 LCR, the draft of which has come, which will have some impact on both deposit markets and loan markets

items.statement: LCR impact estimated at 10 to 15 percentage points, based on analyst reports.
items.quote: On the first one, I think it's a fairly e asy calculation to do because the LCR disclosures are public and at least I think all the analyst reports that we've seen as of yesterday for the major banks talk about between a 10 to 15 percentage point impact and I think that's a fair estimate

items.statement: Recoveries pace to vary and may not continue; credit cost to normalize upwards.
items.quote: On the recoveries, I think we have been saying for some time that the pace of recoveries will vary and may not continue at the same pace, because we were still collecting out of the pool of NPAs that got created in fiscal ’21 and fiscal ‘22. So, that pace will come-off and therefore, the credit cost will also normalize upwards.

items.statement: Cards portfolio less than 5% of loan book; seen as growth business with investments.
items.quote: As far as cards is concerned, it's less than 5% of our loan portfolio and whatever happens in the credit cost there has flowed into the overall numbers. I would say that we see i t as a growth business and we are investing in growth in that business in terms of both products and distribution and our

items.statement: Yield on advances stable; no real increase in market pricing; competition in corporate and mortgages.
items.quote: I think the yield on advances really has been at a stable level over the last year. If you look at all the categories that you mentioned, there has been no real increase in market pricing which would have taken the yields up.

items.statement: OPEX growth has been coming down; Q4 adjusted 12-13%, this quarter 10%-odd; no material increase expected.
items.quote: We don't give guidance on expenses or different components of expenses, but as you would have seen, the OPEX growth has been coming down over the quarters and the adjusted growth for Q4 was also between 12% and 13%, this quarter it 19 is 10%-odd. So, I would expect that should be a fair

items.statement: No material tightening in cards and personal loans; minor tweaking ongoing.
items.quote: I don't think we are looking at really any material tightening. I mean there is minor tweaking and refinement that we keep doing.

items.statement: Corporate loan growth steady at around 10%; competitive intensity remains.
items.quote: So, I think if you look at for the last several quarters, our corporate book has grown at around 10%, it could be 8% to 9% in one quarter, it could be 11% to 12% in another and that is a pretty steady pace, no change in approach.

items.statement: Yields on home loans and auto loans increased between FY22 and FY23, but not going up further now.
items.quote: So, I think if you look at, for example, products even although it has been very competitive, but products like home loans, auto loans or a number of asset classes, yields have gone up between certainly FY'22, '23, that is not going up any further now.

items.statement: No change in branch expansion plans.
items.quote: On the branch, no change as such.

items.statement: Targets lignite volume in excess of 9 million tons for current year.
items.quote: Current year, we should be in excess of 9 million. And the year thereafter, we would like to improve on that.

items.statement: Plans 4x revenue growth by 2030, with lignite, coal, and critical minerals contributing equally.
items.quote: By the end of this decade, you should see our revenues being quadrupled. Of these revenues, a major share would come from, again, our existing business, lignite and coal, which you know very well. And the remaining would come from these new age critical minerals.

items.statement: Targets lignite volume of about 15 million tons per year by end of decade.
items.quote: So by the end of this decade, you should see volumes in a year about 15 million tons from lignite in Gujarat.

items.statement: Plans capex in excess of INR3,000 crores for current year and next two years.
items.period: current year and next two years
items.quote: Capex plans are very ambitious. In excess of INR3,000 crores current year and for the coming 2 years also.

items.value: INR3,030 crores, INR3,424 crores, INR3,000 crores
items.quote: This capex for INR3,000 crores is over the next -- is INR3,000 crores -- INR3,030 crores this year. Next year, it would go to INR3,424 crores thereafter, again, INR3,000 crores and thereafter, again, INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Plans capex in excess of INR1,700 crores for coal blocks.
items.quote: In excess of INR1,700 crores spread over some time.

items.statement: Cumulative capacity of three Odisha coal blocks is 26 million tons per annum.
items.quote: The cumulative capacity of all 3 coal blocks in Orissa is 26 million tons per annum.

items.statement: Current margins are in the range of 30% plus, expected to continue.
items.quote: Prices in terms of margins, while 2 years ago, the margins were in excess of 50%. They are now in the range of 30% plus. Then again, we expect these margins to continue, but we are not in the business of forecasting, but we do take forecasting views into consideration.

items.statement: Lignite pricing is developed in response to imported coal as main competitor.
items.quote: What has changed in the past 2.5 years is lignite pricing has been developed as a response to our main competitor that is imported coal. So that is a bigger metric, which controls our prices.

items.quote: Mission 18.0 aims at targeting 18 lakh tons of sales of lignite in the monsoon quarter. This was -- this stood at barely 6 lakh last year.

items.statement: Mission 2000 aims to increase active customers to over 2,000.
items.quote: And Mission 2000 is to, again, take the number of our customers, active customers in excess of 2,000.

items.statement: Lignite contributes over 90% of revenues currently, expected to continue for 2-3 years.
items.quote: So GMDC is going to keep on focusing on its core which is lignite and which contributes in excess of 90% of our revenues currently. So for the coming 2 to 3 years, you should see something like that continuing to happen.

items.statement: Debt equity ratio will not exceed 1% under any scenario.
items.quote: But in no case does our debt equity ratio rise above 1%. So these are solid plans backed by serious numbers.

items.statement: Open to all ideas for divesting cross holdings in other Gujarat PSUs.
items.quote: We would be open to all ideas.

items.statement: Plans groundbreaking for Baitarani-West coal mine in Q1 FY26.
