items.statement: Customers willing to pay INR350 for administration; learning component from INR500 to INR2,500.
items.quote: So in terms of the PAPMs without the learning component, we see that the customers are willing to pay about INR350 just for the administration. Learning component, we see that they're willing to pay -- we actually have a slab-based system based on which university, what kind of learning programs, so from INR500 all the way to INR2,500, we can do it.

items.statement: Average PAPM for the quarter was INR679, almost same as last quarter.
items.quote: Yes, we are currently at INR679 of PAPM for this quarter, which is almost same as last quarter.

items.statement: Salary inflation impacts gross margin percentage due to large fixed markup base.
items.quote: That's right, Dhvani, because with the consistent increase in associate salaries, the salary inflation is impacting the gross margin as a percentage.

items.statement: 75% of business is on fixed markup model, impacting gross margin percentages.
items.quote: So while the incremental growth is happening mostly on variable markup model, given the large base that is on fixed markup, almost 75% of our business is still on fixed markup model, that's kind of impacting the gross margin percentages.

items.statement: Total cash balance stands at INR439 crores as of 30th June 2024.
items.quote: Total cash balance stands at INR439 crores as of 30th June 2024.

items.statement: Received TDS refund of INR115 crores during the quarter.
items.quote: Free cash balance has improved during the quarter, owing to TDS refund of INR115 crores received during this quarter with full allowance on our 80JJAA claims.

items.statement: Standalone material margins improved to 31.3% vs 29.4% YoY; standalone EBIT margin ex-A&P at 14.9%, up 1.6% YoY and 30 bps QoQ; ECD EBIT margin ex-A&P at 19.8%, up 2.3% YoY; Lighting EBIT margin ex-A&P at 11.3%, up 20 bps QoQ
items.quote: Despite an increase in raw mater ial prices during the quarter, our standalone material margins improved to 31.3% versus 29.4% a year ago. I'm also happy to share that we delivered a standalone EBIT margin of 14.9% excluding A&P spend

items.statement: Price increases taken across categories to offset commodity inflation; 1.5% price hike in fans in mid-May; fourth consecutive quarter of price increases; evaluating further hikes depending on RM basket evolution
items.quote: You've, of course, seen raw material prices have trended upwards in Q 1 FY25. To combat the pressure on gross margins, we've taken price increases practically across categories, being industry leading in that

items.statement: Early signs of improvement in consumer sentiment; intense summer boosted cooling products; supply chain glitches limited some sales; weather patterns unusual making outlook uncertain
items.quote: We are keenly watching consumer sentiments and the underlying demand scenario, which is showing some early signs of improvement. We have witnessed an intense summer in several regions of the country, which has, of course, helped the sale of our cooling products.

items.statement: Premium saliency in large domestic appliances at 25.6%; fan premiumisation moved from 17-18% to 24-25% range, targeting 40% in 3-4 years; BLDC fans a growth category, currently #2 player
items.quote: Premium saliency of large domestic appliances also improved and was at 25.6%. Moreover, three premium models of water heaters were launched to aid the premiumisation in that segment.

items.statement: Solar pumps executed ₹21 crores in Q1; healthy pipeline being built; execution rate improved QoQ from ₹28 crores in H2 to ₹21 crores in last quarter; order book not disclosed
items.quote: In solar pumps, and you're aware that solar pump is an area that we've forayed into recently and continue to gain traction in that segment. We executed orders worth about ₹21 crores in the quarter that went by.

items.statement: No expansion plans disclosed; strategic sourcing plan rolling out to control key value chain parts; in-house manufacturing payback quick due to high asset turnover; equally split in-house/outsourced for fans
items.quote: None that we are in a position to disclose yet.

items.statement: Paid ₹300 crores towards NCDs for Butterfly acquisition; ₹300 crores debt remaining, expected to be paid by July next year; net cash positive; committed to strong dividend, debt reduction, and operational investments
items.quote: You are aware on the balance sheet side that we paid ₹300 crores towards NCDs that we had taken on for the acquisition of Butterfly. We still have ₹300 crores of debt left from that acquisition.

items.statement: Ambition to grow portfolio in double-digits and expand profits faster than revenue; no forward margin guidance; Butterfly turnaround expected from H2 onwards; lighting growth trajectory started
items.quote: So overall, our ambit i on continues to grow in double -digit for the portfolio as a whole and expand our profits better than the revenue growth

items.statement: Weather patterns unusual creating demand uncertainty; commodity prices trending up (copper, aluminium, ABS); regulatory headwinds; competitive intensity never abates; price erosion in lighting continues
items.quote: Weather patterns have been quite unusual, and while this created a spike in demand in this season, it's of course difficult to see how this pans out.

items.statement: A&P spends increased ~30% YoY and ~60% QoQ; launched #PicturePerfectFan campaign; 41 new products launched in Q1; 2 innovation patents filed; alternate channels at 17% of sales, growing 30% YoY; e-commerce ₹100 crore+ for 4th consecutive qu
items.quote: A&P spends have increased ~30% YoY and ~60% QoQ. We've launche d a successful marketing campaign around #PicturePerfectFan, which I hope many of you have seen during the

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 13.38%; management hopes to continue at same level but will not revise guidance upward yet
items.quote: It would be difficult for me to comment because it is quite dynamic in terms of the product mix. We hope to continue at the same level. Let us see if something is going to be favorable for us in Q2.

items.statement: Export revenue maintained at 8-10% of total; US market weakness expected to persist for next three quarters before improving
items.quote: Export is a little concern in terms of slowness in the market, primarily the US market . But still we are able to maintain that 8% to 10% of the content of export in our total revenue.

items.statement: Content per vehicle roughly 2x vs 2019 levels; could reach 3x in coming years as digitalization shifts from LCD to TFT and connected solutions
items.quote: If I take X as my reference in 2019, we have been quite easily like 2x times or marching towards 3x times in the future to come.

items.statement: Robust order books for next two years with confirmed business from various customers; new product development on track
items.quote: We have got very robust order book s f or th e next two years with confirmed businesses from various customers. And we are in the right path in terms of the new product development with various customers.

items.statement: Capacity planned on two-shift basis with N+1 approach; third shift kept for contingency; in-house line machine building allows flexible capacity addition
items.quote: Generally on an assembly line we take on our two shift bases in terms of our capacity calculation depending on customer requirement, generally we plan for N + 1 , something like that.

items.statement: Labor case contingent liability increased to Rs. 55 crores due to interest accumulation; no new cases filed
items.quote: The increase in contingent liability on account of labor case is on account of the interest accumulation for one more year. So, there is no additional labor case which ha s coming.

items.statement: E-cockpit and disc brake projects in intense testing and validation; SOP expected in next 12-18 months
items.quote: In the next 12 to 18 months, we should go into SOP of these two products.

items.statement: Battery Management System prototypes in final development stage; first samples expected next month; telematics platform under customer testing; no revenue expected this financial year
items.quote: we have not given any revenue guidance as such. O nce the products are tested by the customers and accepted , post which we will be able to share revenue credit. But we are not taking any revenue credits for this financial

items.statement: Aspirational target of Rs. 3,600 crores revenue by FY26 remains on track; double-digit revenue growth expected in FY25 based on past three-year trend
items.quote: Yeah, it's pretty on target, yeah.

items.statement: Outperformance vs industry continues in both volume and value; historical average outperformance 5-10% vs vehicle growth; driven by market share gains and content increase
items.quote: If you average out, I think it should be quite easily close to a double digit, somewhere certain quarters it is like 5%, certain quarters are even like 10% when compared to the vehicle growth.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin expected around 33-34% as costs return with hiring and customer acquisition pickup.
items.quote: So we expect the margin to taper off a little bit from here, maybe at around 33-34%, and that should be the steady state margin from now on.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 37% in Q1 includes ~2-3% seasonal benefit, cost optimisation savings, and lower acquisition costs; will normalise as gross adds rise.
items.quote: So EBITDA margin is 37% for the current quarter. So, if you see about 2% to 3% was the operational leverage, which we were supposed to get, because in Q4, there are higher collections and therefore collection related cost s will also be there, which has not been in Q1

items.statement: Unique business enquiries grew 15% YoY to 25 million in Q1; annual run-rate ~100 million, 30% above pre-COVID levels.
items.quote: Unique business enquiries grew to Rs. 25 million representing year-on-year growth of 15%.

items.statement: Traffic flat; may use digital/video advertising if flatness persists.
items.quote: In terms of traffic, yes, there is a flatness, and we believe that, if that flatness continues, we will try and address that through digital advertising and through digital video advertising.

items.statement: Gold/Platinum now 50% of paying suppliers (up from 48%) and 75% of revenue (up from 72-73%); ARPU growth driven by category-based pricing on high-value categories.
items.quote: Our Platinum and Gold customers, which constitute approximately 50% of our customer base and 75% of the revenue continue to have low churn and grew very well in terms of both ARPU as well as count.

items.statement: Silver monthly churn ~6%/month, Silver annual ~36%/year; Gold <1%/month, Platinum ~0.5%/month; stubborn churn in metros delays net-add recovery.
items.quote: So, Gold and Platinum, less than 1% per month, and Silver monthly is about 6% per month, and Silver annual is about 36% p.a. or 3% to 4% per month.

items.statement: No net-add guidance for FY25; will reassess quarterly until net adds return to 5-6K/quarter.
items.quote: I'm in no position to commit any numbers on the net add as of now. I can only, say let's go quarter-by-quarter and as soon as we hit 5, 000, 6,000 again, then only I can give you any year end number.

items.statement: Acquired 10% stake in Baldor Technologies (IDfy) for identity/KYC/verification platform.
items.quote: we are pleased to share that we have got into an agreement to acquire 10% stake in M/S Baldor Technologies Private Limited, which operates I Dfy, an integrated identity platform offering products and solutions for KYC, background verification, merchant onboarding, buyer onboarding, risk mitigation and digital privacy.

items.statement: No price increase for Silver monthly/annual in 5-6 years (only removed 20% COVID discount); ARPU gains from category-based pricing on top 10% customers.
items.quote: we have not increased the prices on the top tier of the customer. As you know, we told you that we've been experimenting with the category -based pricing, and we hav e been developing a framework for city and category-based charging

items.statement: Busy Infotech: net billing Rs 23.4 cr (+4% YoY), revenue Rs 15.5 cr (+15%), deferred revenue Rs 51.5 cr (+41%), EBITDA Rs 1 cr (7% margin), 9.7K licenses sold, 373K total licenses.
items.quote: Busy has done a net billing of Rs. 23.4 crores in this quarter, representing a Y-o-Y growth of 4%. The revenue from operations have grown by 15% to Rs. 15.5 crores. The deferred revenues have grown by 41% to Rs. 51.5 crores. EBITDA for the quarter is at Rs. 1 crore with margins of 7%.

items.statement: Consolidated collections Rs 366 cr (+14% YoY), deferred revenue Rs 1,474 cr (+23%), revenue Rs 331 cr (+17%); standalone collections Rs 341 cr (+15%), revenue Rs 315 cr (+18%).
items.quote: Consolidated collections from customers were Rs. 366 crores in the quarter, representing year-on-year growth of 14%. IndiaMART standalone collections from customers for the quarter were at Rs. 341 crore registering year-on-year growth of 15%.

items.statement: Consolidated net profit Rs 114 cr; cash from operations Rs 136 cr; cash & treasury Rs 2,319 cr as of June 30, 2024.
items.quote: Consolidated net profit for the quarter was Rs. 114 crores. Consolidated cash generated from operations was Rs. 136 crores. Consolidated cash and treasury balance stood at Rs. 2,319 crores as of June 30, 2024.

items.statement: Plan to reduce supplier-to-buyer matchmaking ratio from 5 to 4 to improve lead maturity and reduce retail buyer noise.
items.quote: If you see the number of times a buyer is being introduced to a supplier. The ratio of total business enquiries delivered to unique business enquiries. That ratio we are slowly and slowly again converting. So that ratio we are looking at probably going towards more like four, from six.

items.statement: Channel partner model unchanged (~50% of sales); insourced sales staff from third-party payroll to reduce attrition and acquisition cost.
items.quote: About 50% sales were coming from our own staff, but they were not on IndiaMART role, they were on a third-party temp, staffing rol e. While there are channel partners, the channel partners have their own. So, what we have done is, stop using a third -party payroll, temp staffing service, to contain the employee attrition a bit

items.statement: No immediate ONDC integration; will join only when B2B traction becomes significant.
items.quote: Until unless they become popular enough in the B2C category, there is no point being a very early adopter there.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio guided at 46-47% for FY25, targeting 45-46% next year and 43-45% over 2-4 years
items.quote: We continue to maintain, for the full year basis, closer to 46 to 47% number, which we've started and guided towards last year, for the current year.

items.statement: Net flow guidance of 12-15% of opening ARR AUM (~Rs 2 lakh crs), implying Rs 25,000-35,000 crs for FY25
items.quote: On the net flows, we continue to be in 12 to 15% of our opening ARR AUM as our net flow guidance. Our opening ARR AUM was around about Rs 2 lakh Crs. So effectively, 12 to 15% of that would be in the region of Rs 25,000 Crs to around about Rs 30,000-35,000 Crs.

items.statement: Dividend payout philosophy maintained at 70-80% of profits
items.quote: On dividend payout, you're right. The broad philosophy continues to remain the same. It continues to be in the region of 70 to 80%.

items.statement: TBR income guided at Rs 400-600 crs for FY25, with steady-state quarterly run-rate of Rs 140-150 crs
items.quote: From a perspective of the TBR income on a quarterly basis I am still comfortable with that earlier number which is effectively the Rs 400-450 to 600 Crs for the year, effectively in the ballpark range of, on absolute south side round about a Rs 100-110 Crs a quarter absolute south side. And on a steady state basis, Rs 140-150 Crs a quarter.

items.statement: Asset Management net flows guided at Rs 8,000-10,000 crs for FY25, requiring Rs 13,000-14,000 crs gross flows
items.quote: I wouldn't look at it only from a quarter perspective, but from a year perspective, getting about Rs 8 to 10,000 Crs net flows from the asset management side pretty much stays on track.

items.statement: Mid-market + Global AUM guidance maintained at Rs 8,000-11,000 crs
items.quote: It will be around that number, it will be having in that ballpark number of Rs 8,000-11,000 Crs.

items.statement: Lending yield expected at 4.75-4.9% for next couple of quarters, steady-state target north of 5%
items.quote: For the next couple of quarters, we see a little bit of rate reduction. I think 4.75% to 4.9% is the more realistic number. On a stable state basis, we would want to come back to the north of 5%.

items.statement: Global business on track to launch in H2 FY25, technology onboarding in second half, targeting mid-September go-live
items.quote: We are in the second half of our technology onboarding program, we are pretty much on track to go alive mid-September, and that's really where it is.

items.statement: Asset Management gross sales ~Rs 3,500 crs in Q1 FY25 despite pre-IPO fund outflows; pipeline strong for new funds and international mandates
items.quote: On the asset management front, despite planned outflows from our pre-IPO flagship funds, our flows remained healthy, with gross flows of Rs 3,500+ Crs.

items.statement: Mutual Fund distribution team expanded from 20-22 to 27-28, targeting 40-50 by H2 FY25
items.quote: Historically, we used to have only around about 20-22 people in the Distribution team. We've expanded that to around about 27-28. I expect that team to go up to 40-50 people over the next half of this FY.

items.statement: UK litigation settled with Rs 87.6 crs exceptional provision (net of tax) to avoid 4-5 years of ongoing costs
items.quote: An amount of Rs 87.6 Crs have been disclosed as an exceptional item (net of taxes) towards provision for full and final settlement pertaining to the ongoing litigation in the UK against 360 ONE entities.

items.statement: Unlisted/private equity approach remains conservative: only offer co-investments from blind pool funds after high diligence bar
items.quote: We’ve typically not behaved like brokers, we don't end up syndicating too many transactions on the unlisted side. The only transactions we offer to our clients on the unlisted side, both in terms of co -investments or sometimes in the form of direct sales, are transactions which we are doing typically from a blind pool basis on

items.quote: From an activity of ARR to TBR, it is only a one time activity because we have just done a simple reclassification of the inactive ARR to TBR so that the retentions on the active ARR can kind of come out absolutely clearly.

items.statement: Full year NIM guidance remains 4.5% to 4.8%.
items.quote: However, our ove rall guidance for the full year remains intact. We will be closing the year in line with the guidance that we have given in the earlier quarters -which overall NIM will be in the range of 4.5% to 4.8

items.statement: Full year ROA guidance remains 1.5% to 1.8%.

items.statement: Overall credit cost for the year expected in 20 to 30 bps.
items.quote: Overall credit cost for the year will be in the range of 20 to 30 bps.

items.statement: SME segment expected to grow 35% over last year.
items.quote: Our expectations for full year is - SME will show a growth of almost 35% over last year.

items.statement: Corporate banking book expected to be flat year-on-year.
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, we will have a flat corporate banking book, but I do not think that there will be any major surprises going forward.

items.statement: CD ratio guidance remains comfortable up to 85%.
items.quote: Our guidance was also earlier that we are comfortable up to 85% of the CD ratio and we will continue with that guidance.

items.statement: NIM impacted by 40 bps due to penal charges regulatory change.
items.quote: Almost 40 bps kind of an impact has happened on account of this regulatory change, this quarter.

items.statement: Cost of funds expected to level off in coming quarters.
items.quote: The signs of policy rate reduction are clear now and it is anticipated that the cost of funds will level off in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Savings account cost in the range of 3%.

items.statement: Systemic credit growth robust; chase for deposits expected to continue.
items.quote: The systemic credit growth is still robust and we do no t expect the chase for deposits to abate

items.quote: Approximately, we have -- it will be in the range of INR 120 crores, INR 130 crores.

items.quote: And we also believe that it cannot last too long. It can be maybe one week, 10 days or 15 days. That is what we also think will be the case.

items.quote: In India, we are already at 4.8% PBT, just to – in our view.

items.quote: the EBITDA margin of the current financial year was 13.5% in order to maintain the trend in EBITDA margin
