So, we are assuming that yes, even if 20 gigawatts of that con verts, that's a fantastic opportunity out there that the company can deliver

items.statement: Hydro business requires additional Rs 500 crores of debt and guarantees over next few quarters, with cash conversion cycle exceeding 10 years.
items.quote: And the hydro basically is going to require additional Rs. 500 crores of debt and additional guarantees. A bank guarantee should be issued, which is going to not c onvert into margin and cash in reality

items.statement: Slump sale of hydro and gas businesses to related parties expected to provide net worth boost of Rs 296 crores (excluding taxes) and unlock Rs 700 crores non-funded limits and Rs 500 crores cash consumption limit.
items.quote: This transaction would have an impact of positive Rs. 296 crores excluding taxes which will provide net worth boost to the company. And this is significant.

items.statement: Transaction provides positive impact of Rs 214 crores plus Rs 38 crores (approx Rs 252 crores) net liability reduction, plus gas consideration of Rs 44 crores, and hydro premium of Rs 100 crores.
items.quote: This transaction provides a positive impact of Rs. 214 crores plus Rs. 38 crores, which is about Rs. 252 crores net liability reduction, which will improve net worth of your company and will further be boosted by consideration of gas Rs. 44 crores.

items.statement: Hydro business EBITDA projected at ~7% on Rs 1,000-1,100 crores topline for next three years, but net free cash flows expected negative for 2025 and 2026.
items.quote: However, if you look at the next, I mean, till 2030 you have the projection, but let's say, apple to apple 3 years, if you look at the next three years, average Rs. 1000 crores – Rs. 1,100 crores of topline is what we are forecasting for hydro. At an EBITDA level which is there what you're able to see is around 7%.

items.statement: Core services business growing consistently double-digit quarter-on-quarter with margins converting to cash within 6 months.
items.quote: In fac t, this year we are booking the highest core order value ever consistently quarter-on-quarter no w for several quarters. So that's something which is working well, good margins that converts i nto cash within 6 months

items.statement: Strategy shift to focus on four areas: core services, steam upgrades, FGD EPC, and Durgapur non-coal (pressure vessels, cryogenic, industrial) targeting Rs 18,000 crores market.
items.quote: With these four areas, as I said, we have an Rs. 18,000 crores marke t in these four areas. This will not be a quarter-on-quarter choppy business. This is stable quarter-on-quarter business, maybe slightly boring, but predictable

items.statement: Hydro projects face uncontrollable delays (geology, hydrology, topology, clearances, land acquisition, local issues) causing cost overruns and ceiling of price variation clauses.
items.quote: if you refer to the page 6, the reasons for delay are not controllable. It is geology, hydrology, topology. It is the critical electrical, mechanical work where we are depending on external parties. It is delays on the clearances wh ich are again in the hands of the developers. There are local issues on site which are environmental related issues etc. So those are the issues which are beyond our c

items.statement: Promoter GE Vernova ended depromoterization plan; will continue as promoter and supports strategy to focus on lower-risk, high-margin business.
items.quote: On 25th of July 24, GE Power India Limited issued a public disclosure mentioning that GE Steam Power International BV, the promoter, has ende d its plan to exit from GE Power India Limited and end its plan to depromoterize. GE Steam Power International BV will continue to be the promoter of the

items.statement: Hydro business not standalone; depends on GE Vernova consortium for technology and project execution; no third-party buyer feasible.
items.quote: Hydro, unfortunately, as I said earlier, is not a standalone business. It has dependencies o n other parts of GE Vernova to be able to compete in the market. Therefore, there is no third buyer who could buy this as a standalone entity. It is practically not possible because it's always a joint consortium order in partnership with other parties

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 FY25 revenue Rs.1,218 crores, EBITDA Rs.93 crores at 7.6% margin, PAT loss Rs.47 crores; all improved QoQ
items.quote: In line with our guidance the consolidated Q1 revenue stands at Rs.1,218 crores showing improvement quarter -on-quarter basis. The Q1 EBIT DA stands at Rs. 93 crores and EBITDA margin stands at 7.6%.

items.statement: Services business targeting 8-10% EBITDA margin for FY25
items.quote: steady state margin that we are expecting is in the range of 8 -10% EBITDA margin , that is what we are targeting for this particular financial year.

items.statement: Digital business targeting 5-7% growth in FY25
items.quote: overall we are targeting that we should be able to have at least 5-7% kind of growth in the digital business.

items.statement: Targeting 25% of revenue from data center products in medium term
items.quote: have set an ambitious target that approximately 25% of our revenue should come from our data center suite of products in the medium term.

items.statement: Targeting 4-5% sustainable fixed cost reduction across businesses
items.quote: We are targeting to reduce fixed costs, at least to the extent of 4 -5% on sustainable basis.

items.statement: Open order book Rs.9,883 crores at end of Q1 FY25
items.quote: We are happy to share that despite a significant order d escoping, our open order book stands at Rs.9,883 crores at the end of Q1 FY25 backed by steady order wins.

items.statement: Digital business order book Rs.377 crores
items.quote: We expect the future growth to be driven by robust order book of Rs.377 crores, healthy order pipeline and execution strength backed by the right team of leadership and consultants.

items.statement: Optical Networking Q1 FY25 EBITDA Rs.88 crores at 10.9% margin, substantial QoQ improvement
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stands at Rs.88 crores at 10.9% of revenues. EBITA margin reflects substantial improvement on Q -o-Q basis and stands low lower on Y-o-Y basis due to lower cable volumes.

items.statement: Global Services Q1 FY25 EBITDA Rs.25 crores at 6.9% margin
items.quote: Our selective order intake and execution focus has helped us achieve Q1 FY25 EBITDA of Rs.25 crores and EBITDA margin of 6.9%.

items.statement: Digital Q1 FY25 EBITDA loss Rs.17 crores, loss trending down YoY and margins improved QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA loss for Q1 FY 25 stands at Rs. 17 crores , t he EBITDA loss is trending downwards on Y -o-Y basis and also sugge sts improved margins Q-o-Q basis

items.statement: US inventory normalization expected in 1-2 quarters, then improved optical cable demand
items.quote: We do see the inventory levels coming down, and certainly between next one to two quarters, this should result in improved demand for our optical cable products.

items.statement: North America optical cable demand projected 13% CAGR to 2028; 9-12M incremental home passes in 2024
items.quote: CRU has projected that the North American optical cable demand is expected to grow at approximately 13% CAGR till 2028. The fiber deployment in the region stay ed strong at more than 9 million homes passed in 2023 alone and between 9 -12 million incremental home pa sses additions are expected in th e year 202 4.

items.statement: Highest ever optical connectivity attach rate 23% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We are happy to share that we recorded our highest ever optical connectivity attach rate during the last quarter at 23%.

items.statement: Provisional EU anti-dumping duty; STL confident on merits, has Italy facility to serve customers
items.quote: We are very confident on the merits of our case. We believe that with the right calculation levels, we do not believe there should be any case for anti-dumping and we are making all our representations with full effort.

items.statement: Italy facility scaled up, now one of largest in Europe; no specific capacity disclosed
items.quote: since we had acquired that facility, we have invested in scaling it up. And it's truly a world class facility. Now it's probably one of the largest facilities in Europe.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by Rs.769 crores from FY24
items.quote: We are happy to share that the net debt has reduced by Rs. 769 crores from FY24.

items.statement: Reiterated 15-20% consolidated growth with sustained margins; may revise projections by end of Q2
items.quote: Keeping in mind the continuous focus on government infrastructure development and efforts to strengthen the manufacturing sector, we hereby reiterate our earlier guidance and expect a growth of 15% to 20% on a consolidated basis with sustained margins.

items.statement: Expects 16-17% EBITDA margin for FY25, looks sustainable
items.quote: And we look forward to growing in this year with a 16% to 17% EBITDA margin, which looks really sustainable.

items.statement: Crane capacity to increase to 15,000-18,000 units by Q3 FY25
items.quote: But in any case, the capex which is also currently happening, by quarter 3, our cranes capacity will increase to anywhere between 15,000 to 18,000 cranes.

items.statement: Acquired 82 acres land; possession and capitalization expected in Q2 FY25; 22 acres development to start Q4 FY25
items.quote: And hopefully, within quarter 2, these lands will come into our possession and will be capitalized in our books. Most probably in quarter 2. There is very rare chance that slid es to quarter 3. And out of this -- the smaller chunk, around 22 acres, we intend to start development there as early as maybe quarter 4 within this year to increase our capacity for certain type of cranes further

items.statement: Order booking is okay; momentum tepid in July but expects improvement post mid-August
items.quote: And order booking with respect to the current business scenario is okay. So I mean, obviously -- yes, I won't say that the momentum is great as of now. But like I said, it will start improving around 10 to 15th of August.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 212 bps YoY to 17.11%; sequential dip of 85 bps due to lower revenue and higher provisions
items.quote: The operational revenues grew by 12.82% to INR734 crores with an expansion of 212 basis points in EBITDA margin to 17.11% from 15%.

items.statement: Annual price increase planned from January 1st; steel prices cooled off after recent increase; CEV V norms may reduce costs
items.quote: But going forward, we do our annual price increase, which we will do in the coming month of January, or 1st of January onwards. This will also be coupl ed with price increase on account of CEV V BS V norms where the costs are going down

items.statement: 50-50 JV with Kato Works for truck, crawler, rough terrain cranes (50-200 tons); JV to start FY26, target INR300-400 cr in 2-3 years, INR1000+ cr in 4-5 years
items.quote: The joint venture intends to produce medium and large-sized cranes, mainly truck cranes, crawler cranes and rough terrain cranes, for the growing Ind ian market. And in future, the JV also plans to utilize the technology which will be cultivated by the expertise of ACE and Kato to introduce a wide range of value-added products for the export market

items.statement: EV cranes ready, awaiting CMVR approval; expect 60-70% higher revenue per crane, better margins, 3-year payback for customers
items.quote: EV crane, I think with respect to revenue, it is going to be definitely better, 60%, 70% more for the crane, because the cost of electric machines are better. And the customer is able to recover this for a l ower cost of operation on account of fuel. So I think it will be a 3 - year payback period. And our margins would also be better compared to our conventional diesel engine things with respect

items.statement: Defense revenue target 3.5-4% of total in FY25 (up from 2.5%); medium-term target 5-10%
items.quote: With respect to defense, we have been increasing our business an d our, let's say, medium - to long-term target is 5% to 10% revenue generation contribution from defense. So this year, hopefully, from 1.5%, we should be able to be somewhere between 3.5% to 4% in the current period

items.statement: Infrastructure contributes ~45-50% of revenue; diversifying into defense and exports to mitigate government spending slowdown risk
items.quote: Today, infrastructure contributes about 35% of our revenue, 10% is real estate. So that's about 45%, 50% from infrastructure and real estate, and with real estate is 10%. there is a slowdown on account of government spending with respect to infra. I'm sure there will be some effect on us.

items.statement: Exports ~8-8.5% of revenue in FY25; target 15-20% in 3-4 years
items.quote: This year again, it's similar, 8%, 8.5%, obviously o n an increased base. And I think it will be start increasing further in the next year. This year, I think it will remain at about 8%, 8.5% of the increased revenue base

items.statement: Pre-buying expected in Q3 FY25 due to CEV IV to CEV V transition; hopes to hit 4-figure revenue mark in Q3
items.quote: I think earlier we were thinking of Q3. I'm still hopeful that we are in position to achieve it in Q3. And I think it should be possible because we expect, because the emission norms are changing from BS IV to BS V for construction equipment, and they are called CEV IV to CEV V. So we expect prebuying to happen in quarter 3 starting from September.

items.statement: Acquisition talks progressing; may have news in next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: So work is already progressing on that, and if everything goes well, maybe -- I think we have mentioned quarter-to-quarter, so maybe over the next 1 or 2 quarters we might have some news for you.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 2.3% to 2.5% for FY25 excluding Arena
items.quote: we are confident in terms of maintaining the EBITDA percentage between 2.3% to 2.5%.

items.statement: PAT margin target 1.3% to 1.4% on steady-state basis
items.quote: we think on a steady-state basis have sustained about 2.3% to 2.5% of operating profit, and about 1.3 to 1.4 percentage of PAT is something that we are gunning for.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 PAT margin 1.42% excluding Arena, highest Q1 revenue at INR19,328 crores
items.quote: Our profit after tax grew 13% year-on-year with a PAT percentage of 1.42. This has also been the highest Q1 revenue recorded at INR19,328 crores

items.statement: Inventory provisions increased to 13 bps from normal 6 bps impacting gross margin
items.quote: Our inventory provisions for the current quarter is at 13 bps, 1 -3 which normally as you know will be about 6 bps that's the incremental inventory provision that we're seeing.

items.statement: Turkey notebook PC market declined almost 30% per analysts; Arena incurred loss
items.quote: The notebook PC market declined almost 30% as per analys ts. We incurred a loss for the quarter

items.statement: India commercial PC growing strongly; enterprise and government decisions delayed by elections but recovering
items.quote: with mid -market definitely commercial PCs is growing strongly. There were two types of delays. One is enterprises, which are closely watching the outcome of the election result and some of them have actually now gone forward to make those decisions

items.statement: KSA recovery expected after government project readjustments; TSG impacted by India election delays and net revenue accounting
items.quote: And on KSA we do see recovery, Nitin. And there was a very visionary set of projects some of them got readjusted and right sized, but as we look at this quarter and going forward we do see recovery in KSA.

items.statement: Africa showing profitable growth recovery in East, West and Egypt; mobility and Technology Solutions returning
items.quote: Africa as already mentioned, we've seen a nice uptick both on top line and bottom line this quarter, both on East and West. Whether we'll have more surprises, I can't really say, but looks -- largely looks promising and same with Egypt.

items.statement: Cloud business grew 35% to INR899 crores; managed services only INR21 crores (<2% of cloud revenue)
items.quote: In terms of numbers our cloud revenue for the quarter is INR899 crores, previous year INR668 crores I mean showing a growth of 35% out of which managed services is about INR21 crores.

items.statement: Cloud services expected to stay under 5% of cloud revenue; professional services in migration, spin-offs, modernization
items.quote: We also work with our hyperscaler partners to drive consumption in workloads and basis their programs. But we do see a growth in the services segment, but it will never be very large. It'll probably go to less than 5% still.

items.statement: Formed new entity in Malaysia for cloud and professional services; entered South Africa in Q4 FY24; offices in Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan for Central Asia expansion
items.quote: We have had an interest to enter Singapore and Malaysia. So we just formed an entity recently in Malaysia. And our goal there is to work with our cloud partners, the hyperscaler partners to be able to make a foray and entrance in both the cloud resell and the professional services side

items.statement: Turkey demand correction due to high interest rates and Eid holidays; June-July uptick 30-40% but need 1-2 more quarters to confirm
items.quote: Between June and July, we already see an uptick of about 30% to 40% business between the 2 months. So we believe there is a correction that is happening. The demand is softening because of the high interest rate.

items.statement: Paynet divestment process ongoing awaiting regulatory approvals; expected to reduce interest cost
items.quote: the Paynet divestment the process is on. We are to get, I mean, approval from few regulatory authorities. So we're just keeping our fingers crossed in terms of Time line. As and when that gets consummated, Aejas, I think that's going to help us in terms of our interest cost.

items.statement: Finance cost INR149 crores in Q1 FY25 vs INR148 crores Q1 FY24 and INR185 crores Q4 FY24; gross debt INR3,180 crores, net debt INR1,659 crores
items.quote: For the current quarter, it is INR149 crores. For Q1 of last year, it is INR148 crores. For Q4, it is INR185 crores. This is factoring plus interest together, you can call it as finance cost.

items.statement: ProConnect revenue INR228 crores with EBITDA up 21% and PAT up 61%; India INR138 crores, UAE/KSA INR90 crores
items.quote: the consolidated ProConnect numbers are INR228 crores of revenue with the EBITDA growing by 21% and the PAT growing by 61%. Out of which India is about INR138 crores and UAE and KSA is about INR90 crores.

items.statement: Expect better quarters ahead driven by Q2-Q3 mobility NPIs, AI PCs, infrastructure growth in India, UAE, Saudi Arabia
items.quote: the upcoming quarters are also our higher seasonality quarters because of all the trends that we see in the environment, the NPIs that are going to happen in Q2 and Q3 on mobility, the AI PCs that are coming up. The growth in infrastructure in India, UAE, Saudi Arabia will all contribute to a larger market size that we can tap on.

items.statement: Expect to launch 17.25 million sq ft in FY25 including 12.7 million sq ft new launches and 4.56 million sq ft new phases in existing projects
items.quote: overall, the company is expecting to launch 17 million square foot, including phases of the launch projects. New launches to the extent of 12.7 million square foot is expected, and 4.56 million square foot of the existing launch projects, the new phases will be opened up for launch, a total of 17.25 million.

items.statement: Expect industry average realization growth of about 9% in FY25 with project-level variation
items.quote: my expectation is, the industry will look at an average of about 9% in terms of average growth.

items.statement: Deployed Rs 762 crores for land acquisitions in MMR, Goa and Bengaluru in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The company deployed Rs. 762 crores for land acquisitions in MMR, Goa and Bengaluru.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin of about 30%; current Q1 FY25 margin at 22%
items.quote: Those numbers will evolve and change. They will get closer to our target number, which is at about 30% of EBITDA.

items.statement: Expected margins: Provident 27-32%, Puravankara 30-35%, Purva Land >35%, Mumbai outright >30%, JDA ~15%
items.quote: If you look at margins, typically we expect in Provident between 27% and 32% margin; in Puravankara, between 30% and 35%; Purva Land in excess of 35%.

items.statement: Demand remains robust; challenge is supply catching up especially in Bangalore, Mumbai, Pune, Chennai
items.quote: So, from the market point of view, today the struggle for all of us is really to keep up with the demand, and that is the challenge.

items.statement: Mumbai MMR contribution increasing; new launches and Mumbai projects to improve average realization mix
items.quote: this year, with Mumbai MMR coming into play, definitely it will have some impact on our average realizations, average contribution increases.

items.statement: State elections may cause minor launch delays of a month; target remains to meet annual launch plan
items.quote: A quarter here, a quarter there could be because of the planned sanctions, maybe you would miss it by a month, not much a nd then it would spill over into the next quarter

items.statement: Board and shareholders approved QIP up to Rs 1,000 crores; evaluating options, allocation between debt reduction, acquisitions and operations to be decided later
items.quote: Our Board has approved us to raise the funds for QIP to an extent of Rs. 1,000 crores. At the same time shareholders have also approved it. We are currently evaluating all our options to raise capital including the QIP.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 sales Rs 1,128 crores, collections Rs 965 crores (39% YoY growth), average realization Rs 8,746/sq ft (6% YoY growth)
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, our sales were Rs. 1,128 crores, while collections were at Rs. 965 crores, representing a growth of 39% year-on-year, indicating an improvement in our operating efficiency.

items.statement: Net debt increased to Rs 2,237 crores; net debt/equity 1.17%; cash Rs 1,044 crores; debt per sq ft Rs 912 (under Rs 1,000 comfort level)
items.quote: Our net debt increased from Rs. 2,151 crores in Q4 FY '24 to Rs. 2,237 crores in Q1 FY '25. Our net debt to equity ratio at the end of the quarter was 1.17%.

items.statement: Cost of debt at 11.64% as of June 2024; slight increase due to land loans
items.quote: As of 30 June 2024, our cost of debt stood at 11.64%. Despite a slight increase due to higher rates in land loans, we are continuously working on maintaining our average cost of debt down.

items.statement: Delivered 929 units (1.16 million sq ft) in Q1 FY25 vs 446 units (0.49 million sq ft) in Q1 FY24
items.quote: We have delivered 929 units with an area of 1.16 million square feet in Q1 FY '25, when compared to 446 units with 0.49 million square feet in Q1 FY '24, which has more than doubled

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue Rs 676 crores (101% YoY), EBITDA Rs 148 crores (22% margin), PAT Rs 15 crores vs loss of Rs 17 crores in Q1 FY24
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, our total revenue grew by 101% year-on-year basis to Rs. 676 crores. Our EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 148 crores with 22% EBITDA margin. PAT for Q1 FY '25 was Rs. 15 crores.

items.statement: NCR entry planned with asset-light model; expect results by next financial year end
items.quote: NCR, we just put the team on the ground, so we are hopeful that in the next financial year. We need to track very carefully, it's a new market, it takes some time to acquire and do the right acquisitions from the brand and strategy point of view.

items.statement: Construction outflow ~Rs 300 crores in Q1 FY25 (contractor Rs 247 cr + raw material Rs 65 cr); collections ~3x construction spend
items.quote: last quarter we have incurred or paid Rs. 247 crores on contractor cost and Rs. 65 crores on cost of raw material. So, if we total that, about Rs. 300 crores plus we have spent on purely in construction cost on our projects.

items.statement: Management declined to provide specific disbursement, ROA, ROE, or NIM guidance for FY25, stating it is too early and they are introspecting.
items.quote: We said earlier we don't want to give any guidance, right.

items.statement: Management expects NIM to decline as debt-to-equity increases with growth, focusing on better quality projects with relatively lower yields.
items.quote: Currently, the NIM is high also because of the low debt to equity. So once the debt to equity keeps on increasing, as we start growing, NIM will come down.

items.statement: Management expects 20-30% of stressed assets to be resolved by March 2025, but cannot specify which quarter.
items.quote: What we can say, going forward, we expect in the next 9 odd months, at least around 20% to 30% of our stressed assets to be resolved by March '25.

items.statement: Management targets debt-to-equity ratio to potentially double from current 1.4x over the next 18-24 months to fund growth.
items.quote: So therefore, if we are able to execute our plan successfully, we should be able to achieve in the next 18-24 months a significantly higher number, possibly doubling of the debt-to-equity ratio.

items.statement: Outstanding sanctioned amount pending disbursement is ₹300-400 crores; new sanctions in Q1 were ₹525 crores.
items.quote: Outstanding, we have another ₹300 to ₹400 crores to be disbursed. So that is the additional amount we have sanctioned.

items.statement: Management sees immense potential across infrastructure value chain including renewables (₹15 lakh crores over 10 years), roads, wastewater, and compressed biogas, aligned with government's ₹11.11 lakh crore infra budget.
items.quote: The potential only in renewables across the country over the next 10 years, will be close to ₹15 lakh crores. That is the investment that would be required.

items.statement: Strategy to de-risk portfolio by moving across full energy value chain (generation, transmission, distribution) and into non-energy infrastructure (roads, wastewater, sewage), focusing on smaller ticket projects (<5% of AUM).
items.quote: We want to ensure that no fresh disbursement is more than 5% of our AUM at any point of time, from now on going forward.

items.statement: No fresh NPA slippages in Q1; gross Stage 3 declined by ~₹2 crores, net NPA declined by ~₹2 crores to ₹140 crores (~3% of assets); ₹115-120 crores impairment reserves provided for stressed assets.
items.quote: Currently, if you take a look at our net NPA, it declined by ₹2 crores. Compared to March it's come down to ₹140 crores. Our endeavour is that as our balance sheet keeps on growing, as our loan book keeps on growing, this figure does not increase much, so that as a proportion, it will always keep on reducing.

items.statement: Plan to diversify fund mix beyond 97% bank borrowing by deepening bank engagement and accessing mutual funds and other sources.
items.quote: At this point of time, nearly 97% of it comes from the banks. So, one thing is to deepen our engagement with the banks so that we get more line from a more number of banks. And more importantly, also get into other sources of funds, like look at mutual funds, it's a very significant area, which we intend to focus on.

items.statement: Q1 disbursement of ₹566 crores arrested AUM decline; portfolio increased to ₹5,577 crores (~₹170-180 crore increment); PBT ₹59 crores vs ₹19 crores QoQ; ECL provision ~₹5 crores; RoA 2.77%; D/E improved to 1.4x.
items.quote: In Q1 we disbursed ₹566 crores. To provide a perspective our disbursement in the first quarter of this year was almost similar to what the company had disbursed in last financial year. Because of which the downward trend in our AUM has been arrested and we will witness a small increment of around ₹170 - ₹180 crores in our AUM.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth projected at 25-30%, EBITDA growth 10-20%, PAT growth 20-35%
items.quote: In 2025, we have projected revenue growth of approximately 25%, 30%; EBITDA of around 10% to 20% and a PAT of 20% to 35%.

items.statement: International business to contribute 12-15% of net revenue in FY25, targeting 30% in 2-3 years
items.quote: Over the next 2 years, we will intensify our focus on elevating our international business, aiming for it to contribute 12% to 15% of our net revenue income, up from single-digit contribution currently.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 net take rate improved to 11.2 bps, up 33% YoY from 8.4 bps
items.quote: Our take rate in payment has been consistently improving, standing at 11.2 basis points in Q1 FY '25, which is a growth of 33% year-over-year.

items.statement: UAE take rates increased to 19.5 bps, India take rates increased to 9.9 bps from 7.8 bps
items.quote: Specifically the UAE take rates have increased to almost 19.5 bps. The Indian take rates has also increased from an earlier 7.8, which was there in last quarter to 9.9.

items.statement: Expect substantial TPV increase in Q2 and Q3 FY25 vs Q1 due to festival season
items.quote: We expect that in Q2 and Q3, you will see a substantial increase in TPV.

items.statement: Value-added services (financial products distribution) to contribute 2-4% of revenue in FY25, targeting 7-10% in a couple of years
items.quote: For the full year, we expect our other value-added services include distribution of our financial products to contribute 2% to 4% of our revenue this year, going to around 7% to 10% in a couple of years.

items.statement: Board approved majority stake investment in Rediff.com (INR36 cr revenue, INR4-5 cr loss) for AI-driven financial product cross-sell
items.quote: Today, we also announced that the Board has approved an investment in Rediff.com for a majority stake.

items.statement: Board approved acquiring remaining 26% in Infibeam Digital Entertainment, making it a wholly owned subsidiary
items.quote: Infibeam Avenues' Board has approved acquiring remaining 26% in Infibeam Digital Entertainment, making it a fully owned subsidiary.

items.statement: Board sanctioned new subsidiary for AI operations focusing on AI-enabled fraud detection and prevention in fintech
items.quote: Additionally, the Board has also sanctioned creation of a new subsidiary for artificial intelligence operations focusing on AI-enabled fraud detection and prevention, particularly within the fintech sector.

items.statement: GeM revenue not recognized due to arbitration; IP ownership confirmed, payment amount uncertain
items.quote: on the fact that all intellectual property that we are providing to GeM belongs solely to us. I think those are 2 important things, in fact, but we can definitely talk about. What we do not know and what we are not able to talk to you and tell you is how much we get paid and hence we've not been able to recognize revenues so far

items.statement: Phronetic.AI filed US patent for activity-based management using AI; expect decision in 6-12 months
items.quote: Phronetic.AI, which is our AI vertical has filed for a patent with US patent office regarding system and methods to implement activity-based management using artificial intelligence.

items.statement: Incorporating company in GIFT City for cross-border payment aggregator business
items.quote: Furthermore, we are incorporating a company in the GIFT City to start the payment aggregator business within that jurisdiction and look aggressively to do cross-border payments through our subsidiary.

items.statement: ODigMa demerger planned; ODigMa annual revenue ~INR30 cr, profit <INR1 cr
items.quote: ODigMa will be about INR30 crores. And about profitability would be about -- I mean these are annual numbers, and profitability will be about less than INR1 crore.

items.statement: AI vertical (Phronetic.AI) set up as separate company; pilot phases complete, partial rollout underway, contracts expected in 4-8 weeks
items.quote: We are now rolling out the second phase, which is not the full rollout, but a partial rollout with many of our clients. And we expect that in the next 4 to 8 weeks, we'll be able to share more in terms of several contracts that get converted.

items.statement: Target 200-plus stores by FY26 and 25-30 new stores in FY25
items.quote: We have given the guidance that definitely in FY '26 we will be 200-plus stores. And we will be expanding, let us say, over 25 -30 store every year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 8% to 10% range
items.quote: We have been giving you guidance that our EBITDA margin will remain like that , from 8% to 10% we have been giving guidance .

items.statement: CAPEX per store increase largely attributable to inflation and generator price hikes
items.quote: No, sir. This is largely attributable to inflation directly . B ecause as y ou will find even this pollution normsand other thing has kicked in for generators , so prices of generators have gone up, inflation is there of course

items.statement: Gross margin slightly up to 15.2% in Q1 FY25 from 15.1% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: There is a slight increase in gross margin at 15.2% compared to last year Q1 gross marginwhich stood at 15.1%.

items.statement: Comfortable maintaining current gross margin levels despite compressor product shortage
items.quote: And , let us not profiteer because of shortage.

items.statement: AC and refrigerator prices increased 10-15% across the board
items.quote: And in working capital also we are facing that the air conditioner prices have gone up by 10% to 15% across board, it is there for even refrigerators also

items.statement: Price hikes not expected to dampen demand due to low penetration (~3%) and premium preference
items.quote: Actually, we do not think that the price is going to impact the demand , because I have been telling that the penetration is very, v ery low. In fact , around 3% of penetration is there

items.statement: No significant tightening in consumer finance lending observed; recoveries remain good
items.quote: I do notthinkit has come to any level which is hurting us or hurting our business. It is not like that. It is part of India where the recoveries are good

items.statement: Fund raise proceeds used for working capital; Rs. 8 crore allocated to general corporate purposes, not fully utilized
items.quote: We have used only Rs. 8 crores for general corporate purposes, which we stillhave not utilized it fully.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 trends so far very encouraging
items.quote: So, far it is very encouraging.

items.statement: GMA contribution expected to be equal to or better than FY24 level this financial year
items.quote: With a reasonable confidence, I can say that, this financial year will be equal to or better than FY '24 GMA contribution.

items.statement: Store additions projected at 40-45 for FY25, with longer-term capacity for 60 stores annually
items.quote: For this year also, we have projected 40 -45 stores. I mean, again, I'm saying that I don't want you to project something very large in the immediate future.

items.statement: Long-term store opening target is 10-15% of store count annually, implying 60-70 stores per year in 2-3 years
items.quote: In another two to three years, this 40 should go to a 60 or a 70 per year. We are working like that.

items.statement: Blended gross margin expected to remain in 14.5%-15.5% range regardless of mix changes
items.quote: I think 14.5%, 15%, 15.5%, those are the kind of ranges we play in from a gross margin standpoint. You have to look at a blended gross margin.

items.statement: GMA mix stabilized around 23%, not returning to 27-28% levels; food share up due to agri inflation
items.quote: A broad trend line will be around the current run rates of around 23% , is the sense we get. But otherwise, it's been a good year.

items.statement: Apparel recovery strong with 70-80% of fixes done; apparel now highest growing category
items.quote: Apparel has done a very smart recovery. We did very quick improvements there, primarily around leadership, team, sizes, all of that is in place. In fact, 70%, 80% of the work is already done.

items.statement: Quick commerce impact estimated at 1-1.5% SSSG CAGR in metro stores; no store declining
items.quote: But, okay, if you say a city that is not having any intense quick commerce versus a city that has quick commerce, there could be a 1% to 2% SSSG CAGR impact.

items.statement: Home delivery model preferred over pickup points; 40-45% deliveries within 12 hours, 86% within 24 hours
items.quote: We ignore the time between 11:00 p.m. and 06:00 a.m. in the morning. Ignore this time. We don't count that as delivery time. But I think around 40% -45% of our deliveries happen within 12 hours.

items.statement: Store size variable, historically 30,000-35,000 sq ft; larger stores seen as opportunity but no fixed template
items.quote: Historically we were at 30,000-35,000 square feet. Obviously, we see opportunity in the store size being larger for sure, but forget the range, don't go by the 5%-10% vagaries of average store size every year.

items.statement: Wage inflation rising rapidly; investing in talent and capabilities for 10-year horizon
items.quote: I think we've been all talking about product inflation, but I think at a lower level, wage inflation is also going up rapidly. Okay. That's one thing which is very, very clearly being observed.

items.statement: Private labels remain long-term journey; meaningful scale expected at USD7,000-8,000 per capita income
items.quote: India is still a USD2,500 -USD3,000 per capita income country. Private labels play out beautifully when at least the country is at a USD7,000-USD8,000 kind of per capita income.

items.statement: DMart Ready focused on value positioning, not convenience; EBITDA losses acceptable given brick-and-mortar profits
items.quote: will be on value. Amit Sachdeva: Neville Noronha: We are very clear because in the consumer ’s mind, DMart stands for value. We want to maintain that

items.statement: Minimax format still experimental; market not yet ready for that model
items.quote: It's still an experimentation. We feel that the market is not yet ready for that model.

items.statement: Mumbai Metropolitan Region fully covered by DMart Ready except a couple of unserviceable pin codes
items.quote: We are present in all but a couple of pin codes, which are actually not very serviceable. But, yeah, MMR, Mumbai Metropolitan Region, we are fully covered.

items.statement: First three orders free promotion on DMart Ready showing good traction; repeat usage after 2-3 orders
items.quote: We are seeing some good kind of traction there on that promotion. The idea here is to let customers sample our service. And our data has suggested that people who use our service for two or three times tend to stick with us.

items.statement: Full-year pre-sales guidance of Rs 17,500 crores, implying 20% growth
items.quote: we have guided to grow our pre-sales by 20% for the fu ll year and achieve Rs 17,500 crores

items.statement: Full-year price growth guidance of 5% to 7% year-on-year
items.quote: We are guidi ng to about 5% to 7% year-on-year price growth for the full year

items.statement: Full-year embedded EBITDA margin guidance of about 31%
items.quote: Our embedded EBITDA margin for the quarter was at about 33%, which is higher than our guidance for the full year at about 31%.

items.statement: Operating cash flow guidance of approximately INR 65 billion for the full year
items.quote: we will also see an acceleration in operating cash flow generation in line with our guidance of operating cash flow of approximately INR65 billion for the full year

items.statement: Palava and Upper Thane sales target of Rs 8,000 crores by end of decade at 20% CAGR from Rs 2,300 crores in FY24
items.quote: we expect that for the full year, we will deliver about 20% growth in Palava an d Upper Thane in line with our medium-term guidance of growing sales in Palava and Upper Thane from Rs 2,300 crores for Fiscal ‘24 to Rs 8,000 crores by the end of the decade, which is a CAGR of about 20

items.statement: Added three new projects in Q1 with GDV of about Rs 11,000 crores, over 50% of full-year business development guidance
items.quote: In terms of business development, we added three ne w projects this year this quarter with the GDV of about Rs 11,000 crores, therefore that is more than 50% of our full year guidance has already been delivered in the Q1 itself

items.statement: Q1 embedded EBITDA margin at 33%, above full-year guidance of 31%, despite 43% JDA mix
items.quote: Our embedded EBITDA margin for the quarter was at about 33%, which is higher than our guidance for the full year at about 31%. And this was in spi te of the fact that 43% of the pre-sales for this quarter came from our JDA projects

items.statement: Q1 price growth was about 2%; steady mid-to-high single digit price growth momentum continues
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier, we delivered predictable pr ice growth in line with our overall guidance of having price growth below wage growth. We are guidi ng to about 5% to 7% year-on-year price growth for the full year, and in the first quarter, the price growth was about 2

items.statement: Continued strong housing demand across segments; conversion rate improved to 8.2% in Q1 from 7.3% YoY
items.quote: in Q1, we had almost 24,000 walk-ins happenin g. But the most interesting part was that our conversion was almost 8.2%. If we compare it with o ver the quarter-to-quarter, just to give an idea, last year the same quarter the conversion was about 7.3

items.statement: Adding premium products in Palava (Rs 15,000-16,000/sq ft carpet) alongside mid-income; not replacing mid-income
items.quote: Our strategy is to add premium product in addition to our mid-income segment. It i s not replacing our mid-income segment, it is additive

items.statement: LTCG changes net positive for primary market; lower tax rate reduces transaction costs, resellers reinvest gains
items.quote: Therefore, from both the perspective of those who a re buying new homes as well as those who are reselling their existing homes and buying further property, in terms of the primary real estate market this change in long-term capital gains not only mak es the economy more efficient, but it is also net positive for the primary real estate

items.statement: Bangalore pilot nearing conclusion; evaluating new city for pilot entry in H2 FY25
items.quote: we will conclude our pilot phase in Bangalore. We have also started studying which new city will be considered by us for the next piloting an entry. We are currently co nsidering a couple of cities and expect to make a decision on the next city that we will do our pilot in the latter half of this current fiscal year

items.statement: Annuity income target of Rs 5 billion per annum by FY26 to cover interest costs; high street retail under construction
items.quote: As you know, we are targeting an annuity income of about Rs.5 billion p er annum by Fiscal ‘26 so that we can cover all our interest costs from annuity income

items.statement: Pune sales target of Rs 3,000 crores for FY25; Q1 saw Rs 1,000 crores pre-sales
items.quote: We clearly see ourselves achieving over Rs 3,000 cr ores of sales from Pune this year

items.statement: Consolidated operating revenue grew 64% YoY to INR156.4 crores, adjusted EBITDA grew ~300% to INR43 crores, and EBITDA margin expanded from 6% to 15% YoY.
items.quote: Revenue is the highest ever in the Q1 in any quarter 1 ever in history at INR156.4 crores. Adjusted EBITDA, which is INR43 crores or close to INR43 crores, is also highest ever in any Q1. And PAT is INR22.9 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: Standalone consumer group operating revenue grew 18% YoY; EBITDA swung from negative INR1.25 crores to positive INR7.23 crores, with margin improving from -3% to 14%.
items.quote: operating revenue up 18%. And again, here, you can see the leverage in the business. Costs have gone up. Just three -- the cost actually down by 2% for a standalone account, which has shown a 700% increase in our EBITDA. It was actually negative INR1.25 crores last year to this year, a positive INR7.23 crores of EBITDA

items.statement: OLX classified business adjusted EBITDA margin expanded from 24% to 27% QoQ; costs are fully baked in and include April increments, so margins should expand further as revenue grows.
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA, which is a proxy for our operating performance, is up from 24% margin to 27% margin for the quarter.

items.statement: Consumer group traffic is ~40 million monthly users with strong brand affinity; marketing spend as % of revenue is declining and no increase is deemed necessary.
items.quote: The traffic in the consumer group is almost 40 million users a month, which is reasonable growth there as well. So -- and if you look at the brand affinity versus its direct competitor, it's again very, very strong. So we feel the marketing expense is okay.

items.statement: OLX India has ~31 million monthly unique customers, almost entirely organic; marketing expense is near zero.
items.quote: OLX, as you know, is a very, very strong brand. It gets almost 31 million customers a month, unique customers, which comes almost through brand-related apps which people have on their phones. So the marketing expense is almost 0 in this company.

items.statement: Remarketing supply mix shifted to 42% retail (up from mostly repossession); retail supply now nearly equals repossession supply in volume.
items.quote: almost 42% of it now being retail supplier vehicles. This has enable d us to get to a flattish to plus positive 4% revenue growth, but a 12% increase in profits

items.statement: Repossession supply continues to degrow for 12-16 months due to lower NPAs in auto lending, constraining remarketing revenue growth despite retail strength.
items.quote: repossession suppl y for us continues to be a challenge and that speaks well of the Indian economy, I would say, the fact that NPA are lower in banks and NBFCs for automotive, automotive lending is a result of repossession being lower

items.statement: Management expects margin expansion in OLX and consumer group driven by revenue growth, not cost cuts; costs are stable for next 9 months post-April increments.
items.quote: In fact, as I said again, this carries increments in April for OLX -- the team at OLX, which, of course, is now fully baked in here as well. Every company has increment cycle and ours is April, and that's also been factored in here. So definitely, in the next 9 months, we should see a very stable cost environment.

items.statement: Non-auto OLX business (homes, jobs, electronics) is already profitable; future investment is in bandwidth and people, not significant cash outlay.
items.quote: The non-auto, the non-used car part is profitable as well today. We don't see further cash going into it. I think the investment is really in resources and bandwidth more than cash.

items.statement: OLX used car classified revenue grew ~8% QoQ to INR46.68 crores operating revenue; growth driven by more dealers and higher ARPU, not seasonality.
items.quote: As you can see, the company's revenue growth, as earlier discussed, has gone from INR43 crores in the last quarter, operating revenue, 43.4 to 46.68 in this quarter. So that is the growth 7% or 8% quarter-on-quarter sequential.

items.statement: OLX revenue growth comes from adding dealers and upgrading packages (higher ARPU), not from price hikes; focus is on increasing platform liquidity.
items.quote: It's mostly -- it's a combination of it. But obviously, our attempt right now is not so much right price, but it's about really making s ure we get more people onto the platform

items.statement: Buyback not currently possible under Companies Act due to brought-forward losses; will consider once losses are wiped out.
items.quote: On the buyback, as per the Companies Act compliance, unfortunately, we're not able to do a buyback right now. But the question I think is also to say that because we have the INR782 crores of balance, we will buy back when probably the Companies Act allows us to do so which is once we wipe out all the brought forward losses.

items.statement: Total cash balance of INR782 crores; company is debt-free.
items.quote: We are obviously a debt-free company and carrying a cash balance of equivalent of INR782 crores.

items.statement: OLX franchise stores and CarWale abSure/signature stores total ~250+ outlets; all franchisee-operated, asset-light model.
items.quote: I think the total, as I said, the total number of stores are close to over 250 stores between OLX and CarWale abSure plus signature.

items.statement: Remarketing retail margins higher than repossession margins; retail is 42% of volume, repossession 46% of volume.
items.quote: The retail is about 42% of our business, and the B2B repossession, supply from repossession is about 46% of our business. So this is a rough ratios of the percentages of revenue. The margins, we don't have a cut right now on the different margins, but we did disclose -- I mean, we did indicate the previous speaker as well that obviously, the margins from retail are higher than the margins on repo.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance increased from 20% to 25% for FY25
items.quote: Based on the business momentum, it gives me immense pleasure to announce that we are increasing our guidance of reve nue growth from 20% to 25% for this financial year, and I want to reassure our investors that we are dedicated to consistently grow each quarter from

items.statement: Core banking system revamp on schedule to complete by end of FY25
items.quote: As mentioned in our earlier earnings update, we are revamping our entire core banking system, including peripheral applications, and it should be completed by end of this fiscal. The project is on schedule, and we expect to concl ude it by end of this financial year

items.statement: CMS throughput grew 26% YoY to nearly INR 20,000 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: CMS throug hput grew by 26% on a year-on-year basis, approximately INR 20,000 crores, as Rishi earlier said

items.statement: EBITDA margin increased to 12.2% in Q1 FY25 from 11.6% in Q1 FY24; overall margins range bound around 31%
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter was INR53.2 crores, a 31.4% growth on a Y-o-Y basis, with EBITDA margin increasing to 12.2%, which was earlier 11.6% in quarter 1 FY '24.

items.statement: Digital payment services margin around 22-23%; DMT pricing driven by industry, no forecasted impact
items.quote: On an overall basis, with margins largely remaining range bound, as I said in my opening statements as well, there is expected to be an absolute growth coming around in terms of the bottom line as well. However, let's not forget one point, which I had earlier mentioned in my flow as well that we continue to invest into the technology and digital as well as our people stack as well.

items.statement: Digital throughput grew 141% YoY to nearly INR 44,200 crores; UPI ecosystem share increased to 1.42% from 1.27%
items.quote: Our digital footprint is expanding, with digital throughput growing by 141% year-on-year to nearly INR44,200 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: Digital payments now 15% of revenue (up from 6% in FY24), CASA renewal income 43% of CASA revenue (up from 33% in Q1 FY23)
items.quote: In FY '24, the digital payment services was contributing 6% and we are expecting that to be closing at around 16%, 17%. In addition, CASA, and I explained the statistics of our renewal income that how it is adding and becoming an increasing part of our CASA and overall revenue.

items.statement: AEPS ecosystem challenges stabilizing, no degrowth expected; micro ATM lost sheen, not expecting significant growth
items.quote: In the case of AEPS, after navigating through the various ecosystem challenges, which the system had encounter ed for last 12 months, the situation is now stabilizing. As a result, we are not expecting any degrowth from these levels in the upcoming quarters despite a digital economy growing at an accelerated pace

items.statement: Added 8.1 lakh new CASA accounts in Q1 FY25; 42 lakh average digitally active customers; 68% CASA accounts active
items.quote: In fact, in this quarter, we have added 8.1 lakh accounts. We have on an average 42 lakh digitally active customers as of the end of the quart er 1 '25

items.statement: CASA revenue grew 40% YoY to INR 93.6 crores; renewal income grew 54% YoY to INR 40.4 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, revenues from CASA stood at INR 93.6 crores, a growth of 40% vis-à-vis INR 66.9 crores in quarter 1 FY '24. Now we come to the renewal income or the annuity income as we say. Renewal income for CASA grew by 54% year-on-year to INR 40.4 crores

items.statement: Digital payment services revenue surged nearly 8x YoY to INR 66.8 crores; 19 B2B partners and growing month-on-month
items.quote: Revenue from digital payments surged from INR 7.7 crores in quarter 1 FY '24 to INR 66.8 crores in quarter 1 FY '25, marking a nearly eightfold year-on-year increase.

items.statement: Total revenue INR 436.9 crores (25% YoY growth); 70.5 crore transactions (74% YoY); throughput INR 1.46 lakh crores (39% YoY)
items.quote: Our total revenue for the quarter reached INR436.9 crores, marking a 25% Y -o-Y growth. Our margins have rem ained range bound around 31

items.statement: Cost-income ratio 25.4%, intend to maintain around 25% despite continued investment in people and technology
items.quote: As I have been saying, operating leverage is a key part of o ur strategy, and it is playing, leading to cost income ratio of 25.4%, which we again intend to maintain range bound around

items.statement: Average deposits increased 37% YoY to INR 1,699 crores; highest new CASA customers from Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Gujarat
items.quote: The average deposits have increased by 37% to INR 1,699 crores, demonstrating robust growth in our customer balances.

items.statement: UPI customer retention 80%+ vs 60-65% for non-UPI; UPI customers keep 30-40% higher balances
items.quote: We have seen UPI customer not only the fact that is more active, but also keeps a higher balance to the extent of ab out 30% to 40% than a non -UPI customer. And also, the renewal rates are far higher at about 80% plus compared to 60%, 65% for a non -UPI

items.statement: Own vs API channel revenue mix shifted to 72:28 (own:API) in Q1 FY25 from 65:35 in Q4 FY24
items.quote: I think quarter 4 '24, that number was 65-35 quarter 1 -- I mean, 65-35 skewed towards own to API, quarter 1 '25, that number is 72 and 28.

items.statement: CMS business 10% YoY revenue growth to INR 39.4 crores; 250+ clients; 62% from NBFC/MFI sectors
items.quote: CMS business experienced a 10% year-on-year growth, reaching INR 39.4 crores during the quarter, while CMS throug hput grew by 26% on a year-on-year basis, approximately INR 20,000 crores

items.statement: Company will continue to outperform industry growth by over 1.5x leveraging multi-segment presence and inorganic strategies
items.quote: We are confident that we will continue to outperform the industry growth by over 1.5x leveraging our presence in multiple industry segments, our global footprint, extensive product portfolio, very strong customer relationships and inorganic growth strategies.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 25% despite new product ramp-up costs
items.quote: But on the long term, as I said, on a consolidated basis, we are still guiding that we'll maintain EBITDA margin of 25% for our group companies.

items.statement: Capex plan of Rs.170-180 crores for FY2025 and FY2026 including Exotech expansion, glass business and maintenance
items.quote: So roughly, you can consider on a broad level around Rs.170 crores to Rs.180 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 26.6% in Q1 FY2025, up 51 bps YoY and 33 bps QoQ
items.quote: I'm delighted to share that the consolidated EBITDA margin for the quarter improved 33 basis points on a Q-o-Q basis and 51 bps Y-o-Y to 26.6%.

items.statement: Walter Pack has new programs starting from October 2024 to June 2025 with significant customer launch expected soon
items.quote: So, we have new programs that are starting from October this year to next year June. So, there are a whole lot of programs that we've already been on.

items.statement: Consumer durables contributes 21% of consolidated revenue; target mix: 25% consumer, 30% two-wheeler, rest four-wheeler in 3 years
items.quote: So, the consumer goods has contributed 21% in the total revenue.

items.statement: Export growth dependent on global economic conditions including US elections and Middle East conflict
items.quote: Yes, barring some unforeseen circumstances in the global economic scenario. So, people obviously are closely watching what's happening in the U.S., what will happen with the war that's ongoing in the Middle East.

items.statement: Total debt Rs.533 million at Q1 FY2025 end; repaid Rs.150 million during quarter; net cash position Rs.234 million
items.quote: The total debt for the Q1FY2025 is Rs.533 million. During this quarter, we have repaid Rs.150 million to the banker.

items.statement: Cover glass business: ISO certification achieved; first purchase order expected in Q2 FY2025; meaningful revenue from FY2026
items.quote: we expect to get our first purchase order for th is business within this quarter, and we will start supplying in a phased

items.statement: Exotech capacity expansion expected on-stream by Q1 FY2026; running at 95% utilization currently
items.quote: Exotech, we expect by Q1 of next year, the capacity should be on-stream, and we should be able to augment and that should be our credit.

items.statement: Export revenue target 13-15% of consolidated revenue in 3 years from current 7.5%
items.quote: At the moment, 7.5% of my console revenue is exports, which I hope will grow in the next 3 years to be 15% of my consolidated revenue.

items.statement: Dixon Technologies added as new client for consumer durables and telecom segments; supplies started for telecom
items.quote: We've also added Dixon as a new customer, and this will open significant new opportunities for us in the consumer durables segment.

items.statement: Inorganic acquisition strategy active; targeting synergies and strategic fit; strike rate ~10%; next acquisition likely next year
items.quote: So, I think sometime in next year is when we would like to do this. But as you know, inorganic acquisitions, we have marked in the business for acquiring companies just for the sake of acquiring.

items.statement: Two-wheeler organic growth expected in line with industry; four-wheeler growth driven by premiumization and new products
items.quote: Separately, the two-wheeler industry growth will be more in line with the organic growth of the industry. And we will outperform the automotive industry because we've added a lot of new-generation products.

items.statement: Stand-alone business two-wheeler share ~50%; SJS historical EBITDA margin ~30% sustainable
items.quote: But any other questions you have on this topic I mean, largely of broadly answering you, two-wheelers are roughly about 50% of our sales of our stand-alone business.

items.statement: KFC store count on track to double in 3 years, targeting close to 500 by end of December 2024
items.quote: We had called out in December '21 that we would double the store count in 3 to 4 years' time. Quite happy to say that we are on track to double the count in 3 years' time. So by end of December '24 we should be close to 500 restaurant count.

items.statement: Pizza Hut store openings will be muted this financial year, far more cautious approach
items.quote: We are going to be extra cautious in store opening. And we don't see a big chunk being opened in this particular financial year.

items.statement: Pizza Hut store additions likely similar to last 1 year trend of 18 stores, lower than historical 35-40
items.quote: So maybe that can be active as -- that can be taken as a reference point maybe.

items.statement: KFC expansion may be revisited if restaurant EBITDA goes significantly below 19-20% target
items.quote: We have always called out we would like our KFC margins to be 19%, 20%, near to 20%. If it goes significantly below that, yes, we will revisit our expansion strategy.

items.statement: KFC restaurant EBITDA margin at 18.8% despite -6% SSSG, limited by operating deleverage
items.quote: The restaurant EBITDA came in at 18.8% vis-a-vis last year, it had a drop because of the operating deleverage, which we had.

items.statement: Pizza Hut restaurant EBITDA improved to 4.6% from loss last quarter, includes additional marketing investments
items.quote: Overall restaurant EBITDA came in at 4.6%, again, compared to the previous quarter, where we actually had a loss, 4.6% was quite a healthy margin compared to the previous quarter.

items.statement: Sri Lanka restaurant EBITDA at 13.2%, up 20 bps YoY on 11% SSSG and double-digit transaction growth
items.quote: Overall restaurant EBITDA came in at 13.2%, which is a 20 basis points improvement over last year.

items.statement: KFC took a small 1% price increase on select SKUs, no price increase on Pizza Hut
items.quote: So we have taken a very small price increase of 1%. And it was not across the board. There was some opportunity of price corrections on some of our SKUs, that's what we did.

items.statement: KFC underlying demand steady, marginally negative excluding Navratra impact in April
items.quote: Apart from April month, I would say it is still steady -- still a little bit negative, but marginally negative.

items.statement: Pizza Hut ADS improved 17% sequentially to INR 48,000, reversing 6-7 quarters of decline
items.quote: The ADS came in at INR 48,000, as Sanjay called out, big improvement sequentially 17% over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Sri Lanka SSSG grew 11% backed by double-digit transaction growth
items.quote: SSSG was 11%, backed by double-digit transaction growth.

items.statement: KFC delivery mix increased to 40% from 36% YoY, Pizza Hut stable at 50%, Sri Lanka at 38%
items.quote: KFC had delivery mix of 40% versus 36% last year.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues impacting some pockets with no let-up or bounce back seen
items.quote: There is an impact. There's -- I don't think -- we have not called it out in the past because these are things that perhaps we just have to live with.

items.statement: KFC margins cannot sustain at 18.8% if -5% to -6% SSSG persists for multiple quarters
items.quote: If the environment continues to be minus 5%, minus 6% for a long period of time, we will certainly see an impact on the margins.

items.statement: Corporate costs jumped to INR 38-39 crores in Q1 due to wage inflation, expected to remain at similar run-rate for rest of year
items.quote: So that's the increase along wit h a slight increase in additions of the account because of the increase in the overall store base. That's the only increase

items.statement: Published third ESG report under GRI, SASB, BRSR standards with limited assurance, received IGBC Gold Certification for one KFC restaurant
items.quote: We published a third ESG report under GRI, SASB and BRSR standards. We're really the only Indian QSR company to publish a full-fledged ESG report.

items.statement: Management expects to continue current performance run rate in coming quarters if price stability and demand persist
items.quote: We are hopeful that no such geopolitical issues will come up and the supply chain of the commodity and price levels more or less will remain in range, we should be able to continue this run rate in the coming quarter as well.

items.statement: Food and FMCG business targeting 30-40% year-on-year volume growth for next three years
items.quote: I can tell you one thing that we are looking at 30%, 40% growth year-on-year for the next three years.

items.quote: that’s the reason why the food and FMCG margins are like this , plus and minus it is not a significant movement in margin, but by design is that we are ba sically investing whatever we are earning at a gross margin level, into the infrastructure for distribution as well as on other heads

items.quote: In Q1 FY '24, my EBITDA margin was 6.7% and in this quarter it is 10.1%.

items.statement: NIMs compressed to 16.72% from 17.74% YoY due to higher leverage
