items.statement: Liquidity buffer target maintained at 15-17% of AUM in steady state
items.quote: Our intention is to maintain around 15% to 17% of our AUM in the form of liquidity. This is broadly the thumb rule that even bigger NBFCs are actually following.

items.statement: Stage-3 provision coverage at 52%, overall at 1.63%; comfortable maintaining current levels
items.quote: We have a Stage-3 provision coverage of 52% and then overall provision coverage of 1.63%. So, we will continue to remain optimistic as well as cautious.

items.statement: Disbursement growth expected at 25-27% for FY25 with loan count growth of 18-20%
items.quote: Our disbursals are expected to go up by about 25%-27% and with a little bit of push up in the ticket size, which will come because of inflationary increases, you will probably see the number of loans growth by about 20%-22%.

items.statement: Borrowing diversification: bank share reduced from 79% to 74% QoQ, 84% to 74% YoY
items.quote: Our borrowings from banks, the proportion of borrowings from banks reduced from 79% in March to about 74% as of now. If you compare it on a year-on-year basis, it has dropped from 84% to 74%.

items.statement: Rating upgrade discussions ongoing; best case end of calendar year, more likely with March 2025 results
items.quote: Realistically, I would probably think the best case, if I have to put my neck out and say, is probably end of this calendar year or end of this year, or the more reasonable and the logical case would be if we are able to go with the March results, March '25 results, you know, I will say it has a very high probability of getting converted.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost expected to rise in Q2/Q3 as capital market transactions materialize
items.quote: You will definitely see a jump up in the cost of funds in the next quarter. So, given that these did not happen last quarter, you probably saw the rate going down from 9.58 to 9.49 or so. But definitely the number will inch up once we have capital market transactions coming in.

items.statement: Target steady-state leverage of 3.75x-4x in 2.5-3.5 years with spreads 12-13%, NIMs 14-15%, ROA ~7%, ROE >20%
items.quote: At a steady state, steady state means 2-3 years down the line, we intend to be somewhere close to 3.75 x to 4x leverage. I am talking about leverage perspective, not debt-to-equity, debt to equity means it will be 2.75 to 3 and leverage of 3.75 to 4.

items.statement: AUM growth target of 30% CAGR for next 2-3 years
items.quote: So, we are looking at 30% CAGR growth for the next two to three years.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio to remain at 35%
items.quote: Our cost to income, which is a clear metric of measuring what is the cost that you incur for the income what you get is at 34-point something in this quarter. We will remain at 35%.

items.statement: Lending rate cut of 50-75 bps on incremental loans from August, portfolio yield impact ~1/3 of that
items.quote: In fact, I think we will probably be introducing this as early as this month, which is the month of August. So, sometime during this month is what we are looking at and yes, this will be on incremental loans. So, you will not see the yields dropping by 50-75 basis points. You will probably see it dropping by one-third of the 50-75 basis points because it will take time to impact the portfolio yiel

items.statement: Steady-state spreads 12-13%, NIMs 14-15%
items.quote: While doing so, our spreads will be close to 12% to 13% and NIMs will be close to 14%, 14.5%, 15% and that eventually translates to ROA of close to 7% and ROE, which will go beyond 20%.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu growth to catch up strongly this year after lagging Andhra/Telangana last year; no stress in TN/Karnataka
items.quote: Yes, very much so and it will be very stronger this year.

items.statement: Static pool NPA peaks at 2-2.5% around 3-3.5 years; LGDs very low, recover ~99% of principal at NPA
items.quote: So, on this, typically what we see there is some level of peaking that happens around the three, three and a half years timeline. This used to be about two and a half, three years earlier, but that has got pushed because of the collection efforts. So, 3 to 3.5 years there is a peaking that happens, which probably goes to about 2-2.5% on a static pool basis, sort of stabilizes, but it's also import

items.statement: Annual technical write-offs ~25-30 bps of opening book; actual credit losses ~15-20 bps
items.quote: Generally, our experience has shown that our write -off tends to be somewhere around 25 to 30 basis points of our opening book. If you look at the last five years, we would probably have written off somewhere close to 60 to 70 cro res of loans. So, that's the overall number, but broadly on a year-on-year basis, the technical write-off works to about 25 to 30 basis points

items.statement: 70-90 new branches in new locations this FY, mostly South; branch splitting of 200-225 large branches to complete in 9-12 months
items.quote: Point #2, as I said in an earlier question, 70 to 90 new branches wil l be formed in new locations, mostly in the South and good numbers in the rest of the country. Those number of officers will be a clear addition to Five-Star in this financial year

items.statement: Steady-state borrowing mix target 50% banks, 50% capital market/securitization/DFIs over 2-3 years; currently AA mandate requires 25% incremental from capital markets
items.quote: So, Vijay, I think in a steady state, this is not immediately, but maybe over the next two to three years, we are probably looking at banks to be at about 50% and balance coming in from capital market, securitization, DFIs and all that.

items.statement: UPI AutoPay/NACH mandate now near 100% pre-disbursement; bounce charge Rs 500 per instance
items.quote: It's near to 100%, Kunal. So, they can either choose for a UPI auto pay or they can choose for an online NACH. Both these mandates are to be set up prior to the disbursement.

items.statement: Rating upgrade discussions ongoing with ICRA/CARE; best case end of calendar year, high probability with March 2025 results; at least 2-3 quarters away
items.quote: But realistically, I would probably think the best case, if I have to put my neck out and say, is probably end of this calendar year or end of this year, or the more reasonable and the logical case would be if we are able to go with the March results, March '25 results, you know, I will say it has a very high probability of getting converted. But I would probably think it's at least two to three q

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds 9.48% this quarter from banks/DFIs; capital market borrowing would be ~9.60-9.65%
items.quote: So, largely banks are willing to lend to us at lower rates, even the IFC funding that we got was at lower rates. So, I th ink it's broadly numbers it's coming from DFIs and banks, which has contributed to the lower rate. I think once we get to the capital market, participants feed the mutual funds or the others, this cost will probably look like more around 9.60%, 9.65% rather than 9.48

items.statement: Maharashtra expansion accelerating this year after COVID pause; will become key market
items.quote: This year is an expansion year for Maharashtra. You already see us putting a good number of branches. Definitely I think from this year onwards Maharashtra will become a key market for us.

items.statement: Expects buoyancy in volumes to continue for next couple of months (August and September) with similar levels to June and July
items.quote: Therefore, for the coming months, we expect this buoyancy in volumes, at least for the next couple of months to continue.

items.statement: Land acquisition completed at Mundra; ICD Jhajjar land acquisition expected to complete by December 2024, operational by mid-FY26-27
items.quote: On the ICD front at Jhajjar, land acquisition is expected to be complete by December 2024 and we believe we will be operational by mid-financial year 2026-27.

items.statement: Initiated steps to add capacity in Mundra and Chennai markets through land acquisition and partnership
items.quote: We have initiated steps to add capacity in the markets of Mundra and in the Chennai market. These are through acquisition of land parcel and through a partnership in Chennai.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 volume handled at 159,000 TEUs, up 8% YoY and 4% QoQ
items.quote: The total volume handled for Q1FY25 stood at 159,000 TEUs, depicting a growth of 8% as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 15.8% from 14.7% QoQ; gross margin improved to 32.9% from 32.4% QoQ
items.quote: The EBITDA in this quarter, EBITDA margin has actually improved from 14.7% to 15.8%. There has been a consistent increase in EBITDA margin in the last two quarters.

items.statement: June and July volumes were extremely strong, among highest levels; July volumes continued at June levels
items.quote: June was an extremely strong month in which our volumes, as indicated by you, were one of the highest. And I'm happy to share with you now as we talk on August 2nd, August 3rd, the volumes in July continue to be almost at the same levels as of June.

items.statement: Exports remain muted but expected to pick up when seasonal bans lift and manufacturing incentives take effect
items.quote: However, exports still continue to be muted and not at the pace in which we would like it to be. If that also starts p icking up, like all the inputs which are there for exports, the manufacturing sector, the incentives which are there, and some of the bans which are there on certain commodities, seasonal bans which are there when they get moved, I think exports should also start to pick up

items.statement: JNPT facilities contribute ~40% of revenue, Mundra facilities ~30%
items.quote: In JNPT, our contribution is about 40% and Mundra facilities contribute close to 30%.

items.statement: Geopolitical situations and trade disruptions create uncertainty for volume outlook beyond next couple of months
items.quote: Beyond that, I think a little too early to talk about, given the geopolitical situations which are there.

items.statement: Market share increased to 14% in Q1 FY25 from 13% in Q1 FY24, outpacing CFS market growth
items.quote: For Q1 2025 the market share is estimated to be 14% as compared to 13% during the same period last year.

items.statement: Evaluating MMLP projects for CFS facilities in partnership with MMLP operators; early stages, will share when concrete progress made
items.quote: We are still at the early stages of evaluating MMLP locations in which we can have CFS facilities which are in partnership with the MMLP operators that we could run.

items.statement: DFCC opportunities shortlisted; will bid when tenders open
items.quote: On the DFCC front, we have shortlisted few locations that we will bid for once it opens.

items.statement: Aim to achieve total sales of about INR1000 crores over the next 4 to 5 years including Hyd-Air acquisition
items.quote: So our ultimate aim like I have been telling in my previous calls also that over the next 4 years to 5 years our aim is to have a total sales of about INR1000 crores over the next 4 years to 5 years.

items.statement: Expect new age sectors like solar, EV and robotics to contribute more than 50% of overall business over next 4 to 5 years
items.quote: Now in terms of the split we expect that over the next 4 years to 5 years I think the new sector would contribute more than 50% to our overall business.

items.statement: Total capex for FY25 expected to be INR35-40 crores for remaining year after INR20.3 crores spent in Q1
items.quote: For Aeroflex, I think for this financial year, we expect to do a total capex of the remaining year, I would say we do expect to do a total capex of about INR35 crores to INR40 crores till March 2025.

items.statement: Plan to invest approximately INR18 crores at Hyd-Air over next one year for facilities, machines and quality lab
items.quote: Additionally, we are planning to invest approximately INR18 crores for updating the facilities and the machines at Hyd-Air, which includes also the installation of a brand-new high-tech quality lab and also the procurement of new machineries.

items.statement: Assembly and fitting business contributed 36% of Q1 revenue, constrained by capacity; flexible hose segment 55%
items.quote: The assembly and fitting business contributed about 36% of our revenue for this quarter. And like I said, if it wasn't for the assembly section constraints of capacity, I think this percentage would have been even higher.

items.statement: Metal bellows Phase 1 EBITDA margin expected at 26-30% at optimum capacity; Phase 2 could be higher
items.quote: So, once the Phase 1 is fully completed and the production is up and running at an optimum capacity level, the EBITDA margin for metal bellows should range anywhere in the region of 26 % to 30% on an average.

items.statement: Expect volume growth of 15-20% on like-to-like basis over next 2-3 years; aim to grow higher
items.quote: Yes, I think that's most definitely. I think our aim is to grow, you know, higher than that, but that is definitely achievable.

items.statement: USA and Europe to remain biggest markets; aim to continue 25-30% growth despite industry growing at 5-6%
items.quote: I would say that even though our industry overall on an annual basis might be growing at about 5% to 6%, but if you see our growth over the last four to five years, we have been growing at about 25 % to 30% and we would want to continue that momentum over the next two to three years.

items.statement: Strong traction from end-user industries; received trial orders from defence Tier 1 suppliers and new age sectors
items.quote: We have already in talks with, two, three of our major customers to develop bellows for them, you know, as soon as we are, capable to start manufacturing them.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis causing container delays and shipping cost increases; expect it to continue at least till December
items.quote: I think this Red Sea crisis I think is not going to go at least for the next few months or at least till December. I think it's now actually a part of the life only.

items.statement: Freight cost increase of INR81 lakhs impacted EBITDA; mix of FOB (40-45%) and CIF (55%) contracts; sharing freight increases with customers
items.quote: It is important to note that despite our record margins, our EBITDA would have been even higher if it wasn't for the sharp rise in the shipping cost, which amounts to approximately INR81 lakhs.

items.statement: Metal bellows Phase 1 commercial production expected by December 2024; full capacity revenue potential INR85-95 crores
items.quote: At a full capacity level, once we reach that capacity, say in the next, I think, 1 years, 1.5 years, we would expect a turnover from the Phase 1. We expect the turnover of approximately INR85 crores to INR95 crores, approximately.

items.statement: Domestic business contributes ~18% of revenue; investing in domestic sales team for faster growth than exports
items.quote: And with regards to our domestic business, so domestic business right now contributes about, you know, approximately 18% to our overall business.

items.statement: Hose capacity expanded by 1.5 million meters to 15 million meters per annum as of August 2024; remaining 1.5 million by end of Q3
items.quote: We are also pleased to an nounce the successful expansion of our host capacity by 1.5 million meters, which leads to an increase of our total capacity to 15 million meters per annum as of August 2024

items.statement: Added 5 new assembly stations taking total to 34; automatic welding machine ordered for H2 FY25 to reduce manual dependency
items.quote: We have introduced five new stations in the assemblies and fittings, which leads to our total assembly stations of 34. And like I said that we are in the process of adding more assembly stations and automated welding machines.

items.statement: Loan book growth target of 22% to 24% for FY25
items.quote: We intend to organically grow our secured book and are confident of growing our loan book as initially targe ted that is 22 % to 24% for FY 25

items.statement: ROTA target of 1.4% for FY25
items.quote: We intends to expand our ROTA, as originally planned, to 1.4% for FY25, and continuously ROTA expansion going forward.

items.statement: Credit cost target range of 0.1% to 0.23% for FY25
items.quote: We intend to keep it in the same range as we do for the current fiscal that is 0.1 % to 0.22% or 0.23% range.

items.statement: GNPA target of 2.45% to 2.55% by end of FY25
items.quote: Just going forward, we intend to improve our GNPA level of around 2.45% to 2.55% level as we move by the end of the year.

items.statement: Net NPA target below 1% over next 9 to 15 months for universal banking license eligibility
items.quote: We intend to take it below 1% and that is what is required for the universal banking license over the next 9 months to 15 months period so that we are able to tick all boxes for the universal banking license requirement.

items.statement: Branch expansion target of 200+ branches by end of FY25 from 177 currently
items.quote: We begin year with 177 number of branches. We intend to close this year with 200 plus branches.

items.statement: Plan to open 24 to 26 branches in FY25 with majority outside Punjab
items.quote: we are intending to o pen around 24 to 26 branches as part of this present expansion, which will be consisting of three in the state of Jammu, three in Rajasthan, eight being in Haryana, and the rest being in Punjab

items.statement: NIM improved to 4.2% in Q1 FY25 from 3.8% in Q4 FY24 due to higher yield on advances and stable cost of deposits
items.quote: Our net interest margin improved to 4.2% in Q1 FY25 against 3.8% in Q4 FY24, and same is attributed to increase in the yield on advances and a constant cost of deposit during the quarter.

items.statement: Yield on advances expected to increase slightly in Q2 and more in Q3 before stabilizing
items.quote: We will be able to see some slight increase in the Q2 and Q3, before stabilizing for the Q3. So, the up-string available in the yield will not be that steep as we are talking about 11.2 % to 11.4%, but there will be some increase which we are able to see from 11.2 % to next as level we move forward.

items.statement: Cost of deposits remained constant at 5.8% in Q1 FY25 vs Q4 FY24
items.quote: If we look into our cost of deposit, our cost of deposit remains constant. It was 5.8 % in Q4 FY24 and it is 5.8 % in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: MCLR increased by 20 bps in Q4 FY24; 60-70% of book repriced, 25-30% remaining
items.quote: Since we increased over MCLR by 20 basis points in Q4, FY24, for which , we are able to reprice 60% to 70% of the book, but around 25% to 30% of the book remaining to be repriced.

items.statement: Disbursements of Rs. 754 crores in Q1 FY25, up 62% YoY and 12% QoQ
items.quote: The Bank has made the highest quarterly disbursement of Rs. 754 crores, a growth of 62% on a year-on-year basis and 12% on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Loan mix shift: Agri 35% (down from 37%), Mortgage 27% (up from 26%), MSME 21% (up from 19%), Corporate 10% (up from 9%), Consumption 7% (down from 8%) QoQ
items.quote: Our advances consisting of agriculture 35%, which was 37% a quarter back, that is as on 31st of March 2024; mortgage 27% against 26% a quarter back; MSME, 21% against 19% a quarter back; c orporate and NBFC, 10% against 9% a quarter back; and consumption lending at 7% against 8% a quarter

items.statement: SMA-1 at 3.59% and SMA-2 at 2.83% as of June 2024, up from 2.98% and 2.56% a year ago due to heat wave and elections
items.quote: The SMA number, if we talk about the SMA-2, is 2.83% against 2.56% on June versus June. And SMA-1 figure is 3.59% against 2.98% June versus June.

items.statement: No substantial stress building in Agri, Mortgage, or MSME books; collection efficiency at 98%+
items.quote: As of date, we are not seeing any substantial stress building up, whether we talk about the agriculture and which is evident even from the numbers available in the agri as well as all the three segments, our numbers in the NPA perspective, net NPA perspective, it's almost similar as we've done in the last year.

items.statement: LCR at 215% in Q1 FY25; pro forma LCR guidelines impact estimated at 13-15% on balance sheet
items.quote: We have an LCR of 215% on Q1 basis. So, with this effect, we have a sufficient opportunity to grow our loan book, maintaining the high LCR.

items.statement: EBITDA expected to grow at least 80% YoY in FY25 from Rs. 150 crores base
items.quote: we are looking at about more than 80% growth in our EBITDA as compared to last year. At last year we were at about Rs. 150 crores of EBITDA, we are looking at least 80% growth in that within this year

items.statement: Dadri plant total capex Rs. 500 crores, Rs. 250 crores spent last year, balance in FY25
items.quote: Dadri plant, the total CAPEX for this project is Rs. 500 crores. Out of the Rs. 500 crores, we had already spent Rs. 250 crores last year, and the balance will be spent within this year

items.statement: Steel cord 2 lakh tonnes facility capex Rs. 2,500 crores over ~5 years
items.quote: We are looking at a Rs. 2,500 crore investment for a 2 lakh tonnes facility to be done in a phased manner

items.statement: Q1 FY25 volume 76,000 tonnes, up 140% YoY across all three streams
items.quote: The absolute number of volumes that we have done is close to 76,000 tonnes

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 7.6%, up 260 bps YoY; PAT margin 3.9%, up 70 bps
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin also rose by 260 basis points to 7.6%, and PAT margin grew by 70 basis points to 3.9%

items.statement: Cost-plus model: prices adjusted same day for stainless steel, monthly for carbon steel; 80-85% inventory sold with confirmed orders
items.quote: every month, by second or third of the month, we get to know the new pricing, and accordingly we change our prices, and our new orders are booked at the new prices. Similarly, in stainless steel, it is a more volatile commodity. So, wherever, whenever there is a change in my raw material price, we also change our finished prices

items.statement: Each quarter in FY25 expected to be better than previous; Q2 > Q1, Q3 > Q2, Q4 > Q3
items.quote: My second quarter should be better than the first, third should be better than the second, and fourth should be better than the third

items.statement: Specialty wire vertical launch in Q3 FY25: hose wire first, then steel cord; steel cord commercial production by Nov-Dec 2024
items.quote: we are looking at starting production by November or December of this year, commercial production, after all successful trials and everything. And within the same month, we will also start selling the product. We will first look at hose wire and then we will look at steel cord

items.statement: Steel cord customer approval takes 1-1.5 years; hose wire needs no approval, 40-50% capacity usable immediately
items.quote: in steel cord, we are looking at a one-year approval process practically from the customer, wherein hose wire we will be able to see the revenues within the fourth quarter of this year

items.statement: No further capital raise needed; all capex funded from internal accruals
items.quote: we do not see the company needing much cash because we are at a good run rate for EBITDA. Every year we are growing at a good pace. So, all our CAPEX plans for the next many years we should be able to do with our own accruals

items.statement: Specialty wire 20,000 tonnes pilot capex Rs. 150 crores spent; part of 3.5 lakh tonnes campus
items.quote: right now for this 20,000 tonnes, we have spent about Rs. 150 crores of CAPEX, which is very low as per the industry standard, because this is part of a very big facility of a 3.5 lakh tonnes campus

items.statement: Peak revenue potential Rs. 5,000 crores at current commodity prices when Dadri fully ramped
items.quote: once the Dadri is fully ramped up, as far as revenue goes, if you look at the current commodity pricing, I would say that we should be able to achieve about Rs. 5,000 crores of revenue at peak

items.statement: ROCE improved from 18.46% to 23.85% in Q1 FY25; target 20-25% sustained
items.quote: the quarter ending June, our ROC E from about 18.46% last year jumped to 23.85%. And we will see a positive impact on ROCE every year. Our focus is to maintain at least 20%-25% kind of a ROCE level

items.statement: Consolidation of Balaji Wires and Bansal High Carbon: job-work started Q1, lease by Q3 FY25, full shutdown in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: within the third quarter, we will take these two companies on lease. So, these two companies, they did about Rs. 40 crores of EBITDA last year. We are paying them about Rs. 6.5 crores per year, both combined, to take this complete revenue and EBITDA in Bansal Wire

items.statement: Q1 FY25 net cash from operations negative Rs. 41 crores due to Dadri inventory/debtor build-up; working capital cycle 70 days (inv 30, rec 43, pay 12)
items.quote: the net cash generated is a negative of Rs. 41 crores for the first quarter, and this is because of the investment in our Dadri facility. To start our production, the initial level of stocks, the initial level of customer, d ebtors, all of that has been created

items.statement: JLR holds full-year EBIT margin guidance of greater than or equal to 8.5% and net cash target despite aluminum supply disruption
items.quote: We will hold our guidance on our key full -year ﬁnancial deliverables of greater or equal to 8.5% EBIT, and achieving net cash

items.statement: Key aluminum supplier flood expected to constrain JLR production in Q2 and Q3
items.quote: Most front of mind is that one of our key aluminum suppliers has been impacted badly by a ﬂood, and this will disrupt our inbound supply. It's not impacting us currently but we do expect it to constrain our production through the balance of Q2 and into Q3

items.statement: JLR order backlog at 104,000 units at end of Q1
items.quote: Order backlog at the end of the quarter was 104,000 units. So still in line with where we would be expecting it to be.

items.statement: JLR Q1 EBIT margin 8.9%, 6th consecutive quarter above 6%
items.quote: EBIT 8.9%. This is the 6th quarter in a row that we have had EBIT of over 6%.

items.statement: CV business Q1 EBITDA 11.6% up 220 bps YoY, EBIT 8.9% up 240 bps YoY, no one-offs
items.quote: EBITDA at 11.6% is at 220 bps growth over last year and an EBIT of 8.9% is 240 bps growth over last year.

items.statement: PV ICE EBITDA margin maintained at 8.5% YoY, EV pre-R&D EBITDA margin improved 6% YoY
items.quote: On the ICE part of the business, we've been able to maintain our EBITDA margin on a year-on-year basis at about 8.5% and substantially improved our EV pre R&D EBITDA margins by 6% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: JLR Q1 investment spend GBP 951 million, engineering GBP 678 million at 66% capitalization, full-year guidance GBP 3.5 billion
items.quote: We are also making sure we bring to market BEV solutions that are perfect for our bran ds, with their oﬀ road mastery, their luxury drive credentials. So we a re learning from others that have gone before us, making sure our powertrains are perfect, and we will get close to GBP 3.5 billion by the end of the

items.statement: Tata Motors standalone capex running at Rs. 8,000 Cr annual rate
items.quote: We are clocking at the Rs. 8000 Cr rate that we had committed and we'll be there in that zone.

items.statement: Domestic CV demand expected to gradually improve on infrastructure capex, monsoon, festive season
items.quote: Domestically, we expect a gradual improvement in the domestic demand during the rest of the year as the investments in infrastructure, healthy monsoons, favorable macros, new launches, festive demand, all of that is coming through.

items.statement: PV industry retail declined in May-June due to heat and elections, inquiries firm, bounce-back seen in July, festive demand expected
items.quote: it was actual ly interesting to see that the inquiries remained ﬁrm in May and June despite the declining retail and that pretty much indicated that in the coming months the retail is going to come back. It was customers who are taking slightly more time in terms of con verting to retail and we did see some level of bounce back in July. And we expect that in the upcoming festive season, the demand

items.statement: JLR Range Rover wholesales up 25% YoY, Defender retail flat at healthy level, Jaguar wholesales down due to model discontinuation
items.quote: a strong success, wholesales were up 25% YoY and retail's up 20% YoY, driven largely by the removal of production constraints as we ﬁnished the ramp up at our Solihull plant. Defender a little bit weaker in terms of wholesales, but that is just the timing eﬀect. If you look at the retail line for De fender, it is fairly ﬂat and fairly ﬂat at a very healthy level , signiﬁcantly over 100,000 units p

items.statement: CV M&HCV volumes up 10% YoY led by 19T segment, passenger carriers up 39%, SCV/pickup facing financing headwinds
items.quote: the M&HCV volumes grew by 10%, whereas the passenger carrie r, including buses, grew by 39%, but within that, let me tell you that bulk of the growth in M&HCV was actually led by the medium commercial vehicle segment, the 19 ton segment

items.statement: CV commodities flat in Q1, likely flat in Q2, cost reduction efforts accelerating
items.quote: Cost reduction eﬀorts, as I said, was a bright spot in the quarters gone by and in fact, the commodities also remained ﬂat in Q1 and likely to remain at an overall ﬂat level in Q2 as well

items.statement: Demerger of CV business into new listed TML (60:40 asset split) targeted appointed date July 1, 2025, completion in 12-15 months, tax-neutral, 1:1 share entitlement
items.quote: the appointed date for this tran saction we are targeting the 1 st July, 2025. And when the demerger happens, whoever is on the record date, the shareholder of Tata Motors will be eligible for one share each of the CV Company, that is TML, and one share in the existing TML, which will be called TMPV. This is the nature of the transaction. One of the most important number in this entitlement ratio

items.statement: Revenue growth of 18% YoY in Q1 FY25; confident of double-digit growth going forward
items.quote: We have achieved a consolidated revenue of ₹ 2,197 crores for the current quarter as against the income of ₹ 1,859 crores for the corresponding quarter of previous year, a growth of 18% year-on-year.

items.statement: Expects pricing pressure to stabilize in coming quarters
items.quote: Now, that being said, when will the pricing stabilize? I wish to stabilize this today, but I don't have control on that. It should happen soon, we are hoping in the coming few quarters things should slowly stabilize.

items.statement: Kakinada Phase-I production to gradually begin during FY25; total spend ₹1,018 crores so far
items.quote: Our Greenfield expansion at Unit-III is progressing rapidly and the upcoming production activity in the 200 acres Phase-I is expected to gradually begin during FY'24-25.

items.statement: Maintenance capex around ₹250-300 crores for the year
items.quote: I would say that would be the number, around 250-300 crores.

items.statement: New capex guidance expected next quarter or quarter after; will invest as capacity reaches 90% utilization
items.period: next quarter or the quarter after
items.quote: I think we will have a new CA PEX guidance more towards next quarter or the quarter after, because right now we are trying to complete Kakinada project, also we have few CS projects where we are investing money in

items.statement: Custom synthesis seeing strong growth with several Phase-II and Phase-III molecules; BioSecure Act driving more opportunities
items.quote: we are getting a lot of Phase-II, Phase-III molecules, lot of fast track molecules where it is in advanced stages and it's waiting for regulatory approvals from the CS companies and from multinationals. So, we are seeing a lot of opportunities coming our way

items.statement: Material consumption at 40% of sales revenue in Q1 FY25 vs 39% previous quarter due to product mix change
items.quote: Material consumption for this quarter is at about 40% of the sales revenue as compared to about 39% in the immediate previous quarter, and 39% for the corresponding quarter of previous year due to change in product mix.

items.statement: Pricing pressure on large volume generics (Naproxen, Gabapentin, Dextromethorphan) but offset by volume growth; raw material prices stable in Q1
items.quote: We are experiencing pricing pressure across our large volume products like Naproxen, Gabapentin, Dextromethorphan; but we being one of the largest producers and player and having long-term contracts with our customers, we are able to maintain sustainable market share, and, in fact, growing in those products.

items.statement: Stable demand for established generics; emerging generics gaining market share; nutraceuticals at ₹178 crores in Q1
items.quote: Our nutraceuticals business amounted to ₹178 crores for this quarter.

items.statement: Generics to custom synthesis mix at 51:49 in Q1; targeting 50:50 balance long-term
items.quote: Product mix for generics to custom synthesis is 51% and 49% respectively.

items.statement: Peptide business advancing from building blocks to fragments (tetramers/decamers); pilot plant ready, ordered 2-3 commercial 500L reactors
items.quote: Now we have started working on Tetramer and Decamer, basically four chain amino acids, 10 chain amino acids, either through solid phase or liquid phase and our pilot plant is almost ready where we will be producing decent quantities and also we will be taking this forward commercially. We have already ordered a few 500 litre reactors to take this forward.

items.statement: Logistics and supply chain challenges persist with freight hikes and long transit times; maintaining safety stocks and diversifying supply base
items.quote: Logistics and supply chain challenges continue to persist, resulting in significant freight hikes and long-transit times due to rerouting and vessel cancellation. In response, we have been vigilant and are closely monitoring each shipment diligently implementing our risk mitigation measures.

items.statement: US FDA inspection at Unit-II completed with one procedural observation
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that we had a successful US FDA inspection at our Unit-II production facility. It was a general CGMP inspection, which was completed with one procedural observation.

items.statement: Kakinada plant ready for commercialization by end of FY25 but regulatory approvals will take 1-2 years before revenue contribution
items.quote: The Kakinada plant would be ready for commercialization towards the end of '24-25 but it would take time to like make it for the product to be approved going through all the regulatory requirements. So, if you want to really see the benefits from Kakinada plant, it would take another two years.

items.statement: Long-term asset turnover target of 1x expected in 2-3 years from current 0.6-0.7x
items.quote: If we are looking at a very long-term horizon, then it is one-to-one is what we are expecting.

items.statement: Future generic pipeline (Ticagrelor etc.) fully backward integrated; commercialization from FY26 as patents expire
items.quote: So, even on all the future generics we are filing right now which are going to come off-patent, some in '25, some in '26, some in '27, all of them we have completely backward integrated.

items.statement: Tyre cord fabric demand uptick driven by 2-wheeler segment and tyre exports; favourable monsoon expected to boost tractor and 2-wheeler tyre demand
items.quote: The demand for tyre cord fabric is experiencing an uptick, primarily driven by increased demand in the 2 -wheeler segments and growth in tyre exports. Additionally, a favourable monsoon season is anticipated to boost the demand for tractors and 2 -wheeler tyres in the near term.

items.statement: Margins expected under pressure due to lower prices in Chinese market
items.quote: However, margins are expected to remain under pressure due to lower prices in Chinese market.

items.statement: Polyester Tyre Cord Fabric trials to start in Q2 FY25 with approvals expected by end of Q4 FY25
items.quote: Notably, trials for Polyester Tyre Cord Fabric are scheduled to commence in second quarter FY '25 with approvals from tyre companies expected by the end of fourth quarter of FY '25.

items.statement: Filament yarn demand rising since May 2024; Mother Yarn and Draw Texturized Yarn expansions meeting growing demand
items.quote: In the filament yarn sector, there has been a noticeable rise in demand since May '24. Expansions in production of Mother Yarn and Draw Texturized Yarn have facilitated meeting the growing demand for these products.

items.statement: Increased raw material costs from supply chain issues passed on to customers; margins improved due to higher VAPs and stable Chinese prices with cost optimization
items.quote: Increased raw material costs arising due to supply chain issues were passed on to customers. Margins have improved, thanks to higher VAPs and stable prices in Chinese market with ongoing efforts focused on cost optimization.

items.statement: Routine capex of INR35-50 crores for FY25 including modernization and energy saving projects; large expansion capex completed in Q4 FY24
items.quote: See, in addition to routine capex, we also continuously do modernization and energy saving projects. So on a year -- on a whole, we will be spending somewhere between INR35 crores to INR50 crores on these capex depending on how the -- how these projects progresses.

items.statement: Hybrid power commissioned July 2023 reduced power costs; 25-33% of Bharuch plant power from hybrid renewable, expected to remain in 20-35% range with seasonality
items.quote: So at Bharuch plant, about -- between 25% to 33% power depending on the season and generations is coming from the hybrid renewable power and the balance is from the grid.

items.statement: Polyester Tyre Cord Fabric targeting ~10% of domestic demand; commercial production expected from Q1 FY26 after approvals by end FY25
items.quote: We'll not be able to give a quantitative number, but we are targeting ab out a 10% capacity for the domestic demand. And once, as mentioned in the opening comments, the process will start with fabric being given for trials and we'll go through a detailed review -- detailed approval process of the tyre company. So hopefully, by end of FY '25, we should have approvals from multiple customers and sho

items.statement: Supply chain issues from Red Sea crisis and container freight increases easing but still above Q4 levels; normalization expected as US tariffs kick in from August
items.quote: So supply chain, as you would be aware, was an issue in quarter 1, mainly because of certain increases in the container freight from China and East countries to particularly the state is p art of the world. And because a lot of containers and ships were getting diverted and also the Red Sea crisis. So that has actually slightly come down, but it is still higher than what it used to be in Q4 even w

items.statement: Optimistic on sustained volume growth in remaining quarters vs prior year; capacity ready at 92,000 tons with 20,000 tons in Q1
items.quote: We are definitely optimistic that better volumes should remain -- should happen in the balanced quarters compared to the corresponding quarters of previous years. And we are definitely as all our capexes, and capacities are on stream. We are ready to take benefit of that if the continued demand is there from our end users.

items.statement: Value-added products portfolio expansion to continue in Nylon Filament Yarn with multi-level value addition opportunities
items.quote: Yes, there is opportunity on value -added products, and that would be another focus area, particularly for the Nylon Filament Yarn segment. And the value addition actually does not stop at one level, you can go down up to 1, 2, 3 levels of value addition as well.

items.statement: Bangladesh garment shift impact too early to assess; potential yarn demand upside if garment demand shifts to India
items.quote: But as of now, I mean, it's too early to just 2 days story to comprehend whether it will actually lead to a better demand in India or not. But we will see how does it open up. But as and when if the opportunity arises, we will definitely try to take benefit of that.

items.statement: Cost control efforts on all controllable costs to continue; focus on portfolio optimization and cost reduction amid geopolitical risks like airfreight
items.quote: So there is a definite effort to control all controllable costs and that is also reflected in the quarter, which has gone by. And our effort from the management side is to look at costs from all angles and also look at optimization of the portfolio, which has a look for products where the cost is high and the margins are low, it is also reflected in the margins being on an aggregated basis better

items.statement: Q2 demand steady; hopeful for good volumes in Q2 but no monthly numbers provided
items.quote: The demand has been steady. So hopefully, as I said, we don't have any forecast to say what will be the number, but we are hopeful that quarter 2 should also give good set of volumes.

items.statement: Raised INR 150 crores via warrants over 18 months; INR 90 crores allocated for capex to create new assets and increase capacities and range, possibly at one or two locations including a greenfield plant.
items.quote: The capital expenses or capital deployment will be almost to the extent of INR 90 crores after that. So, all this is going into creating new assets and increasing our capacities and range.

items.statement: Targets 20% top-line growth for FY25 and aims to maintain similar growth for the next 3-4 years.
items.quote: So we try to maintain this kind of a growth number for coming 3-4 years.

items.statement: Confirmed on track to achieve aspirational building products revenue of INR 160-170 crores for FY25.
items.quote: I think we are on track. We are doing reasonably okay as to our plans. And today, what looks like that we should hit the numbers as we have projected.

items.statement: Expects margins to improve further from current 9.5% as building materials volume increases; improvement will take a couple of quarters.
items.quote: A couple or 2 more it will really go up. It will not happen overnight. But yes, that is the trend and that is the direction we shall move.

items.statement: Building products gross margin (value addition) is 30-35%; dedicated building product companies achieve EBITDA margins of 15-19%.
items.quote: Raw material to value addition will be 30-35% in case of building product.

items.statement: Building materials industry growing at 9-11% annually driven by infrastructure, housing, and government focus; expects continuous growth.
items.quote: See market is growing, as I've been saying, about almost double digit 9%, 10%, 11%, somewhere in between. And this will continue to grow as India is focusing on developing infrastructure.

items.statement: Agriculture volume growth of 12% YoY in Q1 FY25; new markets growing faster in percentage terms, mature markets contributing volume due to lower raw material prices improving affordability.
items.quote: In percentage terms, certainly new markets offer higher percentage in terms of growth from last QoQ growth. But in terms of total volume, even the mature volume and we are seeing a good demand because raw material prices have come down.

items.statement: Industrial segment volume dropped to 1,295 MT in Q1 FY25 from 5,091 MT YoY due to EPC contractor payment cycle risks; will restrict growth and wait for post-monsoon clarity from October.
items.quote: We will be certainly growing both on agriculture side and building materials side. And on industrial side, we will wait and watch and see how things pan out in terms of overall cash flow cycles of EPC contractors.

items.statement: Column pipes offer much better margins than agri pipes due to engineering value addition; focusing on quality and automated processes in limited geographies.
items.quote: Yes. Column offers much better margins as compared to agri pipes because here, a lot of engineering also gets into processing as well as in manufacturing.

items.statement: Building products capacity at peak utilization can generate over INR 200 crores revenue; INR 10 crores spent in Q1 FY25 adding to prior capex.
items.quote: You see, at the peak utilization, as we have been mentioning, we would be able to generate a business volume of over INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Effective tax rate fell to 15% in Q1 FY25 due to higher depreciation and brought-forward losses from fire; not sustainable, will revert to 26-27%.
items.quote: The tax rate because of the higher depreciation allocation and the brought forward loss after the fire, both things contributed to the lower tax rate, which will not be sustained.

items.statement: Not entering micro/drip irrigation due to different business DNA and government engagement; focus remains on agriculture pipes and building products.
items.quote: No, we are not getting there because drip irrigation is a bit just a little different in terms of its DNA and ways of working, where we are not very clear that whether we should be venturing that area.

items.statement: Expects ethanol production in excess of 21 crore litres in FY25 and close to 25 crore litres in FY26 from existing assets
items.quote: see in FY 25 we are looking what we mentioned in the previous one of a number in excess of 21 crore litres, right an d it was also explained that with maize the capacity is a little lower. items.statement: Targets double-digit increase in sugarcane availability for next sugar season on standalone basis
items.quote: We're looking at a possible double-digit increase in the cane availability for our Sugar business for next year.

items.statement: Power Transmission order book at record ₹306 crore, up 12.5% year-on-year with 12% increase in order booking this quarter
items.quote: The Power Transmission business rep orted a 12% increase in order booking this quarter and a record closing order book of ₹306 crore, which is an improvement of 12.5% over the corresponding period

items.statement: Power Transmission seeing excellent demand in compressor gearbox, small hydro, API, and integrally geared gearboxes domestically and internationally
items.quote: The Company continues to witness excellent de mand for its products, including in the high technology compressor gearbox market and a recent addition once again, has been a demand for the high power, small hydro turbine applications both domestically and

items.quote: So, the expansion in the existing facility is very much on trac k. In fact, I anticipate that this facility will be commissioned six weeks in advance. items.statement: Refined and pharmaceutical-grade sugar now comprise 70% of total sugar production
items.quote: We continue from an operating perspective to focus on premium products such as refined sugar and pharmaceutical-grade sugar, which now on a collective basis comprised of 70% of the overall sugar production of the Company.

items.quote: The debt position of the Company on a standalone basis on June 30 th 2024 increased to ₹1,150 crore as compared to ₹920 crore on June 30th, 2023. The standalone debt at the end of period under review comprises of ₹245 crore of term loans and all such loans are with interest

items.quote: Presently, sugar prices are at their recent highs, and we are selling refined sugar at ₹3990 per quintal at ex-factory for a refined grade sugar and sulph itation sugar at ₹3940 per quintal ex -factory as well, pretty good prices. items.statement: Revenue growth of 18% YoY in Q1 FY25; constant currency growth at 18%
items.quote: We have achieved a consolidated revenue of ₹ 2,197 crores for the current quarter as against the income of ₹ 1,859 crores for the corresponding quarter of previous year, a growth of 18% year-on-year.

items.statement: Expect double-digit growth in both volume and price based revenue going forward
items.quote: As we said like it is in line with our double-digit growth, which we always say that we are very optimistic about our double digit growth be it both volume based and price based which is reflected in our revenue.

items.statement: Maintenance capex estimated at ₹250-300 crores for the year
items.quote: I would say that would be the number, around 250-300 crores.

items.statement: Kakinada Phase-I production expected to gradually begin during FY25; total spend including advances ₹1,018 crores
items.quote: Our Greenfield expansion at Unit-III is progressing rapidly and the upcoming production activity in the 200 acres Phase-I is expected to gradually begin during FY'24-25.

items.statement: Ordered two to three 500-litre reactors for GLP-1 peptide fragments at Unit-1
items.quote: We have already ordered a few 500 litre reactors to take this forward.

items.statement: Custom synthesis growing with several Phase-II and Phase-III molecules; existing major commercial projects yielding positive results
items.quote: The Custom Synthesis segment is advancing with several new projects across all clinical phases and we are working on several Phase-II and Phase-III molecules.

items.statement: Material consumption at 40% of sales revenue in Q1 FY25 vs 39% in Q4 FY24 and Q1 FY24 due to product mix change
items.quote: Material consumption for this quarter is at about 40% of the sales revenue as compared to about 39% in the immediate previous quarter, and 39% for the corresponding quarter of previous year due to change in product mix.

items.statement: Pricing pressure on large volume generics (Naproxen, Gabapentin, Dextromethorphan) but long-term contracts help maintain market share; expect stabilization in near future
items.quote: We are experiencing pricing pressure across our large volume products like Naproxen, Gabapentin, Dextromethorphan; but we being one of the largest producers and player and having long-term contracts with our customers, we are able to maintain sustainable market share.

items.statement: Stable demand for established generics balances pricing pressure; emerging generics gaining market share; future generics to commercialize in FY26
items.quote: We have been diligently meeting our customer requirements through strategic supply chain management and operational excellence. The industry continues to observe pharmaceutical shifts that create room for expanding market opportunities.

items.statement: Logistics and supply chain challenges persist with significant freight hikes and long transit times; maintaining safety stocks and diversifying supply base
items.quote: Logistics and supply chain challenges continue to persist, resulting in significant freight hikes and long-transit times due to rerouting and vessel cancellation.

items.statement: BioSecure Act creating more Phase-II and Phase-III opportunities in custom synthesis; generic side interest but long haul due to price sensitivity
items.quote: Now, with Bio Secure Act, we are seeing more number of Phase-II and Phase-III molecules than what we saw before. Coming to whether it is implicable even to the generic side, yes, we are seeing interest coming on the generic side too.

items.statement: Successful US FDA inspection at Unit-II with one procedural observation
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that we had a successful US FDA inspection at our Unit-II production facility. It was a general CGMP inspection, which was completed with one procedural observation.

items.statement: Peptide business advancing from building blocks to fragments (tetramer, decamer); pilot plant nearly ready with 50-litre reactors
items.quote: Now we have started working on Tetramer and Decamer, basically four chain amino acids, 10 chain amino acids, either through solid phase or liquid phase and our pilot plant is almost ready where we will be producing decent quantities.

items.statement: Contrast media: shipping commercial quantities of iodine-based products to brand companies; Gadolinium compounds in Phase-III development
items.quote: On the contrast media, we sell both to several of the brand companies, I mean the innovators and also to the generic houses. In some of the Iodine-based products we have been successful, and we have been shippi ng commercial quantities to a few of the brand companies

items.statement: Long-term asset turnover target of 1x expected in next 2-3 years with Kakinada capex and new API products
items.quote: I would say in a long-term, yes, that's a safe assumption to have in the next two to three years.

items.statement: Domestic explosives volume grew 16% YoY, in line with annual guidance for FY25
items.quote: The domestic explosives volume for the quarter grew by 16% year-on-year basis, which is in line with our annual guidance for the year '25.

items.statement: Defence revenue guidance for FY25 is INR1,500 crores, expected to be comfortably achieved with INR2,500 crores order book
items.quote: With these developments and considering the current Defence order book of INR2,500 crores, we will be sailing through our annual Defence guidance of INR1,500 crores comfortably.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 is around 25%, higher than last year's 23%
items.quote: we expect that EBITDA margin should be more than 23%. As far as direction is concerned, definitely, the current EBITDA margin of 27%, 28% is on a very good or higher side. But we expect that 25%, we should be able to achieve.

items.statement: Capex plan for FY25 is around INR800 crores, with INR200 crores spent in Q1
items.quote: This year, we have given that we are expecting the capex to be around INR800 crores. And in the Q1, we have done around INR200 crores.

items.statement: Current total order book stands at around INR4,750 crores plus, with Defence order book at INR2,500 crores
items.quote: So the current order book stands at around INR4,750 crores plus. So Defence is also around INR2500 crores and currently, no big orders have come in this quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin reached close to 28%, up 826 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for the quarter reached to the levels close to 28% and the same grew by 826 bps.

items.statement: Government budget for FY25 with increased capital outlay on infrastructure, housing and roads will increase demand for explosives
items.quote: The government budget for FY '25, with increased capital outlay and greater emphasis on infrastructure development, housing and roads, is bound to increase demand for explosives.

items.statement: Defence revenue grew 32% YoY to INR204 crores in Q1 FY25, first lot of indigenously developed loitering munition delivered
items.quote: We are pleased to share that the Defence revenue stands at INR204 crores for this quarter, registering a growth of 32% year-on-year basis. The company has delivered first lot of indigenously developed loitering munition to the armed forces.

items.statement: Defence order decisions slowed due to elections and government formation, but Pinaka orders expected soon
items.quote: Pinaka orders are also likely to come soon, but because of elections and then government formation, certain decision-making has slowed down for a couple of months, but we are expecting orders to receive very soon.

items.statement: Expanding presence in Kazakhstan and Thailand with manufacturing units, Problast South Africa acquisition completed
items.quote: We are expanding our presence in 2 new countries, namely Kazakhstan and Thailand very soon. The acquisition of Problast, South Africa is in line with the company's intent to expand its operation in the international markets.

items.statement: Chaff and flares production facility inaugurated, first private company in India to manufacture 100% indigenous chaff and flares under IDDM route
items.quote: We have recently inaugurated this facility to produce chaff and flares and these are acting as electronic countermeasure devices for protecting the military air crafts. So as you are aware that our company is the first company in India to start these products as 100% indigenous under the IDDM route.

items.statement: Total investment in Defence business till date is around INR1,000 crores plus
items.quote: So it's around INR1,000 crores plus.

items.statement: Global geopolitical situation driving good demand for ammunition products, but RFP and order timelines are lengthy
items.quote: If you look at the global geopolitical situation, the demand for these products seems to be very good. But the time line on submitting RFPs, getting orders and then starting the supply chain or starting the supply, it takes its own time.

items.statement: Domestic explosives volume targeting plus 15% growth for FY25, Q1 achieved almost 16%
items.quote: And in this year also, we are targeting plus 15%. So in this quarter, we have almost crossed 15% level.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 27-29% by Q4 FY25, with Q2 around 24-25% due to pricing pressure and rising input costs
items.quote: By Q4, certainly, Nikhil, we are going to target reaching those kind of EBITDA levels. However, a word of caution, the next quarter, again, is going to be similarly balanced about 24%, 25% EBITDA levels because of pricing pressures, and raw material input costs are rising this quarter.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA per tonne of INR25,000 in next 2-3 years via machine optimization and AI integration
items.quote: I think going forward, we ourselves are targeting reach ing EBITDA margins of about INR25,000 per tons in the next 2 years to 3 years, by way of implementing various initiatives that we are doing, which means optimizing o ur existing machines leading to lower cost of production as well as integrating AI mechanisms in our operations, which is going to help reduce our costs quite substantially

items.statement: Modernization capex of INR735 crores over 2-3 years to expand capacity 50% to 675 tpd on existing machines, funded by INR535 crores term debt and INR200 crores internal accruals
items.quote: So we are targeting expanding by 50%. From the current 450 tonnes per day, we are planning to reach 675 tonnes per day on all our existing machines only. They are not going to be any new machine that is going to be added and which is going to help reduce our cost of production going forward.

items.statement: Normal maintenance capex of INR30-odd crores per year to remain low for next 3-4 years due to modernization spend
items.quote: Normal capex is about INR30-odd crores every year because I don't know you may have been there in the earlier calls, we are spending a capex amount of about INR735 crores on this modernization scheme and that is going to be part and parcel of maintaining all our machines, our pulp mills, our chemical recovery, our power plant.

items.statement: Term debt of INR535 crores from SBI, Yes Bank, Indian Bank; SBI sanctioned INR250 crores; debt to be secured in next fortnight
items.quote: So this is by way of INR535 crores as bank term debt and INR200 crores internal accruals. The term debt is being secured from our existing bankers, which is SBI, Yes Bank and Indian Bank. And for the information, SBI has already sanctioned INR 250 crores.

items.statement: Peak debt under INR600 crores by March 2026; current debt INR385 crores, additional INR430 crores, repaying INR220 crores in interim
items.quote: So currently , our debt is at a level of INR 385 crores. By the time these projects are commissioned, which would take about 2 years from today, our further deb t that we will undertake is INR430 crores, which will take it up to INR815 crores. But in the interim -- in the 2 years, we would have repaid INR 220 crores of existing debt, so our peak debt will be under INR600 crores as of March 2026

items.quote: For the quarter under review, operating revenue was around INR281 crores, with EBITDA reaching INR72 crores and EBITDA margin at 25.51%. The profit after tax for the quarter was INR38 crores, resulting in PAT margin of 13.61%.
