items.statement: Cash and equivalents of INR 1,700 crores as of June 2024; evaluating inorganic acquisition opportunities in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu; no promoter exit intention
items.quote: currently, our cash and cash equivalents as mentioned in our earnings presentation, it's around INR 1,700 crores. And as of now, we have not yet decided it how do we deploy it? We are still looking at a lot of inorganic opportunities

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 1,041 crores as of June 2024 vs net debt of INR 565 crores a year ago
items.quote: Aster India, net cash stands at INR 1,041 crores as on 30th June, compared to net debt of INR 565 crores as on 30th June 2023

items.statement: Mature hospitals (6+ years) delivered 23% EBITDA margin and 30% ROCE in Q1 FY25; core hospital segment at 21% EBITDA margin
items.quote: our mature hospitals (with more than 6 years in operation) contributing to almost 73% of our hospital segment revenue, delivered our operating EBITDA margin of 23% in Q1 FY25, with the ROC E standing at 30%

items.statement: O&M hospital EBITDA margin target of 15-20% (currently 11-12%); ROCE accretive at 15-20%
items.quote: we are expecting in a range of 15 %, in that around that range, 15% – 18%, or if you can take it to 20%, well and good. But at present, we are aiming to take it, some of the hospitals are at around 11% now, 11%- 12%

items.statement: Kerala cluster (55% of hospital revenue) grew 14% YoY revenue, 30% YoY EBITDA; ALOS reduced to 3.1 days; ARPOB at INR 42,000 (+12% YoY)
items.quote: The Kerala cluster delivered operating EBITDA margins of 22.7% aided by reduction in ALOS to 3.1 days and price growth. The APROB of Kerala cluster also witnessed an optimum growth of 12% YoY at INR 42,000 in Q1 FY25

items.statement: Karnataka/Maharashtra cluster (34% of hospital revenue) grew 38% YoY revenue, 55% YoY EBITDA; occupancy improved to 62% from 55% YoY
items.quote: The revenue of the cluster grew by 38% YoY and operating EBITDA grew by 55% YoY in Q1 FY25 while delivering an operating EBITDA margin of 21.2%. With the scaling performance of a new Whitefield Hospital at Bangalore location, the cluster witnessed a notable improvement in occupancy levels, rising to 62% in Q1 FY25 from 55% in Q1 FY24

items.statement: Price increases of 3-3.5% targeted annually; spread across geographies and departments based on market position and case mix.
items.quote: Around three, three and half percentage is something which we always look for price increase growth.

items.statement: ARPOB expected to grow 7-8% CAGR over next 3-4 years driven by case mix change and non-metro pricing headroom.
items.quote: We see that still in the future, I'm talking about medium term, between three to four years, we should be really able to grow at least 7 to 8 percentage.

items.statement: Kerala cluster EBITDA margin can mature from 22.7% to 25% via brownfield expansion and manpower optimization.
items.quote: We see that with the current EBITDA margin of 22.7%, it can really mature at 25% so that is something which is possible for Kerala cluster.

items.statement: Karnataka-Maharashtra cluster EBITDA margin can reach near 30% as Whitefield matures and occupancy improves.
items.quote: If you are something at INR 70K specifically in Karnataka, Maharashtra, you can look at my EBITDA margin something like near 30%.

items.statement: Andhra-Telangana cluster target mid-teens EBITDA margin initially, eventually closer to 20%.
items.quote: The target is to take the EBITDA margins to the mid-teen and eventually all our efforts is to see if we can take it beyond 20%, or close to our, not beyond, at this point, closer to 20% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Capex requirement ~INR 1,000 crore for 1,700 bed expansion; greenfield non-metro INR 1-1.4 crore/bed, brownfield/leased INR 60-75 lakh/bed.
items.quote: The CAPEX requirement that we have is nearly INR 1000 crore for all these 1700 beds.

items.statement: No immediate equity raise needed; cash from GCC sale and operating cash flows sufficient for capex and M&A; dilution only if share swap for platform merger.
items.quote: we do not need immediate further funding for our investment plans. So basically, any thought on dilution, we are definitely not looking at unless dilution is happening naturally as Alisha was highlighting, you know, if ther e are some share swap opportunities

items.statement: Whistleblower complaint under investigation; relates to undisclosed related party transactions and conflicted business activities; financial impact not significant.
items.quote: So, that is still under investigation actually, so nothing is in finalized actually, once we get the investigation report, only the board will take appropriate decisions.

items.statement: Strong super-specialty growth in Kerala: oncology +31%, cardiology +26%, gastro/liver transplant +21-22%; high-end cases rising.
items.quote: So almost a 31% oncology growth we have, and specifically th e cardiology department has grown by 26%. Gastro, right, basically where we do liver transplant, that has grown by more than 21, 22

items.statement: Shift to daycare surgeries and single-room upgrades driving ARPOB growth; insurance penetration improving affordability for quaternary care.
items.quote: most of the tertiary, quaternary care work is migrating towards daycare activity. That sense it puts less pressure on the system in terms of manpower, equipment and other resources required to sup port this

items.statement: Promoter pledge reduction targeted by end of current financial year; overseas loan structure makes pledge appear higher than required.
items.quote: We are hoping towards the close of this year. So, Damayanti, I think our efforts are towards reducing the pledge definitely. There is a goal towards kind of reducing it towards the close of the year.

items.statement: Brownfield expansions at Medcity (80% occupancy, +100 beds) and Kannur (95% occupancy, +100 beds) to be margin-accretive.
items.quote: Aster Medcity is where I have 80% occupancy, near 80% occupancy, with a 750 bed hospital, I'm adding 100 beds. So and also in Kannur, where I'm 95% occupancy, I'm adding another 100 beds.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Kerala ~55%, Karnataka-Maharashtra ~38%, Andhra-Telangana ~11%; Karnataka share may exceed 40% in future.
items.quote: Kerala's 55% and Karnataka and Maharashtra is around 35%, 38% revenue contribution and 11% is the Andhra and Telangana.

items.statement: Management aims to sustain current gross margins and expects EBITDA margin improvement to follow as investments gain leverage
items.quote: My take right now, would be, say, let's sustain these gross margins and then take the next leap forward in sometime.

items.statement: No major greenfield capex planned beyond Hyderabad plant; only regular maintenance and NPD capex expected
items.quote: Our large capex was on Hyderabad plant, which we've done. Our purpose is to now leverage that. As of now the regular capex of NPDs and expansions and capacity improvements and other things that we do, any large capex as of now, not yet.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 249 bps YoY to 33.1% driven by price increases, mix improvement and cost savings
items.quote: Gross margins expanded by 249 basis points year-on-year, and 237 basis points quarter-on-quarter sequentially, and stands at 33.1%, driven by a combination of price increase, mix and cost savings.

items.statement: Implemented two price hikes in fans category totaling 3-3.5% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We've done price increase in our fans category in two tranches in quarte r 1. One was early April and the other one was in June, largely in the ball park tune of about 3% to 3.5% is what we passed on to the consumers

items.statement: ECD segment grew 5.8% YoY in Q1 but 14.5% over Jan-Jun period; fans grew high-teens over Jan-Jun
items.quote: Our mark-to-market performance is better. For this period of January to June, we've grown at about 14.5% in ECD and high -teens in fans.

items.statement: Lighting business grew 10.2% with high-teens volume growth in consumer lighting and deep double-digit B2B growth
items.quote: Overall, our Lighting and Switchgear business has grown by 10.2%.

items.statement: Export degrowth due to geopolitical issues in African markets with high dependency on one country
items.quote: We degrew in exports because we were slightly dependent on one African country where there have been geopolitical situations.

items.statement: Large size inquiries and tenders in lighting B2B segment have started regenerating post-elections
items.quote: Large size inquiries and tenders have started regenerating post -elections.

items.statement: Hyderabad Industry 4.0 plant commenced commercial production; will take couple more months to stabilize operations
items.quote: We've initiated commercial production at our greenfield Hyderabad plant designed as an Industry 4.0 facility. This plant would deliver superior products at competitive costs and offer proximity to South and Western India markets. It will take a couple of more months to stabilize the operations.

items.statement: Spark Sanchay program delivering ~2% annualized cost reduction; McKinsey costs to cease from Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our Spark Sanchay program aimed at driving cost leadership is deeply ingrained in the organization, consistently delivering approximately 2% annualized cost reduction and helping us in mitigating commodity and pricing risk.

items.statement: Added 250-300 LFR stores in Q1; cover all national accounts and 40-45 of ~80-84 regional accounts
items.quote: We've added close to about 250 to 300 more stores in quarter one. So we're increasing our penetration within the account as well as the breadth of accounts that we deal with.

items.statement: Employee cost at INR 77 crore includes increment impact and wage variability; senior onboarding complete, no major restructuring planned
items.quote: So Achal, this quarter, the employee costs had impact of the increments and other things. Over a period of time, as I said, we've made investments on the structure, and I think is this the going rate.

items.statement: TPW fan contribution ~25-30% of industry; company in line with industry mix
items.quote: Firstly, the industry, depending on brand to brand, would hover between 25% to 30% as TPW contribution to the overall fans.

items.statement: Lighting market share gains consistent over last few quarters; team execution driving outperformance
items.quote: In lighting, we've been seeing a consistent market share gains over the last few quarters, and we are inching up, and that's a good encouraging sign for us.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected to be higher than Q4 FY24's 5%, targeting high single digit to double digit; EBITDA margin expansion guidance of 100 bps maintained
items.quote: Our guidelines has been that we want to grow EBITDA by at least 100 basis points, even in the current really difficult market condition, we are committed and you look at this quarter also the EBITDA has gone up by 100 basis points and is now close to 13%.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue growth target of 12-15%
items.quote: Medium term, we would love the growth rates to move to 12% to 15%, but we are hoping for the market to correct, and we are also very watchful on profitable growth.

items.statement: Capex guidance of Rs 100 crores for FY25, largely for Tommy Hilfiger COCO stores, IT and store renovations
items.quote: So, our capex is likely to be in the range of 100 crores, largely to be spent on some COCO stores on the PVH side, some IT capex and some renovation of stores.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 80 bps to 55.2% in Q1 FY25 driven by better price realization, premiumization and sourcing efficiency
items.quote: GP has moved up to 55.2%, a gain of 80 basi s points with dual benefit of better price realization as well as lower, more efficient product cost

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps to ~12.9% post-IndAS in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Most of these GP gain has flown into EBITDA which saw nearly 20% growth to Rs. 123 crores versus last year value of Rs. 103 crores.

items.statement: Wholesale channel grew >15% in Q1 FY25 after delayed spring-summer billing to align with season
items.quote: We have seen growth across brands and in every channel. There is growth in volume as well as in price realization. A key highlight was control on discounting where we delayed EOSS to end of June, while industry had been discounting by mid-June.

items.statement: Market conditions remain subdued due to elections, heat wave, fewer wedding dates; expect slightly better conditions ahead
items.quote: Markets have been difficult for a couple of quarters. Summer, there were some specific issue linked to elections for example. The global warmin g or warming in India is the reality, May saw that. The markets are sort of challenging and subdued currently

items.statement: Adjacent categories (footwear, womenswear, kidswear, innerwear) now >20% of AFL revenue, growing double-digit; USPA adjacent share ~30%
items.quote: The share of adjacent category like footwear, womenswear, kidswear, innerwear has crossed 20% revenue share of AFL and has grown in the last one year at double digit.

items.statement: Footwear category facing regulatory changes; monitoring policy developments and preparing supply chain
items.quote: As far as the footwear results is concerned, there are some regulation changes, and we are in touch with the policymakers and we are making sure that our supply chain is geared for whatever the change required.

items.statement: Net retail space addition target of 15% for FY25; added 40,000+ sq ft net in Q1 with ~30 new stores
items.quote: We remain committed to growing net retail space by around 15%, and hopeful of furt her acceleration of build-up in square footage in times ahead

items.statement: Online D2C business grew >60% YoY in Q1 with improved channel profitability; online contribution ~25% of revenue
items.quote: There is handsome growth in online direct -to-consumer b usiness that has grown more than 60% year -on-year and delivered higher channel profitability as well

items.statement: Arrow brand at low single-digit EBITDA, targeting mid-single digit in near term; Flying Machine ~1 year behind Arrow in turnaround
items.quote: Arrow remains in a low single digit brand and our first task is to take it to mid-single digit brand and in the current market condition believe the wedding dates are in the second half that the performance will improve.

items.statement: US Polo approaching Rs 2,000 cr scale, double-digit pre-IndAS EBITDA; expected to match Tommy/CK profitability in medium term
items.quote: U.S. Polo is very close and it's also double digit pre IndAS EBITDA brand of scale that we are talking about. So, in medium term, I can say confidently it will be a similar profitability brand.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 225 crores end-Q1; may rise ~50 crores next quarter due to seasonal inventory build; committed to debt reduction from free cash flow
items.quote: Our net debt was around 225 crores. There is a seasonality, next quarter it could go up by 50-odd crores here because we have to build the inventory for the season and a bigger scale.

items.statement: 60 Tommy Hilfiger stores converted to COCO model; no CK stores converted
items.quote: We have 60 stores in Tommy Hilfiger which are now COCO stores.

items.statement: A&P spend ~3% of revenue in Q1; typically 3-4% for full year
items.quote: So, in Q1, typically it is slightly lower than 3% because the campaigns happens towards the end of season. So, we are in between that 3% to 4% spend, but for this quarter it was around 3%.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 15% for FY25 stands; long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 12-13% sustainable ex inventory gain/loss
items.quote: No, I think on a long -term basis, 12% to 13% EBITDA margin is sustainable. This quarter was impacted slightly by product mix.

items.statement: Bihar plant to be operational by January adding 45,000 tonnes capacity; debottlenecking of 35,000-40,000 tonnes at existing plants over 3-4 quarters
items.quote: we expect Bihar to be operational by January, which will add -- so previously, we had guided for end of quarter 4, and we have tried our best to prepone that. So we are confident by January, we will be able to commercialize production at Bihar facility, which will help us have a strong March quarter in the current financial year, which would be a production capacity of around 45,000 ton nes, which

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 9.6% impacted by adverse agri-heavy product mix and higher A&P spend (>2.5% of revenue); long-term 12-13% sustainable
items.quote: The two major reasons for that one has been product. While we have grown across segments, both have been higher in the agriculture space where the -- of course, it's a volume driver, but the margins are slightly lower. And second is also the A&P costs have significantly increased, which is a conscious effort.

items.statement: April-May demand robust; June-July saw destocking due to PVC price decline but last-mile demand remains strong on affordable raw material, real estate and infrastructure growth
items.quote: Of course, in June, towards the end, we saw some weakness in PVC prices, which always means that there will be destocking in the channel. And that trend has continued in July. But I have always maintained that any restocking or destocking averages out over 12 months. What is important is the last mile demand. And that, I believe, continues to be strong because of the confluence of many factors lik

items.statement: Agri share of revenue increased Y-o-Y in Q1; plumbing and SWR also grew but agri was major contributor
items.quote: Correct. So agri has increased that at the gross margin level, their product mix is there. But as the EBITDA margin with increase in advertising expenses as well as losses in bathware, we have ended up with a lower EBITDA margin compared to normal.

items.statement: CPVC raw material prices to remain range-bound with no major upside; PVC prices affordable and range-bound, anti-dumping duty already factored in
items.quote: No, I believe that's already actually factored into the pricing. So it's tough to predict raw material prices, but I think even CPVC, there is no major upside. Most of the variables have been factored in. So I think CPVC raw material prices should continue to be range bound from here onwards because PVC also is becoming extremely affordable.

items.statement: PVC raw material manufacturers struggling at current spreads; government support possible but timing uncertain
items.quote: I believe that current PVC prices not be sustainable for PVC raw material manufacturers. If you look at the spreads between the feedstock and PVC are at very, very low prices, and I don't see feedstock prices correcting. So current prices of PVC, most PVC raw material manufacturers will really be struggling. So maybe you could see some support given by the government.

items.statement: Bathware revenue ~Rs.5 crore, water tank revenue ~Rs.10-12 crore in Q1; bathware net loss ~Rs.4 crore; A&P spend Rs.14 crore vs Rs.11 crore YoY
items.quote: So bathware would be around Rs.5 crores for the quarter. Water tank, just give me a minute. Water tank is around Rs.10 crores to Rs.12 crores exact number Karl will share post -- but Rs.10 crores to Rs.12 crores of water tank and Rs.5 crores of bathware.

items.statement: Aquel bathware annual run-rate expense Rs.15-18 crore (Rs.5-6 cr manpower + Rs.10-12 cr branding); gross margins higher than piping once in-house manufacturing scales
items.quote: So annual level, I would say, Rs.5 crores to Rs.6 crores on manpower and Rs.10 crores to Rs.12 crores on branding. This will slightly increase because we are now expanding our footprint to south and east over the next couple of quarters. But around -- you can take around Rs.15 crores to Rs.18 crores on a 12-month basis.

items.statement: Working capital improved to 80 days (from 95 days Mar'24); receivables 61 days (from 83 days); inventory 70 days (from 52 days); channel finance sanctions increased to Rs.155 crore
items.quote: Our overall working capital stood at 80 days in June as compared to 95 days in March 2024. As we had guided, Receivables have shown marked improvement at 61 days in June '24 from 83 August 02, 2024 Transcript - Prince Pipes and Fittings Limited Q1 FY25 Earnings Call days in March end. Inventory days stood at 70 days in March as compared to 52 days

items.statement: No inventory gain or loss in Q1; industry-wide phenomenon as price increase concentrated in late May/June
items.quote: This is not only for Prince, we are not the only industry player. If you see across players, this has been the situation because the price increase was not across the 3 months. It was mostly in the end of May or in June

items.statement: ROE to return to ~16% in 2-3 years as new capacity ramps up; gross block asset turn to improve with capacity additions
items.quote: So we are a growing organization, and we intend to keep adding the capacity, which will go back to gross block, which will not immediately give the top line and the contribution. So in next 2 to 3 years, we'll be again back to 16% as we add capacity and we start realizing the output from it.

items.statement: No plans for OPVC capacity; focus on distribution-driven products and private projects; selective about new segments
items.quote: So at this point of time, we do not have any plans for OPVC. We have always been more focused on distribution and private projects. And we believe there is enough and more room for growth, and we are adding capacity. And we have enough on our plate with now water tanks and bathware being the 2 new segment.

items.statement: Debottlenecking capex across Jaipur, Silvassa, Kolhapur, Haridwar, Chennai; Bihar plant has land for significant expansion over 2-3 years
items.quote: And the existing debottlenecks that we're doing around 35 to 40 KT additional will be at the existing plant. So it would be a combination of Jaipur, Silvassa, Kolhapur, Haridwar, Chennai across facilities because the good part is the demand is not coming from 1 or 2 geographies.

items.statement: Lucknow 450-bed tower expected to cost around Rs. 700 crore plus
items.quote: So, I think this will be around Rs. 700 crore plus for the beds.

items.statement: Mohali 250-bed hospital on 50-year lease; developer bears building cost, Max provides equipment and security deposit
items.quote: We will be providing the medical equipment, the security deposit, which is interest bearing, and loose furniture. The entire project cost will be incurred by the developer, including the land and building, etc.

items.statement: Nanavati Phase I (241 beds) structure up this month, completion expected by end of FY25
items.quote: For 241 beds in Nanavati (Phase I), the hospital structure will be up in this month and the project completion is expected by end of this fiscal year, as communicated earlier.

items.statement: Max Smart Saket (375 beds) fast-tracked, completion expected by Q1 FY26
items.quote: For 375 beds at Max Smart (Saket Complex), the project was fast-tracked in Q4 and we expect its completion by Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Mohali 155 beds on schedule, completion expected by Q1 FY26
items.quote: For 155 beds at Mohali, work on the 2nd floor slab is underway, while the work on ramp area side is reaching ground level. All high-side equipment has been ordered and the project is on schedule. We expect the completion by Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Sector 56 Gurgaon Phase I (300 beds) basement slabs nearing completion, completion expected by Q2 FY26
items.quote: For 300 beds at Sector 56, Gurgaon (Phase I), basement slabs are nearing completion and the project is progressing as per plan. Orders for all high lead-time items have been placed. We expect completion of the first phase by Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Max Vikrant Saket Phase I (415 beds) facing delay due to forest approval litigation, expected couple of quarters delay
items.quote: We expect some delay due to ongoing litigation involving DDA and Delhi Government regarding cutting out trees in the eco-sensitive zone near Asola Bhati Wildlife Sanctuary and the Ridge areas without approval.

items.statement: Dwarka hospital (303 beds) expected to break even at EBITDA level by Q4 FY25 (8-9 months from launch)
items.quote: We do think that by the 8th to 9th month we should be in a breakeven state, which means that in Q4, we should start to see breakeven numbers at EBITDA level for Dwarka hospital.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin 26.5% in Q1 FY25 on like-to-like basis, down 2% QoQ due to merit increase, GST on variable fee, lower immigration footfalls
items.quote: Network operating EBITDA stood at Rs. 487 crore, reflecting a growth of 12% year-on-year while declining by 2% quarter-on-quarter. Operating EBITDA margin stood at 26.5% for the quarter.

items.statement: ARPOB for existing network improved 7% YoY and 3% QoQ to Rs. 80,100 driven by oncology, orthopedics, renal, robotics and tariff revisions
items.quote: Average Revenue Per Occupied Bed (ARPOB) for the quarter improved to Rs. 80,100, growing by 7% year-on-year and 3% quarter-on-quarter. Year-on-year improvement in ARPOB was largely due to growth in oncology, orthopedics and renal sciences as well as increased number of robotic procedures. This was coupled with tariff revisions for self-pay, insurance and institutional segments.

items.statement: Occupancy at 77% on existing network, up from 74% YoY and 75% QoQ; occupied bed days grew 5% YoY and 2% QoQ
items.quote: Our average occupancy for the network increased to 77% from 74% in Q1 last year and 75% in the trailing quarter. While occupied bed days grew by around 5% year-on-year and 2% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Higher-end clinical mix (more robotics, oncology) lowers EBITDA margin percentage but raises EBITDA per bed; surgical vs medical mix shift improves ARPOB
items.quote: We have clearly seen a change in the clinical mix. It's moved to a higher-end clinical mix. And like I've mentioned in the past, when you do higher -end surgeries, you do more robotics and more oncolog y, etc., they typically have lower margins in percentage terms, but higher margins in value terms

items.statement: International patient revenue Rs. 158 crore; muted growth due to political situations and credit-risk actions in some countries; immigration footfalls down 48% due to visa changes in Canada, UK, Australia
items.quote: The international patient revenue stood at Rs. 158 crore. There was a temporary impact on patient flows from some countries due to political situations and credit-risk management related actions taken by us, which accounted for the muted growth in this segment.

items.statement: Lucknow and Nagpur acquired hospitals ramping well: 60% avg occupancy, Rs. 99 cr revenue and Rs. 18 cr EBITDA in Q1, ARPOB Rs. 45,300, annualized EBITDA per bed ~Rs. 30 lakhs
items.quote: For Q1, these hospitals contributed Rs. 99 crore to the revenue and Rs. 18 crore to the operating EBITDA, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 21% and 64% respectively. And more importantly, this was done within the first three months of us acquiring these facilities. Collectively, their ARPOB stood at Rs. 45,300 and annualized EBITDA per bed at approximately Rs. 30 lakhs.

items.statement: Tax rate 22.8% overall; Q1 rate 26% due to losses in Sahara entity where DTA not recognized; expected to normalize around 22%
items.quote: That's right. So, overall rate is 22.8%. The rate has gone up this quarter because we have losses in the new ent ities, mainly the Sahara hospital entity. Sahara hospital transaction was Rs. 993 crore. We funded this by Rs. 840 crore of loan into the entity. And as Abhay alluded to in his speech, we are changing the cost and capital structure in the company. So, since we have losses in the company

items.statement: Non-MF revenue share target of 20% in 3-3.5 years, growing ~2% per year (~0.5% per quarter)
items.quote: We still reaffirm our commitment to grow this, scale this to at least 20% in the next 3, 3.5 years. I believe we are on track. We'd like to grow this by about 2% every year. So about 0.5% every quarter.

items.statement: Non-MF revenue expected to grow mid- to high-20s, possibly up to 30% for next quarter or two
items.value: mid- to high-20s, maybe up to 30%
items.quote: We've said earlier that we'd like to scale MF 15%, non-MF 20%, non-MF to scale 31%. And I think for a quarter or 2, we could expect mid- to high 20s, maybe up to 30% growth from non-MF.

items.statement: Cloud migration net margin impact not expected to exceed 0.5% at any point, positive from year 4-5
items.quote: We do not expect, at any point of time, the not impact margin to be more than 0.5%. It could be higher in the initial one or two years closer to 0.5%. But going forward, because of the rationalization that is going to happen on the various resources that we are using for this platform, we expect that from the fourth or fifth year, this will become, in fact, very positive to us from an overall marg

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 45.4%, up 320 bps YoY despite absorbing annual salary increments
items.quote: We had -- we have completed the quarter with a INR150-plus crores EBITDA for the first t ime, which is a 45.4% quarter. You will also understand that April is the time when most of the company goes through its annual salary increment(28.50). Traditionally, the impact of the increment has been upwards of 2 percentage of revenue. So even eating that cost, we are able to kind of come to an operating

items.statement: MF yields stable with <1% quarterly depletion; equity mix >3% supporting yields; no disproportionate price discounts
items.quote: You've seen that play out actually, and the leads have been largely stable with the quarter-on-quarter depletion being less than 1%, right? it's 0.7% depletion in yields. And we also had said that there's not going to be a disproportionate reduction in price or price discounts. And kind of the last few quarters have been in line with what we have guided.

items.statement: Equity AUM grew 55%+ YoY; equity net inflows INR90,000 crore (70% of industry); NFO collection 82% (INR20,000+ crore); SIP registrations ~90 lakh (100% YoY growth)
items.quote: see crossed INR90,000 crore s in the quarter, this was 70% of industry's equity net inflows. And of the INR1,27,000 crores, this was INR90,000 crores, so a strong number. Within this new fund offerings, we were at a staggering 82% collection. So this is a number upwards of INR20,000 crores, upwards of 82% collection and just vindicates the overall direction in terms of the market share and market

items.statement: Non-MF revenue grew 31% YoY, outpacing MF (26%) for second consecutive quarter; KRA 100%+, Pay 44%, Account Aggregator 100%+ on small base
items.quote: the non-MF revenue grew by 31% year-on-year, driven largely by a very impressive growth that we are seeing in both Pay as well as in The AIF and Rep(28.00) revenue growth is a little muted, but you've heard the plans that we have for both, especially with the Rep with the Bima Central going live only in April and more and more integration is happening. We expect that the revenue growth will be mor

items.quote: The only thing we don't like about the market is that pricing is significantly lower just competitive price. items.statement: Balance sheet healthy with sufficient cash reserves
items.quote: Company is healthy, the balance sheet is very healthy as of now, enough cash in the bank. So, from that perspective, Company is all okay.

items.statement: Potable spirits revenue share increased to 26.7% from 13%; sugar share fell to 45.7% from 53%; ethanol share dropped to 15.5% from 21.7%
items.quote: On the revenue mix for the Quarter: Sugar contributed 45.7% of the quarter revenue down from 53.0%. Ethanol is at 15.5%, down from 21.7%. Power is 2.1%, down from 4.3%. Revenue from chemicals is 9.5% as against 7.4% and potable spirits is 26.7%, up from 13% in the corresponding quarter of last year.

items.statement: Sugar EBIT contribution rose to 60.6% from 29.7%; ethanol EBIT share fell to 19.6% from 43%; potable spirits EBIT share increased to 11.7% from 1.2%
items.quote: On the profit mix for the Quarter: Sugar has contributed 60.6% of the quarter earnings before interest and taxes up from 29.7%. Ethanol is 19.6%, down from 43%; power is at 4.2%, again down from 17.6%. EBIT from chemicals is 2.8% as against 7.9% and potable spirits is at 11.7% as against 1.2% in the corresponding quarter of last year.

items.statement: Ethanol production 120.55 lakh litres (72% from maize); sales 145.12 lakh litres (68% from maize) vs 335.3 and 357.45 lakh litres last year
items.quote: The total production of ethanol during the quarter from all the feedstocks was 120.55 lakh litres, including 86.33 lakh liters from maize and damaged food grains, 72% of the total production, versus 335.3 lakh liters in the corresponding quarter last year. Total sale of ethanol during the quarter from all feedstocks is 145.12 lakh liters including 99.08 lakh liters from maize and damaged food grai

items.statement: Average sugar realization increased 7% to Rs 38,967 per tonne from Rs 36,387 per tonne
items.quote: The average sugar realization in this quarter has been 38,967 per tonne as against 36,387 per tonne in the corresponding quarter which is higher by about 7%.

items.statement: Cane crush dropped to 0.4 lakh tonnes from 7.45 lakh tonnes; sugar production fell to 0.04 lakh tonnes from 0.51 lakh tonnes due to lower cane availability and yields
items.quote: The Company crushed 0.4 lakh tonnes as against 7.45 lakh tonnes in the corresponding quarter mainly due to lower availability of the sugarcane and lower yields last year. This was due to lower yield and impact of the heavy rains in 2023 as well. Sugar production during the quarter is 0.04 lakh tonnes which was 0.51 lakh tonnes in the corresponding quarter of last year.

items.statement: Red rot disease in 238 variety managed through three-year transition to 118 variety; last year's impact exacerbated by El Nino heavy rainfall
items.quote: the thing about last year is you can largely view it as a black swan event because we also had the El Nino water effect on us, so the heavy rainfalls early in June and July further expedited the impact of red rot. So, we don't foresee it being that large of an issue this year and we see our seed transition happening quite seamlessly.

items.statement: Engineering division order book stood at INR 3,394 crores at end of Q1 FY25
items.quote: At the end of Q1 FY25, the total order book for the Engineering division stood at INR 3,394 crores.

items.statement: UP contract residual value of Rs. 813 crores planned for significant execution by end of current financial year
items.quote: Regarding the UP project, the current residual value is around Rs. 813 crores roughly which, as was mentioned earlier, we are planning to execute a significant part by the end of the current year.

items.statement: UP contract to be substantially executed by end of this year subject to fund releases and government approvals
items.quote: UP contract would get substantially executed by the end of this year. However, it is also a function of the funds which get released for the contract for completing the remaining portion and the second element is of course the approvals which we receive from the government, but we are very hopeful that by the end of this year, a substantial portion will get completed.

items.statement: Legacy project cost overrun impact to continue in next quarter and taper out thereafter, mostly completed by end of fourth quarter
items.quote: I would expect that the next quarter would continue to face this particular project's impact and only thereafter it will start to taper out. By the end of the fourth quarter, most of the contract will get fully executed.

items.statement: Chemical segment growth guidance of roughly 15% for FY25 with margins maintained if input prices, forex and supply dynamics remain stable
items.quote: We had indicated an overall growth of roughly 15% for the Chemical segment. If there is a change in it as the quarters progress, we will again advice on the call.

items.statement: Roha resin project at advanced stage, commercial start expected next financial year, 3-4 years to reach optimum capacity utilization
items.quote: The resin project is now at an advanced stage of execution at Roha, we are expecting the commercial start of that operation in the next financial year and it will take roughly 3-4 years for it to reach optimum capacity

items.statement: Engineering segment guided for 15-20% topline growth with margins moving towards FY23 levels, up from FY24
items.quote: For engineering segment also, the indication that we had given earlier during the current call is a 15% to 20% topline growth. We also have been indicating that we should be moving towards the margin levels achieved in the financial year 22-23 and therefore upwards from what we ended for 23-24.

items.statement: Roha investment of Rs. 400 crores includes Rs. 125 crores for new technology to improve profitability, targeting asset turnover over 2x on Rs. 275 crores
items.quote: Out of the Rs. 400 crores odd investment, roughly around Rs. 125 crores are targeted towards a specific technology intervention, which has other benefits beyond capacity augmentation and we expect an asset turnover of over 2 times should be calculated on the figure of 275 crores.

items.statement: Chemical plant utilization at 65-70% with headroom for growth before Roha capacity comes online
items.quote: That is roughly in the 65% to 70% range.

items.statement: Sri Lanka contract has 10-12% remaining unexecuted, can be completed within current financial year if fund flows materialize
items.quote: The remaining contract, which still remains to be invoiced is somewhere around 10%-12% and as soon as we get significant commitments or clarity on further fund flows, we should be able to close out the balance unexecuted portion at a very quick pace. This can easily happen within the current financial year.

items.statement: Engineering consolidated margins lower than standalone due to losses in engineering subsidiaries that typically improve in second half
items.quote: In terms of the engineering segment, the reduction in the margin from a standalone to the consolidated is largely on account of the losses which we have made in a couple of our engineering subsidiaries. Typically, these subsidiaries scale increases in the second-half of the year and their profitability should improve.

items.statement: Chemical segment margin improvement due to overseas subsidiary performance and full quarter consolidation of MAPRIL acquired June 2023
items.quote: As far as the chemical segment is concerned, is largely because of improvement in performance of some of our overseas subsidiaries as well as the consolidation of the subsidiary MAPRIL which was acquired in June of 23, in the last week of June 23, so in the current year we have consolidated 90 days, full quarter numbers while in the previous year it was only one-week number.

items.statement: MAPRIL expected to grow around 15% similar to standalone chemical segment
items.quote: You should see similar level of growth what we have seen in the standalone segment of the chemicals, around 15%.

items.statement: O&M services and spares contribute around 20% of engineering segment revenue
items.quote: Around 20% of our engineering segment revenue will come from the services and spares.

items.statement: Large international project opportunities under evaluation but not in enquiry bank due to uncertainty of conversion timing
items.quote: In the enquiry bank, there is nothing of that nature. But the opportunities exist and we are evaluating it, but they are not a part of the enquiry bank.

items.statement: Consumer division focused on scale growth over EBITDA positivity, reinvesting surpluses into team and infrastructure expansion
items.quote: The focus over the last few quarters, as we spoke little bit in more detail during the last concall, was to ensure that we achieve a much larger scale of operations. And therefore, without immediately focusing on achieving EBITDA positivity, the primary focus for the time being is to reinvest whatever surpluses are being generated by the business into further growth.

items.statement: Forex EBIT margin guided at 40-45% for full year
items.quote: We have guided the market to a 40% to 45% range, and I believe that's the range that we will operate for the full year.

items.statement: Travel EBIT margin medium-term target 4.5-5% over next 4-6 quarters
items.quote: Our medium-term estimate is that the margins will go up to close to 4.5% to 5%. We have expanded our margins in the current quarter by 40 basis points from 3.45% to 3.85%, and we believe that over the next 4 to 6 quarters, we should be moving to the 5% range that we have guided the market to.

items.statement: Forex revenue growth guided at 10-12% adjusted for one-time events
items.quote: From a revenue point of view, I'll still guide the market to a 10%- 12% growth on the forex revenue side. You have to adjust for onetime events that happen.

items.statement: Sterling EBITDA margin guided at 33-37% for full year despite expansion
items.quote: I we will still hold the EBITDA margins between 33% to 37% through the entire period, irrespective of these ramps that's happening, and that's a very, very healthy stable EBITDA.

items.statement: Group tax rate guided at about 30% for full year
items.quote: Yes. So I think going forward we can consider a tax rate of about 30% for the group.

items.statement: Sterling adding 20 resorts and 1,000 keys over next 12-18 months
items.quote: We have a total of 20 new resorts in the lineup to be added to our portfolio, which is currently at 50, and a growth of 40 over the next 12 to 18 months, or 1,000 keys.

items.statement: Sterling reached 50 resorts, added 9 in last 12 months, 5 in ramp phase
items.quote: With the addition of two resorts, one in Dehradun and the other in Udaipur during the quarter, I'm happy to inform you all that Sterling has now reached its first milestone of 50 resorts, hotels, and retreats in India.

items.statement: Forward bookings strong, short-haul/domestic trending double-digit growth, long-haul picking up for winter
items.quote: If I look at the forward bookings that we currently have, they look fairly strong. We had also mentioned in the previous call that the impact of elections will see a longish holiday /summer season, and we are witnessing that specifically in our short- haul or domestic volumes forward bookings, where they are actually trending double-digit growth. Long-haul is slightly picking up, but we believe th

items.statement: MICE forward bookings indicate close to double-digit growth
items.quote: MICE volumes, adjusted for the government business, grew about 20% Y -o-Y, reflecting the strong demand from the corporates for MICE events and indicating the corporates' appetite to spend. We managed large groups ranging from 300 to 2,500 people, and our forward bookings on this look very strong and indicate close to a double-digit growth at this point in time.

items.statement: India DMS order bookings good for upcoming season starting late October
items.quote: The upcoming seasons, which starts from late October and goes until the end of March or early April, has good order bookings for that period.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin stable at 7.6% despite headwinds
items.quote: Consequently, EBITDA m argins remained stable and resilient at 7.6% despite headwinds that we saw in some of the geographies that impacted certain segments of our businesses.

items.statement: Travel B2C gross margin improved 50 bps, EBIT margin expanded 40 bps to 3.85%
items.quote: Gross margins have improved, specifically on the B2C business, by about 50 basis points, largely contributed by the domestic and the short-haul segments. Consequently, EBIT margins improved by 40 basis points.

items.statement: Sterling EBITDA stable at 34%, impacted by new resort ramp-up and talent investment
items.quote: Our EBITDA stands stable and healthy at 34%. I will address two points which reflect the slight drop in EBITDA percentage values over the same time last year. First, we have five resorts, all in Udaipur, which opened in the last five months and are in the ramp phase.

items.statement: Sterling has 20 resorts in pipeline with 1,000 keys to launch progressively in next 12-15 months
items.quote: As mentioned, we have a strong pipeline of 20 resorts and over 1,000 keys to be launched progressively in the next 12 to 15 months.

items.statement: Input costs stabilized for land and airline, supporting volume growth
items.quote: It's important to highlight that input costs have stabilized, whether it is land or airline. Despite that, our volumes have grown.

items.statement: International volume share increased to 52% from 45%, domestic 40%, non-air 8%
items.quote: As mentioned in our previous earnings call, the shift to international is visible. In the current quarter, the international volume was close to 52%, which moved up from about 45%. Domestic continues to be about 40%, and non-air contributes 8% of our volumes.

items.statement: DEI renewed 91% of portfolio under renewal (70% of total portfolio)
items.quote: Also, it's also been a very, very unique year, as I mentioned before, because this is a year when more than 70% of our total portfolio is under renewal and the good news is more than 91% of that has been renewed.

items.statement: DEI signed 13 new partnerships worth ~INR 35 cr in Q1
items.quote: We've had new businesses nearly about 13 -odd partnerships signed for this -- in this quarter alone, which tantamount to about roughly about INR35 crores of new business.

items.statement: Sterling 19 resorts ranked #1 on TripAdvisor, 65% in top 5, 42 of 50 rated 4.5+
items.quote: 19 of our resorts are ranked number 1 in their respective locations on TripAdvisor, and 65% of our resorts are in the top 5. 42 out of our 50 resorts are ranked 4.5 and above out of 5 on TripAdvisor.

items.statement: Budget announcement allowing TCS with TDS expected to boost consumer discretionary spending
items.quote: I would like to mention the recent announcement in the budget that allows the setup of TCS with TDS. We believe that this will leave a little more cash in the hands of the holidaymaker and should allow or help consumer discretionary categories like ours, where customers will have more money in their hands to spend.

items.statement: Sterling remains debt-free with cash reserve of INR 2,000 million
items.quote: We continue to remain debt-free with a healthy cash reserve of about INR 2,000 million.

items.statement: Sterling investing in leadership and manpower in advance for 20 resort expansion
items.quote: Second, with the expansion of almost 20 resorts and 1,000 keys, it was necessary to start investing in leadership and manpower in advance, which is what has happened in Q1 of this financial year.

items.statement: Provision of USD 0.5 million (INR 5 cr) for doubtful debt due to FTI bankruptcy
items.quote: In this quarter, we have to take a provision for a doubtful debt of close to about USD 0.5 million between entities in East Africa and in Asian Trails. This was necessitated by the sudden declaration of bankruptcy by a large European travel unit called FTI which happened to be one of our customers.

items.statement: Forex card loads grew 13% YoY, incremental float generation INR 210 cr
items.quote: Card loads increased by 13% year-on-year, and the incremental float generation was INR 210 crores.

items.statement: Sterling occupancy stable at 69%, ARR stable at INR 7,100, available room nights up 9%
items.quote: With that, our available room nights actually increased by 9%. The occupancy was stable at 69%, mainly due to the fact that we have five or six resorts currently in the ramp phase. We had an average room rate (ARR) stable at INR 7,100 during the quarter.

items.statement: Sterling non-member room nights grew 12%, F&B grew 6-7%
items.quote: However, the growth in non -member room nights by 12% over last year, coupled with the growth in F&B of about 6% to 7%, resulted in an overall revenue growth of 9% to 10%.

items.statement: Sterling EBITDA margin to be held between 33% and 37% during investment year
items.quote: I'm considering this year as an investment year, but I we will still hold the EBITDA margins between 33% to 37% through the entire period, irrespective of these ramps that's happening, and that's a very, very healthy stable EBITDA.

items.statement: Group tax rate guided at about 30% going forward
items.quote: So I think going forward we can consider a tax rate of about 30% for the group.

items.statement: Outbound travel value targeting close to FY20 level of INR2,400 crores
items.quote: We are quite optimistic that we should be very close to the 2020 numbers.

items.statement: Domestic leisure business expected to sustain double-digit growth
items.quote: We believe the double-digit growth on this business is here to stay.

items.statement: Sterling expansion using asset-right, low or no capex model via management contracts and revenue share
items.quote: The focus of expansion has always been using an asset-right model. And no capex model or a low capex model.

items.statement: Sterling portfolio expanded to over 2,700 keys across 50 resorts in 45 destinations
items.quote: Now today, after all the expansion that we've done 8 or 9 resort, we are currently above 2,700 keys.

items.statement: MICE business pushed to Q3 but new MICE business expected in Q2-Q4, overall quantum to grow
items.quote: They do come back in Q3, they will come back in Q3. But having said that, in Q2, Q3, and Q4, we would even generate new MICE business. So that component overall, from your perspective, should not get impacted. In fact, we see expanded inventory, it could infact grow.

items.statement: Short-haul international holiday portfolio growing at 30% with better margins
items.quote: We are actually seeing the short-haul. That also sits on the international holiday side a bit. That portfolio is growing at 30%.

items.statement: Forex margins volatile due to retail vs wholesale mix shift in peak season
items.quote: When you are in a peak travel season, your retail volumes will actually go up and your wholesale volumes will come down. And when your retail actually goes up, the margins on the retail are higher as compared to margins on the wholesale, typically the wholesale margins are 1/3 of what we do on the retail side.

items.statement: International holiday gross margins operate at 14-16% range for both long-haul and short-haul
items.quote: Both of them run at a gross margin range between 14% to 16%.

items.statement: Sterling room revenue drives GOP; F&B net margins 20-25% after indirect costs
items.quote: In terms of food and beverage, they are actually the typical direct gross margins should be about 60%, but if you have to take the direct or the indirect cost to it like salary wages, heat light power etc it would be in the range of 20% to 25% in terms of margins.

items.statement: Shift toward short-haul and domestic holidays; long-haul volume recovery still subpar vs 2020
items.quote: The recovery on short- haul or the growth on short- haul will be much faster, much bigger as compared to long -haul. It's also important to highlight here that when yo u look at input costs between 2020 and 2025, they are very different, input costs have gone up

items.statement: Focus on catching domestic customers young to build repeat lifecycle toward short-haul and long-haul
items.quote: The more customers who come into the domestic are the ones who will stay with us for a longer period in time. The long-hauls are more mature customers who have done maybe two domestic trip with us, one or two short-hauls and then that's how they go to long-haul.

items.statement: RBI discussion paper on money changer consolidation still work in progress; no concrete policy decision
items.quote: Nothing, Himanshu. We haven't heard anything back from the regulator. I think it's still work in progress. We believe from some of the other circulars that have come out, I think there is a method in the madness I would say, but very difficult to call out at this point as to how the regulator is thinking about it.

items.statement: No active capital allocation plans; holding INR250-300 crores free cash on balance sheet
items.quote: Currently, we are focused on keeping the cash on the balance sheet. Business is coming back stabilizing. We've been saving in last 4 or 5 quarters of good profitability and we continue to build on it. At this point in time, there are no active conversations, no plans on any capital allocation at this point in time.

items.statement: Business highly seasonal; one quarter does not make or break the year
items.quote: As you know our business is highly seasonal and we have always mentioned that, that one quarter doesn't make or break the business.

items.statement: Geopolitical and economic unpredictability; geographical diversity acts as hedge
items.quote: You'll appreciate that we live in a highly unpredictable world where geopolitics and economics seem to be mixing at a much higher rate and therefore we need to be protective against that.

items.statement: Capital Markets Day scheduled for August 23 at Jio Convention Center
items.quote: Just as a last point we are hosting a Capital Markets Day on August 23 at the Jio Convention Center.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 sales growth guidance of double-digit over FY24, targeting 2x GDP growth (13-14%)
items.quote: we continue to maintain the guidance of our ambition to grow at a minimum of 2x of the GDP, which in this year at a 6.5 to 7 is somewhere between 13 % to 14% is what we think we should be able to grow.

items.statement: Domestic demand remains strong across infrastructure, data centers, real estate, and manufacturing despite CPCB-IV price increases
items.quote: the demand is not dropping, the demand is strong and overall, since the infrastructure of the country is growing, the power demand in the country is growing, the affluence of the country is growing, everybody wants more power and so demand continues to remain strong despite price increases.

items.statement: Gross margin at record 37.8% driven by pricing, CPCB-IV mix, commodity tailwinds, and cost reduction; not sustainable indefinitely
items.quote: I think we have had for the last few quarters almost a perfect storm of capitalizing on the pricing increases that we have done. The mix of course with CPCB-IV+, and the fact that commodities have helped us, and we have been able to continue the cost reduction game.

items.statement: Order books are strong with zero channel inventory for CPCB-II; CPCB-IV ramping up strongly
items.quote: the order books are scaling up and order books are pretty strong. So, we are tending to align to the hypothesis that the demand is now agnostic of the price increase that the CPCB-IV calls for.

items.statement: CPCB-IV+ pricing 15-25% higher than CPCB-II; copper and aluminum costs rising offsetting iron/steel softness
items.quote: It's anywhere in the range between 15% to 25% is what the pricing increases have been.

items.statement: CPCB-IV+ contributed 30-40% of Power Gen sales in Q1; LHP/MHP/Heavy Duty expected to be ~90% CPCB-IV+ going forward
items.quote: Close to 5000 sets were sold during the last two quarters. So, roughly I would say that somewhere about 30%-40% of the sales in the quarter were with CPCB-IV.

items.statement: Power Gen user industries: data centers, manufacturing, infrastructure, commercial realty; residential real estate picking up
items.quote: So, I would say it's a data center, manufacturing, infrastructure and commercial realty.

items.statement: Competition launching CPCB-IV+ nodes; some price readjustment expected in specific nodes but overall pricing structure expected to hold
items.quote: Certainly, always once you start to see what competition is pricing at, we will need to take some adjustment actions based on our own , we command a certain premium as compared to competition based on the product quality and the robustness and the features that we offer to our customers.

items.statement: Exports grew 13% QoQ driven by Middle East and Africa recovery; Europe flat; global inventory well-stocked, demand-constrained
items.quote: exports did grow in this quarter, and we are mainly seeing that increase come from two areas, Middle East has recovered quite well, and Africa is starting to recover.

items.statement: Heavy data center gensets supply-chain constrained (global allocation); India-made products have sufficient capacity with minor spikes
items.quote: the heavy data center applications are fully booked and are completely supply chain capacity constrained, which means that the very largest of sets which are made by Cummins Inc. globally and are not made in India, we are pretty much on allocation basis.

items.statement: Data centers contribute ~10% of Power Generation business globally and in India; heavy data center order books strong
items.quote: data centers contribute to roughly around 10% of Cummins' power generation business. And that similar kind of trend holds true in India as well.

items.statement: Ashwath Ram stepping down as MD; transition to Shweta Srivastava; strong team built for sustainable strategy execution
items.quote: I feel very good about having had enough time to work with the team, come up with a strategy, be able to execute it and then transition it into a mode which can be sustainable in the future.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic short-term due to transition turbulence, geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain challenges, and commodity volatility
items.quote: We remain cautiously optimistic about the short -term, but quite optimistic about medium and long -term outlook.

items.statement: CPCB-IV transition complete; channel inventory zero; only CPCB-IV sales from current quarter
items.quote: So, the channel inventory is zero. So, that which is what accounts for as we were draining the inventory throughout the previous quarter. So, the transition has happened, and we ended up with depleting all the inventory.

items.statement: R&D peak spending done; only sustenance and improvement expenditure going forward
items.quote: We are done with the peak R&D expenditure, so now it's only going to be sustenance and improvement kind of expenditure as far as that is concerned.

items.statement: Overall stock inventory at OEMs and dealers amongst lowest in couple of years; will rebuild over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: the overall stock inventory at all our OEMs and dealers is also pretty low, amongst the lowest it's been in a couple of years.

items.statement: FMCG industry value and volume growth at ~6.5-6.6%; rural growth recovering, aided by better monsoons, moderate inflation, and high rural employment.
items.quote: Good news on the consumption front. The quarter has been -- the growths on value and volume have been about the same at about 6.6%, 6.5% for the FMCG industry. The rural growths are starting to come back, which has -- which have been lagging urban for some time.

items.statement: Targets 2% cost efficiencies annually; manufacturing cost base to be 8x FY14 level in FY25.
items.quote: And in '24 -'25, we will be at 8 t imes what we started in '13-'14. So this continues. We continue to target 2% of cost efficiencies every year

items.statement: Operating margin at 16.5% in Q1 FY25; management prioritizes top-line growth over margin expansion, willing to accept 16% margin to drive volume.
items.quote: I think it's the time to drive top line right now. We, as a FMCG industry in India, have suffered the top line growths that are required. And I would not mind if my margin stays at 16% rather than going to 18%.

items.statement: Commodity costs rising marginally: flour, sugar, cocoa up; palm, laminates, corrugated boxes balancing; milk costs up, SMP to rise. Expect 4-5% inflation, may take selective price increases.
items.quote: Commodity costs are going up marginally. Flour costs are up. Sugar costs are up. Palm is the balancing factor. Cocoa is through the roof. The cocoa costs are completely through the roof. Laminate cos ts -- so the two -- three costs which are balancing out flour, sugar and cocoa are palm, laminates and corrugated boxes

items.statement: Price rollbacks largely done; slight difference between volume and revenue growth may persist due to base effects but will even out.
items.quote: We've do ne what we had to. There might be a few promotions here and there, but as far as rollbacks are concerned, we've done what we have to. As we were saying, we expect 4% to 5% inflation in the coming months on the back of flour and sugar and cocoa. So -- and if that happens, we will start to take slight price increases in the future

items.statement: Direct reach at 28.2 lakh outlets; rural distributors increased to 30,000; rural performance better than urban.
items.quote: our direct reach is now at 28.2 lakh outlets. Our uptick in rural distribution, we've gone up to 30,000 rural distributors. And if you look at our rural performance, it's a better performance than what it is for ur ban, which is

items.statement: Manufacturing footprint: 54 factories (16 own, 38 third-party), 154 lines (81 own); Ranjangaon dairy collecting 300,000 liters milk, 90,000 liters from 3,300 partner farmers; processed cheese plant commercialized.
items.quote: We've got a mega food factory which is in Ranjangaon. We've got fully integrated factories in -- which have got four plus lines and have more than one category. And then we've got small factories which give us the ability to be nimble. So we've got a very robust and a very solid manufacturing footprint which is holding us in good stead in the current times.

items.statement: Adjacency business resurgent: Fudge It, Croissants, Rusk, Millet Breads, Cheese, Drinks (Lassi) performing well; targeting 1.5x base business growth.
items.quote: We have seen a resurgence in our adjacency business. The Fudge It product has been doing extremely well. Croissants have been doing very well. Our Rusk and Millet Breads have also done well for us. Similarly on cheese and on dri nks, drinks has been a good story for us, especially Lassi

items.statement: E-commerce at ~4% of sales, purely B2C; used as innovation test bed with precision targeting.
items.quote: We've been seeing great growths in this channel. So, hopefully, it's -- today at -- Vipin, at about what, 4% of our total sales? Vipin Kataria: Yes, Varun, so we are at about 4%.

items.statement: Weighted distribution: urban ~95%, overall ~90%; focus on extraction from high-potential outlets via Bain project; rural width expansion continues in focus markets.
items.quote: In our urban markets, our weighted distribution is almost 95%. So we reach all close to 95% of the weighted outlets. At an overall company level, we are at about 90% weighted distribution.

items.statement: Cheese market share in low double-digits (~10-12%); Amul 6x larger; aim to improve via Bel tie-up, own factory efficiencies, innovation over next 3-6 months.
items.quote: The market share on cheese, we are very small, Abneesh. We -- it's predominantly -- we are number two in the industry, but we are in -- just in about double-digit numbers while -- so there's a lot of bunching at the bottom with low 2%, 3% share. So a lot of players are at 2%, 3% share. We are just about in double digits. And Amul is 6 times of our share.

items.statement: Ranjangaon factory qualified as ultra mega plant; PLI benefits accruing from April 2024; UP and Bihar units also starting to receive incentives.
items.quote: Ranjangaon facility will start being counted as an ultra mega facility starting April this year. So which means the incentive that we will be eligible for will be higher. And also the units in UP and Bihar will start getting the benefits.

items.statement: Adjacency margins: Cake and Rusk double-digit; Bread near double-digit; Croissant gross margins ~25% above base but investing; Dairy in investment mode with depreciation drag.
items.quote: Cake and Rusk are in the double -digit te rritory. Rusk would probably be accretive to our overall margins. And bread, as you know, we used to be negative margins. We brought it to a stage where they are almost touching a double-digit margin. So that's a great achievement in a category like bread. And croissant, the gross margins are fantastic. We continue to invest the gross margins. The y are pr

items.statement: Dairy business run rate >INR700 cr; Cheese ~INR250 cr; Drinks ~INR220 cr; Cheese+Drinks ~INR460-470 cr.
items.quote: So our total business -- dairy business would be over INR700 crores, out of which cheese and dairy put together would be about INR460 crores, INR470 crores.

items.statement: Salty snack (Time Pass) still in experimental stage after 5+ years; testing market viability, internal capability for impulse category, and profitability given fragmented unorganized competition.
