items.statement: Lead times for new deals longer than expected due to pricing complexity; revenue growth slower than anticipated
items.quote: So it's slower than what we had expected, that which we can certainly say. The exact reasons, maybe we'll come back to you next quarter.

items.statement: Added 62 employees this quarter; wage hikes above industry average to retain and attract talent
items.quote: Yes, we have added 62 Nucleics to our team and talking about growth in Southeast Asia, Australia, etcetera, yes our conversations with the customers in those geographies, they are continuing and we are quite confident that the growth will start happening in coming quarters.

items.statement: Building Islamic banking version of FinnOne Neo for Middle East and Malaysia markets
items.quote: So look, we essentially work on these 3 product suites, which are FinnOne Neo, the FinnAxia and Payse, which we also talk about. We keep enhancing them, so the latest enhancement is in FinnOne Neo, we are now building the Islamic version, which is used in the Middle East, Malaysia etcetera. So that's a significant functionality enhancement that we are doing.

items.statement: Plans to onboard senior sales leaders in different regions; CFO and CHRO joined last quarter
items.quote: Sales senior leadership yes, definitely that is our plan. You would be aware that just last quarter, we both our CFO and CHRO have joined. So that way the management team is strong and yes sales side we definitely plan to onboard our leaders in different regions.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 180 crore investment to set up alkaline battery plant with 360 million units capacity
items.quote: the Board of the company has approved an investment of Rs. 180 crore to set up an alkaline plant with a capacity of 360 million units.

items.statement: Expect mid-single-digit growth in battery segment
items.quote: I would say that the battery overall, our outlook is really, mid-single-digit growth.

items.statement: Target double-digit growth in flashlight segment
items.quote: I would say, certainly, beyond 10% to 15% is what we are looking at, at this point of time.

items.statement: Lighting segment to reach breakeven this year, mid to high single-digit EBITDA margin in 2-3 years
items.quote: this year, our effort has to be at least we cross breakeven level. And the next that mid to high level of I think it's a 2- to 3-year journey from there.

items.statement: Alkaline plant expected to commission within a year, internal target August 2025
items.quote: So, 1 year from now, but the internal target is to try to do it faster. So, let us say, we are on 5th of August, we could talk of a 1st of August kind of date.

items.statement: Alkaline plant funding mostly through borrowed funds with some internal accruals
items.quote: we will get something borrowed outside because there could be some interest benefit on that. So, that will be looking, but yes, partially it will be given internally, but most of that will be a borrowed fund.

items.statement: Alkaline battery market growing at around 20% annually
items.quote: It is already growing at double-digit. It is growing at around 20% odd. And we expect that trend to continue for, I mean, in the foreseeable future at least.

items.statement: Rural demand recovery expected with normal monsoon boosting flashlight sales
items.quote: Given the prediction for a normal monsoon, a rebound in agriculture is expected, which will strengthen the rural economy, rural spending recovery. This will provide a much-needed relief to the flashlights market.

items.statement: Alkaline battery revenue grew 67% in Q1 FY25 on small base
items.quote: Though of a small base, on the back of a 52% growth last year, we realized a 67% increase in value terms during the quarter.

items.statement: Rechargeable flashlights now 35% of flashlight portfolio, battery-operated at two-thirds
items.quote: Battery operated is still two-thirds. Rechargeable, which is the one that we started practically from last year, has now come up to 35%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA and PAT increased 14.2% and 18.5% respectively due to cost initiatives and favorable input costs
items.quote: For the quarter, both increased by 14.2% and 18.5%, respectively. These came as a result of cost initiatives and favorable input costs.

items.statement: Lighting segment turned positive EBITDA at 3.1% in Q1 FY25 vs break-even last year
items.quote: the business turned with a positive EBITDA at 3.1% vis-à-vis the break-even situation last year.

items.statement: RTM implementation challenges mostly resolved, full benefits expected from H2 FY25
items.quote: Most of those challenges are behind us. Some still remain, which we are working upon. And I think the full benefit of the RTM and, let us say, no challenge kind of operation would certainly happen from the second half of this year.

items.statement: Alternative channels (modern retail, e-commerce, quick commerce, institutional) at 15% of revenue, targeting 16%+ by year-end
items.quote: currently we are at about 15% of the alternative channels that I mentioned, and I think obviously it is our day-to-day endeavor to go higher than that and maybe by the end of the year, we would try to go beyond 16% at least, if not more.

items.statement: Credit growth guided at 13-14% and deposit growth at 11-12% for FY25
items.quote: As far as our guidance is concerned, in line with the growth of the economy, the credit will be growing at around 13 % to 14% and deposit growth we will be around 11 % to 12% for FY 25.

items.statement: NIM guidance for March 2025 set at 2.90% due to rising deposit costs
items.quote: On the guidance side, what we are saying for March 2025, NIM, we are seeing a guidance of 2.90%, considering the fact that the cost of deposit is going up and the Yield on Advances is not coming to that extent.

items.statement: Yield on Advances guidance for FY25 at around 8.50%
items.quote: As regards the Yield on Advances is concerned, there also, presently we are at 8.60%, and we feel that at around 8.50% plus, the guidance will be there as far as that is also concerned.

items.statement: Net Interest Income growth guidance for FY25 at 13%
items.quote: Net Interest Income growth has been at around 13% in FY24. And on the guidance side, we say that the Net Interest Income guidance will again be at 13% for FY25.

items.statement: LCR guidelines may reduce LCR by 10-15% and pressure margins
items.quote: The ballpark calculation that we have done on these numbers, and what the industry has also done is that the LCR may come down by between 10 % to 15%.

items.statement: DCCO circular impact on CET-1 around 10-15 bps and credit cost around 15 bps
items.quote: On the C ET-1 side, the impact will be at around 10 to 15 basis points, because overall the guideline is such that it will not impact the CRAR. So CET-1 impact will be around 10 to 15 bps. And on the credit cost side, it will be also at around 15 basis point.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY25 at 0.70%
items.quote: On the guidance side, we would say that the Credit Cost would be at 0.70% for the current financial year.

items.statement: Slippage ratio guidance for FY25 at around 1.20%
items.quote: We are confident that we will be able to keep the slippage ratio at around 1.20 % only during the current financial year.

items.statement: Gross NPA guidance for March 2025 at around 4% and Net NPA at around 0.90%
items.quote: As regards the guidance is concerned for FY25, we are saying that we will be at around 4% by March'25 on the Gross NPA numbers. On the Net NPA, we were at 1.22 % in March '24. We have now closed at 0.99 %. On the guidance side, we are saying that we will be at around 0.90% by March'25.

items.statement: ROA guidance for FY25 at 0.80%
items.quote: For the guidance we are giving at 0.80% for FY25, for the entire financial year, for FY25 0.80%.

items.statement: Targeting at least 5% recovery from written-off accounts (~Rs.2,000 crore) in FY25
items.quote: We are targeting at least 5% recovery from written off account during this financial year. That is the internal target we have kept for the field. So our Rs.40,000 crores is 5%. We will be getting at least Rs.2,000 crore.

items.statement: Expecting large ticket NPA recovery of around Rs.500 crore in Q2 FY25
items.quote: We are expecting a good recovery in the big ticket size of around Rs. 500 Crores, if I give a ballpark number in this quarter itself on the large ticket NPA accounts.

items.statement: IT and digital budget for FY25 around Rs.2,000 crore; onboarding Big 4 consultant by end of Q2
items.quote: On the expenditure side, as far as the digital and IT is concerned this year also the budget is around Rs. 2,000 Crores and we expect that good amount of money will be spent both on the digital and the IT side for this year also.

items.statement: Plan to raise Rs.5,000 crore capital via Tier-I and Tier-II bonds in FY25 to absorb ECL provisioning
items.quote: Also, we have a plan to raise around Rs.5,000 Crores in capital in the form of Tier-I and Tier-II. Tier-II, we will be raising in this current quarter and Tier-I, maybe in the quarter three or quarter four.

items.statement: ECL provisioning impact to be spread over 5 years; manageable with profitability and capital raise
items.quote: We are expecting when the guidelines come, it will be spread across the five year period, and once it is spread across the five year period, we have sufficient cushion with respect to the profitability, which we will be achieving and improvement in the CRAR, which will happen.

items.statement: Management remains positive on FY25 growth but refuses to give hard revenue or PAT margin numbers
items.quote: We would want to refrain from giving any hard numbers per se, Aman, but we continue to remain hopeful.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin is 25% but varies by contract mix; hardware lowers margins, pure software/transaction raises them
items.quote: Typically, we target to have a 25% EBITDA.

items.statement: Order book is healthy and looking up but exact numbers not disclosed due to various stages
items.quote: Order book is looking healthy. Can't comment on exact numbers at this point because they're all at various stages. But it's looking up.

items.statement: Green shoots from Project Butterfly contributed close to 30% of Q1 FY25 revenue
items.quote: we have seen very healthy growth in our green shoots, which has contributed close to 30% of our QI number.

items.statement: Steady revenue growth expected over next three quarters without lumpiness; spillover from milestone-based contracts will continue
items.quote: we're looking at a steady revenues going forward as much I can tell you

items.statement: Investing cash reserves in sales capabilities internationally and domestically; sent senior presales resource to U.S.
items.quote: we are deploying our cash reserves to strengthen our sales capabilities. We have also sent a senior presales turned sales resource from India to the U.S.

items.statement: Renewed large PSU managed services deal at better price; customer onboarding component renewed at significantly improved pricing for 7 years
items.quote: we were able to renew one of our large managed services deal with the PSU at a better price.

items.statement: Government payments typically delayed 90+ days but do not default; DSO range-bound at ~150 days, no election-related sluggishness
items.quote: our DSO is range bound. It's about 150 days -- quite in the same range of what we had in Q4. We haven't seen any sluggishness due to elections or anything as additional factors impacting our payments.

items.statement: Closed two small logos in Americas (Central America and U.S.), one direct and one via individual contractor; investing in U.S. partnerships and rainmakers
items.quote: this quarter, we closed 2 small logos in the Americas, one in Central America and one in the United States.

items.statement: Named in Gartner and Omdia reports for communications space, validating technology differentiation
items.quote: two very, popular analysts like Gartner, one of them is Omdia Both are very established analysts, reputed analysts in the U.S. region. And we have been named in both of their reports to look forward to in the communications space.

items.statement: Transmission services deal closed; now handling last-mile SMS/email delivery in-house to capture additional revenue
items.quote: We also closed the transmission services deal. It was a green shoot that we had been trying to focus on so that we can make our communication value proposition more sticky with our customers, and we have been able to close the deal in that direction as well.

items.statement: Government managed services contract won for 7 years, transaction-based; focusing on urban local bodies modernization and smart city surveillance/ERP projects
items.quote: The new contract which is from a PSU is for 7 years. It's a transaction-based contract and it is there, and I wouldn't want to comment beyond that.

items.statement: AI used to suppress redundant customer communications saving one client INR100 crores/year; AI auto-designs complex statements and rewrites test cases improving implementation efficiency
items.quote: in fact, one of our customers have saved almost INR100 crores in their communication spend in a year.

items.statement: Headcount ~535; attrition below industry; hiring only in sales; using AI to rightsize teams and improve delivery efficiency
items.quote: There are about 535 people, as we speak. Attrition rates are not too bad at industry level, I would say or below. And in terms of hiring, we continue to hire in sales.

items.statement: Two current engagements via system integrators; rest direct; bidding directly where qualified, partnering where size requires
items.quote: Currently, we have two engagements which are through system integrators and among all our customers. The rest of them, we are directly servicing.

items.statement: BSNL remains a good customer; government invested heavily; payments delayed but not defaulted
items.quote: So, they're a good customer. In fact the government invested very heavily in them.

items.statement: Aiming for 30%+ gross margin and 10%+ EBITDA margin by FY26-27
items.quote: We are looking at getting us to the 30-plus percent gross margin and 10-plus percent EBITDA. And we strongly believe that we should achieve this by '26, '27.

items.statement: Targeting 60-40 KEA to SME/retail mix by end of FY25
items.quote: So we would be looking at ending the year with a mix of about 60-40.

items.statement: Contract Logistics business expected to grow at 30% CAGR over next 3 years
items.quote: we are looking at this bu siness growing at a CAGR of 30% in the next 3 years because the opportunity that is available in the market is huge

items.statement: Gross margin improved 100 bps QoQ to 27% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Corresponding gross margin has improved by 100 basis points and stands at 27 percentage for Q1 FY'25 as compared to 26 percentage for the quarter ended March 2024.

items.statement: Express EBITDA grew 33% QoQ to INR20 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for the Express business stood at INR20 crores in Q1 FY'25 as against INR15 crores in Q4 FY'24, representing a growth of 33 percentage.

items.statement: Targeting INR0.10 per kg yield increase annually through mix shift
items.quote: We are hovering at an overall yield of about INR11.8. So we look to increasing it by INR0.10 paisa for the next two years by changing the mix.

items.statement: Allocated INR30 crore for technology and INR40 crore for infrastructure over next two years
items.quote: We have set aside very clearly when we did our QIP also INR30 crores for technology and another INR40 crores for infrastructure, which means the size of the new hubs that we lease out as we move forward.

items.statement: QIP of INR169 crore completed; net cash positive INR196 crore as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: As on June 30, 2024, the company is debt-free with a net cash positive of INR196 crores after a successful QIP of INR169 crores.

items.statement: Merger with Contract Logistics expected by Q1 FY26 latest
items.quote: We believe that the latest by first quarter of next year, we should get the merger done.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 expected to be strong due to pre-festive inventory build-up
items.quote: This quarter, July, August, September, as you know, is supposed to be the -- one of the largest quarters for the pre-festivities inventory. And therefore, we should see a very good second quarter.

items.statement: Current KEA/SME/retail mix at 63/19/18; wallet share with large customers ~30%
items.quote: Plan mix for the quarter ended June 2024 for KEA, SME and retail stood at 63 percentage, 19 percentage and 18 percentage, respectively.

items.statement: Launched first module of GATE technology for associate tracking
items.quote: We have launched the first module of our new technology. We have named it GATE, Gati Associate Tracking Engine.

items.statement: Infrastructure modernization Phase 1 implemented; Ahmedabad, Kolkata, Pune hubs starting this quarter
items.quote: We now have Ahmedabad, Kolkata and Pune, which we will start from this quarter.

items.statement: Legacy issues 99% resolved; ECLM provisions reduced over last 4 quarters
items.quote: So I can only say that 99%, it is over. I cannot say 100%. But yes, old legacies are over. You've seen the ECLM provisions reduced in the last 4 quarters from what it was 4 quarters back.

items.statement: Maintain sales growth guidance of 10% plus with EBITDA margins between 12% to 14%
items.quote: We continue to maintain our guideline of sales growth of 10% plus, with EBITDA margins between 12% to 14%.

items.statement: Expect 40% plus value growth with some improvements in EBITDA for MDF segment
items.quote: Going forward, we expect 40% plus value growth with some improvements in EBITDA license.

items.statement: Standalone MDF EBITDA margin guidance of 15% for FY25, consolidated may be slightly lower due to Andhra ramp-up
items.quote: On a standalone basis, we are confident of this 15%. For Andhra you're right, it will take some time to ramp up, but we are confident that by Q4, even the Andhra capacity or even the consolidated margin, will be at 15% plus.

items.statement: Plywood volume growth guidance of 10%, may revise if Q2 performs similarly
items.quote: Yes. But I maintain that we should have about 10%, maybe 11%, maybe 12% of the value growth. For the moment, yes, we have higher growth. And if the Q2 also goes accordingly higher and we may revise our guidance for the whole year.

items.statement: MDF Andhra capex increased to INR730 crores from INR700 crores due to cost escalation, not capacity addition
items.quote: Costs have been shooting up. And I think there are certain elements that we had expected to be completed at lower cost for instance, roads in media, et cetera, have cost, slightly higher than what we had thought.

items.statement: Particle board new facility with continuous process expected to start by end of FY25
items.quote: This new facility is expected to start by end of this financial year.

items.statement: PBC board facility at Andhra started production in May 2024, expected to add almost INR100 crores revenue by next year
items.quote: This facility is also ramping very fast and will add to almost INR100 crores revenue by next year.

items.statement: No substantial capex planned for next 1-1.5 years after particle board commissioning, sharp deleveraging expected
items.quote: At this point in time, yes. Because currently, we don't have any closing capex. And I think considering the current scenario, and we have already taken on large capex. We are not going to go for any substantial capex for the next year, 1.5 year after So they'll be sharp deleveraging effect taking place.

items.statement: MDF margins expected to bottom out, improvement driven by capacity utilization and value-added products
items.quote: If you look at our -- if you look at our standalone numbers, so we had about 14% margin. And I think that, yes, this would be the bottom because going forward, we are going to attempt to increase value -added products, we are going to attempt to increase ca pacity utilization

items.statement: Plywood EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 12-14% despite 4% price hikes (2% in June, 2% in August) as raw material costs also increased
items.quote: we increased 2% from 1st of May, and we have increased 2% from 1st of August. We have increased 2% from 1st of June and 2% from 1st of August. The 4% price has been taken across in all of our plywood products. But the cost of raw material has gone up. On the region for a higher EBITDA can be higher quantity of sales or growth in the growth is higher than a title bit of EBITDA will be higher. But t

items.statement: Plywood price hikes of 2% each in June and August 2024 (total 4%), laminate price hike of ~3% on August 1, 2024
items.quote: We have already taken a price hike as on the 1st of August. And this is close to a 3% price, this is due to raw material cost.

items.statement: Plywood demand strong across Tier 2/3 cities and metros, Eastern and Southern India performing very well
items.quote: Actually, the market for plywood and especially for Century Ply, we have gone down to below even 75,000 tons we have gone now. So we are seeing pull from everywhere. This time for the whole of first quarter for the month of July.

items.statement: MDF value-added products (pre-laminated) to increase from zero in Q1, improving realization and margins
items.quote: in MDF currently, while there is no clear visibility of price hike, but considering the state of margin across the industry I think it is only logical that prices should start to increase. However, as of now, we don't have any price rise in if there i s a development, then if there's an opportunity we will definitely take on. But having said that, value-added products are going to increase perhaps

items.statement: Timber costs increased 5-7% sequentially in North (INR6.5-7/kg) and South (INR5.5/kg), may increase further in next 2 quarters due to plantation cycle
items.quote: As compared to last quarter, it has increased marginally in the range of 5% to 7% for the rest of the year, while we hope it remains steady, but given the plantation cycle, it's hard to pay there to fall business, it might mainly still increase in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: MDF imports down ~50% to 15,000-16,000 CBM/month due to freight crisis, but trend may reverse as freight normalizes
items.quote: If I look at the last 3 months data, I would believe it's about in the range of 15,000 to 16,000 CBM. So it's come down by about 50%. But as the freight crisis emerges, we see that the trend goes upwards or downwards but it's come down in the short term on account of freight.

items.statement: Singapore subsidiary sale completed April 2024, INR13.33 crores exceptional item from derecognition of assets/liabilities
items.quote: The resulting difference amounting to INR13.33 crores is shown as exceptional item in consolidated profit and loss account in compliance to accounting standards.

items.statement: Digital revenue target of 25% of radio revenues achieved in Q1 FY25
items.quote: You would recall that we had guided earlier that our aspiration and ambition is to get 25% of revenues from the digital segment.

items.statement: INR15 crores invested in Gaana platform in Q1 FY25, expected to decrease in subsequent quarters
items.quote: We have made investments on this new platform, which is close to INR15 crores this quarter. However, the key takeaway is that this is expected to come down in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Radio EBITDA margin at 21.8% excluding digital in Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for the year, excluding digital, stood at INR20.5 crores as compared to INR19.2 crores in Q1 FY '24. EBITDA margins were at 21.8%.

items.statement: Radio pricing increased ~5.8% YoY in Q1 FY25 due to political business, prices stabilized
items.quote: There was some bit of price increase, about 5.8% of price increase. But I would not read much, it's one time because of the political event. Good part to say on the pricing, it has stabilized, and we don't see any further drop.

items.statement: Gaana subscription price doubled to INR599 from July 1, blended price impact gradual as existing users renew
items.quote: Our pricing earlier used to be INR299, which was not feasible. But recently, you would have seen from 1st July, we have increased the price to INR599.

items.statement: H2 FY25 pricing optimism, potential price increases from September, no price declines expected
items.quote: Generally, media, not just radio, any media, the price is based on supply demand in the H2, we believe, starting September could have a chance where we could look at certain price increases as the business comes back and the media is always skewed towards H2.

items.statement: Cash balance INR355 crores as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains robust with a cash balance of INR355 crores as of June 30, 2024.

items.statement: Inventory utilization at 72% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The inventory utilization for this quarter is about 72%.

items.statement: Multimedia solutions grew 10%, activations grew 42%, original content pushed to next quarter for margin discipline
items.quote: Otherwise, other business of multimedia solutions has grown 10%, activation has grown by about 42%. Just as I said, this is the one business where we believe we wanted to have a much better margin because that remains our guiding principle across the company, and that's the reason we have pushed that business to this quarter.

items.statement: Gaana investment front-loaded in Q1-Q2 FY25, costs expected to decrease in subsequent quarters
items.quote: So, it's a planned expense. I would say for the first quarter, it's a little on the higher side. But as we see for the next quarter, this cost will come down.

items.statement: Management expects similar quarter-on-quarter growth going forward
items.quote: Yes, we can see a similar growth quarter on quarter. Yes.

items.statement: Margins under pressure due to new contracts and higher coal mix; expected to improve as ash share rises
items.quote: The major reason in the first instance being the coal and ash handling business because there are new opportunities, new businesses coming up. We are taking time to learn and understand the actual cost involved in every tender.

items.statement: Margin improvement expected as ash handling becomes majority and contract efficiencies kick in
items.quote: Going forward, this margin will get better and also the mix of coal and ash also will get better with ash taking over majority where we will have a larger margin. The margin will get better going forward.

items.statement: Immediate capex of about INR100 crores for EV and ash/coal fleet combined; may increase with business growth
items.quote: Currently, I think we immediately have current capex which is close to about INR100 odd crores for both the fleet, both EV and just put together. But going forward, yes, as the business goes, this might grow also.

items.statement: Ash handling fleet expansion to 1,500-1,600 vehicles would require INR75-100 crores capex for owned fleet (10-15%)
items.quote: So, even if you double the capacity to 1,500 or 1,600 vehicles from the band 800, we'll be about 150, 160 fleet will be owned fleet, which will be about INR75 crores to INR100 crores of capex requirement, if at all we own those fleets.

items.statement: New large public sector power plant clients added; expect 7,000-10,000 tons/day additional volume in 2-3 months
items.quote: I think we are looking at another addition of about 7,000, 8,000 to 10,000 tons per day going forward in two to three months to add.

items.statement: Legacy pond ash of 1.7 billion tons must be cleared in 3-6 years; fly ash generation of 185 million tons/year
items.quote: The legacy pond ash has to be cleared within the next three years. There is already a fine and penalty being imposed by Ministry of Environment. But looking at the volume, I think it might go up to five to six years to remove the legacy ash.

items.statement: Strategic focus shifting to ash handling over coal trading due to larger growth potential
items.quote: Yes, our focus is more majorly on ash, because that's one area which we think is going to grow a lot in the country. So, major focus will be on ash going forward.

items.statement: INR1,000 crore enabling resolution for future working capital needs; no immediate deployment plan
items.quote: We don't need to go to a process because we are a very fast -growing c ompany. If there's a potential requirement, this will only be an enabling factor

items.statement: Sherisha Technologies (promoter) loan repayment of INR27 crore done; balance INR19 crore by Sept 15 for working capital
items.quote: This loan out of the total INR46 crore loan, INR27 crore of the loan has been repaid as on day and balance also will get repaid by 15th of September.

items.statement: Ash handling realization varies by distance and disposal avenue: INR400/ton at 100km, INR800-900/ton at 200km
items.quote: Different customer, different location has different pricing depending on the number of kilometres you have to dispose the ash for. So it ranges if it's 100 kilometres it is INR400 a ton if it's 200 it's INR800, INR900 a ton

items.statement: Green mobility revenue INR5.47 crore from 539 EVs; target 2,000 vehicles by March 2025 with ~INR7-8 lakh/vehicle/year yield
items.quote: This year like we said last time by end of this year it will go up to 2000 vehicles by March next year. And the potential revenue could be roughly about yield per vehicle could be roughly about 7 to 8 lakhs per vehicle on a yearly basis.

items.statement: Green mobility gross profitable; EBITDA profitability expected as fleet scales and corporate costs absorb
items.quote: So I think we are on the gross level we are profitable. I think as we increase the fleet and then the corporate expense and the total team expenses get divided, we'll be profitable even at the EBITDA level.

items.statement: Working capital cycle 60-90 days (payables 15 days, receivables 60-90 days); no improvement expected
items.quote: Currently, working capital cycle is between 60 to 90 days. Where our supplier, we pay on a 15-day basis. But from the customer, we get between 60 to 90 days.

items.statement: Real estate segment saw sales of 1.15 million square feet and revenue of INR 1,086 crores in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: In Q1 FY'25, the real estate segment saw sales of 1.15 million square feet and revenue of INR 1,086 crores.

items.statement: Overall price realization reached INR 9,483 per square foot, the highest till date.
items.quote: The overall price realization continued its upward trajectory coming in at INR 9,483 per square foot this quarter, which is our highest till date.

items.statement: Strong demand continues for new launches and under-construction properties with end users as largest buyer segment.
items.quote: We are still seeing strong demand for new launches as well as under construction properties. In our key markets, end users remain the largest buyer segment.

items.statement: Leasing portfolio stands at 8.7 million square feet with consistent office rental collections.
items.quote: In Q1 FY'25, the Brigade leasing portfolio stands at 8.7 million square feet with consistent office rental collections.

items.statement: GCCs, flex space operators, PFSI and technology firms continued to drive office leasing activities.
items.quote: Across the office segment, GCCs, flex space operators, PFSI and technology firms continued to drive leasing activities.

items.statement: Management does not provide presales guidance for FY25.
items.quote: We have not given guidance, and we actually don't share guidance.

items.statement: Launch trajectory remains same as previous quarter; launches skewed towards second half of FY25.
items.quote: As we had shared in the previous quarter. The launches trajectory remains the same. Whatever we have launched has been replenished in the land bank as well.

items.statement: Q2 launches expected to be similar to Q1 levels, subject to approvals.
items.quote: Similar to what we achieved in first quarter. Or maybe we're not sure because of approvals.

items.statement: Land bank stands at 517 acres with overall GDV of INR 50,000 crores, Brigade share INR 39,000 crores.

items.statement: Launch pipeline guidance of INR 10,000-11,000 crores GDV for FY25 remains unchanged.
items.quote: Yes, that is similar to what we mentioned earlier.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR 1,113 crores, EBITDA INR 328 crores, PAT INR 83 crores for Q1 FY25.
items.quote: Consolidated revenue, including other income for quarter 1 FY'25 stood at INR 1,113 crores. Consolidated EBITDA for quarter 1 FY'25 stood at INR 328 crores. Consolidated PAT after minority income for quarter 1 FY'25 is at INR 83 crores.

items.statement: Q1 sales lower than Q4 due to seasonal pattern and election-related approval delays.
items.quote: It's fairly typical for Q1 to be running at a lower rate than Q4. In fact, across the industry, Q4 tends to be the highest in the year. So we're not too worried about it. Also, there were some slowness in approvals due to elections, etcetera.

items.statement: Strategy remains land-driven; mid-segment pricing has moved up to INR 90 lakhs-1.2 crores in Bangalore.
items.quote: Now I would say that's comfortably upward of INR 90 lakhs to INR 1.2 crores. So there is an overall change in the market itself in terms of what qualifies as mid-segment, and that's due to multiple factors, mainly affordability and growth in per capita income as well.

items.statement: Hospitality revenue grew 13% YoY in Q1; occupancy up 9%, ARR strategy balanced with occupancy focus.
items.quote: The revenue that we have seen has actually gone up by 13% if we compare it to Q1 of last year. So there was growth and a typical hospitality strategy varies between an occupancy versus an ARR strategy.

items.statement: Brigade Twin Towers awaiting OC; one tower (0.6M sq ft) to be strata sold, other for leasing.
items.quote: Twin Towers, yes, we are still awaiting OC. So I cannot say it's completed just yet, we're still awaiting OC, and that should be we should be able to get in the next couple of months.

items.statement: Mahan Energen Phase II 1600 MW ultra-supercritical expansion targeted for completion by June 2027
items.quote: Speaking of the future, the Mahan Energen Phase II Ultra-supercritical expansion project of 1600 megawatt capacity is well underway to achieve its targeted completion by June2027.

items.statement: Advanced preparation started for three 1600 MW projects at Raipur, Raigarh, and Mirzapur
items.quote: We have started advanced preparation for setting up three more projects of 1600 MW each at Raipur, Raigarh, and Mirzapur.

items.statement: Awaiting NCLT approval for Lanco Amarkantak and Coastal Energen acquisitions adding 1800 MW operating and 1320 MW under-construction capacity
items.quote: We are awaiting NCLT approval of the resolution plans for Lanco Amarkantak and Coastal Energen, which will expand our operating capacity by 1800 MW and add another 1320 MW of under-construction capacity.

items.statement: Target capacity of 30.67 GW by FY29-30 including brownfield expansions of 4800 MW and inorganic opportunities over 1000 MW
items.quote: In addition to this, we are also evaluating further brownfield expansion projects of 4,800 MW and inorganic opportunities of more than 1,000 MW, which together will take our target capacities to 30.67 GW by FY 29-30.

items.statement: Government estimates peak demand growing from 250 GW to 400 GW by 2031-32 requiring 80-90 GW additional thermal capacity
items.quote: The government has revised its power demand projections within just two years. It estimates that peak demand will grow from 250 GW currently to 400 GW by 2031-32.

items.statement: Three states have invited bids for 6400 MW thermal supply with 25-year PPA duration
items.quote: Bids for supply of 6400 MW from thermal power have already been invited by three states, while more b ids are expected from other states soon

items.statement: Merchant revenue realization Rs 7.45/unit, fuel cost Rs 2.89/unit, contribution Rs 4.56/unit vs Rs 3.71/unit last year
items.quote: In merchant sales, we had a revenue realization of Rs. 7.45 per unit on an average for the quarter and the fuel cost was Rs. 2.89 per unit, so there was a contribution of Rs. 4.56 per unit.

items.statement: Carbon tax would be change in law and passed through under PPA, citing Rs 400/tonne GST Compensation Cess precedent
items.quote: See, any carbon tax would be a change in law and therefore it would be passed through under the PPA.

items.statement: Strategy to keep 80% capacity under long-term PPAs and 15-20% for merchant sales
items.quote: As per our internal assessment, we are keeping around 20% under merchant. That should be a sort of balancing act, whereby we don't want to expose ourselves to market risk for more than the 20%.

items.statement: Bangladesh PPA for 1500 MW for 25 years, receiving regular payments with 4-5 months average arrears
items.quote: have signed the agreement for 1500 megawatts and the PPA is for 25 years. So, there is no question of future as regards to the already concluded agreement. As far as payment is concerned, we have started getting good payments from last few months and every process is well

items.statement: Green ammonia co-firing pilot study at Mundra in technical feasibility stage
items.quote: We are carrying out a pilot study. So first we have to establish whether the green ammonia can be co-fired with the coal or not.

items.statement: Credit available for merchant capacity from banks and financial institutions based on standalone viability
items.quote: Credit is available nowadays even for merchant capacity also. There is a clear indication from Government of India that since now the rates in the market are quite attractive, the financial institutions and banks should look at standalone viability of the capacity now since the merchant market is quite matured.

items.statement: Q1FY25 had a slow start due to general elections and lower movie releases; 476 movies released vs 581 in Q1FY24 and 550 in Q4FY24, an 18% YoY and 13% QoQ decline.
items.quote: Q1FY25 had a slow start, due to the general elections campaign in April and May and a lower number of movie releases. During the quarter, 476 movies were released (including different versions/languages), compared to 581 in Q1FY24 and 550 in Q4FY24, reflecting an 18% decline year-over-year and a 13% decline quarter-over-quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR 945 mn, EBITDA INR 66 mn, net loss INR 42 mn in Q1FY25.
items.quote: Consolidated revenue for Q1FY25 was INR 945 million, up from INR 853 million in Q1FY24. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 66 mn, compared to INR 163 mn in Q1FY24. Net loss of INR 42 mn in Q1FY25, compared to a Net profit of INR 25 mn in

items.statement: Upcoming release lineup includes Auron Main Kahan Dum Tha, Stree 2, Vedaa, Khel Khel Mein, The Goat, Devara, Joker, Vettiyan, Deva, Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3, Singham Again, Sitare Zameen Par, Pushpa 2.
items.quote: Looking ahead, with the continued success of 'Kalki 2898 AD' in July and an exciting lineup of upcoming releases across languages, including 'Auron Main Kahan Dum Tha,' 'Stree 2,' 'Vedaa,' 'Khel Khel Mein,' 'The Goat,' 'Devara,' 'Joker,' 'Vettiyan,' 'Deva,' 'Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3,''Singham again,' 'Sitare Zameer par, and 'Pushpa 2,' we are hopeful for a positive turnaround in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Nova Cinema: license secured for one screen in UP; three screens under construction, two completed; first launch expected mid to late this month in Meerut.
items.quote: Yes, the license to operate one of the screens in UP has been secured. As mentioned earlier, three screens are under construction, and two of them are now completed. For one of the screens, we're just waiting for the right movie release, likely by mid to late this month, to officially launch it in UP.

items.statement: Product sales revenue grew 84% YoY to INR 26.5 crore with 20-22% operating margin; cost of goods sold increased INR 9 crore.
items.quote: Our revenue from product sales has grown by 84%, from INR 14 crores last year to INR 26.5 crores this quarter, carrying an operating margin of approximately 20-22%. Correspondingly, the cost of purchased goods has also gone up.

items.statement: Central government ad allocations remain under a cloud; no meaningful revenue received this quarter; uncertainty persists until new government establishes approach.
items.quote: Yes, the challenges with central government allocations for cinema networks persist. We haven't received meaningful revenue from them this quarter. Given the election period, even regular spending by the central government would have been low , making this a particularly dry qua rter for central government funds

items.statement: TSR network acquisition integration expected by Q3FY25; currently paying fixed fee ~INR 3.3 crore per quarter; revenue ramp-up underway.
items.quote: As discussed earlier, our multiplex network of ~2,000 screens adds significant value to our ad network but comes with associated costs. For single screens or lower-end multiplexes, we typically use a revenue-sharing arrangement, where we give around, let's say, 25% of earnings.

items.statement: Ad revenue share percentage expected to normalize to 45-48% range as advertisement revenue grows; TSR integration to stabilize by Q3.
items.quote: As advertisement revenue increases, the fixed nature of the revenue share will cause the percentage to naturally decrease to around 45-48%, which aligns with our typical range.

items.statement: Corporate ad revenue expected to perform well with strong film lineup; state government traction positive; significant traction expected in next two quarters.
items.quote: advertising, we have a strong lineup of films that should drive revenue in this sector. Additionally, our recent tie -up for South screens has increased our network strength there. As mentioned earlier, our overall product mix is improving with the addition of more multiplex screens. Given these factors, we expect to see significant traction in the next two quarters

items.statement: Advertisement screen network grew to 3,769 screens as of June 30, 2024, up 17% YoY with addition of 535 screens; slight 2% QoQ decline.
items.quote: On the screen network front, our advertisement screen network grew to 3,769 as of June 30, 2024, compared to 3,234 as of June 30, 2023, marking a 17% year-over-year increase with the addition of 535 advertisement screens.

items.statement: Company remains net cash positive with INR 1,066 mn cash balance; net cash position ~INR 50 crore after maintaining reserve for opportunities.
items.quote: Regarding the consolidated funds position, the balance at the end of the quarter stood at INR 1,066 mn. As of June 30, 2024, the company continues to be n et cash positive, even after considering outstanding debt

items.quote: However, from a pure modeling perspective, expectations should be tempered. The revenue potential of the caravan business is directly tied to the number of vans in operation, unlike our core advertising network where the infrastructure is already in place.

items.statement: NeuralGarage partnership for VisualDub AI lip-sync technology for dubbed films; revenue-sharing with no direct costs; pricing mechanisms still being determined.
items.quote: The partnership involves a revenue-sharing arrangement with no direct costs for us. VisualDub not only enhances the viewing experience but also provides practical benefits in film production.

items.statement: SG&A up 2% YoY; employee benefits up 14% due to normalization after converting 20% fixed salary to variable pay last year.
items.quote: SG&A has only seen a marginal 2% YoY increase, and employee benefits have risen by 14%. Although this 14% might seem high, it's due to last year's adjustment in our payout structure, where we converted 20% of fixed salaries into variable pay.

items.statement: Government ad revenue grew 55% YoY to INR 59 mn in Q1FY25 driven by political ads (~INR 4 crore); central government allocations remain low.
items.quote: While state government spending was also lower this quarter due to elections, political parties still see cinema as an effective medium for their campaigns. This quarter, we generated about INR 4 crores from political advertisements.

items.statement: No additional capex for NeuralGarage partnership; no fixed commitment; revenue-sharing model only.
items.quote: In terms of costs, no. The partnership is a revenue-sharing arrangement, so there won't be any additional expenses. There's no fixed commitment from the company in this business arrangement.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected at 9-10% for remaining quarters of FY25
items.quote: This has been extraordinarily good quarter. So, my sense is that last year, we had a margin of 8.2%. This year 10.8% and I feel that anything between 9% to 10% is something which we think we will be able to maintain in rest of the quarters.

items.statement: Animal Feed EBIT/MT expected around ₹2,000 for rest of FY25
items.quote: I think we should be able to maintain it around ₹ 2,000 in rest of the quarters, because I'm very confident because we are definitely covered as far as major raw materials are concerned, where most of the movements take place during the season.

items.statement: Astec CDMO revenue guidance maintained at ₹260-270 crore base growing 60-70% YoY in FY25
items.quote: See typically, I think we maintain our guidance on the CDMO revenues for the full year. As I have repeatedly mentioned, we should not look at CDMO revenues on a quarterly basis. So we maintain the same guidance that from last year, ₹ 260 crores- ₹ 270 crores number. We'll continue to grow that number by 60% to 70% this year, and we are well on target to achieve those numbers.

items.statement: Astec enterprise demand expected to recover fully by end of FY25, export prices to firm up in 1-2 quarters after

And I would say, by end of this year, the demand is likely to come back fully, and the prices might take another quarter or 2 to firm up.

Apart from that, there is a capitalization of herbicide. Money is already invested 99% of that. And then routine capex, everything will be managed through internal accrual easily.

items.statement: Dairy Value-Added Products salience improved from 36% to 42% of sales in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The salience of Value-Added Products has improved from 36% of total sales in Q1 FY'24 to 42% in Q1 FY'25, reflecting our successful portfolio optimization efforts.

items.quote: Yes. We have taken inventory write-downs in Q1 on tune of almost ₹ 18 crores. We brought all the inventory to the existing pricing level in the market. So, any kind of uptick in prices as we get into the subsequent quarters will have a positive impact on our profitability.

items.statement: Animal Feed volumes impacted by subdued milk prices and lower placements; Maharashtra recovery starting July
items.quote: I think if you ask me, this impact has been all around, but the major impact was Maharashtra, but I think that has certainly started improving, particularly from the month of July.

items.statement: Domestic Crop Protection margins expected to match last year's profile despite late season uncertainty
items.quote: Yes. I think Q1 and some part of Q22 is always our in -house products. And then we will start now quarter 2 second half and quarter 3 will be our in -licensing products. So, my sense is that our change in strategy and improvement in our in-licensing product, will definitely make sure that we come to similar margin profile as last year.

items.quote: We felt that we would be better off managing it alone and that is what, I would say, motivated us to go for acquiring 100% stake in this business. items.statement: Revenue growth target of 25% CAGR maintained
items.quote: I would say that I have always claimed that we have had a growth of 25% CAGR always, we work to see that how is it that we can continue to maintain this or better this.

items.statement: API capacity expansion from 100 KL to 250 KL with Rs. 60 crores capex
items.quote: Our current production capacity stands at 100 KL, and we plan to expand it to 250 KL with an estimated CAPEX of around Rs. 60 crores.

items.statement: O&M segment EBITDA margin typically 21% to 23%
items.quote: Yes, it's usually between 21% to 23% EBITDA.

items.statement: MCC pricing moderate this quarter, stable but not increasing, focused on volumes
items.quote: And coming to pricing, this pricing is little in this quarter this is on moderate, there is no not much growth in pricing because we are concentrating on the volumes to our capacities. And going forward it will increase.

items.statement: MCC market expected to grow 7-9% up to 2035 in Southeast Asia
items.quote: See, there are market research studies which indicate that MCC market is expected to grow, especially in the Southeast Asian region it's expected to grow between 7% to 9% up to 2035.

items.quote: I believe, that at least 35% to 40% of our revenue should be coming in from the API, operations and management should add in to around 20%, 25%, and the balance should be from the excipients, not just MCC because we will also have Cross Carmellose sodium. items.statement: Healthy six months order book in place for MCC
items.quote: We have a healthy six months order book in place.

items.statement: Saudi JV $180M sales target deferred due to working capital constraints
items.quote: Now when we look at it deeper, we realized that we need to be gradual in this because $180 million, there is market potential available. But for that, for the kind of bid bond, for the kind of tender valuation which we have to put in money, it will be tremendous and probably our working capital and our cash flow will not permit us to put in that level of funding upfront.

items.statement: Dahej and Jhagadia MCC expansion 95% complete, Rs. 50 crores spent from internal accruals and debt
items.quote: Manav, this Dahej and Jhagadia almost it is in the flag, maybe 95% already we have spent. That Rs. 50 crores were allotted for Dahej and Jhagadia, that is almost incurred.

items.statement: Debt to reach near zero by end of FY25
items.quote: Yes, definitely by end of this year, almost debt would be zero level would be there.

items.statement: API regulated market revenue miniscule in FY25, CEP approvals expected in 9 months
items.quote: Revenue in the API segment in the current financial year, revenue from the regulated markets is going to be miniscule. We might still have some exports in the ROW markets, but revenue from the regulated markets is going to be very small, insignificant actually.

items.statement: No new capex planned for Middle East JVs in next 2-3 years
items.quote: No, none at this moment.

items.statement: Bottom line margins to be maintained in near term, improvement later as capacity utilization increases
items.quote: Yes, Naman, for time being we will maintain, the sustainability is there. And then going forward it will increase. But immediately there is no increase, bottom line margins we will maintain, it will be maintained.

items.quote: Overall, it is 66%. items.statement: CCS environmental clearance expected within 4 weeks after Gujarat Pollution Control Board review
items.quote: So, just four days back we have had another review by the Gujarat Pollution Control Board EC Committee, and I believe we have cleared all their queries. items.quote: So, it is a work in progress as we have said before and we continue to expect meaningful contributions in H2.

items.quote: We have seen favorable progress in these products and expect a healthy contribution in FY25.

items.quote: So, the balance that we have to spend will be around Rs. 10-Rs. 15 crores to meet our CBF, and catalyst to PTA products to produce.

items.statement: Oren Hydrocarbon refurbishment estimated at Rs 40 crore for all plants, currently starting with two plants
items.quote: So, I think we anticipated that we would spend maybe at the outermost about Rs. 40 odd crores.

items.quote: EBITDA for this Q1 stood at around Rs. 849 million with a margin of 38%.

items.statement: Bromine demand steady domestically and encouraging pickup on export side from agrochemicals, pharma, flame retardants
items.quote: We continue to see a steady demand from the domestic market as well as encouraging market pickup on the export side from all end users like Agro Chemicals, Pharmaceuticals and Flame-Retardant manufacturers overseas.

items.statement: Salt demand remains firm with customer contracts in place, dispatch delays due to port logistics temporary
items.quote: However, the demand remains firm, and customer contracts continue to be in place, and we only believe this to be temporary.

items.statement: Bromine pricing stabilized over last couple of quarters, no reason seen for price drop
items.quote: I think the pricing that we are seeing now, I think is stabilized over the last couple of quarters and I don't see a reason for it to drop.

items.statement: Logistics challenges at ports (vessel/container shortage, freight costs, berthing delays) impacting dispatches and shipments
items.quote: We on the other hand has experienced some delays on availability of vessels, containers and increased freight costs which pose some challenge for Indian manufacturers.

items.statement: Flame Retardant Phase-2 expansion will not commission before March 2025, measured approach being taken

items.quote: Not entirely. I think it is a collaboration with IIT Bhubaneshwar. So, working with government institutions have various components, but safe to say a large part of it will come from us.

items.quote: I am pleased to announce that we have successfully closed and raised INR800 crores of equity via the QIP. The funds raised through this QIP is primary in nature and infused into the company entirely.

items.statement: Guidance of launching two projects per quarter this year
items.quote: This is in line with our guidance of launching two projects per quarter this year.

items.quote: I think we are going to pretty much maintain the run rate of about INR150 crores every quarter, which means that about INR600 crores for the whole year.

items.quote: We have also received RERA registration for two towers in Urbania, Thane, which we will be launching in August '23, and these have a GDV of approximately INR1,700 crores.

items.quote: Moving to the consolidated key financial numbers, the revenue of Q1 FY '25 stands at INR422 crores of 55% year-on-year basis. The EBITDA and PAT for this period stand at INR58 crores and INR26 crores respectively.

items.statement: Tractor production grew 1% YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by above normal monsoon forecast and timely southwest monsoon arrival.

items.statement: Two-wheeler segment grew 20% YoY in Q1 FY25 exceeding expectations due to rural sentiment revival and strong motorcycle demand.
items.quote: The 2-wheeler segment, started from a slow base, exceeded expectations with 20% growth in Q1 FY '25 driven by the revival of rural consumer sentiment and strong motorcycle demand.

items.statement: Three-wheeler segment grew 11% YoY in Q1 FY25 due to sustained demand for passenger transport and last-mile e-commerce deliveries.
items.quote: The 3-wheeler segment grew by 11% in Q1 FY '25 due to sustained demand for passenger transportation and last mile operators for e-commerce, food deliveries and other applications.

items.statement: Management maintains broad expectation of moderate growth for FY25 similar to FY24 despite election year dynamics and high base effects.
items.quote: Yes. The broad expectation of growth for the year holds. There is a change. We had already sort of indicated Q1 would be sort of a moderate or very weak growth, knowing that there would be an upcoming election, and we would also come into the summer months with not knowing how intense that summer was, but we had expected some slowdown.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 12% in Q1 FY25 from 11.3% in Q1 FY24 due to revenue growth and reduction in other expenses.
items.quote: EBITDA as a percentage of total revenue improved from 11.3% in April-June '23 to 12% in April-June '24. The improvement in margin is mainly attributable to the growth in revenue and reduction in other expenses during the current quarter.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain double-digit EBITDA margin but will not provide future margin guidance due to technology transition uncertainties.
items.quote: We did now the first step coming back to a double digit, which was very important for us, and we do everything to keep this double digit. For the future, we have to see how the market is growing, what is the product mix, and how fast coming technologies in.

items.statement: Capex will be spent for feasible and profitable localization; no fixed range but investments made when they contribute to top and bottom line.
items.quote: Whatever we have to spend to have a feasible and profitable localization, we will spend.

items.statement: NOx sensor line investment includes export volumes to achieve better utilization and return on investment.
items.quote: Here we get a certain exp ort volume as well because we need in the overall production network, there were volumes which we could bring to India. And therefore, we will get a line where we have India plus export volumes, which is also favourable then for

items.statement: Second Lambda sensor production line inaugurated at Bidadi plant in April 2024; targeting over 8 million pieces annually by 2025.
items.quote: By 2025, we are set to achieve over 8 million pieces annually.

items.statement: Power Tools India elevated to independent region covering SAARC countries effective April 1, 2024; exports from Chennai plant to serve region.
items.quote: India now has become 1 of the 5 independent regions within the Bosch Power Tools global organization. India as a region is now responsible for consolidated figures for India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan and Maldives, or the entire SAARC.

items.statement: Mobility business grew 4.1% YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by aftermarket (8.1%) and Power Solutions (2.3%) growth.
items.quote: The Mobility business has grown by 4.1% in April to June '24 as compared to April to June '23, driven mainly due to the Mobility aftermarket business, which grew by 8.1% on account of higher demand for new generation diesel components. Power Solutions business, which grew by 2.3%, mainly due to growth in passenger car segment driven by high demand for utility vehicles.

items.statement: Building Technologies grew 19.4% YoY in Q1 FY25 on higher security system installation orders.
items.quote: The Building Technologies business grew by 19.4% on account of execution of higher number of orders for installation of security systems.

items.statement: Consumer Goods grew 5.1% YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by grinders, drillers, cutters demand.
items.quote: The Consumer Goods business grew by 5.1%, driven by higher demand for grinders, drillers, cutters on account of the market growth.

items.statement: New Lambda sensor line supports upcoming BS-VI OBDII Stage B regulation effective April 2025.
items.quote: The new production line supports the upcoming BS-VI OBDII stage B regulation effective from April 2025.

items.statement: TREM V norms for tractors expected to roll out by second quarter of FY26; will drive shift to common rail systems.
items.quote: TREM V has been postponed so far. I'm not aware of any recent discussions towards changing the date or if there's any further change in the date, but mostly by second quarter of '26. TREM V should be rolling out and in place.

items.statement: Exports to parent company expected to triple in next 4 years; imports from parent to more than double due to technology transition.
items.quote: We see an increase, and it's a serious number, also in the automotive. But again, still, we are -- our main market is India and SAARC. And wherever possible, of course, we also stepped into the export business with our parent or our affiliated companies, which helps us also in the local volumes because we have a better fixed cost coverage.

items.statement: Power Tools exports from Chennai plant to SAARC region; no plans for local manufacturing in those countries.
items.quote: There are no current plans for setting up any plants in any of these countries. All of them benefit from our current manufacturing plant, which is already in Chennai in India. And we will continue to export from Chennai to these regions.

items.statement: Localization crucial for common rail systems due to higher material share; purchasing team screening supplier market for electrified powertrain components.
items.quote: On the other hand, you also have to see we have a shift from the conventional products to the common rail system where overall we have a higher share of material in the common rail system. Therefore, localization will be even more crucial.

items.statement: Partnership with Hero MotoCorp (world's largest 2-wheeler OEM) for Lambda sensors; Bajaj Pulsar N250 and 400cc models confirm Bosch as preferred technology partner.
items.quote: The new production line supports the upcoming BS-VI OBDII stage B regulation effective from April 2025. By 2025, we are set to achieve over 8 million pieces ann

items.statement: Hydrogen engine technology gaining global recognition as zero-emission powertrain; Bosch working on projects with commercial vehicle manufacturers globally and in India.
items.quote: Hydrogen engine technology is gaining recognition globally as a viable zero-emission vehicle powertrain. In the European Union, it is classified alongside battery electric vehicles or BEVs and fuel cell electric vehicles or FCEVs, as is ZEV powertrain.

items.statement: Early localization risks high capex and fixed costs if volumes don't materialize; conscious call to balance timing against margin impact.
items.quote: Too early localization also is totally counterproductive in terms of our margin. So we will have to balance it against when is localization most appropriate, what volumes justi fy localization with reduced costs and improved performance in terms of margins

items.statement: One-off warranty provision and forex reversal increased other expenses sequentially in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: And this is, of course, this quarter, we have the reversal impact, or you see the reverse impact, and we have 1 warranty case where we have a special warranty where we made a provision in this quarter. So this is actually the reason.

items.statement: PLI scheme DVA application submitted; awaiting formal approval; capex planning not dependent on PLI benefits.
items.quote: We have not officially got any confirmation from the ministry on DVA approval, although there are market speculations or social media or media speculations or news items on this. We do not want to comment on that. We hope to -- we have fulfilled more or less all the requirements to meet the DVA.

items.statement: Portfolio review ongoing for listed entity; no comment on potential exits or mergers in Mobility segment.
items.quote: Yes, I do not want to speculate on things which are very sensitive information. So I would not want to comment on these things right now. All I can say is that we are continuously relooking at portfolio and how we can do it better, not just for ourselves internally but also for our customers in India, and potentially also for the export markets, which are opening up for us.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR2,500 crores for FY26, implying ~25% CAGR

items.statement: Expect strong and sustained demand for automotive and architectural films worldwide

items.statement: Anticipate continued robust demand for PPF in international and domestic markets
items.quote: We anticipate continued robust demand in both international and domestic markets.

This new line is expected to begin commercial production by the second quarter of FY26.

items.statement: PPF plants running beyond capacity; using fungible capacity from other lines to meet demand
items.quote: our plan ts are running at full capacity. In fact, beyond capacity, like I said in my opening address

items.quote: this quarter we achieved 27 % plus and almost it used to be a standard 20% margin average. So companies working towards to reach the aim is to reach to that level, but it will be because of the product mix it will remain good.

items.quote: these products come at a very, very premium and high-end margins. I can assure you that they are even I can say 20%-30% higher than the general product line.

items.quote: there is an opportunity and we are capitalizing on that. So, we have done that in peak summer seasons, we have achieved numbers which were really tremendous. So, that is still continuing.

items.quote: Yes, that has happened. But again, those things are, you know, I mean, I can talk in general, like our aim always has been to have fully backward integrated system, which we always make whatever product we make.

items.quote: I think it was around 18 months timeline, which we have given for a new line. So in that line, we are working like how we should do, should we go into another kind of investment or it should be the PPF. So we are working on that.

items.quote: Fertilizer business, the margins are more or less same. Until a nd unless there is any subsidy revision, I don't foresee any changes in t he raw material prices presently

items.quote: The acceleration of Kharif cultiv ation has been facilitated by the favourable rainfall that is being experienced this year. Improv ed seasonal prospects are expected to maintain the robust demand f or fertilizers during forthcoming quarters

items.quote: In IP segment, domestic prices remained subdued due to dumping of cheap Chinese caprolactam, melamine and basic nylon 6.

items.quote: The demand has been stable across all end user industries. Demand for detergents, as you usually know within India, goes through a bit of moderation during monsoon and then picks up again very strongly after winter and goes on to remain robust.

items.quote: Imports into India, while they did go up between January to May, it has been moderated post that and mainly on account of higher freight rates due to tensions in Middle East.

items.statement: Fully sold out in soda ash; expect to remain fully sold out
