items.quote: According to CEA, there's a potential of another 145,320 megawatts from hydroelectric sources. Only about 32% of this has been utilized so far. So there's an enormous potential for future development of hydro. For the future outlook according to Central Electricity Authority, there are 32 hydro power projects under construction in India with a combined capacity of 16,737 megawatts.

items.statement: Finance cost decreased due to return of bank guarantees and reduced working capital utilization
items.quote: In this quarter, we saw a decrease in the finance cost which is a positive sign for us which was majorly contributed by return of Bank Guarantee from some projects in the shape of mobilization advance and performance guarantee and reduced utilization of working capital limits.

items.statement: Received Rs 64 crore in claimed dues including interest; used to reduce creditors and interest-bearing liabilities
items.quote: In 2024, we have received claimed amount in all dues of approximately Rs 64 crores including interest which has been used to reduce our Sundry creditors and majority of cash surplus was used in lowering interest-bearing creditors beyond 30 to 60 days.

items.statement: New BG limits required at 10-15% of order value (5-10% performance BG + 5-10% advance BG)
items.quote: So, for any project, we require anywhere between 10 % to 20% of the order book, of the order value as new bank guarantee limits. So, if you take on an average between 10% to 15% also, that's the level. So, if I add Rs 1,000 crores of orders, I will need roughly around Rs 100 crores to Rs 150 crores in terms of new BG limits.

items.statement: Bhilwara Jaipur toll road arbitration award reinstated after Commercial Court dismissed PWD appeal; PWD appealed to High Court double bench
items.quote: The appeal made by PWD Government of Rajasthan has been dismissed by the Commercial Court and hence the arbitration award has been reinstated. PWD Government of Rajasthan has appealed against the dec ision of the Commercial Court in the High Court of Rajasthan and more specifically in the double bench because of current rules of arbitration act

items.statement: Pallacia Jaipur project received occupation certificate recently; expects sales velocity to increase with new agency
items.quote: So, we got the OC of that project only recently. So, it's not a very old project. The OC was received only recently. The project did get delayed in terms of completion but there are various reasons for that. But now that it is complete and now that we have received the occupation certificate or the completion certificate now, we are expecting the sales velocity to increase.

items.statement: Open to complete exit from Bandra project for significant upfront value instead of waiting for free sale portion
items.quote: Once that takes place then we will have a choice between several strong and reputed players within the city of Mumbai to partner with and also we may actually even look at a complete exit as well, which will bring us a significant chunk at one go itself instead of waiting it out for the share of the free sale portion to get sold.

items.statement: Competitors in hydro civil space include L&T, NCC, HCC; limited competition in hydro-mechanical where Patel Engineering was not a competitor
items.quote: We have competitors like L&T, NCC, HCC. So, there are a couple of other companies also in the hydropower civil space. So, and I think the competitive scenario is quite decent. But in hydro mechanical, we have very limited competition. So, Patel was never our competition in the hydro mechanical space.

items.statement: Focus on government sector projects; bidding timing and conversion to work orders difficult to predict
items.quote: No, it is difficult to predict the amount because we focus mainly on the government sector. And in the government sector, the projects take time to come up for bidding. So, how many projects will come up for bidding in this financial year itself? And even if they come up for bidding, how many will, the bids will be opened and by which time, by what time, how much time they will take to convert int

items.statement: Target AUM of INR 300,000 million by FY27
items.quote: We are well positioned to drive growth and are on track to achieve our target of INR300,000 million AUM by FY27.

items.statement: Expect ROE of 10.5-11% for FY25, further improvement of 2-2.5% next year, targeting 15% ROE in FY27
items.quote: So as compared to ROE, which was less than 8%, in 1QFY25 we are likely to report ROE, in the range of about 10.5% to 11% for FY25. And we believe that next year, ROE should improve further by another 2% to 2.5%. And from there, once we achieve a scale of about INR 250,000 million plus, by then, I think we will be more or less in a steady state in terms of our branch expansion also on the increment

items.statement: Expect AUM of INR 200,000-210,000 million in FY25
items.quote: So we would be able to achieve INR 200,000 – INR 210,000 million in FY25, I think we are well within our target to reach INR 300,000 million by FY27.

items.statement: Target net fee income of more than INR 20 crores from insurance distribution in FY25
items.quote: We are looking to generate more than INR20 crores in net fee income from insurance distribution in FY25.

items.statement: AUM reached INR 174,579 million, up 56% YoY
items.quote: We maintained a strong growth momentum in Q1 FY25 with our AUM reaching to INR174,579 million, with an increase of 56% year-on-year.

items.statement: Disbursements of INR 56,197 million, up 109% YoY
items.quote: Our disbursement was INR56,197 million during the quarter, reflected 109% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM increased 55% QoQ to cross INR 54,001 million
items.quote: Our gold loan AUM increased by 55% quarter-on-quarter to cross INR54,001 million, supported by our extensive gold loan branch network of 750 branches spread across 9 states and union territories and co-lending partnership with 4 banks.

items.statement: Co-lending AUM increased to 16.4% of total AUM from 11.7% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Our co-lending AUM continued to surge during Q1 FY25, increasing to 16.4% of AUM compared to 11.7% in Q4 FY24 and 6.2% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Yields at 16.3%, up 70 bps QoQ; spreads at 7%, up 60 bps QoQ
items.quote: Our yields were at 16.3%, an increase of 70 basis points and our spreads reached to 7%, increase of 60 basis points quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: NII increased 18% QoQ and 27% YoY to INR 3,013 million
items.quote: The net interest income or NII during Q1 FY25 came in at INR3,013 million, an increase of 18% quarter-on-quarter and 27% year-on-year.

items.statement: Non-interest income increased 35% YoY, co-lending income up 126% YoY and 17% QoQ
items.quote: Our non-interest income increased by 35% year-on-year, supported by strong fee income from co-lending, which increased by 126% year-on-year and 17% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to 64.6% from 70.5% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Following our branch expansion, we are now shifting our focus to improving the efficiency and productivity, the effect of this already started to reflect in our cost -to-income ratio, which has improved to 64.6% in Q1 FY25, down from 70.5% in Q4 FY24, marking an impro vement of 5.9% in this quarter

items.statement: Pre-provisioning operating profit increased 33% QoQ to INR 1,452 million
items.quote: As a result, our pre-provisioning operating profit increased significantly to INR1,452 million, up by 33% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: GNPA and NNPA flat at 2% and 1.1% respectively; Stage 3 PCR at 43%
items.quote: Our GNPA ratio and NNPA ratio remained broadly flat at 2% and 1.1%, respectively. Our Stage 3 PCR ratio stood at 43%.

items.statement: Credit cost increased due to one-off slippages in construction finance, technical write-off of INR 280 million
items.quote: Our credit cost increased in Q1 FY25 due to one-off slippages in our construction finance book, resulting in a technical write-off of INR 280 million.

items.statement: Expect to recover 80-90% of the INR 280 million technical write-off
items.quote: Based on our experience from the past, we should be able to recover 80% to 90%.

items.statement: Plan to add about 50 gold loan branches in current financial year
items.quote: So gold loan segment, we might add about 50 branches in the coming year. So that expansion will not be as aggressive as it was earlier because we already reached one threshold of 750 branches, so now large expanse will be gradual. So about 50 branches or so we will add in the current financial year.

items.statement: Plan to open about 70 micro LAP branches in next 3 quarters, 27 already live
items.quote: We intend to open about 70 branches in next 3 quarters. And already 27 branches have gone live, and we will start seeing some portfolio, but initial few months are the phase where we will build up these branches.

items.statement: Raised INR 5,000 million via commercial paper at A1+ rating; overall cost of borrowing 9.3-9.6%
items.quote: As part of our resource diversification strategy, the company has initiated market borrowings in Q1. We successfully raised INR 5,000 million issuance for commercial paper, getting A1 Plus rating by CRISIL.

items.statement: Board approved fund raise of INR 20,000 million via equity, debt or convertible securities
items.quote: Our Board has also approved fund raise of INR 20,000 million by way of equity, debt or convertible securities through rights issu e, preferential allotment or QIP

items.statement: Recent capital market borrowings at ~9%; all bank borrowings MCLR-linked
items.quote: So, the recent capital market borrowing are in the range of about 9%. And overall cost of borrowing is in the range of about 9.3% - 9.6%.

items.statement: Yield improvement driven by higher gold loan share; gold loan yields better than other products
items.quote: So yield on advances, if you see Q4 FY24 yield on advances was 15.6%, which has gone to about 16.3% on a portfolio basis. And th is is because contribution from the gold loan AUM in the overall portfolio is increasing. Gold loan yields are better than all the other products

items.statement: Cost of funds expected to remain in current range, any increase limited to 10-20 bps and passable to new disbursals
items.quote: So I think cost of funds in this year should remain by and large in this range. But I believe that cost of funds should not increase. If at all it increases, it will not be more than 10 to 20 basis points, which we should be able to pass on to all the new disbursals, which are happening now.

items.statement: Retail AUM over 80% of portfolio; MSME ~28-30%, gold loan ~30%, housing ~23%
items.quote: We remain focused on retail lending with retail AUM constituting over 80% of our portfolio.

items.statement: Launched micro LAP with avg ticket size <INR 0.5 million, yields ~22% vs MSME ~15.5%
items.quote: However, micro LAP will have average ticket size of INR 0.5 million, all the loans will be below INR 0.8 million. And these are the loans at the yield in the range of about 22% as against the MSME yield in the range of 15.5%.

items.statement: Gold loan branches at 750, productivity of INR 70 million AUM per branch
items.quote: These branches have started to scale up and have reached the productivity of INR70 million AUM per branch.

items.statement: End-to-end loan lifecycle digitized; new loan origination and management systems live in Q1 FY25
items.quote: I'm pleased to report that all our technological initiatives have successfully gone live in the first quarter of FY25. This positions CGCL to reap significant long-term benefits.

items.statement: MSME and housing finance saw temporary stabilization due to seasonality and tech transition; growth expected back from Q2
items.quote: Due to seasonality effect and transition of a new loan origination system and loan management system during the first 2 months of the year, the MSME and housing finance saw temporary stabilization. However, we are confident that our growth momentum will be back from Q2 onwards and will continue in coming quarters.

items.statement: Gold price decline from import duty cut increased LTV on existing portfolio; reaching out to customers for additional margin
items.quote: So gold loan reduction on the import duty have resulted in the gold loan prices going softer. And so on the existing portfolio, our LTV has gone up, so we have to see that our LTV come within the acceptable range. And for that, we will reach out to our customers and inform them about this so that they can provide additional margin.

items.statement: Gold loan business turned profitable at operating level after crossing INR 50 million AUM per branch breakeven
items.quote: loan has become profitable because we have crossed INR 50 million AUM in all the branches. And normally gold loans become breakeven above INR 45 million. So all the gold loan branches of 750, have started contributing

items.statement: Target double-digit consolidated revenue growth and hold operating margin at FY24 levels in FY25
items.quote: we continue to strive towards achieving our target to deliver double-digit revenue growth and hold on to operating margins in FY25.

items.statement: Sector demand improving gradually with rural growth ahead of urban; expect volume trends to sustain improving trajectory
items.quote: During the quarter, the sector continued to witness gradual improvement in demand trends with rural growth ahead of urban.

items.statement: Expect to hold operating margin at FY24 levels in FY25 despite mild commodity inflation
items.quote: we are confident that we'll be able to maneuver margins through pricing, driving a more favorable mix and ongoing cost optimization initiatives to hold operating margin at FY '24 levels this year.

items.statement: Pricing growth to pick up through the year as Saffola oil price drops move into base and mild copra inflation expected in Q2
items.quote: Pricing growth is likely to pick up through the year with Saffola oil price drops moving into the base completely from Q2 and mild inflation expected in some commodities in Q2, particularly copra, which will further aid domestic revenue growth through the course of the year.

items.statement: Gradual escalation in copra prices positive for Parachute as it allows leveraging pricing power and procurement advantages
items.quote: Gradual escalation in copra prices is positive for the brand as it affords us the opportunity to strategically leverage the brand's pricing power and procurement system advantages thereby gaining volume traction and market share.

items.statement: Foods and premium personal care share to cross 25% by FY27 with 20-25% CAGR and visible profitability improvement
items.quote: We will sustain the aggression to drive 20-25% CAGR in these portfolios and expect the composite share of foods and premium personal care portfolio to cross 25% by FY '27, accompanied by a visible improvement in their profitability.

items.statement: Foods business grew 37% in Q1 with core Oats at 20%+; expect to surpass internal expectations for the year
items.quote: Foods had a robust quarter and registered 37% growth with core Oats portfolio growing at 20% plus.

items.statement: Digital-first brands target Rs 550-600 crore run rate by FY25 exit and double-digit EBITDA margin by FY27
items.quote: We expect the digital first brands to exit FY '25 at a Rs. 550-600 crores run rate this year and striving to achieve double-digit EBITDA margin by FY '27.

items.statement: Parachute coconut oil volume offtake grew 8% in Q1; composite coconut oil portfolio market share reached highest-ever 64% on MAT basis
items.quote: Parachute which has witnessed strong 8% growth in volume offtakes during the quarter, which was reflective of the consistent market share and penetration gains witnessed by the brand.

items.statement: Project SETU Phase-1 launched in 6 states with promising direct coverage expansion in urban and rural markets
items.quote: We launched Phase-1 of Project SETU in 6 states comprising a mix of stronghold and opportunity markets. The initial results have been very promising with direct coverage expansion in urban and rural markets.

items.statement: Plan to scale up Project SETU Phase-1 markets and expand into more states during FY25 to enhance direct reach and weighted distribution
items.quote: During the course of this year, we will scale up Phase-1 markets as well as expand into some more states.

items.statement: Value-added hair oils facing competitive headwinds in bottom-of-pyramid segment; national players using high BTL and zero pricing strategy
items.quote: No, I am talking about national players who have gone into zero BTL and high BTL driven strategy, which is not necessarily the best strategy long term.

items.statement: Kaya collaboration gives exclusive rights to scale efficacy-based personal care products outside clinics; Rs 100 crore revenue opportunity over 4 years
items.quote: We believe this is a Rs. 100 crores revenue opportunity over the next 4 years. And we'll add another growth lever to our digital first business, thereby further activating the portfolio diversification agenda of the India business.

items.statement: International business maintains double-digit constant currency growth; export business scaled to $25 million; Bangladesh concentration risk reducing over 3-4 years
items.quote: The export business has scaled to $25 million and continued its healthy run. The broad-basing of the business has not only strengthened the growth prospects of the business but has also added margin upside potential in the medium term and also consistently reducing the concentration risk in Bangladesh business over the last three to four years.

items.statement: Elevated food inflation and spatial distribution of rainfall are key factors to monitor for demand outlook
items.quote: That being said, elevated food inflation and spatial distribution of rainfall will be key factors to be monitored.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of 30% growth for FY25
items.quote: Our revenue increased by 26% over the last year and is in sync with a guidance of 30% revenue increase in FY'25.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 32-33% for FY25
items.quote: Our EBITDA increased by 9% and is currently at 33% of the revenue which again is in sync with the guidance that we have been giving for our adjusted EBITDA.

items.statement: Music licensing plus artist management revenue growth guidance of 25-26% for FY25
items.quote: I can give you the comfort that the music revenue - which is a combination of music and artist management - is on track to achieve our guidance of 25% - 26% growth in the FY'25.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue excluding Carvaan to grow at 30% CAGR over next 3 years
items.quote: At the consolidated company level, we expect revenue, excluding Carvaan, to grow at a CAGR of 30% over the next 3 years and PBT to double over the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Video vertical to grow at 25% CAGR over next 5 years
items.quote: We believe, over the next 5 years, we should be able to grow this business at 25% CAGR.

items.statement: Pocket Aces to reach breakeven by end of FY25
items.quote: End of the year, you will find Pocket Aces at a breakeven level. We are not there yet, but we will be there before the end of the year.

items.statement: Plan to invest over INR 1,000 crores in new music content over next 3 years
items.quote: If I talk long term, over the next 3 years, we will be investing over INR1,000 crores in new music content.

items.statement: Content investment of around INR 300 crores plus targeted for FY25
items.quote: At a very broad level, we are looking at number of anything around a little upwards of INR300 crores.

items.statement: Content charge-off increased 48% YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: This quarter the charge-off on account of new content has gone up by 48% year-on-year.

items.statement: Music licensing revenue growth temporarily matching content charge-off; profitability to improve after 18 months
items.quote: We are currently in a transitional state where our new content expenses are going up in a step-function manner, resulting in the incremental revenue just about matching the content charge-off.

items.statement: Maintain 5-year payback period on content investments
items.quote: With all this investment in new content, we maintain our guidance of a 5-year payback period.

items.statement: Events business has single-digit margins but triple-digit IRRs due to short capital lock-in of 15-30 days
items.quote: On the margin side, it will always be single-digit margin, but on the IRR side, it becomes triple-digit IRRs if the money is deployed properly.

items.statement: Artist management gross margins: music artists 20-40%, influencers 15-20%
items.quote: Typical margins on the music side of artists can vary anything between 20% to 30% to 40%, while on the influencer side is between 15% to 20% as the gross margin from which you deduct the expenses of your team members out there.

items.statement: Content acquisition pipeline includes music of major upcoming films: Stree 2, Jigra, Skyforce, Kanguva, Bazooka, Sudeep Kiccha film
items.quote: Our lineup for the next 12 months is all in place where we have the music of some of the biggest films of the year.

items.statement: Released 330+ original and premium recreation songs across 9 languages in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Overall, we released 330 + original and premium recreation songs across multiple languages which includes Hindi, Bhojpuri, Gujarati, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi and Bengali.

items.statement: Tauba Tauba from Bad Newz is Spotify's #1 song in India since July 9 and global #1 music video on YouTube for 28 days
items.quote: This song has topped every possible chart in the country - be it a Spotify, Instagram, Radio, YouTube you name it and we're there. It's the Spotify's no. 1 song in India since 9th of July. In fact, it is the global no. 1 music video on YouTube since the last 28 days.

items.statement: Two songs from Stree 2 are global #2 and #3 music videos on YouTube; Saregama holds global #1, #2, #3 positions
items.quote: Both the songs are doing extremely well. One of them is global music video no. 2 and the second song is global music video no. 3 on YouTube music video charts. That means global no. 1, no. 2, no. 3, all belong to Saregama today.

items.statement: Artist management portfolio expanded to 150+ influencers/artists with 100M+ followers on Instagram and YouTube
items.quote: During the quarter, 30 -plus new influencers and music artists were added, making our overall portfolio upwards of 150. These artists, among them, have over 100 million followers and subscribers on Instagram and YouTube.

items.statement: Diljit Dosanjh Dil Luminati tour: 11 concerts in Canada and USA with 50,000+ attendance in Vancouver
items.quote: On the live events side we have started the Dil Luminati tour of Diljit Dosanjh in Vancouver with a record-breaking turnout of over 50,000 fans. Overall, 11 concerts were held in Canada and U.S.A.

items.statement: Carvaan revenue was INR 24.7 crores in Q1 FY25; shifting to e-commerce and modern trade only
items.quote: As promised earlier, from this quarter onwards, we have started sharing the Carvaan revenue number separately. This quarter, Carvaan revenue was INR24.7 crores, which is a significant drop over Q1FY24.

items.statement: Carvaan retail network being cut dramatically; will become e-commerce and modern trade only by end of FY25
items.quote: We have cut down our retail network dramatically, and we will keep on cutting it down over the next 2 quarters. By the time we end this financial year, it will become only an e-commerce and a modern trade product.

items.statement: YouTube revenue pressure in April-May due to political and IPL advertising; stable from June onwards
items.quote: In April, May combined we saw more advertising money flowing on news, elections and then on IPL, which happens every year because most big advertisers want to advertise on IPL and nothing else. And this is what was expected, and I had said this in my last quarter's analyst call also. June became completely stable, and we were back to normal, and July has been going very steady for us.

items.statement: Free-to-paid streaming transition: two partner platforms moved behind paywall from Q2 FY25; base effect over from Q2
items.quote: Two of our partner platforms - who had contributed revenue on the free side in Q1 FY'24 - from Q2 onwards completely moved behind the paywall. This impact gets over from Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Target to acquire 25-30% of all new music releases in India; licensing revenue to double in 3-3.5 years
items.quote: Overall, with a stated goal of acquiring 25% to 30% of all new music releases in India, the licensing vertical should double its revenue in 3 – 3.5 years, which is 25% to 26% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Content investments to be funded through internal accruals and QIP money; no additional fundraise needed
items.quote: And this entire investment is going to be funded through our internal accruals or the QIP money. No additional investments or fundraise is needed.

items.statement: Cash balance over INR 600 crores as per investor presentation cash flow statement
items.quote: We have disclosed this Swapnil, it is more than INR600 crores if you see our cash flow statement in the investor presentation.

items.statement: Video vertical capital allocation capped at 18% of total capital; targeting 8-10% margins in 12-18 months
items.quote: not more than 18% of the total capital allocated will ever go towards the films, series or video segment of ours. Within that, we hope that in the next 12 to 18 months, we will reach a situation whereby we should be able to generate 8% to 10% margins and a much higher IRR

items.statement: Government and judiciary actively working to curb piracy; technology enables fast detection via app stores
items.quote: There is a very strong conviction at the government level to kill this concept of piracy and get everything on the legitimate side, not just on the music, but even on the film side. Even judiciary is very actively helping us out as content IP owners to help control piracy and put the people who are indulging in it behind bars.

items.statement: Capex plan for FY25 is Rs. 1000-1100 crores; investments of similar or slightly higher order
items.quote: Outlook on the CAPEX, I think CAPEX plan for this year will be about Rs. 1000 – Rs. 1100 crores. I think that number remains around that.

items.statement: Expect robust growth in Q2 FY25 driven by rural recovery and normal monsoon
items.quote: With expected normal monsoon , we could witness robust growth in Q2.

items.statement: Rural growth at 17% in Q1 FY25, first time rural doing better than urban; industry grew 13%
items.quote: First time we have seen a double digit. I am a strong promoter that given the kind of demography , given the kind of infrastructure, what government is trying to build in terms of roads and other connectivity and also the public transport, the population itself given that I think the single most vehicles or mobility is two-wheeler.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin improved 90 bps to 11.5% in Q1 FY25 vs 10.6% YoY; driven by material cost reduction, product and geographic mix
items.quote: The Company's operating EBITDA margin improved by 90 bps at 11.5% as against 10.6% during last year first quarter and as you know, Q4 last year financial year 24 was 11.3%.

items.statement: TVS Credit book size crossed Rs. 26,351 crores, grew 20% YoY; customer base over 1.5 crores
items.quote: Book size crossed already 26,000 crores; the book size is Rs. 26,351 crores. Book grew by 20% over last year Q1.

items.statement: Q1 capex: Rs. 300 crores in TVS Credit, Rs. 100 crores in Norton, Rs. 30 crores in EV cycle business
items.quote: The majority of the investments in Q1 where credit service is about Rs. 300 crores. Norton was about Rs. 100 crores and the electric EV cycle business was about Rs. 30 crores and some small amount in TVS Digital.

items.statement: EV capacity not a constraint; 750 dealers covering 450+ cities for iQube; expanding month after month
items.quote: Capacity is not a problem. Only thing is, now when you have 3 variants, you have to look at. There are lot of common parts so but we have to look at wherever the delta is going up , but it's not a challenge.

items.statement: Price hike of 0.2% in Q1 and similar in Q2; commodity mixed with aluminum up but precious metals softening
items.quote: Yes, we took about 0.2% in quarter one. And some small increases we have taken in quarter two, which is also similar to quarter one about 0.2.

items.statement: Product and geographic mix contributed equally with material cost reduction to margin improvement; premium variants like Jupiter ZX, Grande growing
items.quote: Equal, between product mix, geographic mix and the material cost reduction is almost equal.

items.statement: TVS Credit expanded portfolio to used cars, consumer durables, gold loans, mid-corporate loans beyond 2W/3W financing
items.quote: TVS C redit services by leveraging cutting -edge technology and analytics offers products in expanded portfolio, financing for used cars, consumer durables, new and used cars, used commercial vehicles, mid-corporate loan, gold loan, apart from two-wheeler and three-wheeler financing

items.statement: EV exports to ASEAN leveraging Indonesia plant and ASEAN FTA advantage; Europe EV market slow with high inventory and discounts
items.quote: So, we don't foresee a problem because the moment you have in Indonesia, then there is an ASEAN FDA, so that advantage will help us. So, I cannot be able to give you a three -year road map, but we will definitely leverage our EV products from Indonesia to other markets.

items.statement: PLI incentive not recognized in Q1; SOP recently issued, finalizing revenue recognition; will disclose quarter-wise breakup when booked
items.quote: Only recently the government has issued an SOP in this regard. We are in the process of finalizing a revenue recognition for this purpose. Conservatively, we have not recognized PLI incentive.

items.statement: International business revenue Rs. 1,963 crores in Q1; parts revenue Rs. 846 crores; USD realization 83.2; Red Sea challenges affecting transit times
items.quote: In terms of IB total revenue, Rs. 1963 crores for Q1. Parts is about Rs. 846 crores.

items.statement: Other expenses at 11.4% of revenue due to variable costs (Rs. 60 cr), marketing (Rs. 87 cr), digital/innovation (Rs. 35 cr)
items.quote: There are three important things. One is variable nature, packing freight everything has gone up. It's about Rs. 60 crores. This is primarily because of the increase in turnover. And also the investment in brand building activities, which has resulted in increase in marketing expense of almost Rs. 87 crores.

items.statement: TVS Credit net worth Rs. 4,333 crores as of Q1 FY25 vs Rs. 3,865 crores March 2024; capital adequacy 18.9%; no further infusion planned
items.quote: Let me give the net worth of TVS Credit services as of March 24, it was Rs. 3865 and we are at Rs. 4333 crores now as far as net worth is concerned.

items.statement: Acquiring small NBFC with Rs. 5,500 crore book size; awaiting regulatory approvals; will be housed in CIC holding company
items.quote: Now as of now, we are waiting for the regulatory approvals for that new acquisition. It's a small NBFC with Rs. 5500 crores of book size.

items.statement: Norton investment ~Rs. 1,200 crores so far; 6 new models over 3 years; first launch end of CY2025 (FY26); India launch soon after
items.quote: The Norton investment is around Rs. 1200 crores.

items.statement: EV two-wheeler sales 52,000 units in Q1 FY25 vs 39,000 YoY; iQube now 5 variants across 3 battery options (2.2, 3.4, 5.1 kWh)
items.quote: EV two-wheeler sales is at 52,000 units as against last year Q1 of 39,000.

items.statement: Digital/analytics team 200+, software 150+, electronics similar; total 450-500 in new tech areas; ICE headcount not increased
items.quote: Digital analytics team, we have more than 200 people. Software, we have more than 150 people. Electronics, we have similar number. So, all put together, I would say that 450 to 500 people in the new areas of technology we have added.

items.statement: Europe e-mobility business facing slow economy, high inventory, heavy discounts; losses may persist for 1-1.5 years
items.quote: Europe has been very slow this year. Economy has been very slow. And what we have seen is the stock levels in the industry ha ve also gone up substantially. So, the discounts in the market are very high. So, that is the biggest reason.

items.statement: Fair value gain of Rs. 28 crores in PBT from TVS Supply Chain Solutions investment
