So, we are consistent on our dividend policy, and I think that that's something that will continue.

items.statement: Revenue grew 23% y-o-y to record ₹4.63 billion; EBITDA up 36% to ₹1.15 billion; PAT up 32% to ₹804 million
items.quote: The revenue for this quarter grew 23% over the previous year to reach a record quarterly level of ₹4.63 billion revenues. EBITDA and PBT reported a robust 36% and 37% y-o-y growth with a margin expansion of ~240 basis points.

items.statement: Export sales grew 19% to ₹2.16 billion, 47% of total sales; export order booking 66% of total
items.quote: Domestic sales increased by 27% to ₹2.47 billion, while export sales increased by 19% to ₹2.16 billion. Export as a percentage of sales stood at 47% in Q1 FY 25 as compared to 48% in the previous year.

items.statement: Order intake is lumpy quarter-to-quarter; management cautions against extrapolating Q1 export order booking for full year
items.quote: this growth of order book to ₹6.36 billion is truly remarkable, I would caution you when extrapolating this for the rest of the year, though we are confident that we will have good growth in both order booking as well as revenue for this current year

items.statement: Awaiting new government R&D scheme details; current R&D expensed as people costs cannot be capitalised
items.quote: Though we have to wait and see what the new R&D scheme of the Government will be. But suffice to say that the testing requires the actual capex into that.

items.statement: Enquiries now request shorter deliveries; domestic demand driven by steel, cement, waste-to-energy, distilleries, API, renewable investments
items.quote: We are, in fact, seeing customers wanting shorter deliveries, and we think that the domestic market will be a source of growth for Triveni Turbines, not only in the coming quarters, but in the years to come.

items.statement: No acquisitions mentioned; strategy focuses on organic growth, localisation via subsidiaries, and technology expansion
items.quote: We will increasingly be spending more on R&D. And those are data that will come out through our annual report, so you'll be able to see what the investments are. But suffice to say that the strategy as a company to be free cash flow generative will continue.

items.statement: Target 6-8 new restaurant openings in FY25, with 7-9 as bare minimum depending on real estate readiness
items.quote: We are looking at between six to eight restaurants, which are under fit outs, three, four of them almost, some by Durga Pooja in Calcutta, some in terms of, you know, Borivali, Oberoi Mall, we have two, three restaurants, thr ee restaurants there

items.statement: Internal target to reach 20-24% EBITDA margin by FY26
items.quote: We would target to be plus 20%, 22%, but in the range of 20% to 24% of EBITDA, sir.

items.statement: Expect 12-14% annual revenue growth over next five years organically, aiming to double/triple revenue
items.quote: So you're basically looking at around 12 % to 14% growth every year, right? Yes. Okay. And do you see an expansion in margin?

items.statement: Renovated outlets show 15-25% dine-in revenue growth; liquor contribution doubled from 6-7% to ~13-14% post-renovation
items.quote: So wherever we have undergone a renovation and introduced a new menu, new branding, new bar, we have seen anywhere between a 15 to 25 percent growth in the dine-in revenue, whereas our delivery revenue has also grown because of the new additions and the new brand refresh.

items.statement: New CEO to be inducted by end of FY25 (latest by March 2025)
items.quote: Maximum by the financial year. We are looking at the calendar year, but max would be within March, that is the fiscal year.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA grew 13.34% YoY; margins pressured by new store ramp-up (9-12 months to breakeven) and food cost inflation
items.quote: In the current quarter, we have done an EBITDA, which has grown by 13.34%. So at this rate, the moment we start opening restaurants, like Mr. Anjan has explained for the breakeven, etc, we would target to be plus 20%, 22%, but in the range of 20% to 24% of EBITDA, sir.

items.statement: Food cost inflation hurt margins; suppliers pushed back on cash discounts; pricing lever not fully pressed yet, tactical increases during seasons
items.quote: Inflation also hurt us, although we've tried our best to do device mechanisms to get cash discounts from people. We have suppliers who've been with us, b ut this time they were actually against the wall, so we had to adjust and accommodate them

items.statement: Revenue growth primarily volume-driven (renovation-led cover growth, liquor mix); pricing increases tactical and seasonal, not broad-based yet
items.quote: But yes, primarily with volumes, more to do with volumes rather than on the price, but exact number would be I don't have to share, don't have to add this point of time.

items.statement: Three growth engines: Asian brands (Mainland China, Asia Kitchen), liquor-led Episode One, and delivery (26% of revenue) with high AOV
items.quote: The three growth engines would be Asian expansion brands like Asia Kitchen by Mainland China and Mainland China. Wet Lead, which we call it liquor driven food supported, which would be Episode One. And the third one would be the delivery wing.

items.statement: Walter's Burger launched as delivery-only from existing kitchens; first physical outlet (900-1000 sq ft) at Borivali Oberoi Mall; pan-India rollout via all kitchens planned
items.quote: We have tried this in three units as of now in Mumbai City. And very soon, this would be PAN India through all our kitchens. And the profit margins are very high in this because we are not adding any cost.

items.statement: Sweet Bengal expanding via FMCG partners for shelf-stable sweets; products targeted for retail/online by end of FY25
items.quote: We are under works to set up our presence in other parts of India. But alongside that, we have also looked at FMCG partners who would be making and manufacturing sweets for our brand. And these are sweets with larger shelf life. So, by the end of this fiscal year, we should have the products ready, available at different stores, online retailers, and so on.

items.statement: Episode One brand to be reported separately once 3-4 outlets operational with high throughput
items.quote: Once we have at least three, four restaurants, where the throughput is very high, we would start showing separately, sir.

items.statement: Market headwind: 'revenge eating' faded; entire dining/QSR sector weak in Q1 FY25
items.quote: There's been one headwind from the market, which is the last thing I want to express, that the revenge eating , which used to be there, if you see the, I'm not saying that just because the others have not done so well, we should have also not done well, but it's an overall headwind, which has gone into the market, whether it's a QSR, or a dining restaurant, any on e of them, any listed chain or un

items.statement: Election-related bar closures (3-4 days avg) in Bangalore and other cities hurt June weekends
items.quote: For example, there were elections this time, so many places like Bangalore, etc., where food and beverage both, wherever you have a bar, you have to shut it. So all restaurants were shut for on an average of three to four days, with the results coming and counting, as you all know.

items.statement: Warrant forfeiture brought INR 52 cr; not treated as income, added to net worth; paid-up capital now INR 48.23 cr fully diluted
items.quote: Post the forfeiture, the amount which has come is INR52 crores f rom the warrants issue. We currently are having those invested part of the money which has been invested into mutual funds, and partly being utilized for the objects in the issue of renovation and the new restaurants

items.statement: Cash balance INR 163.84 cr as of 30 June 2024; no debt mentioned
items.quote: Sir, as of 30th June, we have INR163.84 crores.

items.statement: Inorganic acquisition only if target has positive EBITDA and potential; international oriental brand deferred to next year/18 months; Chourangi London/US opportunity needs INR 10-12 cr
items.quote: There was like this one which was coming international, which was a very good oriental brand. I don't want to name it. They've deferred their plans. In fact, they're coming maybe in next year or a year and a half. We've been in conversation with them.

items.statement: New CEO to be hired by end of FY25; proven turnaround experience in beverage/food
items.quote: we are going to be inducting a CEO. Finally, we've been able to get somebody of choice. So maybe within th is fiscal, by the end of the year, you will see somebody very competent who's coming in , to independently run the company and get us

items.statement: Same-store growth (SSG) positive in renovated outlets; delivery AOV among industry highest
items.quote: The brand is giving us better SSG wherever we are renovating. So we're very bullish about the fact that we will be able to, by and large, reach there.

items.statement: Real estate delays (Borivali Mall, Bangalore) could push FY25 openings to lower end of 7-9 range
items.quote: So 25 end, we are looking at bare minimum of around seven to nine, depending on Borivali Mall, which can supply us because that's been delayed beyond our comprehension. So and another one, which is in Bangalore.

items.statement: Gujarat entry planned within next 3 years with 2 stores
items.quote: Gujarat is on the plan in the next three years expa nsion. Yes, absolutely. So, it is in our map for the next three years. Within the next three years, we should have two stores running

items.statement: Hyderabad expansion: 2 new properties in process for Episode One
items.quote: Absolutely, sir. We're in process to get two new properties in Hyderabad.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book of 2,191 MW; executed 217 MW in Q1 FY25; secured order wins of 58.19 MW
items.quote: We have an unexecuted order book of 2,191 MW and we have successfully executed 217 MW during first quarter of FY2025. We have secured order wins totalling 58.19 MW peak for solar power projects reflecting our strong momentum in the renewable energy sector.

items.statement: Expects to execute roughly 75% of leftover order book (~1.8 GW) over next 9-12 months
items.quote: If you take 2.1 gigawatt and if you take 75%, we should be somewhere around 1.8 gigawatt roughly.

items.statement: Current bid pipeline stands at 15.5 GW; actively bidding for BESS, hybrid, RTC, pump storage projects
items.quote: Current bid pipeline is, today as we speak, is 15.5 gigawatt.

items.statement: No significant capex needed; can scale 3x without additional capital expenditure
items.quote: The good part of our business is that we don't need any significant capital expenditure. We are like a platform. If you want to give me today, like I have got 2 gigawatt, if you want to give me 3x business, I can deliver 3x business without adding any additio nal capital expenditure

items.statement: Order book split: 30-35% with module, 65-70% balance of systems; module procurement from parent at arm's length when competitive
items.quote: Well, I can give you a sense, we don't reveal the exact number, but we normally tend to be in the range of 30% to 35% with module and 65% to 70% without module, which we call as balance of systems as our projects.

items.statement: Customer base evolving from utility IPPs to include government entities (NTPC, SECI, SJVN, NHPC)
items.quote: So, customer base involvement has happened, you know, we used to significantly undertake projects from utility scale IPPs. Now, there's a government business which is increasing.

items.statement: Focus on domestic market; export markets not ruled out but no immediate plans
items.quote: Look, for us, the domestic market is quite compelling, but that doesn't mean we have ruled out export markets. But our focus right now, there's so much of opportunity that's happening in India.

items.statement: Module prices locked back-to-back upon order receipt; margins protected from module price volatility
items.quote: See, you know, we don't get into, first of all, long-term contracts on module because we, unless there's a firm order, we don't get into procurement. So, as soon as we get an order and our margins are visible there, we immediately lock in prices for modules. And it's back to back.

items.statement: Retention money typically 5-10% of contract value; no bank guarantees invoked to date
items.quote: So, the retention money is roughly, depends on contract to contract, largely in the range of 5%, but they can stretch up to 10% also. And as far as your second question is concerned, have any bank guarantees been triggered as of now? No, we haven't been triggered by any BGs invocation with us as of now.

items.statement: Average realization per MW between 1-1.2 crores; varies by turnkey vs balance of system contracts
items.quote: We, our average realization per megawatt is between 1 to 1.2 crores. So, when we speak average, it could be sometimes lower than 1 crore, it could be sometimes higher than 1 crore.

items.statement: 5B Maverick tie-up exclusive for India; test production complete; deployments expected in couple of months
items.quote: Yes. So, you know, 5B Maverick has completed its test production, etc. In coming couple of months, we might see some of the deployments in terms of 5B Maverick in Waaree Renewable. So, we have a tie up with them.

items.statement: No significant risks seen for upcoming quarter except monsoon rains; macro environment intact
items.quote: See, in upcoming quarter, it's too short and, we have already surpassed one month in that. Except for monsoon rains, we don't see any significant risk in the upcoming quarter that we need to address.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue INR 236.35 crores, up 83.31% YoY; EBITDA INR 41.08 crores, up 206.6% YoY; PAT INR 28.16 crores, up 208.51% YoY
items.quote: Revenue for the first quarter FY25 stood at INR 236.35 crores, representing a growth of 83.31% year-on-year as compared to 128.94 crores in first quarter of FY24. EBITDA for the first quarter of FY25 stood at INR41.08 crores as compared to INR13.40 crores in first quarter of FY2024, representing a growth of 206.6% year-on-year. Profit after tax during first quarter FY25 stood at INR 28.16 crores a

items.statement: 500 MW O&M portfolio currently; expects ~2 GW O&M by early next year as executed projects transition
items.quote: But the tail business, which is O&M, is kind of 500 megawatt for us, but the projects that we complete, by the end of the year, which will be like beginning of the next year, we will have almost like 2 gigawatt of O&M also available with us.

items.statement: Working capital managed through bank guarantees and letters of credit; no significant fund raise indicated
items.quote: We may need some bit of capital, little bit here and there for our working capital limits, but that we manage from our bank guarantees and letters of credits.

items.statement: Election-related disruptions caused 3-3.5 days of disturbance per town but also stimulated hidden consumption demand; green shoots visible in rural and urban markets with improved consumer confidence and employment outlook.
items.quote: So, there were, on an average, almost three to three and a half days of disturbance that we had across our towns, wherever we operate stores in the country. So, but ye s, largely, this is also definitely has been a big driver of economy, we believe, because there's been a lot of spending by the whole machinery, whether the government machinery or the political party machinery and the candidates

items.statement: Footfall grew 36% YoY in Q1; Tier 3 towns grew 11% and Tier 4 towns grew 19% in footfall, driven by natural customer pull without advertising push.
items.quote: Definitely we have seen better footfall. We were still unable to compare it with earlier 5 years before footfall, but still I don't think that the footfall is lower than the earlier footfalls.

items.statement: Apparel ASP declined 3% YoY due to product mix shift from zero weddings in North and strategic value-driven pricing in South; price correction exercise completed and ASPs expected to stabilize at current levels.
items.quote: The apparel ASP de grew by 3%, largely due to the product mix change as a fallout of zero weddings during the quarter in north. While in south, the ASP degrowth was a fallout of the strategic shift towards sharper and more value-driven product pricing that we have been trying to incorporate in the last two years.

items.statement: Offline gross margin healthy; overall gross margin down 60 bps due to LimeRoad revenue decline. Full-year offline gross margins expected to remain at last year's levels. Entity EBITDA 12.6% (V-Mart core 13.4%, Unlimited 18%) including INR 1
items.quote: Coming to margins, the gross margin for the offline business remained healthy, while the decrease in the revenues for LimeRoad business segment, which 100% flows in as margin optically reduced the overall gross margin by 60 basis points at company level.

items.statement: Targeting quarter-on-quarter reduction in LimeRoad EBITDA loss (20-30% per quarter); full-year LimeRoad loss expected to be less than 50% of prior year. Offline margin expansion not targeted in percentage terms; focus on rupee margin growth
items.quote: Yes, Shirish on the LimeRoad side we should definitely see quarter-on-quarter further reduction in the EBITDA loss, it may not be very substantial maybe 20%, 30%. The reduction in loss is something that I would definitely want to visualize and achieve.

items.statement: INR 26 crores spent in Q1 on new store openings and refurbishments. Full-year store opening runway maintained at 50-odd stores (gross), mostly opening in Q2 and Q3. Most unprofitable store closures completed; 3-4 regular closures may still
items.quote: On the capex side, we spent INR 26 crores during the quarter or paid out INR 26 crores majorly on new store openings and store refurbishments.

items.statement: Opened 7 new stores in Q1 (5 North V-Mart, 2 South Unlimited); closed 3 Unlimited stores. Net Unlimited store count at 78 after closing 19 and opening 23 in South over 3 years.
items.quote: During the quarter, the company opened seven new stores, five in North and two in South under Unlimited brand and closed three Unlimited stores.

items.statement: Inventory reduced by INR 144 crores QoQ, improving working capital cycle and freshness for festive season. Free cash flow INR 43 crores in Q1. Further improvement expected but seasonal inventory build-up in Q2.
items.quote: Inventory reduced by INR 144 crores quarter-on-quarter helping improve the working capital cycle and also it will help in improving freshness for the upcoming festive season even more.

items.statement: Freshness index improved ~10% through supply chain automation, better forecasting/allocation, and warehouse upgrades; assortment becoming more agile with fabric/pattern changes. Higher shrinkage provisions due to steep provisioning policies
items.quote: So, Nikunj, we've really worked very highly on the whole freshness index. And the freshness is the inventory freshness and that has been key to us. And that is also resulted due to some margin losses because we've also come on inventory prior to liquidate inventory at a discount. So, our freshness index has bettered by almost 10%.

items.statement: Manpower cost up 17% YoY due to annual increments, higher ESOP expense, and increased incentive payouts linked to sales growth. Attrition reduction efforts yielding results; variable cost structure allows scaling with performance.
items.quote: Coming to manpower cost. The manpower cost was up by 17% on the back of the annual increments slightly higher ESOP expenditure and also increased incentive payouts in line with the sales growth.

items.statement: NPS scores averaging >60 consistently over 8-9 months; 5 lakh+ Google reviews averaging 4.4+. 70% of V-Mart sales from repeat customers via analytics-driven customized communication (no points-based loyalty program).
items.quote: Our NPS scores, which we have started to track since the last almost eight, nine months has averaged at greater than 60 consistently. We've had more than five lakh Google reviews averaging 4.4 plus, and that is a strong testimony to the value proposition and the brand trust that the company is able to generate.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high; some national value-format players experiencing sluggishness. Premium/upper-middle segment under pressure. V-Mart gaining share via quality, fashion agility, and trust. Unlimited South stores outperforming legacy
items.quote: Yes. Sabya, I'm right. There is some pain with a couple of retailers also. They have not been going in line with what they have done. And not necessarily everyone is getting a lot of growth. So there is some pain in the market also, which we are seeing.

items.statement: Like-to-like sales growth strong in Q1 despite zero wedding days; sales per sq ft improved. Targeting 2 consecutive years of ~10% SSG to return to pre-COVID EBITDA margin of ~8.5% (pre-IndAS) by end of FY26.
items.quote: We discussed this also in the past. And I think we did guide towards growing at two consecutive years of around 10% SSG or high single-digit SSG to reach that level by then we should be able to get back to the pre-COVID EBITDA margin level of around 8.5%.

items.statement: Full-year store opening target: 50-odd gross stores (mostly Q2-Q3). LimeRoad losses to reduce quarter-on-quarter; full-year loss <50% of prior year. Offline margin % to be retained; rupee margin growth via volumes. No further price cuts at
items.quote: The runway for the year is still mai ntained at 50-odd stores, a large part of which will be open between quarter 2 and quarter 3

items.statement: Q2 typically loss-making due to monsoon and end-of-season sales; no margin expansion expected in Q2. Festive shift into late Q2/early Q3 creates uncertainty. Inflation at ~5% on high base still pressures INR 20k-35k household budgets.
items.quote: Quarter 2 typically is a loss-making quarter, and we should not see any margin expansion or any improvement there, but definitely we should see betterment coming in from quarter 3 again.

items.statement: LimeRoad Hubli pilot store (Tier 3) showing encouraging early response vs Unlimited; 18-19 days old. Omnichannel traction: online customers visiting offline. 4-5 more pilot stores planned in FY25 before budget allocation decision for FY26.
items.quote: we are trying to experiment that with our new brand, which is a LimeRoad brand, which is more digital, which is more nearer to the audience daily. So that's where we tested with one store until now we ar e learning and in that from the learning stage, you definitely want to experiment more with four, five more stores in this particular year

items.statement: Completed buyback of 10,27,777 shares at Rs 1,800 per share totalling Rs 185 crore; remaining cash reserve Rs 778 crore as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: The company has bought back 10,27,777 equity shares at Rs. 1,800 per share, totalling to Rs.185 crores. Following the completion of this buyback, the company's remaining cash reserve stands at Rs.778 crores as of June 30, 2024.

items.statement: No quarterly or annual EBITDA guidance given due to market volatility; long-term aim to outperform industry growth
items.quote: giving guidance on one particular year or one particular quarter, I think that's something which is difficult and now as you are seeing that geopolitical tensions, etc, are heightened and there is a lot of volatility in the market, and we refrain from giving any quarter or even annual guidance per se.

items.statement: TREM V norms timeline modified to 1 April 2026; all OEMs have nominated and product development is on track
items.quote: the time lines have been modified for 1 April 2026. And so far, all the OEMs have nominated in developing the products on track for 1 April 2026.

items.statement: Auto industry reported decent growth in Q1 FY25 driven by 2-wheeler revival in rural areas, marriage season, new model launches; PV up 5%, UV up 20.1%, CV up 3.8%, 2W up 19.8%
items.quote: For the quarter ended June 30, 2024, the auto industry reported decent growth, largely driven by a revival in demand for 2-wheelers in rural areas, the marriage season and the launch of new models across various segments, reflecting a positive trend for the industry.

items.statement: Consolidated gross profit margin expanded to 26.3% from 20.9% YoY; EBITDA margin expanded to 14% from 10.4% YoY
items.quote: Our gross profit margin for Q1FY '25 expanded to 26.3% from 20.90% in Q1 FY '24. Our EBITDA expanded to R s.96 crores in Q1FY '25 from Rs. 68 crores in Q1FY '24, and registered a growth of 40% Y-o-Y. The EBITDA margin for the quarter also experienced a robust expansion from 10.4% in Q1FY '24 to 14% in Q1FY '25.

items.statement: Gross profit outperformance driven by incremental business additions, favorable product mix, and maturity of RDE products vs low base in Q1 FY24
items.quote: the outperformance is, of course, one due to incremental business additions that we have, plus we've also had a favorable product mix and there has been maturity in our RD products, which was not the case in Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Very few Indian players can cater to targeted export emission segments; globally also limited competition in these tech-centered segments
items.quote: There are very few companies, maybe almost no companies in India that can cater to these segments, right? These are tech -centered segments that require a lot of R&D. So in India, it is very few companies that would be able to o r maybe none that can cater to a lot of the markets that we are addressing globally we are aware of 1,2 players

items.statement: Intent to return incremental cash via dividends, buybacks or other means; not to keep cash reserve much beyond current level
items.quote: And I think that trend would continue in terms of returning back to shareholders, intention is not to keep cash reserve much beyond what we have already. So all the incremental cash reserve that keeps coming in would be returned back, and that can be in the for m of dividends, buybacks or anything else, that comes about as we go

items.statement: Targeting substantial market share in TREM V tractor/off-highway market (currently <5% of sales) and CV 3-4L ICE segment (currently 0% share)
items.quote: for the next 5 years, our focus on growth is first onto the TREM V market or the tractor market currently, tractors, off-highway exports, all put together contributes under 5% of our sales. With TREM V coming in, we are expecting a very good market share there and would become a very significant part of our sales. In addition to that, in commercial vehicles, ICE 3 to 4-liter segment on the stand-a

items.statement: 2W EV battery pack JV with Kinetic: segment attractiveness diminished due to AIS Amendment 3, subsidy cuts, Chinese competition, high field quality risk; cautious, no capex deployment or revenue timeline
items.quote: the 2-wheeler EV market, I think that in itself has evolved a lot over the last maybe 1 or 2 years. And many things have happened regarding battery packs and then, of course, the market in itself. So one, the AIS Amendment 3, the compliances have come in, plus 2-wheeler EV subsidies have been reduced, and there is a lot of competition that has come in from China, from many, many, many small player

items.statement: Export margins better than domestic but working capital higher; ROCE similar or slightly better on net basis
items.quote: in exports, the terms of business, I would guess, is basically EBITDA loss, right? And what we are seeing is that the margins are much better in exports than in Indian business. However, the working capital requirement in exports is also higher than India n business. On a net basis, if you neutralize a higher margin and higher working capital requirement, from a ROCE perspective, it is similar or

items.statement: No debt planned for M&A funding; cash reserves and land monetization sufficient
items.quote: So most likely, we would not require any debt at this juncture and funding any kind of for M&A. And we do have additional land parcels available, which we are looking to monetize and that, of course, is in addition to the cash reserves.

items.statement: CEV norms coming Jan 2025; company has adjacency business but market smaller than tractor/export opportunity
items.quote: The CEV that's coming in Jan 2025? Piyush: Yes. Aashim Relan: So we have business there, especially on the adjacency front, we have a good business there. However, the CEV market compared to the tractor market and export market is a smaller one

items.statement: Management withdrew FY25 volume growth guidance of 8% after 15% degrowth in Q1 and expects to struggle to match last year's volumes in Q2; will reassess after monsoon
items.quote: We already had 15% degrowth in Q1, right? Keshav: Right. Deepak Khetrapal: Q2, as of now, I think we'll struggle to make the same as last year. So if the first half of the year does not give us the required growth, obviously, the full year forecast needs to be relooked at

items.statement: FY25 capex estimated at INR200-300 crores vs earlier INR1,000 crores guidance; Chittapur INR100 crores, Sarni INR25-30 crores, Rajasthan land INR100 crores, Devapur forest clearance payment INR150 crores
items.quote: Again, the first question sorry I just say a couple of maybe INR200 crores to INR300 crores not more than that.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton increased to INR750 in Q1 FY25 from INR650 in Q1 FY24 despite 15% volume degrowth, driven by stable pricing and lower fuel costs
items.quote: I don't think there's any one company in the industry which would have reported an increase in EBITDA per ton over last year's same quarter. And we were at about INR650 last year, we were around INR750 this year

items.statement: Power and fuel cost per ton of cement fell to INR1,337 in Q1 FY25 from INR1,571 in Q1 FY24 and INR1,351 in Q4 FY24; blended fuel cost INR1,785 per million kcal vs INR2,100 last year
items.quote: In Q1, the power and fuel costs for us are down to the INR1,337 per metric ton of cement, which is down from INR1,571 in Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Cement prices in July down 2.5-3% sequentially; July and early August volumes and pricing remain very soft due to persistent rains
items.quote: I would say it is in the region 2.5%, 3% in July over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Q1 demand severely impacted by national elections, extreme heat wave halting construction, and heavy June rains across all markets; Telangana and Karnataka seeing high double-digit degrowth, Maharashtra down 5.5%
items.quote: What's unusual about Q1 quarter this year has been the fact that even Maharashtra, total demand, including Mumbai city, the demand is down over last year.

items.statement: Management expects sharp demand recovery post-monsoon due to pent-up construction and repair work from heavy rain damage, but signals of pickup in Telangana yet to emerge
items.quote: We do expect the demand to rise sharply once the rains stop, because the construction activity has been held up. There's a lot of pent-up, catch-up work that needs to be done

items.statement: Premium cement share reached 23% of total sales in Q1 FY25, nearing 25% target; OPC share remains high at 45-47% of unblended cement due to weak trade demand
items.quote: In Q1 of this year the overall proportion of our premium cements put together has reached 23% and we are very close from the beginning when we started, our target initially was 10%, then we said we want to go to 25%

items.statement: Industry leaders' aggressive capacity additions (organic and acquisitions) and volume-first strategy keeping prices low; pan-India utilization struggling to reach 70%
items.quote: The only way prices become stable is when people accept the fact that trying to sell to the market more volume at a lower price does not help anyone.

items.statement: Green power share reached 24% in Q1 FY25 (highest ever) from 12% last year; waste heat recovery contributed INR9 crores, solar INR2.5 crores in Q1; Chittapur solar expected by mid-September
items.quote: Our total, I would say, green power component in Q1 has reached a high of 24%, which is ever highest for us

items.statement: Chittapur expansion (3 mt cement) and Sarni grinding unit (2 mt) combined capex ~INR2,000 crores; Devapur expansion (2 mt clinker + 1 mt grinding + WHR + wagon tippler) estimated INR1,700-1,800 crores later
items.quote: Chittapur was INR1,500 crores and 500 for Sarni. So, then in terms of project, the y are two different projects, the total capex will be about 2,000

items.statement: Chittapur environment clearance application submitted; expects committee hearing by end-August; Sarni term alteration informally approved by MP Power Gen Board, awaiting formal letter; Devapur forest clearance at Minister level in Telangana
items.quote: We are still expecting that, hopefully, in the meeting that they will hold perhaps towards the end of August, our applications would be coming up before the committee for presentation.

items.statement: Maintained price realizations stable (down only ~1% YoY) while industry lost realizations; refused B2B orders below contribution threshold; aligned trade prices with Category A brands
items.quote: We've seen industry results. And I think any company which operates in our markets, if you look at, they have actually lost realizations per ton on the cement they have sold. We have more or less kept it stable.

items.statement: Trade share 44%, B2B 56% in Q1; lead distance 300-320 km maintained; July volumes very soft, struggling to match last year's Q2 volumes
items.quote: Trade share for us -- I did mention that B2B sales is perhaps 56% and balance 44% would be Trade, yes.

items.statement: Rajasthan limestone land acquisition still in negotiations, no deals closed; Devapur forest clearance payment of INR150 crores critical for Stage 2 conversion this year
items.quote: No, we have still -- we are in negotiations, but we've not closed any deals for the land in Rajasthan. Not till now.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 700 bps YoY to 20.1% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin improved by 700 basis points as compared to last Q1. So from 13.1%, we have improved it to 20.1% for the quarter.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin guidance maintained at around 18% despite Q1 strength
items.quote: But as is basis, currently, we are maintaining our guidance of around 18%.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance raised to 62-62.5% for FY25 from 61% last year
items.quote: last year, our gross margin was 61% this year , considering the improving product mix and better margin in the US market and also the further investment in API, we see it improve -- further improvement of around, say, 150 basis points in our gross margin for the full year

items.statement: API price reductions on dapagliflozin, sitagliptin and paracetamol driving margin improvement
items.quote: We had, say, for example, dapagliflozin, we had sitagliptin. These are now substantial value products for us, and we have a significant reduction in some of these molecules on the API pricing.

items.statement: Penicillin G prices not softening; seeing marginal increase from China suppliers
items.quote: In fact, in the recent times, I'm seeing that Pen G prices are even seeing a marginal increase. So unless we see the large Indian players coming up in market with the offerings, I don't think we are seeing softening in the China suppliers on the PenG.

items.statement: Domestic formulation growth in line with IPM at 8.4% YoY; outperformed in 6 therapies
items.quote: According to IQVIA, we have outperformed – we have registered a growth of 8.4% YoY compared to the IPM growth which grew at 8.7%.

items.statement: Domestic business growth guidance maintained at 8-10% in line with market
items.quote: I'm expecting the mark et to grow somewhere between 8% to 10% and should be similar for us as well

items.statement: Domestic growth driven by volume 1.5%, new launches 2.5%, price 2.5%
items.quote: So in domestic, we have had a volume growth of close to some 1.5%. We have -- the new launches have contributed to around 2.5%. And balances are, I would say, price growth, which is again close to 2.5%.

items.statement: US generics seeing continued single-digit price erosion
items.quote: So like I always maintained, the US generic is seeing a single-digit price erosion at trend continues even for this quarter.

items.statement: US business expected to grow single-digit in FY25
items.quote: So in terms of our U.S. growth, I've always maintained, we are looking at a s ingle-digit growth from U.S. market

items.statement: US launches: Suprep in Q1, dabigatran in Q2 with revenue impact from Q3-Q4
items.quote: In terms of the new launches, we launched in generic Suprep in Q1. In Q2, we have just introduced dabigatran. And among the significant ones, I think that should be the one which we are pretty hopeful which should start showing impact on revenue in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Medical devices initiative signed for hip/knee replacement technology; will impact EBITDA in FY25
items.quote: we have also entered into medi cal devices. We have signed an agreement with companies in the U.S. from where we will get the technology for knee replacement, and we are getting to this resource, and we definitely it will take some time to breakeven. So this business will also actually impact the EBITDA margin in the current year

items.statement: Enzene Biosciences opex INR90 crores in Q1 including depreciation; rising INR20-25 crores per quarter
items.quote: So in quarter 1, there was an expense of around INR90 crores as opex for Enzene, including the depreciation.

items.statement: Forex gain of INR15 crores from Chile booked in other income, not EBITDA
items.quote: But this is mostly from Chile in this quarter that we have had it to the tune of INR15 crores as a forex gain. So that is to be put a part of very -- so that is not part of EBITDA. So that features in the other operating income rather than -- sorry, other income, other income and not in EBIDTA.

items.statement: R&D spend 4.1% of sales in Q1; full year guided at 4.5-5% of sales
items.quote: The first quarter is always within the range of 4.1% because most of our filings are loaded towards Q3 and Q4. So, the annual spend will be within the range of 4.5% to 5% and in terms of absolute.

items.statement: Other expenses to increase INR100-110 crores per quarter from Q2 due to R&D phasing and new initiatives
items.quote: So other expenses some -- on top of quarter 1, it'll increase by around INR100 crores, INR110 crores every quarter.

items.statement: Tax rate guidance revised to 11-13% for FY25 from earlier 13-15%
items.quote: So it will be in the range of 11% to 13% for the full year.

items.statement: Income tax survey: refiled returns for 6 years; no demand received yet; assessment pending
items.quote: Income Tax Department asked us to again file the return, and we have already refiled the return for last six year. Now we'll start the assessment. And once the assessment will get completed then only we'll come to know about the result. So, till date, we have not received any demand against the survey, which has happened in the month in last year.

items.statement: Baddi facility US FDA Form-483 observations successfully resolved
items.quote: We are pleased to announce the successful resolution of all the observations that we had received from Baddi facility. This exemplifies our unwavering commitment to adherence and regulatory compliance.

items.statement: Mirabegron launch delayed to 2026-27 pending patent litigation outcomes per settlement agreement
items.quote: So unless the final outcome of all the litigations on the patent are clear, we would not be -- because we are bound by the settlement agreement, I don't see it getting launched in -- before the agreement date and which will be somewhere, I would say, 26 or 27, somewhere around that time.

items.statement: Non-US international business (RoW) targeting mid-teens growth over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So I maintained the non-U.S. business, we would see mid-teens kind of growth even in the coming years, and that is what we are focusing on. And we will see that coming over a period of next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Australia and Chile supply chain issues in Q1; sales deferred not lost; recovery expected in coming quarters
items.quote: No, it is just for this quarter, we were not able to supply a particular product because of our supply chain issues. And now we have resolved those issues. In the coming quarters, we will recover some -- I mean, large part of that sale.

items.statement: Medical representative count 12,700 excluding managers; focus on productivity improvement not headcount reduction
items.quote: So 12,700 is what our count is, and managers would be over and above.

items.statement: Consolidated MR productivity ~INR5 lakhs; targeting 8-10% top line growth via productivity gains
items.quote: So our consolidate d productivity is at around 5 lakhs , okay? And we are not looking at any significant addition to the numbers that we have. And we have a top line growth aspiration of close to 8% to 10

items.statement: Non-NLEM portfolio price increases realizing 5-6% annually vs allowed 10%
items.quote: So on non -NLEM portfol io, we are allowed to take a price increase of 10% but we realize because of the inventory, et cetera, and some anti -market driven pricing pressures. Generally, we get 5% to 6% increase on the annualized basis

items.statement: Strong intent for strategic inorganic acquisitions; cash reserves available for funding
items.quote: We have today a cash or a decent cash reserve. So I would say, which is I think and whenever any opportunity comes our way, we can figure out the routes to funding to get those to fund those opportunities. At this stage, so there's nothing more that I can share, but I can just tell you that there is a very strong intent to look at inorganic options as well.

items.statement: Product mix shift to anti-infectives in Q2-Q3 may impact margins by ~2%
items.quote: So in terms of the product mix change, might impact margins for two quarters, by say, 2%, that's the kind of estimate that we have and that we may see.

items.statement: Expects volume growth of ~18% and revenue growth of ~35% in Visa & Consular business to continue for the rest of FY25
items.quote: we have done a growth in this quarter about 18% in the volumes. And overall, about 35% on the revenue, we believe that will continue and the growth in the EBITDA should also be on the same line as for the existing business is concerned.

items.statement: Visa & Consular EBITDA margin expanded 600 bps to 29% in Q1 FY25 driven by self-run model transition, higher service fees, and value-added services
items.quote: EBITDA grew by a robust 71% Y-o-Y to INR 121.3 crores in Q1 FY '25 with a margin of 29%, which expanded by 600 basis points as compared to 23% in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Management sees further upside in blended EBITDA margins for FY25 after iDATA integration, though exact number not quantified
items.quote: The exact number, we don't know. But definitely, we see further upside in our margins. If you see last year, we did 21%, year before we were at 15%-16%. So constantly, the EBITDA margins have been growing and definitely, after this acquisition, we definitely feel that EBITDA margins can grow further.

items.statement: Capex incurred for self-run model transition reflected in higher depreciation and employee costs, not directly in EBITDA
items.quote: if you see, our depreciation and our employee costs have gone up compared to the last quarters, and only due to this that we have got people on our own payroll as well as we have invested in new facilities. Therefore, the depreciation has also gone up.

items.statement: Won 14-15 new contracts in last 1-1.5 years, mostly from competitors; more governments outsourcing for first time in pipeline
items.quote: If you see our competitors, we have won 14 to 15 new contracts in the last 1 to BLS International Services Limited August 06, 2024 1.5 years, and most of it was from the competition. Some governments have outsourced for the first time also, that most of this was winning more market

items.statement: iDATA acquisition completed for INR 720 crores; will consolidate from Q2 FY25; iDATA did INR 246 crores revenue and INR 144 crores EBITDA in CY2023
items.quote: We have also announced the completion of iDATA acquisition recently, for a consideration of INR 720 crores. This is a large milestone for the company and we will witness the synergystic benefits from Q2 onwards. iDATA is a profitable company and recorded INR246 crores revenue with INR144 crores in EBITDA in calendar year 2023.

items.statement: Board passed enabling resolution to raise up to INR 2,000 crores via equity (QIP/other modes) for future acquisitions; no concrete M&A plan yet
items.quote: this was an enabling resolution that we passed in the Board meeting and in the follow-up AGM we wish to take that up. But definitely, we are constantly looking at growth opportunities of the company. Organically, we are looking at new contracts, newer geographies and inorganically these acquisitions.

items.statement: Anticipates significant boost to international tourism and visa demand from travel-facilitating measures, rising air capacity and connectivity
items.quote: With increased business confidence and travel-facilitating measures and rising air capacity and connectivity across the globe, we anticipate significant boost to the international tourism and corresponding demand of visa applications.

items.statement: No sizable revenue exposure to countries with current geopolitical tensions; operates in 70+ countries providing diversification
items.quote: We operate currently in a global scenario, where there is every year or every quarter or somewhere we have geo-political tension keeps happening. So, I don't think on an annual basis, this affects our business. We are operating in 70-plus countries.

items.statement: Service fee increases from new contracts at higher charges and re-tendered existing contracts at higher charges driving margin expansion
items.quote: We have gotten an increase in service fee. We have won new contracts at higher service charges, even though existing contract that we re-tendered we have won at higher service charges. So the service fee has increased.

items.statement: Digital Services EBITDA margin expanded 358 bps to 15.2% in Q1 FY25 despite flat revenue; added new banks and CSPs
items.quote: The EBITDA surged by 31% Y-o-Y to INR 11.9 crores in Q1 FY '25, against INR 9.1 crores in Q1 FY '24. The EBITDA margins at 15.2% were up 358 basis points from 11.6% in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents of INR 1,290 crores as of June 30, 2024; used for iDATA and Aadifidelis acquisitions post quarter-end
items.quote: The company continues to maintain a strong balance sheet with cash and cash equivalent of INR1,290 crores as on 30th June 2024, and strong return ratios with ROE of 29% and ROCE of 32% on an annualized basis.

items.statement: BLS E-Services IPO funds (INR 300 crores unutilized) to be used for Aadifidelis acquisition, IT infrastructure, e-stores, and further acquisitions
items.quote: the IPO funding we are going to use for this acquisition, which is in the final stages now. We are signing a definitive agreement. And once that happens, we will be utilizing for that as well as the balance will be used for the growth capital of the BLS e-services.

items.statement: Company has natural FX hedge as all contracts are in USD or Euro; collects local currency equivalent at achieved rate
items.quote: as far as the exchange rate, we have a natural hedge that our all contracts are in USD or in Euro. So, we collect the equivalent local currency matching with the achieved rate. So, we don't have an exchange rate risk inherited into the system.

items.statement: Pakhajan facility commissioned on April 9, 2024 with 20,000 MTPA initial capacity; total capacity now 32,500 MTPA
items.quote: I am pleased to announce the successful completion and commissioning of our Pakhajan facility on April 9, '24. This facility is spread over 42 acres with an initial install capacity of 20,000 metric tons per annum. With this facility, our total capacity now stands at 32,500 metric tons.

items.statement: Expect customer approvals in next few months and >90% capacity utilization in FY26
items.quote: As we had earlier mentioned, we expect our customer approval to be obtained in the next few months and expect to utilize more than 90% capacity in FY '26.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to stabilize to previous levels by Q3-Q4 FY25 and grow further
items.quote: We expect the EBITDA margin will stabilize back to the previous level by Q3-Q4 of this year, which we expect it to grow further.

items.statement: Debt to EBITDA expected to be close to 3x by end of FY25
items.quote: We expect that the debt to EBITDA will be close to three by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target of INR 900+ crores with 19-20% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We are quite confident that we should be able to achieve what we have projected since potential of about INR900 crores plus in FY '25.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target of INR 1,200-1,300 crores with 90%+ capacity utilization
items.quote: We are expecting a revenue between INR1,200 crores to INR1,300 crores in FY'26 because of the selling price.

items.statement: Repair capex of INR 5-10 crores for FY25; no further expansion capex planned until 70%+ utilization achieved
items.quote: Well, generally company spend on a repair capex is about INR5 crores to INR10 crores not more than that for this year. And for the further capex we have not planned anything yet.

items.statement: Volume growth of ~27% YoY in Q1; export volumes grew despite shipping issues; export share 61% of revenue
items.quote: We achieved a notable volume growth of approximately 27% year-on-year. Despite current shipping issues, we have grown our export volumes. Export contributed 61% of our revenue.

items.statement: Trials ongoing with existing and new customers in export and domestic markets; long-term supply agreements expected post-trials
items.quote: We are working with a number of customers in an export and also into the domestic field. Couple of them are new customers who we have identified in the past who could be on our roll call and a couple of them are already existing but we can expand the line with them with the new capacity available.

items.statement: Current debt level sufficient for working capital needs; positive cash flow expected in FY25 as selling and raw material prices drop
items.quote: I think we will be able to manage with the current debt level. We don't expect too much requirement. Purely because of the sales, the selling prices drop and also the buying raw material prices drop. So the overall projection is not something which can be managed with the current thing. And also we will have some positive cash flow generated during this year.

items.statement: Competition from Europe, North America, China; benefit from Make in India and alternate supply chain preference
items.quote: Well, there is some competition come from Europe there is a competition from North America and also there is a competition from China itself. So, competition is always there. We are not in the monopoly zone anymore in today's world. But we are in a unique place with the government support make in India people preference of an alternate supply chain, which is helping us

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty may affect container availability and export stabilization timeline
items.quote: But we can't say due to the geopolitical situation what is going on currently. 100% nobody can say what is going to happen.

items.statement: Focus on industrial segment; expanding in South America, Middle East beyond Europe and USA
items.quote: Well, currently our focus is purely on to the industrial segment of the range and that is where we want to grow. Not only in Europe, USA we are also trying to establish ourselves in like South America, the Middle East and many other regions we are trying to capture.

items.statement: USP is specialty/performance chemicals not commodity; enables 400bps margin premium over largest competitor
items.quote: Well, we are not into the commodity, number 1. We are more into the performance and the so-called specialty chemistry within the rubber the space or also into the lubricant space. And a lot of our specialty chemicals are really specialized in that nature. And that is helping us to hold up the margin and allow us to grow.

items.statement: New customers prefer Yasho for better pricing, alternate supply chain needs, and proven delivery reliability since 2020
items.quote: Well, there are multiple reasons, but definitely one of the reasons could be the better pricing by Yasho offering to them. Number two, as I said earlier, that the people are looking for an alternate supply chain. So that's one of the major reasons also. And I think the last couple of years, since from pandemic 2020, we have proven ourselves that we can deliver the material despite of all the chall

items.statement: India auto segments grew YoY in Q1 FY25 except commercial vehicles; 2-wheelers up 19.6%, 3-wheelers 9.4%, PVs 5.8%, CVs down 1.4%.
items.quote: In Q1 FY'25, strong domestic macro factors resulted in most of the automobile segment growing on a year-on-year basis other than the commercial vehicle segment. The 2-wheeler segment grew by 19.6%, 3 -wheelers grew by 9.4%, passenger vehicles grew by 5.8%, but the commercial vehicles degrew by 1.4%.

items.statement: Overseas 2-wheeler markets (US, Europe) showed negative growth; Asian growth driven by low-end segments, premium struggling.
items.quote: The overseas market especially the U.S. and the European market also showed negative growth for 2 -wheelers. In the Asian region, the growth was largely driven by low -end segments and the premium segment continues to struggle for growth in this region.

items.statement: Overseas business H1 FY25 tough, gradual recovery expected over next 1-2 years.
items.quote: We explained it in the previous calls also that H1 is going to be tough for us for the overseas business. But thereafter, we should see a gradual recovery over the next 1 to 2 years.

items.statement: Consolidated PBT 2.9% in Q1 FY25 vs 3.6% YoY; EBITDA 9.1%; India gross margins improved ~1% YoY excluding Q4 government incentive.
items.quote: Coming to the profitability, we reported 2.9% PBT in Q1 compared to 3.6% last year. And EBITDA was at 9.1%.

items.statement: India margins to improve from current levels in outer quarters; overseas margins to stay flat; overall margin improvement expected.
items.quote: I mean, I don't want to put a number to it, obviously, but margins should certainly improve from the current level in the outer quarters as far as the India business is concerned. Overseas should more or less stay at this level. So on the whole, we should see improvement from the current levels.

items.statement: Renewable energy Phase 1 (36.6 MW solar) from Q2 FY25 to yield INR 200M annual recurring savings (~0.3% margin); Phase 2 (14 MW) approved for FY25 adding INR 70-80M annual savings.
items.quote: The first phase of this initiative is expected to result in 36.6 megawatts of power of sourcing from solar power starting from quarter 2 of this year and is expecte d to give us an annual recurring saving of around INR 200 million.

items.statement: Two new plants commissioned in Maharashtra (plastic moulding, fuel tanks for Bajaj Auto); start-up costs significant in Q1, losses to reduce significantly in Q2, margins from Q3.
items.quote: It's a significant number. And these are two plants which we have started in our plastic moulding business and also we're doing some fuel tanks in Bajaj Auto. So these are the plants we've set up for Bajaj Auto within -- in Bajaj Auto. And this is where I think these are the start -up costs. But going forward, we see that these losses in Q2 will be sig nificantly reduced. And then we start making

items.statement: Lifetime new business wins INR 7,959M in Q1 FY25; cumulative order wins expected to yield annual peak revenue ~INR 1,416M; 48% from EV players, 71% 4-wheeler, 85% non-Bajaj.
items.quote: In quarter 1 of FY'25, our lifetime new business wins was over INR7,959 million, the cumulative order wins are expected to result in an annual peak revenue levels of around INR1,416 million, nearly 48% of our business wins in this quarter has com e from the EV players revenue from supplying to EV players in quarter 1 FY '25 was approximately 8% of our overall revenues.

items.statement: EV revenue ~8% of total in Q1 FY25 (7.8% per CFO); 2-3 wheelers 78% of revenue; Bajaj Auto 44.6% of revenue.
items.quote: revenue from supplying to EV players in quarter 1 FY '25 was approximately 8% of our overall revenues.

items.statement: Two EV powertrain customers beyond Bajaj (one local, one foreign); SOPs expected within FY25; wins across lighting, painted polymers, full-service polymer parts for passenger cars.
items.quote: have 2 EV powertrain customers beyond Bajaj for whom development is ongoing. One is local, 1 is foreign. So those SOPs also, we would expect within this financial year

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR 668M in Q1 FY25 to ~INR 9,160M; net debt/equity 0.59; net debt/EBITDA ~1.3x; RoCE ~16.3%.
items.quote: This resulted in a n et debt reducing by further INR 668 million in quarter 1 of FY '25 and our net debt to equity has improved to 0.59.

items.statement: Debt reduction trend ~INR 50-60 crore per quarter; to continue from free cash flow, barring potential land purchases for growth.
items.quote: So on the average, anywhere between INR50 crores to INR60 crores reduction per quarter has been the trend. So we should be able to continue this. Except that in between, we may have to invest some amount in terms of buying some additional land for our future growth.

items.statement: Interest cost ~INR 44 crore in Q1; reduction of ~INR 3 crore vs Q4 after adjusting for lease reclassification; further reduction expected as debt declines and one-time items cease.
items.quote: If you see Q4 number, Q4 interest cost. It also had a benefit of reclassification of leasing interest between interest line item and the other rental expense. So that way, if you really see in terms of the actual interest cost, there was a reduction of about INR3 crores. already between Q4 and Q1.

items.statement: EV 2-wheeler volumes grew 6.4% sequentially in Q1 FY25; new plant ramp-ups and EV volume growth expected to drive operating leverage in H2.
items.quote: In the current quarter, on a sequential basis, EV 2-wheeler actually registered a growth of close to 6%, 6.4%.

items.statement: Commodity price adjustments impacted revenue in Q1; described as normal transitory adjustments that should correct in outer quarters.
items.quote: These are some of the normal adjustments or price changes which keep happening in this industry, as you know. So this is again a transitory phase. So it should get corrected in the outer quarters.

items.statement: Increasing sourcing from renewable energy; Phase 1 (36.6 MW solar) from Q2 FY25, Phase 2 (14 MW) approved for FY25.
items.quote: We also mentioned earlier that we are increasing sourcing from renewable sources. The first phase of this initiative is expected to result in 36.6 megawatts of power of sourcing from solar power starting from quarter 2 of this year.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded 1 notch to AA- (long-term); short-term rating A1+; net debt/equity 0.59, net debt/EBITDA ~1.3x, RoCE ~16.3%.
items.quote: This improvement has resulted in an upgrade to the credit rating of the company by 1 notch to AA minus for long term, and our short -term rating is at a top notch, which is A1 plus.

items.statement: Global economic uncertainty (geopolitical issues, US recession fears) persists; overseas volume recovery may take 1-2 years.
items.quote: The global economy continues to remain uncertain due to geopolitical issues in Europe and Asia and recession fears in the U.S.

items.statement: Overseas 4-wheeler degrowth driven by IMES (non-auto) and Romania electronics plant due to Europe situation; domestic 4-wheeler flat YoY.
items.quote: So the significant decline happened actually in 2 of our plants abroad, 1 is EMIS and the other was in our Romania Electronics plant, where we saw a substantial decline in the volumes because of the situation in Europe.

items.statement: Management says 20% topline growth is a sensible way to model the company for the next few years.
items.quote: I think that 20% topline growth is a sensible way to model our company at this moment, and we will continue to improve our margins, thus hopefully deliver higher growth on the bottomline.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 20.1% in Q1 FY2025, up from prior periods.
items.quote: We achieved an EBITDA margin of 20.1%, delivering a strong operating margin expansion.

items.statement: Management targets gradual increase in operating profit margins for the rest of FY2025.
items.quote: As we look ahead to the rest of FY2025, we are poised to further accelerate our growth trajectory with gradual increase in operating profit margins and will continue to deliver greater value to all our shareholders.

items.statement: India and Emerging Markets revenue grew 24.8% y-o-y, contributing 73.2% of quarterly revenue.
items.quote: Our growth for India and Emerging markets combined, was about 24.8% y-o-y.

items.statement: Developed Markets revenue grew 36.9% y-o-y, contributing 26.8% of quarterly revenue.
items.quote: Our growth in Developed Markets was about 36.9% y-o-y and it contributed 26.8% to our quarterly revenues.

items.statement: CPCU conversions reached 90.8 million at a rate of Rs. 57.0, driving CPCU revenue of Rs. 5,177 million, up 37% y-o-y.
items.quote: Our CPCU business delivered about 90.8 million conversions during the quarter, at a CPCU rate of Rs. 57.0 that helped us achieve CPCU revenue of Rs. 5,177 million, an increase of 37.0% y-o-y.

items.statement: Gaming vertical led significant growth in both emerging and developed markets.
items.quote: We are seeing a n overall broad-based growth. But I would say that the growth in the gaming vertical, both in emerging markets and developed markets has been quite significant.

items.statement: Management expects CPCU rates to improve over the long term through premium inventory investments and deeper ecosystem partnerships.
items.quote: You will see a better CPCU premium pricing, and we would be able to work better in the market to attract the top dollars. Hopefully, helping us to achieve the higher margin that we intend to deliver because margin expansion is an important execution focus for us for the next few years.

items.statement: Inventory and Data Cost stood at 61.6% of revenue; management is comfortable defending this range.
items.quote: Our Inventory and Data Cost stood at 61.6% of revenue from operations in this quarter, while we continue our platform calibrations on to premium inventories, touchpoints and deeper ecosystem-level partnerships.

items.statement: Employee expenses expected to remain flattish despite revenue growth due to integration efficiencies and GenAI adoption.
items.quote: So as business expands, I would expect to keep our employee expenses largely flattish, at least for the foreseeable future. You will see much higher growth in revenues and a flattish to low growth in the employee expenses.

items.statement: No material changes in collection risk; working capital management remains efficient.
items.quote: We continue to prioritize efficient working capital management and as such there were no material changes in the collection risk.

items.statement: Google has decided not to deprecate third-party cookies and delayed Privacy Sandbox; Affle is prepared and sees status quo for several years.
items.quote: Google has clearly indicated even after 4+ years since it announced that it will deprecate cookies, it couldn’t overcome the complexities and challenges associated with its own privacy initiatives. Co nsequently Google’s privacy sandbox project is also delayed

items.statement: Not in a rush for M&A; will pursue if right target adds disproportionate value; open to developed or emerging markets.
items.quote: We are not in a rush. We have just completed YouAppi's integration. YouAppi is 1 year and full integration has been done in less than a year. So if we find the right acquisition target, we certainly would but we are not in a rush.

items.statement: Investing in premium inventory (CTV, iOS, premium Android) and deeper ecosystem partnerships to drive higher CPCU rates and margins.
items.quote: we are also investing into premium inventories . I see that effect being utilized from a margin perspective, right . Overall, the way Affle is strategizing itself is that we are going more and more premium in a way we are working with different strategic platforms, be it the app stores or the alternate of app stores

items.statement: Real Money Gaming impact in India is neutralized and considered over; new normal established.

items.statement: Albuterol share erosion expected when Amphastar launches

items.quote: There is a n upcoming hearing on the ‘780 August 7, 2024 patent, actually today. So we are monitoring that as well. But we expect to ramp up the product

items.statement: Respimat and Ellipta platform exhibit batches planned in FY25, filing early FY26
