items.quote: I'm pleased let you know that we launched Na rayana Health Insurance in Mysore ass we have said in late June with our first product it's called Aditi, the headline feature which is providing 1 crore cover for surgeries for a price of about ₹10,000 for a family of four.

items.statement: Administrators assessed on 80-20 fixed-variable pay structure tied to financial parameters, cost control, digitization, length of stay reduction, throughput improvement

items.quote: Initially there will be obviously, certainly margin dilution and operational losses. We are not in a position to, you know to give out a particular number or a hard value to quantify that.

items.statement: Tax rate steady state ~13% (Q1 FY25); FY24 11.13% included one-time deferred tax credit from regime change; rate varies with India/Cayman profit mix

items.statement: IndAS 116 impact Q1 FY25: EBITDA increased by INR 148.7 million, PAT decreased by INR 19 million on like-to-like basis
items.quote: Our EBITDA will increase by, because of IndAS our EBITDA has increased by INR 148.7 million, and our PAT has decreased by INR 19 million for Q1 FY25 on a like to like basis.

items.quote: we expect the speciality ingredients to start catching up from the H2 of this year. So we continue to remain consistent on that. And we do hope that once that happens, we should see the EBITDA per metric ton also trending towards the higher end of the guide.

items.quote: I think about 40% of this can be attributed to the stocking of -- the restocking, as I can call it. The balance is in terms of certain geographies where we also got some newer businesses.

items.quote: So there is one which is already under implementation and execution. I think we're looking at getting it commissioned by end of this financial year. And there is something more that is on the drawing board which we are working on.

items.quote: I only -- as I said earlier, that in October, the shipping companies tell us that things would start stabilizing. So till that time, we would like to find ways to ensure that we can engage with the customers and that we can judiciously pass on the increases.

items.quote: Because of the red issue, the incoming raw materials were severely impacted. In fact, we have containers coming almost 30, 40 days after the schedule date of our arrival.

items.quote: Unavailability of containers, port congestion and some of the major ports in the world, combined with higher lead times and rationalized availability of raw materials, adversely impacted the volumes in this quarter.

items.quote: Actually, it's a combination. It's not just one of it. So we have preservatives. We have mild surfactants. We have our non-toxic preservatives, okay? And also some of the new products that we launched; we are seeing some early victories.

items.quote: all the FMCG companies have started taking price cuts, various prices only over the last -- probably most of it happened in the last quarter, very significantly. So now that should start sanctioning demand because good demand from both rural and urban, okay?

items.quote: So we don't cater into soaps. What we do is -- Syndet soap is a specialty for us, which is synthetic detergent soap. So it has nothing to do with what Unilever announced in terms of reducing the farm content by 25%. So there is no connection with our business.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis causing longer routes via Cape of Good Hope, container shortages, port congestion, freight rate increases
items.quote: This is essentially the Red Sea crisis started in November when we had skipped going through the Red Sea. So we skipped Suez Canal there to go through the Cape of Good Hope. So we have ships taking more time to get to their destination. So cont ainers also took more time to come

items.statement: Supply chain deterioration is key risk; if situation doesn't worsen, volume growth momentum should sustain

items.statement: Feedstock price volatility risk; robust raw material management framework in place to manage open positions
items.quote: That's why it's very critical where we need to have a very robust raw material management framework in place, which we have. So we're ensuring that we have the right buying down, the timing of the buying and the quantum of buying to take care of this price volatility.

items.statement: Expect FY25 revenue similar to FY24 level
items.quote: on an overall year basis -- FY '25 basis, we are fairly hopeful and comfortable that we should be able to do a similar level as FY '24 on an annual basis.

items.statement: Order book at INR 26,000 crores as of 30 June 2024

items.statement: Expect INR 4,000-5,000 crores orders soon
items.quote: we should be able to get about INR 4,000 crores to INR 5,000 crores in the near future immediately.

items.statement: Full year order inflow guidance INR 10,000-12,000 crores
items.quote: overall as we have been maintaining, we should be getting order book in the range of INR 10,000 crores to INR 12,000 crores for the full year.

items.statement: PAT margin target 7-7.5% short-to-midterm
items.quote: we will have a PAT margin in the range of 7% to 7.5% on a short-to-midterm perspective. So that is something which we continue to maintain.

items.statement: Core EBITDA margin to be maintained at FY23-24 level for FY25
items.quote: That is the level which we've maintained, we should be able to maintain for FY'25 also.

items.statement: May take a few basis points hit on EBITDA margin in FY26
items.quote: we may take a hit of about a few basis points in FY'26.

items.statement: Core EBITDA margin expected in 6.5-7.5% range for FY25 and most of FY26
items.quote: for this particular year and most of the next year, we should be within the range of 6.5% to 7%, 7.5%.

items.statement: Expect tender pipeline to pick up post-elections in railways and highways
items.quote: now that elections are over, we do expect a lot of tenders and bids to come out, both in railways as well as in highway sector.

items.statement: Bidding strategy: railways EPC, roads EPC, and PPP projects
items.quote: One, we are going to obviously bid our bread and butter, which is EPC projects of railways. Two, we are also looking at some EPC in roads and highways. Three, we are looking at some PPP products as well.

items.quote: Linoleic acid contributed approximately 45% in terms of value , and Dimer acid contributed close to 22% in terms of value.

items.statement: Isostearic acid full container load exports to Europe and US started in Q1 FY25 with additional orders received
items.quote: in Q1 we have successfully made several full container load export shipments to Europe and US. And we have also received additional orders for exporting Isostearic acids to other locations, both for existing and new

items.quote: Our Q1 FY25 EBITDA reaches to Rs.44 crores, signifying a commendable 39% YoY growth. We maintained a healthy margin of 26%.

items.quote: Considering the B2G versus the B2C o r the retail strategy around the pricing, they ’re going to be a differentiated pricing, but it would still be in line with our overall hypothesis

items.quote: It forms the formidable retail opportunity to cater on. It's too early to benchmark or look up to something a number to share. But yes, if I look at the overall size around the addressable market size, it is close to 40,000 plus crores.

items.statement: Fees paid to hospitals stable at 7-8% of revenue for mature projects; higher initially for new projects then declines

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 39% despite expansion activities

items.statement: Nine hub leases signed across Pune, West Bengal and home markets; operational within 12-18 months
items.quote: We have finalized leases for nine hub locations across our home states as well as adjacent geographies, Pune and West Bengal. And these hubs are all scheduled to commence operations over the next 18 months.

items.quote: Our B2C share stood strong at 93%, with wellness contributing to 13.4% of our total revenues.

items.quote: Because of our advanced radiology advantage, initially, in the initial like first five, six months, we see higher revenue coming from advanced radiology. items.statement: Rental expense 7-7.5% of revenue; new hubs drag EBITDA margin by 0.3-0.4%
items.quote: So the rental is approximately like 7% to 7.5% of the top line. I'll give you the exact number, but it's approximately 7% to 7.5%.

items.statement: Medinova merger approved with appointed date April 1, 2024; no material consolidated impact

items.statement: Revenue per test INR462; revenue per patient footfall INR1,621
items.quote: The revenue per test was INR462 and revenue per patient footfall was INR1,621 during this current quarter.

items.quote: But if you basically see the price increase, I think even during the current year, Q1 to Q1, if I consider the organic business, the impact of price increase is less than 1% for this current quarter.

items.statement: Kolkata hub breakeven in 3 quarters; Gulbarga hub expected breakeven August-September 2024
items.quote: I think as of now we have only one hub which is yet to break even, which we launched in almost end of November last year, which we're expecting that center to breakeven maybe in August or September.

items.statement: Renewal ARR expected to grow 45-46% for full year FY25 after 34% in Q1
items.quote: For the year we will be at between 45 to 46%. Just for now, we don't give guidance but on that thing it is so precise you can't really ge t it wrong too

items.statement: Overspent ~$3 million in Q1 FY25 on operating capacity ahead of anticipated growth
items.quote: In anticipation of that growth, we have built up some additional capacity . We have probably overspent by about $ 3 million this quarter in terms of actual operating capacity b ut that's a sign of our confidence that we believe this growth could carry on and that's why we've done

items.statement: POSP premium ₹1,000 Cr, UAE premium ₹213 Cr, Corporate premium ₹272 Cr in Q1 FY25
items.quote: POSP is ~₹1,000 Cr, Dubai is ₹213 Cr, and Corporate is about ₹272 Cr.

items.statement: Health insurance price hikes 15-20 months ago have reversed; renewal rates improving; modular products with strong no-claim bonus helping retention
items.quote: The price hikes that happened in the industry are actually some thing that happened about 15-20 months ago. We've now been through a reversal of that cycle that happened then. items.statement: Savings mix shifted to ULIPs from capital guarantee; ULIP take rates lower; Health and Term take rates stable; multiyear policies lower than prior years
items.quote: The take rate is chang ing because of the mix towards S avings products, because we sell a lot of ULIP s, and I'm sure you must have heard from all other industry players also that right now consu mers want market-linked products and that has always been our strategy. items.statement: Healthcare cost inflation driven by fee-for-service model unsustainable; room rents ₹60-66k vs customer income ₹6-10L; working on lifetime value model with hospitals
items.quote: I think today's healthcare model is focused on revenue per bed. We believe the model of the future will be one that focuses on lifetime value of customer. And the lifetime value of the customer starts from the insurance premium that they pay. And the value you derive is that minus the total healthcare expenses that exist.

items.statement: No shareholder returns before March 2026; evaluating after March'26
items.quote: No, I think, as I said, that is somet hing we want to evaluate after I would say March’26. It is not on the cards anytime

items.statement: UAE insurance premium grew 64% YoY; absolute B2C business building strong brand

items.statement: Target SIP book of Rs 1,000 crore by March 2025
items.quote: Definitely, our next target is to reach the SIP book of Rs. 1,000 crores by March 2025, and we are confident in our trajectory.

items.quote: For this quarter, our quarterly average AUM in June grew by 52% year-on-year and 10% sequentially to Rs. 89,300 crores.

items.statement: Closing equity AUM increased 57% YoY to Rs 93,150 crore with Rs 26,000 crore mark-to-market gains
items.quote: Our closing equity AUM has increased by 57% Y-o-Y to around Rs. 93,150 crores, with nearly three-fourth of these growth driven by mark-to-market gains. The mark-to-market gain for the trailing 12 months stood at a strong Rs. 26,000 crores.

items.statement: Net equity sales of Rs 2,500 crore in Q1 FY25, accounting for ~40% of FY24 total
items.quote: Our net equity sales of Rs. 2,500 crores for this quarter were very robust, and it is accounting for almost 40% of our total net equity sales in FY'24.

items.statement: Market share in equity AUM excluding ETF improved from 2.46% to 2.52% YoY
items.quote: Our market share in equity AUM excluding ETF improved from 2.46% in June 2023 to 2.52% in June 2024.

items.quote: At the end of the month, our monthly SIP book reached Rs. 7.8 billion. We added Rs. 238 crores to our SIP book over the past 12 months and are on track to reach Rs. 1,000 crores by March '25.

items.quote: In June 2024, we collected Rs. 98 crores in STP, reported on an actual realization basis. The average value of STP is Rs. 6,650, which is much higher compared to the SIPs. And please note that the STP value of Rs. 98 crores is not included in the SIP number which I talked about.

items.statement: Full-year revenue yield guidance of 89-89.5 bps excluding one-time withheld brokerage
items.quote: So, if you take out that 2 basis point I think we are fairly confident that in the full year you can definitely consider the top line revenue in the range of 89 basis points, 89, 89.5 basis points, that's something which is a reasonable fare guidance I can give you, keeping the current situation in mind.

items.statement: Payout ratio increased 0.6% sequentially to 62.2% due to indirect channel mix rising to 88.8%
items.quote: If you look at our payout ratio has also increased sequentially by 0.6% to 62.2%. It is mainly due to changes in the indirect mix in our total AUM. The AUM of indirect channel, which is the business contributed by our channel partners, has increased by 0.8% to 88.8%.

items.statement: Employee cost rose 16.2% QoQ due to 15.6% increments and 16 new branches; full-year rise expected 17.5-18.5%
items.quote: You will notice that employee cost has increased by 16.2% sequentially, mainly due to increment of 15.6% as mentioned by us in the last call, coupled with opening of 16 new branches in the 1st Quarter of this year between April, May and June.

items.statement: Full-year employee cost growth expected at 17.5-18.5%
items.quote: So, if you look at the full year, we expect that the cost, which we have been seeing at 16.2% growth, we assume full year rise will be in the range of 17.5% to 18.5%.

items.quote: In the general insurance front, predominantly health insurance business for us, health business grew significantly by 45%, taking our total health book to about Rs. 105 crores, which is significantly renewal revenue in nature for us.

items.statement: New business yield down only ~1 bp over last year; able to maintain yield on incremental flows
items.quote: To give our experience, yields in probably last one year our yield on the new business is probably down by hardly around 1 basis point. We could be able to maintain our yield on the new flows.

items.quote: Of course, I think we already started getting few interest from the wealth RMs or the banking RMs. We also have acquired a few of them. items.quote: I think about 3.5%. So, I think broking has been more or less stagnant for us. But post merger I believe it should see some positive traction.

items.quote: We already have RIA license in one of our company called PruTech Financial Services, which is a 100% subsidiary of Prudent Corporate. items.statement: 16 new branches opened in Q1 FY25; branch expansion driving employee additions
items.quote: Coupled with opening of 16 new branches in the 1st Quarter of this year between April, May and June. The net addition of employees during the current quarter is about 78 people, primarily due to our branch expansion.

items.statement: Insurance business growing faster than mutual funds due to low penetration; 11,000+ distributors converted to POS
items.quote: This business is growing faster than the mutual funds. Obviously, it should grow faster because the base effect is less. We have a network of more than 30,000 distributors, currently around 11,000-plus distributors are converted to POS.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 guidance: 20% revenue growth, gross margin 11-13%, adjusted EBITDA margin 7-9%

items.quote: In line with our strategy to maintain an asset light and efficient operating model, our cloud-based platform provides transparent access to a wide range of benefits and services for clients and their end users.

items.quote: If you were to look at last year, full year, I mean the square meter of space that was occupied by the lounges, all lounges in India put together, were close to around 28,000 square meters, which actually converted by the end of the year to 35,000 square meters.

items.quote: In the first two quarters, we focus on renewing contracts with our vendors, which typically results in lower margins compared to other periods. However, this situation improves in the la tter half of the year when we renew contracts with our clients, leading to relatively higher H2

items.quote: With substantial capex allocation for infrastructure, we expect even more opportunities arising in terms of building of new airports, modernization and renovation of existing airports, as well as rail way stations.

items.statement: Net worth INR 254.5 crores as of June 30, 2024; asset-light, low-cost model supports strong balance sheet
items.quote: Our net worth as on June 30, 2024 stood at INR254.5 crores. Supported by our consistent financial performance and a solid asset-light and low-cost business model, we maintain a strong conviction in the sustained growth of our performance.

items.statement: Board-approved dividend policy covers investment, expansion, and cash returns; dividend declared for FY24
items.quote: We do have a board -approved dividend policy. It is much broader policy, which captures the allocation towards investment and expansion and acceleration of the business. items.quote: As you may recall, the last quarter, we significantly expanded our team by recruiting talent from leading business schools across the country. items.statement: FY25 top-line growth guidance of about 10% plus vs FY24; bottom-line growth expected to be much higher
items.quote: I'm happy to confirm overall the growth guidance for FY 2025 remains same as per last call that is top line growth in range of about 10% plus as compared to FY '24 and our bottom line growth expected to be much higher.

items.statement: Long-term strategic guidance of 10-15% top-line CAGR and maintaining/slightly improving margins
items.quote: Yes, our long-term strategic guidance remains at a 10% to 15% top line growth on a compounded annual growth rate basis and maintaining and slightly improving on the margins.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improvement target of 100-200 bps over next 2-3 years
items.quote: we are committed to improve this margin in the next 2 to 3 years by 100 basis points to 200 basis points at a consol level.

items.statement: Bronze bushing sales of INR20 cr in Q1 FY25; targeting at least INR80 cr for full FY25 from multiple customers
items.quote: As I'm hopeful of a Bush segment contributing at least INR80 crores in sales on an annual basis to FY '25.

items.statement: China demand reasonably positive; confident FY25 will contribute positively to bottom line

items.quote: Thus we are achieving sales of around INR18 crores with Japan-based customers in quarter 1.

items.quote: Broadly India – standalone India about 45% in exports, 55% is domestic.

items.quote: Looking ahead, we plan to open around 25 new stores in this upcoming financial year, anticipating a robust double-digit growth in revenue for 2024-2025.

items.quote: So I'll give you a rough assumption breakout, right? So assume around 40% for water treatment. Between 30%, 35% for what we would call the industrial users. We have about a quarter in plasticizers and PVC additives. And then maybe close to 10%, 15% in real ly speciality things like refrigerants, pharma, agrochemicals

items.statement: Paints trial production revenue goes to CWIP for 3-4 months per plant, commercial revenue only post-capitalization
items.quote: Every plant, which is launched will have a 3 -month period of trial production average. I'm just giving average. So that is the only number that we have to see. So the three plants, which were 30th of April that was announced, most of their production, which has happened after 30th of April are on commercial production, their sale has already started to take place in quarter 2 and quarter 3. Chama

items.statement: Net debt increased ₹330 crores sequentially despite ₹1,000 crores capex spend due to strong working capital cash generation
items.quote: Yes. So, working capital management of our existing business has been able to generate some cash flows. So that has, I mean, led to the lower bad debt increases, okay? So, in this quarter, Q1 specifically, our operating cash flows are much higher than the EBITDA for the quarter because of the working capital management.

items.statement: Birla Opus targeting high single-digit market share exit by FY25 end
items.quote: And you're still maintaining the high single -digit market share exit target, right, for FY '25

items.statement: Underlying volume growth of 9.6% in Q1 FY25; C&B grew 8%, B2B grew 18%
items.quote: For the quarter, we reported underlying volume growth of 9.6% with Consumer and Bazaar (C&B) businesses growing UVG by 8%, whereas our Business to Business (B2B) businesses reported strong UVG of 18%, driven by both domestic and export segments.

items.statement: VAM consumption price averaged $1,022/ton in Q1 FY25 vs $1,137/ton in Q1 FY24
items.quote: VAM consumption in the quarter was $1,022 a ton versus $1,137 in the same period last year.

items.statement: Working capital in absolute terms lower than March 2024, resulting in strong cash flows
items.quote: The working capital situation remained healthy, and in absolute terms, was lower than March '24, which resulted in strong cash flows.

items.statement: Kerala market soft with demand issues; magnitude may differ by company
items.quote: Yes, Kerala vis-à-vis other markets has been soft. There is clearly an issue of demand in Kerala vis-à-vis the normal buoyant conditions.

items.statement: Exterior new product piloted; in Southern Europe such products are 15-20% of exteriors market
items.quote: If you look at markets like Southern Europe, whether you look at France or you look at Italy or you look at Spain, this is like up to 15% to 20% of the exteriors market.

items.statement: No significant pricing rollbacks in Q1; further cuts depend on input price reductions
items.quote: As of now, in the first quarter, we have not taken any significant pricing rollbacks. What you are seeing is really the impact of what we have done over the course of all of last year.

items.statement: Current VAM price fluctuating between $850 and $1,000 per ton due to force majeure at a major producer
items.quote: Currently, the VAM price is fluctuating because one of the big guys had a force majeure, so on. I would say it's between $850 and $1,000 depending on where you are.

items.statement: Rural (Emerging India) growth outpacing urban for 8th consecutive quarter; 14,000 Pidilite Ki Duniyas covering 28,000 villages
items.quote: And now you would see this is the eighth quarter where we have had double-digit growth in rural India. So as far as we are concerned, all the efforts and the focus that we have put in, I mean, to give you a little statistics, we now have 14,000 Pidilite Ki Duniyas, where now currently in a situation where villages below 10,000, we are now covering about 28,000 villages directly.

items.statement: Capex to be 3-5% of sales annually while maintaining double-digit growth ambition; asset turnover to normalize over 2-3 years
items.quote: We are now in a stable equilibrium place, where you will find us spend capex between 3% to 5% of sales every year as long as we maintain our double-digit growth ambition.

items.statement: Capacity utilization between 70-75%; 20 plants undergoing brownfield expansion
items.quote: To give you back of the envelope, we remain between 70 and 75. The moment, we crossed 75, we start looking at fresh capacity. So as we speak, actually 20 of our current plants are undergoing some form of brownfield expansion.

items.statement: Value and volume growth expected to converge by Q2, definitely by H2 if pricing stable and no raw material volatility
items.quote: As far as pricing is concerned, if we keep pricing at the current levels, and we don't have any massive volatility or major volatility in raw materials, starting the second quarter, but definitely by the second half, you will see value and volume converge.

items.statement: Paints foray progressing organically; will assess after one festive season; happy with progress so far
items.quote: As we said, Latika last time, give us a little more time on paints because company with our sales and distribution network and reach just through a channel field, you will always see good results in the first 6 months. I would be best equipped to answer this question after these markets have gone through one festive season and we see where we settle.

items.statement: Domestic subsidiary revenues flat in Q1 due to heat wave and elections; expected to normalize by H2
items.quote: See, as far as domestic subsidiaries are concerned, again, this is because of massive, more of the heat wave and some part of the election. But frankly, by the second half, you will see them all normalize because demand conditions will continuously improve.

items.statement: EBITDA margin likely at higher end of 20-24% range for rest of year if input costs remain benign; will invest more aggressively if stability continues
items.quote: As of now, as we said, we will be in the 20% to 24% range, probably a little more at the higher end. But as we see signs of stability, we will invest back more aggressively for growth.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted from 80% core / 20% growth+pioneer to 55% core / 45% growth+pioneer over last 7-8 years
items.quote: See, I would say when we started on this journey, Percy, we were 80-20, 80 was core and 20 was growth and pioneer. We are now close to 55-45.

items.statement: International exports (Africa, Middle East, Indian subcontinent) growing in strong double-digits consistently for 3 years; 2 factories in Africa
items.quote: Africa is growing substantially for us. In fact, now on a consistent basis over the last 3 years would have been a fast-growing geography. That is also true for the Middle East. So slowly and steadily in our neighbouring Indian subcontinent, the Middle East and Africa, we continue to grow in strong double-digit numbers.

items.statement: Core demand environment remains confident; real festive demand indicators emerge in September; Q2 small due to monsoon
items.quote: The basic indicators of good festive demand and where the new normal only emerges in September. We are all optimistic because there is no reason to see that demand should not be good given what we have seen in the first quarter. But having said that, if you ask me, where is my degree of confidence? I mean, I think we should ask the same question at the end of September.

items.statement: Advertising and sales promotion expenses increased in Q4 FY24 and continued in Q1 FY25; not managed quarter-to-quarter but planned for longer period
items.quote: One of the biggest chunks of this other expenses will be advertising and sales promotion expenses, which is something that we are continuing to dial-up as we see opportunities to build our brands and categories.

items.statement: 90% of rural growth is same-store growth; new outlets contribute <10%; massive penetration and range expansion opportunity in existing accounts
items.quote: See, firstly, Rishi, just let me clarify, 90% of our growth is same-store growth. The new outlets, etc. is less than 10%. So we still have a massive opportunity in penetration in existing markets with existing stores.

items.statement: VAM prices near bottom; largest producer declared force majeure at current levels; comfortable with 20-24% EBITDA band at current VAM prices
items.quote: In fact, the largest one of them actually declared a force majeure in its U.S. and Mexico plants because they found these levels itself not satisfactory. So I would say we are very near the bottom. This is very near the bottom. And as far as price is concerned, if it remains at this level, we are very comfortable with our 20% to 24% range.

items.statement: Real estate cycle benefits for core categories typically appear in years 3-4; currently in year 2; some waterproofing benefit now, multiplier expected end of this year/beginning next year
items.quote: Normally, what we have observed in the past when real estate is taken off, its year 3 and 4 that give you a multiplier much stronger than years 1 and 2. So I suspect starting maybe the end of this year, beginning of next year, you will start seeing the multiplier as long as real estate continues to boom.

items.statement: Tied up with Chinese/German company for electronic adhesives in early stages; constantly adding to B2B portfolio for EV/electronics demand
items.quote: We have tied up with a Chinese/German company in the area of electronic adhesives, which is just beginning off, we are in the initial stages.

items.statement: Targeting profitable double-digit underlying volume growth for full year FY25 barring black-swan events; Q1 UVG 9.6% close to target
items.quote: See, again, barring any black-swan events, that's our clear objective. I mean, we have clearly maintained that for us, success is profitable double digit.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell 200 bps sequentially to 14.4% in Q1 FY25 due to raw material cost pressures
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 9.1 billion, a margin of 14.4% compared to 16.4% in the last quarter.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin declined to 13.8% from 15.6% sequentially due to rising raw material costs
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at a margin of 13.8% compared to 15.6% in the last quarter, given the pressure from rising raw materials.

items.statement: Europe EBITDA margin improved to 13.7% from 13.4% year-on-year despite raw material pressure
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter at E UR 20 million was a margin performance of 13.7% compared to 13.4% for the same period last

items.statement: Expect raw material cost to increase by mid-single digits in Q2 FY25 sequentially
items.quote: We expect the raw material cost to go up further by mid-single digits in Q2 on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Expect mid to high single digit top line growth in Europe in Q2 FY25 year-on-year
items.quote: Next quarter, as of now, our expectation would be a mid to high single digit top line growth.

items.statement: Long-term target remains higher than 15% EBITDA margin
items.quote: No, absolutely. And in line with our long-term vision, we will continue to target higher than 15% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: India TBR and PCR replacement segments saw double-digit volume growth year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: We witnessed a double-digit volume growth in our TBR and PCR replacement segments in India, both on Y-on-Y and on Quarter-on-Quarter basis.

items.statement: India export volumes grew 20% plus year-on-year in Q1 FY25
items.quote: And a 20% plus volume growth Y-on-Y in the export channel.

items.statement: India OEM truck volumes declined almost double-digit year-on-year in Q1 FY25
items.quote: So, in truck, for example, we had a OEM decline of almost double digit.

items.statement: Europe revenue grew marginally year-on-year; UUHP volumes grew 20%
items.quote: Coming to Europe, we reported marginal growth on Y-on-Y basis.

items.statement: Raw material basket increased 5% quarter-on-quarter in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The RM basket went up by 5%, Jinesh.

items.statement: Natural rubber prices around 180, synthetic rubber 180, carbon black 120 in Q1 FY25
items.quote: So, the commodity prices for natural rubber were around 180, synthetic are also at 180, carbon black 120

items.statement: Took 1% price increase in Q2 FY25 so far; need 2-3 more increases to fully cover Q2 raw material peak
items.quote: So, we've taken about a 1% price increase in Q2 as of now, Siddharth.

items.statement: Natural rubber availability constrained due to early monsoons; respite expected from Q4 FY25 onwards
items.quote: With the early monsoons, etc, the availability of natural rubber is quite constrained. So particularly the RM cost pressure is driven by natural rubber and at least in near term it will continue to be there. Maybe we will start seeing some respite from Q4 onwards.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt reduced by more than INR 280 crores to INR 2,250 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We reduced our net debt by more than INR 280 crores in Q1 to a figure of INR 2,250 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt to EBITDA at 0.6x at end of June 2024
items.quote: The net debt to EBITDA for the consolidated operations stood at 0.6x at the end of June '24, almost a similar level as the March '24.

items.statement: Standalone net debt reduced from INR 2,200 crores to INR 1,900 crores in June 2024
items.quote: We reduced our standalone net debt from about INR 2,200 crores to about INR 1,900 crores in June.

items.statement: No change in capex guidance for current year; continue to be judicious about capex outflow
items.quote: There is no change in our capex guidance for the current year and we will continue to focus on profitability, free cash flow generation and improvement in the return ratios.

items.statement: India capacity utilisation: passenger car mid-80s, truck in 70s; no capacity expansion planned in India
items.quote: With some of the strong growth, particularly on the passenger car side, the capacity utilisations have started going up to mid-80s. But through last year, we were in the 70s. The truck continues to be in the 70s.

items.statement: Mix shifting towards replacement and passenger car, fundamentally more profitable but currently offset by steep raw material increase
items.quote: As a result of market dynamics of OE being weaker, the mix is shifting towards replacement and also passenger car continues to grow. So, it's both moving towards a fundamentally more profitable mix.

items.statement: Started supplies to a marquee German passenger car manufacturer in India, improving OE mix and premium positioning
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we have recently started supplies to a marquee German passenger car manufacturer in India.

items.statement: Lost some market share in truck replacement; truck share ~28-29%, passenger car ~20% as of March 2024
items.quote: Up to March '24, probably on a full year basis, we had a truck market share of about 28%-29%. We had a passenger car market share of about 20%.

items.statement: EPR expense of INR 27 crores in Q1 FY25 is a regular recurring item
items.quote: No, Basudeb, the INR 27 crores of EPR expense is a regular item, that's not a one-off.

items.statement: Organisation undergoing Apollo 2.0 transformation including SAP rewrite, people movement, redundancies and new hires
items.quote: During this transformation, expenses will go up. But eventually, it will start coming down. Why I say because we are rewriting SAP, for instance, people movement is taking place. Redundancies are happening, new joinees are coming in.

items.statement: Near-term operating performance expected to remain subdued due to steep increase in natural rubber and other commodities
items.quote: However, given the steep increase witnessed in commodities like natural rubber, near-term operating performance is expected to remain subdued.

items.statement: Received new multi-year orders worth Rs. 1,000 crores from a leading European OEM through JV Marelli Talbros Chassis Systems in April 2024
items.quote: During the last year, we received orders over Rs. 1,000 crores during the last quarter in April 24. We received new multi-years orders worth Rs. 1,000 crores from a leading European OEM through our joint venture, Marelli Talbros Chassis Systems Private Limited.

items.statement: Export sales increased to almost 27% of total turnover, the highest ever
items.quote: However, we have increased export sales to almost 27% of our total turnover. That's probably the highest ever.

items.statement: Aspire to maintain EBITDA margins around 16.5% for the full year FY25
items.quote: We aspire to maintain these margins for the full year as well.

items.statement: Target to increase exports from current 27% to upwards of 30% in the next three years
items.quote: We are consciously working on increasing our exports from current levels of about 27% to upwards of 30% in the next three years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 16.5% in Q1 FY25, up 150 basis points YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q1 F Y25 stood at 16.5% as compared to 15% in the same period of last year

items.statement: EV contribution target of 12% of total revenue, up from 3.3% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Going forward, we are committed to achieving a target of 12% of our total revenue, and orders are in hand.

items.statement: Pune facility for M&M heat shields to start volume production from October, ramping to Rs. 5 crores per month by Q4
items.quote: Volume will come from October onwards from that plant. And it will go up to Rs. 5 crores in the last quarter.

items.statement: Potential capex of Rs. 20-30 crores for new orders, not major Rs. 100 crore capex
items.quote: We are working on some orders where we require some decent CAPEX, not major, not Rs. 100 crore CAPEX, maybe Rs. 20 to Rs. 30 crore CAPEX in one day.

items.statement: Capacity utilization: Gasket & heat shield 88%, Forging 85%, Marelli JV 72%, Marugo anti-vibration 85%, hoses 90%
items.quote: Our gasket and heat shield division, we are around 88%. In forging, we are around 85% and from Marelli, we are around 72%. In TMR, Marugo, they are two divisions. In anti-vibration, it's 85 and hoses is around 90%.

items.statement: Heat shield revenue expected at Rs. 50-60 crores in FY25, gasket division growth anticipated at 15%
items.quote: Out of which, I think the heat shield this year will be around Rs. 50 crore plus. Rs. 50 to Rs. 60 crore will be heat shield. Balance will be gasket.

items.statement: CV demand sluggish industry-wide (VE, Tata, Kaveri, Volvo slow), expected to pick up post Q2 with infra projects and scrapping policy
items.quote: Demand for commercial vehicles was s luggish during the last quarter, which slowed down in demand in both medium and heavy commercial vehicles, and l ight commercial vehicles also. There are some high levels of inventory today with the dealers. Demand for CVs is likely to pick up pace post Quarter 2 of this year, with an uptick of infra projects post

items.statement: Price increases pending for 8-9 months received in last weeks, impact to reflect in Q2
items.quote: There was some price increase pending with our major customers for last 8 to 9 months. That price increase has been received by the Company in the last weeks, which we did in this period also, which was not accounted in the results, which you will see in the second quarter.

items.statement: Export EBITDA margins generally 2% higher than domestic, ranging 16-19% depending on customer
items.quote: EBITDA margin is generally 2% more than the domestic business, so it depends on the customer to customer. Sometimes it is 16%, sometimes 18%, in some cases 19% also.

items.statement: Full order book approximately Rs. 2,000 crores over 5-7 years, commercializing at ~Rs. 150 crores per annum
items.quote: The full order book is about Rs. 2000 crores. These are over 5 to 7 years. So, let's say Rs. 155 crores, Rs. 150 crores, then go to 190, then 220, like that.

items.statement: Marugo Rubber JV EBITDA target 13-14% in next 3 years, currently flat due to Maruti shutdown and manpower issues
items.quote: Our expectation is by next 3 years it should be around 13% to 14% EBITDA.

items.statement: 10% salary increase given, one-time performance incentive of Rs. 70-80 lakhs in Q1
items.quote: We had given 10% salary increase. And in this quarter, one-time expense of performance incentive, which is about 70 to 80 lakhs, has also been debited.

items.statement: Rs. 65 crores from Nippon stake sale (after tax) placed in FDs at 8% interest, reserved for potential big project or JV
items.quote: That Rs. 65 crores, we have put in the FDs which is carrying an average interest of 8%, okay? And this money will be used, number one, if we come out with a big project.

items.statement: Exchange rate volatility (Dollar, Yen, Euro) creates pressure, recovery from customers takes time
items.quote: Of course we are importing also, and especially in the gasket division and in Marugo, we import a lot of stu ff. But you know how Dollar, Yen and E uro is moving. Of course, that pressure is on us and of course we recover from all customers, but it will take some

items.statement: New products: large gaskets for heavy duty, plastic components/gaskets for EV, transportation gaskets for EV, heat shields for Tata/Mahindra, heavy forged components for excavators/highway equipment
items.quote: So, in gaskets, we are working on large gasket for heavy duty applications, we are working on some plastic components for EV, plastic gaskets for EV. We are working on some transportation gaskets for electric vehicles, new heat shield for Tata M otors, Mahindra's. And in forging, we are working on very heavy components now for excavators and the construction of highway equipment

items.statement: Marelli JV expanding focus on exports, EVs, and entering large European LCV manufacturer
items.quote: Our JV with Marelli is expanding its focus on exports and EVs, as well as entering a very large light commercial vehicle manufacturer in Europe.

items.statement: Price increase receipts delayed 6-9 months, causing temporary gross margin compression to 53% from 56%
items.quote: Sometimes we have launched the price increase and not be en received in this quarter, with coming in a subsequent quarter. So, it can be because of that

items.statement: Gasket division EBITDA margin 21.2% in Q1 FY25 vs 16.6% YoY, growth of 28%
items.quote: This segment saw EBITDA of 21.2% in Q1 of FY25 versus Rs. 16.6 crores in FY24, a growth of 28% on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Forgings division revenue grew 21% to Rs. 76.5 crores, EBITDA grew 19% to Rs. 13.4 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The revenue in Q1 FY25 grew by 21% to Rs. 76.5 crores as against Rs. 63.5 crores in Q1 FY24 with a growth of 21%. EBITDA in Q1 of FY25 grew by 19% to Rs. 13.4 crores as against Rs. 11.3 crores in Q1 of FY24.

items.statement: Marelli JV (MTCS) revenue grew 21% to Rs. 69 crores, EBITDA grew 42% to Rs. 9.9 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Revenue for Q1 FY25 stood at Rs. 69 crores versus Rs. 56.8 crores in Q1 FY24, registering a growth of 21% on a YoY basis. EBITDA stood at Rs. 9.9 crores as against Rs. 7 crores in Q1 FY24, a growth of 42% on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Marugo Rubber JV revenue grew 4% to Rs. 31.3 crores, EBITDA flat at Rs. 2.8 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Now, for Talbros Marugo Private Limited, revenue stood at Rs. 31.3 crores in Q1 FY25 versus Rs. 30 crores in Q1 FY24, registering a growth of 4% on a YoY basis. EBITDA stood at Rs. 2.8 crores and remained flattish as compared to Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Middleweight motorcycle segment grew 4-4.5% in Q1 FY25; retail grew low-single-digit despite consumer confusion from new entrants
items.quote: Middleweight, what is happening, the middleweight the entire motorcycle, which has seen only almost about 4 - 4.5 percentage of growth over the first quarter of FY 24.

items.statement: Retail sales grew low-single-digit in Q1 FY25; conversion rates improved despite lower walk-ins due to heat wave and elections
items.quote: Our walk-in was lower during that particular point of time. But the conversion rate has gone up. That's why retail has been good. We have grown retail in a single digit.

items.statement: Confident middleweight segment will return to high single-digit growth for the year driven by new products and festive season
items.quote: I think, yes, directionally, because premiumisation is continuing. And so that's the -- there is no indicator which shows that this will not grow. I'm confident that it is going to actually grow.

items.statement: Sherpa 450 platform (Himalayan 450 + Guerrilla 450) tracking 8,000-8,500 units/month; Guerrilla just launched and ramping up
items.quote: K platform as a whole, if I have to tell you Pramod, which is what, six months old, six months young baby, it is almost about 8,000 to 8,500 numbers per month is what we are tracking.

items.statement: Himalayan 450 crossed 32,000 units in 6 months vs 37 months for previous generation; Guerrilla shipped ~6,000 units so far
items.quote: The first adventure tourer, which we have created, a category in almost about six months of its launch, we have crossed almost 32,000 motorcycle sales as of now, the Himalayan. And now Guerrilla also the same way which we are talking about.

items.statement: Overall capacity 1.2-1.3 million units; modular expansion possible; K platform capacity to meet demand in 1-2 months
items.quote: Overall capacity is 1.2 million Chandramouli, so 1.2 million to 1.3 million because capacity can be modularly increased.

items.statement: ASP increase driven by product mix (>350cc share up) and higher international share; no price hikes taken; commodity benefit ~0.6% YoY
items.quote: One is, of course, the product mix, because we have greater than 350cc that share is going up. And also, we've had an increase in the share of international markets, which also is kind of contributing.

items.statement: Spare parts & accessories share trending at ~15%; commodity prices largely stable QoQ; aluminium showing pressure but VAVE to help
items.quote: I think the share of spare parts and accessories are doing well continues to be trending at around 15%. So that also obviously, but not necessarily on an ASP level, but certainly it helps us from a GC standpoint.

items.statement: Royal Enfield EBITDA margin 26.5% in Q1 FY25 vs 25.6% YoY; VECV EBITDA margin 7.7% vs 7.9% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 26.5% as against 25.6% last year.

items.statement: VECV margins flat YoY; expects price management to improve industry margins as heavy-duty truck mix improves
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin in quarter one is 7.7% against 7.9% last year.

items.statement: Royal Enfield total sales 227,736 units in Q1 FY25 vs 225,368 YoY; domestic 204,686 units; exports 23,050 units (+26% YoY)
items.quote: Our total sales stood at about 2,27,736 motorcycles in this quarter as against 2,25,368 in Q1 FY24. In India, we sold 2,04,686 units in Q1.

items.statement: VECV highest ever Q1 sales 19,702 units; heavy-duty trucks 4,689 units (8.4% share); LMD 7,842 units (34% share); buses 5,232 units; exports 1,192 units (+57.5% YoY)
items.quote: I am happy to inform that at VECV, we recorded our highest ever first quarter sales of 19,702 units in quarter one 2025 financial year.

items.statement: Exports grew 26% YoY to 23,050 units; retail up in international markets; LatAm strong, Europe showing green shoots, APAC picking up
items.quote: In the international markets, our volumes stood at 23,050 units, marking a growth of 26% over last year. Our retail volumes have increased steadily in these markets.

items.statement: VECV exports 1,192 units in Q1 FY25, up 57.5% YoY
items.quote: Exports in quarter one grew to 1,192 units, registering a robust growth of 57.5% over Q1 of financial year 24.

items.statement: VECV opted for new 25% tax regime (from 35%); deferred tax write-back of ₹175 cr boosted PAT to ₹319 cr vs ₹180.5 cr YoY
items.quote: Our PAT for quarter one is ₹319 crores against ₹180.5 crores last year. Our PAT has significantly increased because of the write back of deferred tax, because now we have opted for the new tax regime at 25% tax rate.

items.statement: Hunter 350 attracting 19-25% first-time buyers; portfolio-level first-time buyers 12-13%; college connect program launched
items.quote: First-time buyers, maybe about 13%. 12% - 13% roughly in the portfolio level, and Hunter may be slightly higher, maybe about 19 to 25 percentage level first-time buyers.

items.statement: 7.5 million unique monthly website visitors; consumer confusion from new entrants subsiding; walk-in inquiries rising
items.quote: We have 7.5 million unique customers who actually come and visit Royal Enfield website every month.

items.statement: Middleweight segment seeing many new entrants and store additions; no competitor gained significant volume; Royal Enfield retail resilient
items.quote: If you actually look at who has gained, I don't think anyone has gained. So where are the customers?

items.statement: VECV benefited from OBD2 transition base effect in Q1 FY24; CV industry growth supported by ₹11.11 lakh cr capex allocation
items.quote: And we should also note that due to elections, nothing much has happened on the investments on the capital spends from the government. And of course, now it will also be a challenge that they will have to do this entire spend in the remaining part of the year.

items.statement: Royal Enfield market share among top 4 midweight brands in UK, Italy, Thailand, NZ, South Korea, Australia, Continental Europe
items.quote: We are now among the top four midweight motorcycle brands in many countries around the world, such as U.K., Italy, Thailand, New Zealand, South Korea, Australia and Continental Europe.

items.statement: VECV heavy-duty truck market share 8.4%; LMD truck share 34% (38% in July); bus segment highest ever Q1 sales
items.quote: Eicher heavy-duty trucks, we had the highest ever first quarter sales of 4,689 units as against 4,662 units last year first quarter and market share of 8.4% with Eicher brand.

items.statement: VECV formed JV with iTriangle Infotech (VE Connected Systems) for next-gen connected vehicle services
items.quote: During the quarter, VECV also formed a joint venture with iTriangle Infotech, which is now called VE Connected Systems to develop and commercialize next generation surround services linked to the transportation business.

items.statement: Siddhartha Lal absent due to health; B. Govindarajan led call as Royal Enfield CEO
items.quote: Being slightly under the weather, Siddhartha was not able to join the call today. So I will begin with the broad-level EML summary before getting into the updates for Royal Enfield.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on international markets; sentiments not yet at expected levels; green shoots visible

items.quote: And in fact, quarter four and quarter one, if you see there is a slight improvement in our margin, gross margin, like if the EBITA margin has improved by almost 0.7%. items.quote: We have commissioned a plant. I think trial production also is underway. I think in September we will have much higher capacity utilization levels. I wouldn't go so far as to say 100%.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved to 74 days as of June 30; target 72 days in next few quarters and 60 days long term
items.quote: As of June 30th, our working capital cycle stood at 74 days. items.statement: Consolidated finance cost reduced to Rs 27.04 crore from Rs 27.85 crore due to lower interest rates and loan refinancing
items.quote: Consolidated Q1 FY '25, it is 27.04 compared to 27.85. This is slightly due to the reduction in interest rate while we are able to close down some of the higher interest rates loan and then take the lower interest rates and also due to a reduction in sales.

items.statement: Added 12 new customers in US and Europe for engineering services; expanded BD and delivery teams

items.quote: But we don't have an aspiration to reach 10% market share. But I think we will need to cross 5%. That by itself also means that we dramatically expand our current revenue base in the U.S. So, that is the current Phase 1 plan right now.

items.quote: Revenue has actually scaled up in terms of metric tons, but revenue has relatively not grown due to lower raw material prices in substrate and due to the reduced off-take for the PEB business.

items.quote: Since these challenges are internal and not market driven, we remain confident in our short and medium-term revenue growth prospects, specifically our order backlog for process equipment and hydraulics is also at peak levels and continues to grow.

items.quote: However, that being said, yes, the U.S. election, there is always a little bit of a slowdown. We are not too worried about, in at least medium term we are not worried at all, but it's only a few months away and even now I think quarter-on-quarter there is improvement.

items.statement: US tariffs not a concern as >80% manufactured locally in US; exited high-tariff-impact businesses; IOR certified importer
items.quote: Our U.S. business so to speak is majority dominated by, I mean, well above 80%, we manufacture in the U.S., and we stamp drawing engineering work in the U.S., though the detailing work may happen in India, PEs are present in the U.S. So, it is considered U.S. work. So, tariffs and duties do not apply at all.

items.statement: US headcount over 220 employees; hiring sales and engineering resources for US, engineering services, hydraulics
items.quote: We now have over 220 employees in the U.S., and I know that we will continue to grow from strength to strength in their geography.

items.statement: Exited water treatment business completely; stopped taking orders due to margin, scale and entry barrier concerns
items.quote: No, that's one of the what we call our legacy business. So, in fact, water if you see, we have completely exited. We are not taking any orders. We have stopped taking orders on that also because the same reason, margin and scale and no real entry barriers.

items.statement: Body-in-White revenue may touch Rs 200 crore this year from Rs 100 crore last year; added Stellantis, Tivolt; targeting Kia, Hyundai
items.quote: BIW in the entirety was about 100 crores last year and this year it may touch about 200 crores, but it takes a long time for these businesses to scale. So, they are doing well, and they will continue to do well.

items.statement: No plans to enter green hydrogen business
items.quote: We have no plans to enter the green hydrogen business.

items.quote: There are several issues we are discussing at the bo ard and once we have something concrete , we will share with you, but as I mentioned the last time , there is a substantial land bank within the company, and it is a source of some strength from a balance sheet point of view because it is right now not at all appearing on our balance sheet from our asset acquisition

items.statement: Received Rs 28.9 crore from preferential allotment for working capital
items.quote: We received Rs. 28.9 crores. This entire amount was raised for working capital and it's being used to fuel the company's working capital requirements.

items.statement: Future preferential allotment proceeds also earmarked for working capital
items.quote: The purpose of the raising this capital was for working capital and that's what the plan usage of this capital is.

items.statement: In-house annualised revenue capacity of Rs 290-300 crore

items.statement: Price hike of 2.5-3% implemented for Q2 FY25 across brands

items.statement: Targeting mid-teens revenue growth, aiming slightly higher
items.quote: Mid-teens. We're gutting for a little higher than that. But I think it would be safe to say that a mid-teens is a good benchmark to have.

items.statement: Marketing spend target slightly above 4% of sales for FY25
items.quote: The target would be slightly north of 4%.

items.statement: COGS improved to 65.9% in Q1 FY25 from 67.8% in Q4 FY24

items.quote: The gross margin improvement came from paying our suppliers better.

items.statement: Focus on reducing inventory days further and maintaining low debtor days
items.quote: Inventory days have to be moderated better, we are conscious of that and we are working on that. So I think on that front also there will be improvement which will be visible in the near future.

items.statement: Mid-segment to grow faster than premium; mid-segment currently 15-18% of revenue vs 50% for peers

items.statement: Expect growth rate to increase in upcoming quarters driven by urbanization and interior spending

items.quote: Instant Coffee does not kind of come under this ambit. So, I don't think as of now, there is no risk that we see on this track.

items.quote: Brazil, and last time we had discussed that Brazil seems to be having good crops, it had a good crop, but simultaneously, there were news, and the market suggested that Vietnam had El Nino effect and they had certain crop shortages.

items.statement: Global B2B market share estimated 6-7% at 40k tons; targeting 12-13% by FY28 at 17-18% CAGR
items.quote: We probably will end up at around 12%, 13% by '27-'28.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 17-20% CAGR for next 3 years
items.quote: Looking forward, I want to reaffirm our previously communicated expectation of achieving a 17 %-20% revenue growth over the medium term.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 12.5-13% by FY26
items.quote: Ya of course. That should be our target, definitely.

items.statement: General trade segment sluggishness expected to be short-lived with recovery in coming quarters

items.statement: Q1FY25 gross profit margin 31.2%, down 108 bps YoY due to elevated polymer costs
items.quote: Our quarterly Gross Profit margin stood at 31.2% reflecting 108 basis points decline year-on-year primarily due to the elevated cost of polymer, our primary raw material.

items.statement: Q1FY25 operating EBITDA margin 11%, down 20 bps YoY due to polymer cost increase
items.quote: With an operating EBITDA margin of 11% , the margin experienced a slight contraction of 20 basis point year over year due to increase in our primary raw material, polymers.

items.statement: Pentonic line revenue grew 28.6% YoY, contributing 39.6% to top line
items.quote: We are particularly pleased with the performance of our Pentonic Line, which recorded an impressive 28.6% year-on-year revenue growth contributing a significant 39.6% to Linc's top line.

items.statement: Export revenue surged 26.3% YoY, export share increased to 18% from 16.9%
items.quote: This has increased the share of export sales in our top line to 18% in this quarter , up from 16.9% in the previous year.

items.statement: Red Sea situation affected transit times but impact manageable by improving production lead times
items.quote: So Red Sea definitely didn't have bit of impact to exports. So basically it was only affecting the transit times which will of course also affect subsequent order and deliveries.

items.statement: Launched Pentonic 75 made from 75% recycled materials with recycling value of ₹1.25 per pen
items.quote: This innovative plan not only reflects our unwavering commitment to sustainability but also positions us as a pioneer in achieving 75% circularity in the industry.

items.statement: Launched Pentonic pens at ₹30 and ₹40 price points, rolling out nationwide
items.quote: We are in the process of rolling these products out nationwide and we anticipate that this will positively impact our average selling price over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Developing new Pentonic ball pen and gel pen variants at ₹10 price point
items.quote: Additionally, we are developing new variants of Pentonic ball pens and gel pens at a ₹10 price point, the fastest growing segment in the m arket.

items.statement: Launched new school products including Pentonic Gum stick, mathematical drawing instruments, flexible rulers and playing dough
items.quote: We have already launched several new products aimed at school children including the Pentonic Gum stick, mathematical drawing instruments, flexible rulers and playing do ugh.

items.statement: Deli partnership is exclusive distribution arrangement, revenue growth slower than anticipated but knowledge gained invaluable
items.quote: While the revenue growth from Deli products has been slower than i nitially anticipated, the knowledge we have acquired has been invaluable and we are now better positioned to explore these new categories with confidence.

items.statement: Mitsubishi Pencil partnership since 1992, optimistic about deeper manufacturing relationship
items.quote: But, as you know, with the Mitsubishi Pencil Company we've been associated since 1992 and it's a long relationship and we have been continuously talking to them for a deeper relationship in terms of manufacturing Mitsubishi products in India.

items.statement: For ₹10 pen, polymer is 30% of cost; 5% polymer price increase impacts margin by 1.5%
items.quote: So, for a typical Rs.10 pen, the polymer is about 30% of our cost. So to that extent, the polymer, any increase in the polymer prices will affect our margins.

items.statement: Premium product launches at ₹20-40 will minimize impact of polymer price volatility
items.quote: Ya so, as I mentioned, as we launch and increase our volumes, add value products like 20 -30-40rs., it will minimize the impact of polymer prices.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle improved from 86 days to 83 days due to better payable management
items.quote: Our cash conversion cycle improved from 86 days in June'23 to 83 days in June'24 largely due to better management of payable days.

items.statement: Net debt improved to -₹2716 lakhs, Net Debt/Equity -0.1, Net Debt/EBITDA -0.48
items.quote: Our commitment to strategic debt reduction is evident as Net Debt improved further to -₹2716 lakhs resulting in a Net Debt /Equity ratio of -0.1 and a Net Debt /Operating EBITDA ratio of -0.48.

items.statement: Pentonic contribution target 45-50% of revenue, export contribution target 25% for margin improvement
items.quote: Well, so far as Pentonic contribution is concerned, it's already close to 40% and our guidance was that about, anything between 45 to 50%.

items.statement: General trade sluggishness attributed to elections and heat waves by field teams
items.quote: well if we discuss the performance with our sales leaders, you know this is the very obvious excuse which personally I don’t believe in but ya, if you ask me that, what are the reasons of sluggishness, the se two are the main reasons cited by most of our peers

items.statement: Improving production lead times to offset Red Sea transit delays
items.quote: We are working on improving our production lead times so that we can still make up for the delays that are happening on sea, on water.

items.statement: New product rollouts phased across country over couple of quarters
items.quote: So, the premium launches at ₹30 and ₹40, they have just been launched and it will take a couple of months to really scale up , rather a couple of quarters to scale up all India.

items.statement: Targets mid-teen EBITDA margins by end of FY26
items.quote: So that holds right 15%, 16% margins by FY '26 margins? Dilip Banthiya: Yes

items.statement: Aims to be almost debt-free by FY26 then return cash to shareholders
items.quote: We reiterate our commitment to be almost debt-free by FY '26 and thereafter focus on returning cash to the shareholders.

items.statement: Expects annual price increase impact of 150-170 bps for full year
items.quote: And we expect the price increase for the whole year to remain between 150 basis points to 170 basis points.

items.statement: Regular category volume growth guided at 4-5%
items.quote: However, we see that we will be on a muted growth. And overall, we guided that 4% to 5% growth, which we aspire from the regular category.

items.statement: Ad spend guided at 7-8% of IMFL revenue annually; Q1 was aberration
items.quote: First of all, the ad spend that we have always guided would be around 7% to 8% [of our IMFL revenue] annually. The first quarter this year is an aberration.

items.statement: Industry lost 3-4% volume due to election-related excise policy delays in Q1
items.quote: Yes. I think it would be , it is just an estimate, but I think it should be close to about 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Expects margin expansion trajectory to continue with stable raw material basket and premiumization
items.quote: As the year progresses, we expect the broader raw material basket to remain stable. Coupled with ongoing premiumization, we anticipate staying on track with our margin expansion trajectory.

items.statement: Prestige & Above volume grew 14.3% YoY; value grew 19.1%; P&A share 43.4% of IMFL volume
items.quote: Prestige & Above category volume grew by 14.3%. In value terms, the Prestige & Above category registered 19.1% growth. Prestige & Above category accounts for 43.4% of IMFL volume compared to 36.5% in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Magic Moments Vodka sold 1.9 million cases in Q1 FY25; crossed INR 300 cr sales value
items.quote: Magic Moments Vodka continued its growth momentum and recorded 1.9 million cases sales in Q1 FY '25 and cross ed sales value of INR 300 crores for the current quarter.

items.statement: Price increases contributed 170 bps YoY and 55 bps QoQ to IMFL sales value in Q1
items.quote: Y-o-Y basis, there was 170 basis points impact due 4 | P a g e Q1 FY2025 Earnings Call Transcript to price increase in Q1 of FY '25 on our IMFL sales value. On quarter- on-quarter basis, impact of price increases was 55 basis

items.quote: So actually, Himanshu, th ese prices, which had risen up to INR28,000 or so the broken rice and have seen some softening in the April and middle of May. But after th at government has taken one decision of increasing the MSP, again, the sentiment went toward the little price increase.

items.statement: Glass prices saw steep inflation last year (~INR 9,000-10,000/tonne); some softening expected from Q2
items.quote: Last year, we had seen a steep inflation and it was to the tune of something around INR 9,000 to INR 10,000 per tonne . But after that, the gas price and the other input cost price have come down. So, some softening from Q2 onwards, we can see in this.

items.statement: Net debt increased due to cyclical inventory build-up and higher receivables in certain states
items.quote: The increase in net debt over March '24 is primarily due to the cyclical building up of inventory at the plants and higher receivables in certain states.

items.statement: Telangana receivables coming slowly but regularly; supply linked to payments
items.quote: The payments in Telangana are coming on a slower pace. But payments are coming, that's most important. The government agrees that payments will be released to also build up their margins and their stock supply. So, I think we have been getting payments on a very frequent basis. And accordingly, we are supplying based on payments.

items.statement: Focus on improving profitability, cash flow generation and efficient working capital management to reduce debt
items.quote: Going forward, our focus will be on improving our profitability along with the cashflow generation and more efficient working capital management, resulting in debt reduction.

items.statement: Government restricting surrogate advertising; Radico will comply and shift to innovative on-ground marketing
items.quote: First of all, we must state that the government has not said that you cannot advertise. Actually they are talking about advertisement of surrogate brands, which the objective is to prevent misleading ads. However, the government is talking about brand extensions, which can be advertised with the same brand name and you must have a revenue model for it, which is quite justified and logical.

items.statement: Some states planning duty rationalization which is positive for industry
items.quote: In fact, there are few other states, which are planning to rationalize the duty. So, if that happens, it is very good for the industry. So, I think if the governments are now quite proactive and they feel that if it's highly taxed, then it leads to less of sales, etc . So, in fact, they are talking of duty rationalization in states, which is a very good sign for the industry.

items.statement: Regional players launching in P&A and below, not in luxury; organized peers ahead in luxury; two large competitors announced backward integration plans

P&A upwards only organized companies are creating brands and we are ahead of others. items.statement: Rampur Single Malt volume tripled last year; expects 25-30% jump this year
items.quote: Globally, in India, we are also doing, last year also, we tripled our volume. And this year, again, we will see 25%, 30% jump in our last year volume on the Rampur.

items.statement: Food grain inflation worst over; government holding large rice stocks; expects same or softening ahead
items.quote: I think the food grain inflation, I think the worst is over because the government is sitting on a lot of stock of rice, which they ha ve to dispose. items.quote: So, the gold loan AUM which was a little above Rs. 26,000 crore has fallen to Rs. 12,162 crores, so it is less than half. More than a million customer accounts have closed their accounts and safely taken their jewellery.

In addition to that, we also raised funds in aggregate to around Rs. 2,886 crores through term loan, bond, refinance. And also assigned around Rs. 1,769 crores of other loans.

items.statement: Expect RBI to lift gold loan restrictions at an early date but cannot give certainty; committed to full compliance and stronger systems
items.quote: We expect that RBI will lift the restrictions in a short time from now. The RBI processes are involved and therefore we cannot have any certainty of when this will happen. But we anticipate that to happen at an early date.

items.quote: Our gross NPA stood at around 2.2% and net NPA was around 1.1%, which is up by around 40 basis point and 4 basis points respectively when compared to the same period last year. items.quote: Our cash and cash equivalents including committing credit lines from banks and institutions was around Rs. 6,853 crores adequate to meet not just some near-term liabilities but also to support growth in some of the other businesses which continue to operate. Each of them much higher than the minimum threshold of 15% laid down by the regulator.

items.statement: ROE 10.3% annualized, ROA 2.3%; basic EPS Rs 7.2 for the quarter

items.quote: CRE portfolio, I mean, the book is just like sort of tapering off and will become very insignificant just like our capital market. But for the time being, as recommended by auditors, we will increase the provisioning.

items.quote: Our home loan business has seen a slack quarter in April to June. But the government has come out with very strong support and impetus for this business. items.quote: As of now, so I think liquidity concerns are easing slowly. But the growth is impacted also by our conscious strategy on compliance, as well as the industry trends.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA Rs 372.32 cr, PAT Rs 259.58 cr; margins strong despite volume drop due to better product mix
items.quote: Total production was 68,000 tonnes and that translated into a revenue of Rs. 1,000 crores, Rs. 1,004 crores. An EBITDA of Rs. 372.32 crores , and a profit after tax of Rs. 259.58 crores. So, from a margin standpoint, this quarter has been great.

items.statement: Total FY25 capex ~Rs 250 cr: Rs 65 cr for composite mill liner Brownfield, Rs 150 cr for grinding media phase 1, Rs 35 cr captive power

items.statement: New customer conversions slowed due to shipping cost unpredictability and supply chain timeline uncertainty; existing customers continuing
items.quote: customers all of a sudden have gone back to what we saw post COVID which is on a wait and watch, as far a s new conversions are concerned . T hey want to be sure that price remains predictable, and the curr ent shipping regime does not allow for that.

items.quote: Working capital has been a little higher , receivables have moved from Rs. 66 crores to Rs. 77 crores, I think it is just our timing adjustment because we had poor sales reflecting a higher number of absolute receivables, otherwise it's at par with regular.

items.statement: Net cash ~Rs 3,500 cr before buyback and dividend payout
items.quote: Our net cash stands at about Rs. 3,500 crores, that will get adjusted for the buyback cash and the dividend that has to flow out from that.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 500 cr buyback; execution in next few days/weeks
items.quote: We have also done a buyback; Board approved a buyback of Rs. 500 crores. So, that should be getting through in the next few days , next few weeks.

items.quote: Brazil dumping is already terminated. The countervailing duty part, which is 6.5%, that's under the sunset review, and we hope to hear in next two months on the outcome of that, two to three months.

items.statement: Magotteaux at full chrome capacity utilization for years; no direct competitor offers comparable composite/rubber liner design and solution
items.quote: as far as their chrome capacity is concerned , a s we understand, they are capacity constraint, they are fully utilized for last few years. So, there is only so much that they are able to do.

items.quote: As we speak, yes, we attempted for delisting, but somehow it di d not succeed. So, as it stands now, it is status quo. We have not taken any other call.

items.statement: Company on track to achieve volume guidance for FY25

items.quote: The realization of iron ore pellet increased by 3% and 4% respectively on Y-o-Y and quarter-on-quarter basis to Rs. 10,500 a ton.

items.statement: EBITDA margin increased significantly to 30% from 23% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin increased significantly to 30% as compared to 23% in Q1 FY24.

items.quote: Basically, approvals are expected to be placed by December 2024. The project of increasing pellet capacity from 2.7 to 4.7 is running on schedule and same is expected to be commissioned by June 2026.

items.statement: Integrated steel plant 2 million ton capacity: environmental approval process expected to complete by December 2024; project takes 36 months from ground breaking
items.quote: Environment impact assessment study is now finalized and being filed with MOEF for final presentation. The process is expected to be completed by December '24. items.quote: The Board has approved an investment of Rs. 75 crores for this energy efficiency project which will generate an additional power of 11 MW without requiring any additional fuel. items.quote: The Company has recently completed the buyback of 21.5 lakh shares at a price of Rs. 1,400 per share in July 24.
