items.statement: Overseas marine/motor combined ratio impacted by zero premium from legacy US contract while claims continue
items.quote: The moment the premium becomes negative -- or the premium growth becomes negative and the claims continue at the same range, you would see that the combined would go up. And that is what we are seeing here.

items.statement: Combined ratio may worsen or stay flat in first year of growth due to proportional accounting (50% premium earning, upfront commission)
items.quote: So when you grow, like we have grown this time after three or four years of continuous degrowth, of weeding out unprofitable businesses and making the portfolio strong, the day you decide to grow, that first year, there could be -- I'm saying there could be chances that your combined could worsen or remain flat simply because the earning doesn't happen 100%.

items.statement: Profit before tax INR 1,393.16 cr, profit after tax INR 1,036.36 cr in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Profit before tax stood at INR1,393.16 crores in Q1 FY '25 as against INR935.18 crores in Q1 FY '24. And profit after tax stood at INR1,036.36 crores in Q1 FY '25 compared to INR731.79 crores during the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Investment income INR 2,758.99 cr in Q1 FY25 vs INR 2,559.31 cr YoY
items.quote: The investment income stood at INR2,758.99 crores in Q1 FY '25 as compared to INR2,559.31 crores in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Revenue expected north of Rs 1,250 crore in FY25; targeting Rs 900 crore net EBITDA and 20% ROCE within 1-2 years
items.quote: Obviously, we should be north of Rs. 1,250 crore, number one. Number two, is we have said clearly that we will achieve 20% return on capital.

items.statement: Net EBITDA margin expected to return to 50% as renovation and digital costs normalize
items.quote: And we will naturally move back to our 50% net EBITDA margins. And I'm very confident about that.

items.statement: Renovation spend elevated at ~6% of revenue until FY26 end, then drops to 1.5%-1.6% of revenue
items.quote: Please note that the increased investment and allocation in renovation expenses will continue into FY26 until the full portfolio of owned hotels will be fully renovated. Post this renovation expenses will drop to 1.5% to 1.6% of revenue.

items.statement: 107 operational hotels with 10,125 rooms as of June 2024; pipeline of 4,000 additional rooms
items.quote: As of 30th June 2024, the inventory for the group stands at 107 operational hotels with 10,125 rooms, and our pipeline comprises an additional 4,000 rooms.

items.statement: At peak, 700-800 owned rooms shut for renovation in Q1 FY25; 25% of Keys portfolio shut
items.quote: At peak about 700 -800 rooms were shut in Lemon Tree.

items.statement: Signed 3 new management/franchise contracts adding 187 rooms; operationalized 4 hotels adding 331 rooms in Q1 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, we signed 3 new management and franchise contracts, which added 187 rooms to our pipeline and operationalized 4 hotels, which added 331 rooms.

items.statement: Structural demand uptick expected over next 2-4 years driven by rising household incomes and infrastructure growth
items.quote: My best guess is that the 6 million will hit 30 million in the next 5 -6 years, simply because the median income going from $3,000 to $3,500 -$4,000 or $2,800 to $3,500 to $3,800, the number of people who move into this signal limit of the bell curve grows 5x.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 net EBITDA margin 43%, down 4.56 pp YoY; ~50% of decline due to one-off renovation and digital investments
items.quote: In Q1, despite the headwinds faced by the hotel sector due to the election process and the extreme heat wave, Lemon Tree recorded its highest ever revenue at Rs. 268.4 crore, revenue grew over 19% compared to Q1 FY24, while the EBITDA grew 8% YoY, translating into a net EBITDA margin of 43%, which decreased 4. 56% in percentage points over Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Keys portfolio EBITDA margin fell ~10 pp YoY due to Rs 1.8 crore higher renovation spend
items.quote: The Keys portfolio EBITDA margin decreased by ~10 percentage points YoY due to an increase in renovation expenses of Rs. ~1.8 crore over Q1 FY24 which was actually a 100% increase.

items.statement: Group ARR Rs 5,686 (+9% YoY); ex-Aurika Mumbai ARR Rs 5,400; renovated Keys rooms achieving 25% higher ARR
items.quote: Q1 FY25 also recorded a gross ARR of Rs. 5,686, which increased 9% YoY.

items.statement: Travel trade rates up 11%, corporate up 6%, web up 8%, OTA flat in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In commercial rate increase on an aggregate, without Aurika, Mumbai went up 5%. Because we were unable to take more group , I mean, travel trade bookings and MICE bookings because we could turn away some business, we were able to reprice. So, the average rate increase in travel trade was 11%. So as a total, corporate went up 6%. And retail went up, well, OTA remained flat, web went up 8%.

items.statement: RevPAR Rs 3,788 (+4% YoY); occupancy 66.6% (-360 bps YoY) due to renovation shutdowns
items.quote: The occupancy for the quarter stood at 66.6%, which decreased 360 bps YoY. This translated into a RevPAR of Rs. 3,788, which increased 4% YoY.

items.statement: Aurika Mumbai Q1 FY25 occupancy 45.9%, ARR ~Rs 9,000; expected to stabilize by Q4 FY25
items.quote: Aurika Mumbai in Q1 FY25 did 45.9% which is around 300 rooms, now the reason it did this is that we started reducing the crew base and our crew base dropped from 200 plus in Q4 FY24 to about 115 in Q1 FY25, and in fact, has now reduced further to 100 in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Keys portfolio post-renovation targeting Rs 60 crore annual EBITDA and minimum Rs 4,500 ARR
items.quote: Well, I gave a number that when the Keys portfolio is fully renovated, we are expecting an EBITDA of about Rs. 60 crores from Keys, as you can see, a step change from the current EBITDA.

items.statement: Winter free cash flow (2-2.5x summer) directed to debt repayment; aim to be near zero debt in 4 years
items.quote: The broad statement I had given was that in the next 4 years, and I said it last year, we should be close to debt being 0, which means , really, we are in a position, we feel to write down our debt over 4 years.

items.statement: No rights issue planned; company cash positive and can repay debt from internal accruals
items.quote: No. We are cash positive, and we can see that we can write down our debt. In fact, the big question for us will be as and when we list Fleur, we will be a debt-free cash accretive company, and so how will we deploy that cash.

items.statement: Fleur Hotels IPO expected "sooner rather than later"; 80% of group debt resides in Fleur
items.quote: That's a decision for the Board and for our partner, APG but I would expect it to be sooner rather than later.

items.statement: Business development team expanded 4x; sales team increased 50% in last 3 months; 100 management trainees added
items.quote: The third leg we focused on was on business development, and we increased the business development team by 4x. This is actually all captured in the cost structure you are seeing. The business development team grew from x people to 4x people.

items.statement: Managed/franchise fees Rs 29.1 crore (+22% YoY); third-party fees Rs 12.5 crore (+21% YoY)
items.quote: Fees from managed and franchise contracts from third-party hotels stood at Rs. 12.5 crore, up 21% from Rs. 10.5 crore in the previous year same quarter. Total management fees for Lemon Tree were up 22% at Rs. 29.1 crore compared to 22% less in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Renovation shutdowns causing near-term occupancy and margin pressure; 25% of Keys inventory shut
items.quote: During the quarter, ~25% of the total Keys portfolio was shut for renovation, which impacted the ability of the Keys portfolio to increase occupancy which decreased 148 bps YoY.

items.statement: Managed hotel contracts include mandatory renovation clauses with onerous exit penalties (15-year terms)
items.quote: One of the key clauses we have is just this that you must renovate the hotels to our standards. And number two, you cannot exit once you sign a 15 -year contract. And if you exit the penalty is very onerous. Basically, you have to pay us the fees for the unexpired term of the contract.

items.statement: Summer free cash flow ~Rs 50 crore/quarter deployed to renovation; winter FCF 2-2.5x summer used for debt repayment
items.quote: Our free cash flow is, say, Rs. 50 crore every quarter, at least Rs. 50 crore in the summer. That, as I said, is going into renovation. In winter, it is normally 2x-2.5x.

items.statement: Repositioning renovated hotels as "brand of choice" in mid/upper mid-market vs just "leading brand"
items.quote: We don't want to be a leading brand, we want to be the choice in the mid-market and upper mid-market segment.

items.statement: Reducing airline crew dependence at Aurika Mumbai from 200+ to ~100 rooms; targeting 15% crew mix long-term
items.quote: We are far more confident about winter in this hotel. See, if I go back to how Lemon Tree Premier with 300 rooms did in 7 months from an opening occupancy of 40%, it went to 90%. It was fundamentally led by a massive pickup in retail demand month-on-month.

items.statement: Expect growth from second half of FY25 and full-year growth versus last year for Suven Pharma CDMO
items.quote: In summary, we expect growth from the second half of FY25.

items.statement: Suven Pharma overall CDMO business to grow by end of full year FY25
items.quote: So, overall CDMO. Suven is going to grow by end of this full year.

items.statement: Combined Suven and Cohance platform anticipates growth in H2 FY25 with YoY growth in revenue and EBITDA and acceleration from FY26
items.quote: At a combined platform level, we anticipate growth in the second-half of FY25 with YoY growth in both revenue and EBITDA and further growth acceleration from FY26 onwards.

items.statement: Cohance full-year margins expected to be same or slightly better than historical 30% range
items.quote: It will be same, or it will be slightly better.

items.statement: Healthy inflow of RFQs with mix of mid-phase to late-phase projects including commercials; new customers across US, Europe, Japan for Pharma CDMO and AgChem
items.quote: Healthy inflow of RFQs, we continue to see higher momentum of inflows of RFQs which is attributed to consistent efforts by the management, commercial team and R&D supported by a positive industry macro.

items.statement: AgChem demand recovery slower than expected but growth expected based on recovery in second part of FY25
items.quote: Within the AgChem segment, demand recovery has been slower than expected, but we continue to expect growth based on the demand recovery during the second part of the current financial year and beyond.

items.statement: Cohance CDMO segment expected to grow YoY in FY25 with shipment schedules largely towards second-half and purchase orders in hand
items.quote: The CDMO segment is expected to grow YoY in FY25 with shipment schedules largely towards second-half of the year with insight purchase orders in hand.

items.statement: Cohance API Plus delivered 22% YoY growth in Q1 with healthy order book for full-year growth
items.quote: Cohance is experiencing demand recovery. It is evident by the fact that it delivered 22% of YoY growth in Q1 and the order book remains healthy to deliver growth on a full year basis.

items.statement: Suven gross margins improved 157 bps YoY driven by improved business mix; adjusted EBITDA margins at 38%, adjusted PAT at 28%
items.quote: Gross margins improved by 157 bps YoY driven by the improved business mix. Adjusted EBITDA margins were at 38%, while adjusted PAT were at 28%.

items.statement: Cohance Q1 adjusted EBITDA margins at 20% due to higher API Plus mix; CDMO mix to improve in latter part of year
items.quote: In this quarter the mix of API plus is higher than the CDMO. CDMO mix is going to be improved towards the latter part of the year.

items.statement: Incurred Rs.22 crore on Phase-I R&D center at Genome Valley operational since June 2024; Q1 roll CAPEX at Rs.27.4 crore
items.quote: We have till date incurred Rs.22 crore on Phase-I for the R&D center at Genome Valley, which has been in operation since June '24. The roll CAPEX for the current quarter stands at Rs. 27.4 crore.

items.statement: Cohance invested Rs.41 crore in new Vizag facility bought from Avra Synthesis for basic and intermediate supplies
items.quote: Cohance has also invested Rs. 41 crore in a new facility in Vizag bought from Avra Synthesis. This capacity will add to our basic and intermediate supplies, increasing our flexibility towards backward integration.

items.statement: Vizag plant dedicated to specialty and AgChem facility with investments in instrumentation, automation and EHS best practices
items.quote: Our Vizag plant is now dedicated to specialty and AgChem facility, investing in differentiated capabilities for specialty and AgChem business, focused on initiatives to drive continuous improvements including instrumentation, automation while implementing best practices of EHS.

items.statement: Planning GMP facility for Oligonucleotides technology platform to unlock future opportunities with Sapala
items.quote: Hence, we are also crafting a plan towards the GMP facility. In the coming quarters, we will come back with more details around it.

items.statement: Completed first phase of Sapala acquisition acquiring 51% on fully diluted basis (67.5% current equity); consolidation expected from Q2 FY25
items.quote: Sapala acquisition, we have also completed the first phase by acquiring 51% of the state on a fully diluted basis, which implies 67.5% on a current equity basis. We also started working very closely and number consolidation is expected from Q2 of this financial year.

items.statement: Proposed merger with Cohance received stock exchange and SEBI approvals; petition submitted to NCLT Mumbai bench; completion expected in 7-10 months
items.quote: We have received approvals from the stock exchange and SEBI. We have submitted our petition to Hon'ble NCLT Mumbai bench, and we are awaiting the hearing date. Subject to regulatory approvals, we expect the completion of this activity in the next seven to 10 months.

items.statement: Pharma CDMO Phase-3 pipeline includes seven molecules translating into 13 intermediates; geared for backward integration demand
items.quote: Our current Phase-3 pipeline includes seven molecules translating into 13 intermediates. We are geared up to meet customers increasing demand for backward integration by utilizing our existing capacities.

items.statement: Cohance ADC segment receiving enquiries on new adjacent platform payloads; supplying warheads to two commercial products with two pipeline projects
items.quote: ADC segment, Cohance is receiving more enquiries on new adjacent platform payloads and the new orders are also on track.

items.statement: BD team secured RFQs from new customers across US, Europe, Japan for Pharma CDMO and AgChem; deepening R&D engagement with expanded product categories
items.quote: Our BD team has also secured RFQs from a few new customers across US, Europe and Japan, covering both Pharma CDMO as well as AgChem, highlighting our strategic emphasis on broadening our customer reach.

items.statement: Working capital days increased to 127 due to shipment delays from Red Sea/Gulf situation; Rs.100 crore receivables collected by July 31
items.quote: So, Ankit, as we speak, we had certain delays from a receipt of supplies with the customers given the situation in the Red Sea and the Gulf area, so the shipments got delayed, and as a result the customers who pay us on site, the recoveries happened in the month of July. So, almost Rs. 100 crore of debt has been received as of 31st July.

items.statement: Free cash flow of Rs.33 crore in Q1 FY25; cash and bank balance at Rs.64 crore end of Q1 FY25
items.quote: In Q1 FY25, Suven generated a free cash flow of Rs.33 crore with the cash and bank balance now at Rs. 64 crore at the end of '25.

items.statement: Formulations plant (Casper unit) audited by USFDA with two procedural observations received
items.quote: As informed earlier, our formulations plant, which is a Casper unit, which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Suven was audited by the USFDA and we received two procedural observations.

items.statement: Appointed Grant Thornton as statutory auditors and Ernst & Young as internal auditors to strengthen governance
items.quote: We have also appointed new statutory auditors, Grant Thornton, as well as the internal auditors Ernst & Young, reflecting our commitment to strengthening governance and internal control.

items.statement: Clinical trials globally near 22,900 with 52% in small molecules; small molecule pipeline increased 15%+ YoY driving RFQ surge
items.quote: As you understand globally the clinical trial trend is substantially increasing and public domain information says coming closer to 22,900 is the closure number where clinical trials are happening, out of which 52% remains in the small molecules.

items.statement: AgChem recovery dependent on macro factors including destocking, El Niño, drought and customer growth; destocking nearing closure
items.quote: So, before we sort out and we will solve for our growth, we have to solve for the macro changes, whether it is destocking, whether it is El Niño impact or whether it is drought in other part of the countries, coupled with our customer growth, then our growth can come into.

items.statement: Aim to double combined business organically over next five years with M&A as growth accelerator
items.quote: We wish to reiterate our aim to double the combined business organically over the next five years and M&A to act as a growth accelerator.

name: Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences Ltd

items.statement: Healthy occupancy target is 65-70% on total bed capacity
items.quote: I think based on the feedback that we got from investors, we had removed 1 layer of reporting there and we are just now reporting occupancy and total bed capacity. But a healthy occupancy is around 70% -- 65%, 70% is a healthy occupancy.

items.statement: Sustainable ALOS range is 3.6-3.8 days
items.quote: I think the current ALOS 3.9 has not been decided -- 3.62 is what has been reported, anywhere between 3.6 to 3.8 is what is definitely sustainable ARPOB sorry, ALOS.

items.statement: Sustainable ARPOB range is INR 36,000-38,000 for full year
items.quote: I think the numbers are sustainable at the same range, 38,000 -- is -- 36,000 to 38,000 which is a sustainable number.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to expand to 30%+ at Secunderabad as revenue grows
items.quote: So once the growth in revenue happens and there's some assurity there, things should bounce back to a 30-plus kind of an EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Andhra cluster EBITDA margin expected to expand to 27-28% over 24-36 months
items.quote: So as they mature and they grow, we believe that the entire Andhra cluster could expand to 27%, 28% kind of an EBITDA margin. This could happen over the next 24, 36 months.

items.statement: Incremental revenue in Telangana and Andhra to flow through at 35-40% to EBITDA
items.quote: For every incremental revenue in Telangana and Andhra, we should assume 35% of that will flow through to EBITDA .35%, 40% of the incremental revenue will flow through to it.

items.statement: Total gross block addition of INR 700-800 crores for Bengaluru, Nashik and Thane hospitals
items.quote: So as far as the gross block is concerned, the total addition on account of Bengaluru and Bengaluru, Nashik and Thane would be about some INR700 crores to INR800 crores plus.

items.statement: Fixed cost addition of INR 18-20 crores for 3 new centers (Thane and 2 Bengaluru) excluding doctor and consumable costs
items.quote: Fixed cost per center other than doctors and consumables, the cost per center will be around INR6 crores, which is your cost per HR and your other expenditure per center. So we have 3 centers, Nashik into -- sorry, Thane and 2 Bengaluru. Between these 3, we'll have an INR18 crores -- INR18 crores to INR20 crores kind of a fixed cost.

items.statement: Vizag Queen's NRI acquisition renovation capex of INR 20-25 crores, no major medical equipment capex for 24 months
items.quote: But at this point in time, we'll have to renovate the facility to bring it to the standards of what our KIMS Hospital would typically look like, which could incur a capex of INR20 crores, INR25 crores. But on the medical front, I don't see a major capex happening over the next 24 months.

items.statement: Planning further capex in Nagpur to expand beds and add cancer services
items.quote: We are actually planning to do a further capex in Nagpur. We will come out with a plan soon where we expand the total number of beds, and we also had cancer as a service.

items.statement: Nashik hospital fully commissioned, awaiting occupancy certificate post August 15, will operationalize 75-80 beds initially
items.quote: In Nashik, we are fully commissioned and fully ready. We've onboarded a few doctors. We're just waiting for the final OC, occupancy certificate from the local authorities. We should expect that post August 15, and then we are ready to start.

items.statement: Thane and Bengaluru hospitals on track for Q4 FY25 launch
items.quote: Yes. I think all Bombay and Bengaluru, we are pretty confident we'll be able to launch them by the fourth quarter of the financial year. So far, we don't anticipate any delay in either of the projects.

items.statement: Secunderabad brownfield expansion: demolished old blocks, building new tower for incremental 300-400 beds to be operationalized as needed
items.quote: Hence, we have demolished Block 1, Block 2, we're building a new tower there, which can accommodate an incremental 350, 400 beds, but we will operationalize them or -- we will incur that capital over a period of time as and when required.

items.statement: Acquired Queen's NRI Hospital in Vizag (200 beds) for 100% holding, current revenue INR 65-70 crores, target INR 250 crores in 3-4 years
items.quote: coming to the hospital, it's currently doing a revenue of around INR65 crores, INR70 crores. At a point in time, it used to deliver a revenue of INR120 crores, INR150 crores. But given that competition came in and a lot of doctors left the hospital because they didn't see growth, we feel that the potential for this hospital, given the excellent location, is close to getting, scaling up to KIMS Hos

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 26.6% vs 26.3% YoY and 25.5% QoQ; excluding other income 26.1%
items.quote: The gross revenue of INR693 crores, a growth of 13.8% year-on-year and 8.7% on a quarter-on-quarter basis. EBITDA of INR184 crores, a growth of 14.9% on year-on-year and a 13% on a quarter-on-quarter basis. EBITDA margin at 26.6% versus 26.3% in quarter 1 FY '24 and -- FY '25 -- and 25.5% in quarter 4, '24.

items.statement: Nagpur stabilized, would have delivered INR 11 crores EBITDA on INR 52 crores revenue excluding one-time costs
items.quote: If not, it would have been INR11 crores kind of an EBITDA on a INR53 crores revenue. On a INR52 crores revenue, we would have done INR11 crores EBITDA. I think things are now quite stable there.

items.statement: Queen's NRI current margin ~8% on INR 65 crores revenue, expected healthy margin at scale
items.quote: The margin currently is around 8% on a INR65 crores kind of revenue. And we believe over the next 3 to 4 years, we should be able to get to a INR250 crores kind of revenue in this hospital.

items.statement: IP volumes grew 7.5% YoY and 7.1% QoQ; OPD consults 4.2 lakh, up 10.2% YoY and 2.6% QoQ
items.quote: IP volumes grew by 7.5% and 7.1% on year-on-year and a quarter-on-quarter basis, respectively. Conducted 4.2 lakh OPD consults in quarter 1, FY '25, which grew by 10.2% on year-on-year and 2.6% on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Sunshine Hospital showing strong growth after new facility stabilization, Q2 expected to be more promising
items.quote: And the first quarter -- the last quarter, we needed time to stabilize that hospital in the new facility. And after we moved there, onboarding of doctors, growth from the existing specialties led to the growth. In fact, I think Q2 will be even more promising in terms of how things are shaping up at Sunshine.

items.statement: No price hike in Q1; some price hike implemented in July; insurance renewal rates revision expected in August but delayed
items.quote: We'll not take -- we are not taken a price hike in the first quarter. We have done some price hike in July but not in the first month.

items.statement: Three Andhra units to add cancer and mother-child services by end FY25; Queen's NRI already has cancer services
items.quote: So like in the investor presentation, we have 3 units that will add cancer and mother and child by end of this financial year. We have acquired Queen's NRI, which is a hospital that also has cancer.

items.statement: Payer mix improvement: incremental revenue from cash and insurance payers with lower ALOS; reducing scheme patient ALOS
items.quote: There is some marginal improvement in the payer mix, the incremental revenue that came in -- came from a cash and insurance payer where the ALOS is less. So that is one contributing factor. Our constant endeavour to reduce the length of stay for scheme patients, especially corporates and our registry is one function.

items.statement: Nagpur doctors approached by new competitor but none lost; growth remains strong despite competition
items.quote: I think our doctors have been approached by competition, but the good part is, we have not lost anyone. And in spite of competition coming, I think our growth has been -- it's been the best KIMS Hospital August 08, 2024 growth over the last few quarters

items.statement: Supreme Court asked central government to review private hospital price caps; matter at standstill, not seen as current risk
items.quote: Nothing, I think. See basically, now the Supreme Court has requested, the central government are asked to look into that and go over. And then later on, all these hospitals have been contested KIMS Hospital August 08, 2024 and then they are looking at it. I think it looks like it is a standstill and a few governments are working and the state government if you able to work and negotiate with the p

items.statement: Current gross debt INR 1,150 crores as of June 30, 2024; expected INR 1,600-1,700 crores by year-end with new hospital commissions
items.quote: The current gross rate is about INR1,150-odd crores as on 30th of June 2024. By the year-end, when we are commissioning all these hospitals, we will be having a debt of about some INR1,600 crores to INR1,700 crores.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing 8.5%; targeting debt-to-equity 0.75-1.0x and debt-to-EBITDA 1.75x
items.quote: Right. So as far as the cost of borrowing is concerned, as of now, our average cost of borrowing is about 8.5%. We anticipate that the cadence in the same range. We are trying to fund as many projects as possible from our internal resources. As we have said in earlier discussion also that we intend to keep our debt-to-equity ratio within the range of 0.75 to 1. So that remains.

items.statement: Key hires for Karnataka cluster: Sreenath Reddy (ex-Aster CFO) as Director Business Strategy & M&A; Dr. Nitish Shetty (ex-Narayana, Aster) as CEO Karnataka cluster; both investing equity via land parcel at Sarjapur
items.quote: We have Dr. Nitish will come on board as the Managing Director and the CEO of that cluster. He's been -- he was with Narayana Hrudayalaya for 20 years, with Aster for 10 years.

items.statement: Promoter pledge unwinding approved by Board; main promoters' shares to be made public by end Q2 FY25 post AGM on August 29
items.quote: So, what's happening is promoter pledge, what we are looking for, now is approved by the Board, we're going to the AGM that the main promoters who are there, who are having a different business that is infra, then their shares have been pledged. So we are going to make them public so that the main promoters and KIMS will not have any pledge maybe by end of this quarter, next quarter.

items.statement: Capital constraint is only limit to expansion; will reconsider if debt-equity exceeds 0.75:1 or debt-EBITDA exceeds 1.75:1
items.quote: We are currently managing 4,000 beds. We can expand the number of beds, but the limited -- the limit which we are having is the capital constraint. We have said we don't want to exceed a debt equity of 0.75:1, debt-to-EBITDA of 1.75:1. As far as we are within that range, I think we can -- there is no other limitation and it is already there.

items.statement: Average revenue per operating bed grew 21.3% YoY and 12.2% QoQ; average revenue per patient grew 6.1% YoY and 1.4% QoQ
items.quote: The average revenue per operating bed grew by 21.3% and 12.2% on year-on-year and a quarter-on-quarter basis, respectively. Average revenue per patient grew by 6.1% and 1.4% on year-on-year and a quarter-on-quarter basis, respectively.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR1,000 crores by FY27-FY28 reiterated
items.quote: We started the year with a INR1,300 crores open order book. We are well on track to achieve our milestone that we've set for FY '27, FY '28 of INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Open order book at INR1,300 crores at start of FY25
items.quote: We started the year with a INR1,300 crores open order book.

items.statement: Map-led EBITDA margin at 50%, IoT-led at 15.7% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for Map-led business has gone up from INR36 crores to INR39 crores year-on-year and EBITDA for IoT-led business has gone up from INR1.4 crores to INR3.7 crores year-on-year, which translates into 50% margin for the Map-led business and 15.7% margin for IoT-led business.

items.statement: A&M revenue grew 9.5%, C&E revenue grew 16.9% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: A&M revenue grew 9.5%, and C&E revenue grew 16.9%.

items.statement: Won deals with leading electric commercial vehicle OEM and large utility vehicle OEM
items.quote: When it comes to automotive, we won deals for a leading electric commercial vehicle OEM as well as a large utility vehicle OEM.

items.statement: IoT SaaS revenue grew ~90% YoY, hardware sales declined due to funding constraints now resolved
items.quote: I think it's almost 90% growth in the SaaS business of IoT.

items.statement: Investing in product innovation and marketing to unlock growth, impacting EBITDA margin
items.quote: So we have to invest for that. And the other is that we really do believe that one of the things that will unlock growth for us is more people getting to know about us and our solutions. And so we are starting to do that activity.

items.statement: Confident in competitive positioning against Ola Maps and Google Maps; pricing based on value, not reactive
items.quote: MapmyIndia is the premium map provider in the country, offering the best value to customers. We are pretty confident about our market position, and these different dynamics that are at play, we don't see as a risk to our business.

items.statement: Served legal notice to Ola Electric for breach of contract terms and conditions
items.quote: This is to do with a legal notice that we have served to Ola Electric for breach of terms and conditions of our contract.

items.statement: Scheme of amalgamation between ITSS and Wynwy Technologies for go-to-market synergies

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 28-30%
items.quote: EBITDA margin also as we have said in the earlier calls we expect to maintain between 28 % to 30%.

items.quote: The market for premium and mid -premium branded apparel conti nued to be subdued due to the consumer behaviour influenced by an inflationary environment and a nationwide heat wave we experienced this summer.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth was 3% in Q1 FY25

items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 33.4 crores as compared to INR 30.3 crores in Q1 FY '24, that is a growth of 10%. Our EBITDA m argin stood at 26.9%.

items.statement: Plans to spend ~5% of revenue on branding and advertising for full year
items.quote: For the full year, we plan to spend approximately 5% of revenues on branding and a dvertising.

items.quote: Our working capital days have decreased by 5 days to 161 days as of 30 June 2024.

items.statement: Will continue dividend payments, payout ratio to be decided annually

items.statement: Realizes roughly 70% of MRP on aggregate sales

items.statement: Does not see new-age D2C brands as competitive threat, believes enough runway for all
items.quote: Not really Rohan the heat and all honestly we haven't , the market is there is enough room for growth for everyone and a lot of endeavou rs at our end also which we will end up achieving growth on that we don't see these brands giving us heat or anything of that sort.

items.quote: last year in Q1 the provision for returns was 22% and this year the provision for returns has been consistent 25 % as per the provision made in Q4 of last year.

items.quote: So, it depends on different types of EBO s but it's in the range of around 20- odd percent of revenue.

items.statement: Pre-IND AS EBITDA margin around 16%
items.quote: Pre-IND AS EBITDA margin would be around a 10% lower so it will be maybe around a 16- odd percent.

items.quote: So, Rahul, the profitability on the online channel , third party channels is considerably lower compared to our main channels like EBO and MBO because e- comm at present remains a liquidation channel basically for us.

items.statement: Short-term targets: reduce working capital days, reduce inventory, grow at mid-teens profitably

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY25 revenue growth guidance of 25-30% and EBITDA margin range of 33-36%

items.statement: 99acres advertising spend higher than last year; manpower costs under control

items.statement: Naukri advertising spend significantly higher in FY25 vs FY24 due to IPL in Q1; Q2-Q3 lean quarters for advertising
items.quote: In general, we will spend a lot more on advertising this year than we spent last year on Naukri.

items.statement: Non-IT pricing more modest than IT due to different hiring volumes; aggressive pricing for SME segment
items.quote: Our pricing in non-IT is more modest compared to IT because of the different hiring needs of customers of every company and IT companies hire in large numbers while here they don't hire that many people.

items.statement: 99acres listing realization increasing YoY and QoQ driven by premiumization through product upgrades
items.quote: Our listing realization continued to increase Y-o-Y and Q-o-Q as well driven by successful premiumization through product upgrades.

items.statement: JobHai freemium model targeting 1M customers in 5-7 years; blue collar market 4-8x white collar volume but lower ARPU
items.quote: If, JobHai has to be successful, then we would want JobHai to work with a million customers, 5-7 years from now. It should be the platform of choice for SMEs, as well, not just enterprises.

items.statement: Jeevansathi launched super interest and handpicked matches features gaining traction; chat remains free
items.quote: We made several features on the app free a couple of years ago and now we are back to focusing on monetization with new features launched in Q1, such as super interest and handpicked matches gaining good traction.

items.statement: 99acres focusing on channel partner growth (90% of NCR homes via brokers); developing better developer offerings
items.quote: In the north, for example, in NCR, maybe 90% of all homes are sold through channel partners. In a city like Bangalore, maybe 40-50% of all homes are sold through channel partners.

items.statement: Naukri expanded to 70+ cities, targeting 100 cities in 2 years; opened new offices in NCR (Ghaziabad, Faridabad, Greater Noida, Manesar)
items.quote: Our goal is to get to 100 cities in a couple of years. We perhaps are already in more than 70 cities.

items.statement: Naukri works with 120,000+ customers; targeting 200,000-250,000 in 5-6 years; JobHai targeting 1M customers
items.quote: Naukri today works with over 120,000 customers. If you do a good job, you may end up working with 200,000 - 250,000 customers in the next 5-6 years.

items.statement: 99acres competing with Facebook and Google for user engagement; need superior offerings
items.quote: We actually are not competing with the real estate portals. We end up competing with Facebook and Google and there we need superior offerings to get people to engage with the platform a lot more.

items.statement: Jeevansathi competition intensity similar to last year; no change
items.quote: Competition intensity remained similar to last year. There was no change on that front.

items.statement: No further updates on Google in-app billing issue; all okay currently
items.quote: There are no further updates. I mean, all is okay on that front right now. Nothing to worry about at this point in time.

items.statement: GreytHR: allowed Apex Digital to buy out early investors; no longer strategic, now financial investment; hope for IPO in few years
items.quote: When we went into GreytHR, in our heads it was quasi strategic. But over time, we've realized that we would rather invest more in sourcing and recruitment and automation then in getting into an HR services play.

items.statement: AIF funds (12+2 year duration) early for exits; first fund 2019, exits expected 2027-28; patient capital approach
items.quote: Our first fund, our first AIF was 2019. So if you start looking at getting your exits eight years or nine years out, then you're talking about 2027-28.

items.statement: No plan to exit Zomato or Policybazaar holdings; board discusses constantly but taking long-term view for value creation
items.quote: As of now, there is no plan to exit.

items.statement: IT hiring uncertain: July Jobspeak +12% YoY but sustainability unclear; US recession risk; attrition ticking up
items.quote: The July 2024 Jobspeak report has also been very encouraging. The Jobspeak index grew by 12% Y-o-Y in July and M-o-M grew by 11%. Let's see how this plays out over the next couple of months.

items.statement: 99acres growth moderated in June due to election uncertainty; state government changes delay project approvals
items.quote: The business took a hit in June. Maybe again, it had to do with some uncertainty around the elections. And often when state governments change and all these things happen in real estate some of the projects get delayed.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of at least 20% for FY25 maintained but with cautious optimism
items.quote: I would still do not want to jump into any change in numbers, but we are quite cautious and we keep ourselves cautiously optimistic on this year's performance.

items.statement: Order book additions expected to be higher than previous year
items.quote: we definitely would like to achieve a number which will be higher than the previous year's addition into the thing.

items.statement: Aerospace revenue growth target of 30-35% for FY25

items.statement: Medium-term target of 20% EBITDA margin

items.quote: we are looking at a CAGR growth in this by about 40% to 50%.

items.quote: To broaden our clientele in this space, we have added customers like Saab and Triumph Aerospace .

items.statement: Capex plan on track: E-beam equipment installed awaiting AERB clearance; auto cable expansion at Roorkee by Oct-Nov; performance cable main machine install Oct-Nov, trial production by Dec-Jan; Goa compounding plant by May-Jun next year; to
items.quote: Overall expenditure until next year would still be around 500 crores. Bulk of it would be spent this year.

items.statement: E-beam facility with two accelerators installed and commissioned, awaiting AERB consent to operate; fiber draw capacity expanding from 4M to 6M to 8M km; preform plant (100 tons = 4M km fiber) operational by Dec-Jan
items.quote: we are putting up a preform plant . So, we gain control over th e raw material that goes into the fiber . We are adding capacity on the fiber draw towers so that currently we have a 4 million draw capacity. We will take it up to 8 million over two stages

items.statement: BharatNet tender size 15-17M km across 8 states; participated via consortium; price bids expected by end-September; cable portion ~10% of 50-55k cr total spend
items.quote: The total size is about between 15 to 17 million kilometers, but this covers only eight states. There are other states which still have to come up for their piece of the third phase, and we believe that opportunity is going to be as big, if not slightly bigger.

items.statement: Agri cables strong in Apr-May, now lean season till Nov; industrial cables hurt by price changes; auto demand weak last quarter but festival season pickup expected
items.quote: Agri was good both April and May. In fact, we were unable to keep up with the demand between April and May. Now is the lean season. So, the next pick up on agri would happen somewhere around November time frame.

items.statement: Optic fiber volumes up ~10% but realizations lower due to global price decline; fiber prices ~$4 (down from $5.5); expect recovery in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: While optic fiber volumes were better by about 10%, although realizations were lower because of the ongoing low prices on fiber across the globe. We expect the fiber prices to recover over the next 2-3 quarters.

items.statement: Electrical cable capacity utilization ~60%; communication cable overall ~70% (Goa plant full, Urse has spare capacity)
items.quote: Electrical, under 60% now. Around 60% now. Communication, like I mentioned, see, the Goa plant is running full, whereas Urse, there is still some spare capacity. So, we are probably around 70 overall.

items.statement: FMEG segment at 68 cr quarterly revenue (272 cr annualized), near 250 cr breakeven target
items.quote: If you recall my comments from the earlier conversations, I have always been saying that between 250, around 250 crores we should be breaking even and we are there at this point in time. 68 crores is what we have done in this quarter, times 4 is just over 250.

items.statement: Communication cable margins currently 1.5-2%, target to return to 9-10% (double digits) in two steps if volumes recover
items.quote: Yes, if you went back a few years ago, we were close to double digits. We were about 9% or 10%. The aim is to reach there. We may not be able to reach there in one go. It might take two steps before we reach there. But definitely double of where we are today.

items.statement: BharatNet working capital: up to 10% advance, payments within 90-120 days; receivables will expand but managed via advance mechanism
items.quote: The way they have positioned it, you are right with the receivables will expand for sure, but it will not expand straight away by the value that is invoiced because they have factored in a system where they will give you an advance towards managing the working capital.

items.statement: E-beam facility awaiting AERB (Atomic Energy Regulatory Board) consent to operate after inspection
items.quote: We are yet to receive consent to operate from AERB . That is the Atomic Energy Board. They are the regulato ry agency involved in this , and we have called them for an inspection

items.statement: Solar cable competitors: Polycab, APAR, Universal Cables, Vindhya Tele have E-beam lines; Finolex not yet launched product
items.quote: I think a few of our competitors already have a line which is not similar to ours. It is made by different manufacturers. So, Polycab has got a line. I think APAR has got a line. And I am not sure about the others yet.

items.statement: Copper price volatility and channel inventory overhang delaying demand recovery; utility funding delays impacting EHV execution
items.quote: In the meanwhile, quite a number of purchases had been made in the month of April and May by the channel. And there is still some of those stocks available in the channel. It is still not fully dried out.

items.statement: Fiber prices still sub-$4 despite anti-dumping duty; dependent on BSNL/private telco capex pickup for volume recovery
items.quote: Also, in the beginning of, or towards the end of, all through the last year, most o f last year, there was a lot of cheap fiber coming from China. Then in February this year, the government came out with an AD, and to some extent that has stopped. But fiber prices still haven ’t gone back to where they were, let’s say, two years ago

items.statement: EHV business operated through JV with Sumitomo; not consolidated line-by-line; JV order book 300+ cr, breakeven at 230-240 cr
items.quote: EHV is done through the joint venture, right? So, that comes, and since it is a joint venture, we don't consolidate line by line. We are only consolidating at equity level there.

items.statement: BharatNet tender: 21-22 bids received; max 4 packages per consortium; technical bids opened, price bids by end-September
items.quote: There are 21 or 22 bids which have come in. So, I guess they will need some time to go through each of the bids to make sure that everybody is qualified.

items.statement: Preform plant (100 tons = 4M km fiber) to be operational by Dec-Jan; will give control over raw material pricing currently imported
items.quote: The preform capacity that we are putting in now will give us an equivalent of 4 million kilometers of fiber. The preform should be operational by December or January latest.

items.statement: E-beam applications: solar cables first, then automotive, railways (RDSO approval needed), instrumentation; solar market huge at 50 GW target
items.quote: We are talking of what, 50 Gigawatts of solar energy through non - conventional sources. And you are talking of huge solar parks that are coming in. And all o f them require, the panels require to be connected by cables to the inverter and so on

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth target 12%-15% for lighting and consumer durables
items.quote: We anticipate a revenue growth of 12 %-15% for FY25 driven by the rising aspiration of consumers and Government focus on infrastructure and industrial capital expenditure.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA target ₹180 crores for lighting business
items.quote: Our target is to achieve an EBITDA of ₹180 crores for lighting business for the financial year by focusing on higher margins product, cost management and leveraging the benefit of PLI scheme.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth target 12%-15% for steel pipe segment
items.quote: We expect 12%-15% volume growth in steel pipe segment too for FY25.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA target ₹675-700 crores
items.quote: Despite this, we expect to generate an EBITDA of ₹675 crores to ₹700 crores on an annual basis.

items.statement: Lighting EBITDA margin target 12% in next two years
items.quote: In the next two years, EBITDA margin for lighting will be 12%.

items.statement: Steel EBITDA per ton target ₹7,000 in next two years, ultimately ₹8,000
items.quote: And in the next two years, the steel division will be around ₹7,000 per ton. Now, it is at the level of ₹6,000, ₹6,500 and ₹7,000. But our ultimate target is that after the full -fledged product comes, our EBITDA /ton should be around ₹8,000.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 consolidated EBITDA up 36% YoY to ₹159 crores, margin 8.37% (+217 bps)
items.quote: EBITDA for Q1 FY25 incre ased significantly by 36% year -on-year to ₹159 crores from ₹116 crores in the previous year. EBITDA margins improved by 217 basis points reaching to 8.37% compared to 6.2% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Steel EBITDA/MT jumped 38% YoY to ₹6,065 in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Similarly, EBITDA/MT stood at ₹6,065, a jump of 38%, as compared to ₹4,388 in Q1 of FY '24.

items.statement: Lighting Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 9%, targeting 10-10.1% for full year
items.quote: I am also happy to say that in Q1, our EBITDA margin was 9% which will increase to 10.10% in the entire year.

items.statement: Gross margin at least 24% for FY25, expected to improve from Q1 level
items.quote: No, we will do at least 24%. In fact it will also improve because this was quarter one and due to the general election there was a slowdown in projects. So, in the remaining quarter s, our gross margin will improve.

items.statement: Steel pipe order book ₹600-700 crores as of 30 June 2024, primarily oil and gas
items.quote: We have a good order book of approximately ₹600-₹700 crores as of 30th June 2024, primarily from the oil and gas sectors.

items.statement: Net working capital 67 days (inventory 51, debtor 38, creditor 23) as of 30 June 2024
items.quote: As on 30 th June '24, the net working capital days stood at 67 days, inventory days stood at 51 days, debtor days stood at 38 days and creditor days stood at 23 days.

items.statement: Zero-debt company with cash surplus ₹160 crores as of end Q1 FY25
items.quote: We are proud to state that Surya Roshni Limited is a zero -debt company with a cash surplus of ₹160 crores as of the end of Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Dividend will definitely increase; board to consider interim dividend
items.quote: Absolutely it will definitely increase. And we will also keep your words in the board that we should get interim dividend and overall dividend should be good for the year.

items.statement: Steel price erosion ~8% over last 3-4 months; lighting price erosion 9% in Q1, 29% over past year
items.quote: During the entire year, we had price erosion of 29% in the lighting segment. And in the last quarter, in the last three months, the price erosion was around 9%. And similarly, in the steel division, the price has corrected by around 8% over the last three to four months.

items.statement: High-cost steel inventory ~40,000 tons (40% of 90-100k tons) may cause inventory loss in Q2
items.quote: We have an inventory of around 90,000 tons to 1,00,000 tons at any moment. In that, about 40% of trade and other segments are their material. So, around 40,000 tons.

items.statement: Lighting distribution: 70% trade (47% consumer lighting, 18% fans/appliances), 27% B2B professional, 3% export
items.quote: The overall distribution is 70% of the overall light ing division through the channel. In which there is consumer lighting and about 18% are fan and appliances. The remaining 47% is consumer lighting. And the remaining B2B is 27%. Basically, the professional lighting that I was talking about is about 27%. And export is about 3%.

items.statement: ROCE 22.93%, ROE 16.71% as of 30 June 2024
items.quote: As on 30th June '24, ROCE stood at 22.93% and ROE stood at 16.71%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 expected to be the bottom for the year; upward trajectory from Q3 FY25 onwards
items.quote: We very strongly believe that Q2 FY25 in all probabilities, will be the bottom for the year FY25 and we should be on upward trajectory starting from Q3 FY25 onwards.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target maintained at 21%-22% across all products and segments
items.quote: We are aiming at 21%-22% EBITDA across all parts. We may get sometimes more, we may get sometimes less, but our aim is 21%-22%.

items.statement: Railroad revenue share target of 20% by FY28 from 3% in FY24
items.quote: from 3% sales to the railroad industry in FY24 we want --s(EElt'AJI-. ® to get to about 20% in the coming two to three years’ time

items.statement: Capacity utilization expected to reach 75% by mid-FY27
items.quote: If I remember correctly we will reach 75% somewhere in the middle of FY27.

items.statement: Inventory liquidation in North America and Europe caused revenue de-growth in Q1 FY25
items.quote: While we did experience a revenue de-growth on a year-on-year basis, primarily due to liquidation of inventory in North America and Europe.

items.statement: Domestic mining and construction equipment industry grew 5% in April-June quarter; slowdown in new project awards due to elections
items.quote: The domestic mining and construction equipment industry reported a 5% growth in the April and June quarter, hindered by a slowdown in new project award due to general elections in the country.

items.statement: Order book increased in past 1-2 weeks; forward indications from customers for Oct-Dec support Q3 uptrend
items.quote: Our order books have gone up in the past one to two weeks, , b), after interaction with practically all our customers we have got forward indications for the month of October, November, December.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 26% exceeded guided 21%-22% due to cost optimization
items.quote: Despite this slowdown, our commitment to managing operating e xpenses allowed us to maintain a good EBITDA margin of 26%, exceeding our guided margin of 21 %-22

items.statement: Lower utilization main reason for margin pressure; gross profit and PAT margins on track
items.quote: The main significant reason is the lower utilization, otherwise in terms of gross profit margins, PAT margin, we are on track, and we should perform once the volume increases.

items.statement: Four projects ready for execution (heavier piece weight, 10,000 tonnes capacity, ground engaging tools); will trigger investments based on customer visibility
items.quote: There are four projects we have been working on , the soft work has already been over, and one of those projects is to make heavier piece weight. The other is to, for additional capacity of 10,000 ton nes. Third thing is to go into ground engaging

items.statement: Capex to be funded from internal accruals starting FY26 after becoming debt-free
items.quote: Over the years, we have repaid all our short-term and long-term debts and are now focusing on using internal accruals to fuel over CAPEX starting from FY26.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capacity utilization 43%-44%; targeting 75% by mid-FY27
items.quote: The capacity utilization for the current year FY25 will be about 43%-44%.

items.statement: Input prices near bottom; unlikely to fall further, may increase from Q3 FY25
items.quote: We believe the input prices are somewhere near the bottom , is unlikely to go down now, and if at all, they might be on an increasing trend from the third quarter onwards.

items.statement: Price reduction of 1.5%-1.75% quarter-on-quarter in last two quarters due to input cost reduction
items.quote: In the last two quarters, there have been some reduction in the input cost. So, the price reduction is to the extent of 1.5% to 1.75%.

items.statement: American railroad customers adopting China Plus One strategy, boosting railroad entry
items.quote: The increasing induction of China Plus One strategy by customers, is also positive development, with companies like American railroad seeking to suppleme nt their supply chains from non-China countries, bolstering our entry into the railroad sector

items.statement: Products 25%-28% cheaper than European competitors on landed cost basis including freight and logistics
items.quote: No, for sure our cost s are definitely 25 %-28% lower and these are all comparisons based on landed cost at the customer end, which includes all the in ward cost in that respective countries, the freight cost, or any other logistic cost, is all put together

items.statement: Productivity improvement target 7%-8% year-on-year; automation largely completed
items.quote: But we will see year-on-year, definitely 7% to 8% increase in productivity level.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Middle East, Russia-Ukraine) increasing voyage times; expects normalization by January 2025
items.quote: By the end of the calendar year, whether it's Russia Ukraine war, or the Middle East tensions, or things like that, they should all subside, and the world should be more peaceful effective January 25.

items.statement: Replacement market currently served through OEM customers (~10% of sales); dedicated facility planned if long-term contracts materialize
items.quote: moment we do cater to replacement market, but through our existing OEM customers. In the past we used to do that 1% directly. So, in fact we may be doing close to 10% of the sales in the replacement market, but it goes through our OEM

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR 4,000 crores implying 20-25% growth from FY25
items.quote: Sir, look, we have given guidance of INR 4,000 crores for FY26. Obviously, some of the inflation numbers have been factored in. But if we talk about volume growth then I think maybe we have to do 20% and then another 20% to reach this number roughly.

items.statement: Maintenance capex for FY25 estimated at INR 15-20 crores (1-2% of gross block)
items.quote: So maintenance capex would like normally it would range between 1% to 2% of the gross block. So I think for the current year I think there may be a maintenance capex anywhere between INR15 crores to INR20 crores

items.statement: INR 100 crores capex incurred in garment division last year to double capacity
items.quote: I think we added about INR100 crores capex last year in this.

items.statement: Potential solar power capex of INR 200-225 crores planned in a couple of years after current capex stabilizes
items.quote: So, the maximum solar that we can put within the guidelines, the regulations of the state, I think the company will have to spend about INR200 to INR225 crores for that.

items.statement: Garment capacity doubled last year; can generate INR 200-250 crores sales at full utilization
items.quote: So, current capacity, if we operate fully, we can do about INR200 to INR250 crores sales if possible.

items.statement: Denim fabric utilization at ~94% last quarter; no further denim capex planned as capacity sufficient
items.quote: Denim fabric utilization, I think is about I think last quarter is about 94%. So we are almost fully utilizing our capacity.

items.statement: Denim business grew ~20% YoY; aggressive growth outlook for denim
items.quote: And the second part is, with regards to denim, I think denim, on year on year, we've done about a 20% growth in that business. And that is a number that, so we are very aggressive on that front.

items.statement: Bangladesh monthly sales run-rate INR 25-30 crores (60-65% fabric, balance yarn); LC-backed and insured
items.quote: See, we have a sale of almost INR25 to INR30 crores monthly from Bangladesh. As of now run rate that's there.

items.statement: Yarn margins historically average ~10% (range 3-5% to 15-20%); currently under extreme pressure
items.quote: See, if we take out the average of the last decade, then yarn margins have always been around, means if you take out the long term average, it will be above 10%.

items.statement: Garment margins can reach 15-20% at full capacity utilization; fabric adds 4-5% value addition over yarn
items.quote: Garmenting margin if the capacity utilization is complete then it can go up till 20%, maybe 15% to 20% range is also there in the garmenting. Fabric side if I don't count my yarn margin so I can add anywhere between so yarn margin can be added 4% to 5% for the value addition on the fabric front.

items.statement: Target revenue mix in 2-3 years: yarn ~35% (from 45%), fabric ~60%, garment 5-6% (from 3%)
items.quote: So, on that front, I think we are saying that the endeavour is that over the next two years, yarn business goes down to about 35% and fabric business goes up to about 60%. And garment goes up to 5%, 6% from the current 3%.

items.statement: Long-term (3-5 years) target: yarn ~25%, fabric significantly higher, garment 10-15%
items.quote: I think this number over 3 to 5 years period will definitely go around 25%. And the fabric composition that is both denim and synthetic side will increase significantly. I think garment composition today is about 3% of the business. This may go up to about 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Cotton spreads improved slightly (2-3% / INR 5-7 sequentially); yarn prices moving up nominally
items.quote: The percentage change is what probably I think like INR5 to INR7. So maybe I think 2%, 3% there's an increase on the percentage change, if you ask me.

items.statement: Power cost and employee cost (20% of conversion cost) are key focus areas for continuous cost optimization
items.quote: the biggest cost for our company is Sangam ( actually power cost and then there is employee cost, that is salary and wages. So that contributes about 20% of the conversion costs.

items.statement: Long-term debt ~INR 850 crores peak (incl. undisbursed); current drawn ~INR 670-700 crores; WC utilization ~INR 350 crores
items.quote: So I think the long-term debt would stand around, just one second. It's about INR850 crores currently that would include any kind of undisbursed loan. So, right now we are at I think INR670 or INR700 crores.

items.statement: Cost of funds: WC 7-7.5%, long-term 8.75-8.8% (below 5% net of interest subvention)
items.quote: Cost of fund, see working capital would range around 7%, 7.5% and long-term debt would be around about 8.75% to 8.8%. This is and if I net off with the subsidies that we receive as interest subvention, it would go down below 5%.

items.statement: Interest cost peaked; will stay at current levels for some time as undisbursed loans draw down and repayments continue
items.quote: So, I think we will see these levels for a certain time. And as I said there are certain term loans that are still to be drawn down. So, that will add to the interest cost, but then there are also repayments that are happening. So overall number would remain in this range.

items.statement: Peak annual repayment ~INR 100-110 crores over next 7-8 years; current EBITDA comfortably covers repayments
items.quote: Over the next seven to eight years where the debt has to be repaid, I think the peak repayment is around INR100-INR110 crores in a year. So, even the current EBITDA levels are very comfortable to take care of the repayment.

items.statement: Export share ~33-35% (1/3 of sales); present in 60+ countries; denim largest exporter by volume
items.quote: So, about 65% to 70% of our sales or maybe like two-third of our sales come from the domestic market and one-third of our sales come from the export market. So, there is a significant presence across the globe. We are supplying to, I Sangam ( think over maybe 60

items.statement: Rajasthan interest subvention scheme available for up to 5 years, covering loan tenor
items.quote: So, see, the major benefit that is coming from the scheme is actually the interest subvention. So, that is broadly, I think, once we start taking the benefits, we can take up to five years.

items.statement: Bangladesh disruption short-term negative (supply chain impact); orders and payments resuming with interim government
items.quote: So, having said that, we already are seeing that with the new interim government in place in Bangladesh, the orders have started coming in again and also the payment cycles and the banking issues, whatever was there in the short term, we are seeing that they're getting resolved.

items.statement: No debt trap seen; worst-case current EBITDA covers all debt service even if no growth
items.quote: Assuming worst case scenario that even if EBITDA is not added in future, even if no EBITDA is added and all debt is added, today's EBITDA level can still be taken care of.

items.statement: ROE currently sub-10% due to low margins and high capex; historically ~20%; expected to recover as margins improve and capex yields revenue
items.quote: I think a couple of years back, the ROE was around 20%. So, yes, right now there's a low base and the profitability and the margins are low. So, that's how we are seeing that number. It looks very, very low.

items.statement: Textile sector in difficult phase for 6-8 quarters; full recovery may take 1-2 more quarters
items.quote: Currently, it looks like that even in the current times, it is still a difficult time that we are going through. And going forward, probably I think it may take one, two more quarters for actually full recovery to start and results to improve.

items.statement: Garment division has capable team in place; no immediate hiring challenge
items.quote: So, the challenge today, we do not have a challenge with the personnel. I think we have a good team already taking care of the business and that team is going to continue for the future as well.

items.statement: No equity raise or preferential allotment planned currently; open to evaluating if opportunity arises
items.quote: But currently, there are no such plans.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 consolidated revenue growth target of 18-20% on gross accounting basis; net accounting may reduce reported growth by 5-6%
items.quote: if you were to consider the full revenue at the gross level, then we expect to maintain that 18%-20% growth.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin target of 10-11% on gross revenue basis
items.quote: at EBITDA level, console level, we are targeting about 10%-11% as we had mentioned earlier. We are still on the same target.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin target of around 13% for full year FY25
items.quote: we are continuing to work on a full year basis at a standalone level to be in the range of around 13%, 13 plus percent

items.statement: 70% of BTS defense invoicing expected in H2 FY25; Q2 slower for subsidiary due to summer seasonality in France
items.quote: We expect 70% of the billing for this part of the business to come in the second half of the year and perhaps a little bit more even towards Q4.

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 6.34%; standalone at 9.6%; both down year-on-year due to adverse mix with low BTS contribution
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter was INR 16 crores, which is down year-on-year, with the EBITDA margins reported at 6.34%.

items.statement: Subsidiary EBITDA margin improved to 3% in Q1 FY25 from -0.7% in Q1 FY24; restructuring benefits expected from Q2 onwards
items.quote: In our subsidiary, we saw a slight improvement, with the EBITDA margin improving to 3% as compared to negative 0.7% in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Order book grew marginally to INR 1,674 crores at end of Q1 FY25; healthy pipeline with strong order booking expected in domestic defense and space BTS
items.quote: Next, on our order book position, this has grown marginally to INR 1,674 crores at the end of the first quarter.

items.statement: Order book composition: ER&D 32%, EMS 42%, BTS 30%; average execution period of 13-15 months
items.quote: Breakup will be in the same like what we have given as the revenue which is ER&D is about 32% and EMS is about 42% and BTS will be about 30% that will be in the same order it won't change.

items.statement: BTS contribution was 26% of revenue in Q1 FY25 vs ~30% in FY24; expected to be ~30% for full FY25
items.quote: FY '24, it was 30%. Whereas Q1, we are at 26%.

items.statement: BTS business carries ~20% EBITDA margin vs EMS at 11-12%; higher BTS mix in H2 expected to improve margins
items.quote: typically with respect to business we should be operating at close to a 20% EBITDA level. Whereas EMS should be at around 11% to 12% level.

items.statement: Top 5 customers contribute ~50% of revenue; 10-15% of FY25 growth from new customers, rest from repeat customers
items.quote: Roughly I would say our top five customers contribute to about 50% of the overall revenue and the rest is after that.

items.statement: Healthy pipeline from North American customers in qualification phase and domestic Indian market for defense, space and railways
items.quote: From a geography standpoint I would say the two areas where we are seeing the healthy pipeline is one is some North American customers which are like I mentioned little bit earlier we are in the phase of qualification right now which we expect to secure orders for and forecast by the end of this year those are from North America and also domestically for the Indian market we are also seeing a very

items.statement: Competitive intensity increasing but positioned in high-end technology areas (radar, electronic warfare, railway PIS) with IP advantages; China Plus One and Make in India tailwinds
items.quote: the way we are positioni ng is what is important. For example, the, BTS business, the domestic defense space et cetra, I think the opportunity is exploding in terms of Make in India or the positive indigenization list. The pie is only increasing and we choose to operate at a certain high end of the technology areas like the radar, electronic warfare, et cetera

items.statement: Capex planned for FY25; debt reduction target of INR 10 crores despite capex
items.quote: By the end of the year, we should bring it down by another at least INR 10 crores because we have some capex coming up so the cost will be there to that extent.

items.statement: Working capital increased by INR 20-25 crores in Q1 vs March; target to return to March levels (~61 days) by end of September
items.quote: In terms of working capital, there is a slight increase in Q1 and roughly about INR 20 crores, INR25 crores over the March levels. But by the end of September, when we come to you with the balance sheet, we plan to be at the same level like March.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt at INR 190 crores; target to reduce to INR 180 crores by September and INR 170 crores by March FY25
items.quote: At consol level, we are at INR 190 crores and it should come down by about INR 10 crores, INR15 crores. So, we should be about INR180 crores.

items.statement: Interest cost expected to remain at INR 35-40 crores for FY25
items.quote: We will maintain that to be in the same level.

items.statement: Other expenses and manpower cost reductions from subsidiary restructuring are permanent; Q1 levels expected to be maintained
items.quote: the reduction in both manpower cost as well as other expenses, mainly from the subsidiary, is a result of the actions taken over the past six months. And we can say that we expect levels to be maintained at the Q1 levels.

items.statement: Standalone revenue grew 4% YoY to INR 133 crores in Q1 FY25; consolidated revenue flat at INR 246 crores due to Ind AS 115 net accounting on UAE defense contract
items.quote: at a stand-alone level, the revenue from operations for the quarter was about INR 133 crores, which grew by 4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Adjusted consolidated revenue growth would have been 7% to INR 264.5 crores in Q1 FY25 excluding Ind AS 115 impact of INR 23 crores gross invoicing vs INR 4 crores recognized
items.quote: Had it not been for this accounting treatment, the adjusted consolidated year-on-year revenue growth would have been 7% to INR264.5 crores for Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Supply chain risk monitored for PCB boards from France for a large defense customer; mitigating actions in place
items.quote: one area of risk which we continue to monitor closely is around the delivery of their PCB boards from our supply base in France, which is specific to one of our large customers in the segment.

items.statement: Standalone employee cost ~15% of revenue; subsidiary shifting manpower to India to improve gross margin; standalone targeting 25%+ growth vs subsidiary at high single digit/10%
items.quote: on the standalone part of the business which is a manufacturing business employee costs are one part of the thing maybe to the tune of about 15% or so of the standalone revenues.

items.statement: Gross NPA 1.65% in Q1 vs 1.54% in Q4; credit cost 2.36% vs 1.88% in Q4; guided blended credit cost 2-3% (secured up to 1.5%, unsecured 2-3%); collection efficiency 95.5% in June

items.statement: Expect credit costs to stabilize and improve from Q2; believe current levels represent peak credit costs

items.statement: NCERT book release timing critical: if after December, adoption shifts to next year; state government adoption varies (e.g., West Bengal partial NEP adoption)

If the books are released later, then that number might drop also.

items.statement: Sales returns trend lower at 14-15% vs last year; returns occur till November but fully provisioned in March
items.quote: Yeah, the trend is lower than last year, so it's around 14%-15%.

items.statement: Net cash reserves to fund content development, marketing, potential acquisitions and strategic partnerships
items.quote: This provides us with ample reserves to invest in content development, marketing, potential acquisitions and strategic partnerships.

items.quote: As of now, the company's total order book stands at INR646 crores including unexecuted order book of INR303 crores approximately, indicating a strong pipeline and promising future.

items.statement: Order book expected to double to INR600 crores by end of FY25
items.quote: Order book, as I explained in previous discussion, order book is expected to be double. Today, it is INR300 crores plus. It is expected to be double by end of current financial year

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 20% plus for FY25
items.quote: But overall, as I already explained, we are expecting this year to make the EBIT crossing 20% as far as year is concerned.

items.statement: Zero export contribution currently, targeting 2 international orders by calendar year-end

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 6,300 crores by FY27
items.quote: We feel we have just started to get materialized with a lot more potential leverage yet to contribute as we grow and achieve our goal of INR6,300 crores by 2027.

items.statement: FY25 PAT margin guidance of 3-3.5%

items.statement: Export contribution guidance of 9-10% for FY25
items.quote: Sir, we have already given the guidance in the last quarter that in this year we will go up to 9%-10% from the exports. So, we will sustain this growth up to 9%-10%. This quarter is 11%, but 10% is sustainable for this year.

items.statement: Volume target of 350-360 kg per month for FY25
items.quote: This year, we are targeting to keep up to 350-360 kgs per month we will produce in this year.

items.statement: 100% capacity utilization target by 2027

items.quote: Cash flow positive, we are expecting after INR5,000 crores, when we will reach INR5,000 crores revenue in 2026 end. Then we will start generating cash flow positive?

items.quote: To support our growth ambitions, we have planned a fundraiser of INR270 crores, which will be utilized across the multiple parameters, and will help the company to achieve the goal of INR6,300 crores by FY27.

items.quote: Our capacity utilization now stands at 45% of the -- excluding our acquisitions.

items.statement: FY25 subsidiary revenue guidance INR 500-600 crores
items.quote: About the revenue guidance, already we have given INR2,700 crores from a parent company and INR500 crores to INR600 crore s from the subsidiaries, both the subsidiaries

items.quote: The gross margin stood at 6.4%. The quarterly volatility in gross margins is due to product mix changes. Structurally, we would like to reach 7-8% gross margin through product mix and exports.

items.quote: Nothing, because our inventory is totally hedged in the MCX. So, we don't have any impact of any rise or fall also on the inventory.

items.quote: With a strong focus on corporate partnerships, currently 65% of businesses drive from corporate clients while the remaining 35% come from distributors. Our goal is to elevate our corporate business share to 100% over the next three years.

items.statement: Tanishq vendor onboarding process complete, awaiting board approval

It's all about the waiting process, because it is a lengthy process with such a big company to onboard the clients.

items.statement: Exports 11% of revenue in Q1 FY25, expanding in Dubai, Singapore, Malaysia, planning US entry in two quarters
items.quote: Exports, which contribute 6% to our overall revenues in FY24, have done phenomenally well four us. In Q1 '25, exports contributed 11% of the total revenue for the quarter on a much wider basis because of the robust increase in overall revenues as well.

items.statement: GML usage 10% in Q1, targeting 30-35% in Q2, 100% by Q3 FY25
items.quote: Already this quarter, we have shifted that we were using 10% of GML. This quarter, we will be using approximately 30% of GML. And December quarter, 100% we will be using GML.

items.statement: Fundraise of INR 270 crores via combination of QIP and preferential allotment, timing to be announced
items.quote: Maybe a combination of both. As and when required we will inform the exchange -- everybody.

items.quote: Yes, already we have hired 18-carat operations head. We have hired 22-carat operations head last month before. We have development head hired. So, we are now ahead international sales head also. He will be joining from September.

items.statement: Jewellery market expanding at 15-16% CAGR, organized segment at 18-19%, targeting 40-43% market share by 2028
items.quote: Speaking about the industry, we operate i.e. jewellery market is expanding at a robust rate of 15%-16% and expected to reach 145 billion by '28. The overall jewellery sector has seen an approximate 8% revenue CAGR during FY '19-'24, with the organized segment growing at a much faster rate of 18%-19%.

items.statement: Extraordinary demand seen post duty cut, comparable to 2008 levels, exhibition fully packed
items.quote: No, no, it's extraordinary growth we are seeing because right where we were in the exhibition from 9th August, I just skipped today. Today also exhibition is going on. So I think historic buying is there in the total historic booking is there.

items.statement: Targets Rs 1,000 crore standalone revenue by FY26 with organic at Rs 700-750 crore, BuLi at Rs 100 crore, inorganic at Rs 150 crore
items.quote: I would say Rs. 700 crore to Rs. 750 crore for organic, around Rs. 100-odd crore for BuLi and another about Rs. 150-odd crore for inorganic.

items.statement: Battery chemicals brownfield capacity to contribute Rs 200-250 crore in FY26; Greenfield to add more in H2 FY26
items.quote: The capacity which are coming online in the Brownfield in Dahej in this year itself can contribute around Rs. 200 crore to Rs. 250 crore.

items.statement: Achieved financial closure for bulk of Greenfield battery chemicals CAPEX with favourable terms; construction commenced
items.quote: I am glad to share that we have achieved financial closure for bulk of the CAPEX with favourable terms. Construction work has already commenced and we remain on track for strategically commissioning this facility in FY26.

items.quote: Out of 400 MTPA capacity of electrolyte salts and additives, we have commissioned 200 MTPA and started shipping commercial quantities to international customers based on approvals received. items.quote: I still feel that we will need more than 2,000 MT capacity in FY26. So, by second-half of FY26, we would need at least 5 giga or 10 giga kind of electrolyte support.
