items.quote: We also got in-principle environmental clearance. So, as we see one or two quarters more with a very limited CAPEX, we have an ability to increase capacity also at least two times by just some debottlenecking.

items.statement: BuLi Chem has very good order book for Q2 with full capacity utilization expected
items.quote: In fact, Q1 was better than earlier and in Q2 also we are seeing a very good order book where we feel we will be fully utilizing its capacity.

items.statement: Targets 16-17% EBITDA margins for battery salts; ROCE of 20%
items.quote: In the past also we have said that we expect like ROCE of 20% and also we are targetting, depending on price of lithium somewhere around 16% to 17% kind of EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Lithium raw material prices stabilized in $11.5 +/- $1.5 range; organic chemical prices also bottomed out
items.quote: We saw raw material prices hit their bottom and now they generally trade in a narrow band of around $10 - $12 or $13, so let us say $11.5 +/- $1.5 for last one or two quarters.

items.statement: Strong demand for non-Chinese lithium salts and electrolytes from derisking standpoint; MoUs and pricing commitments initiated with international customers
items.quote: We continue to see strong demand for non-Chinese supply of lithium salts and electrolytes from derisking standpoint and have accordingly initiated discussions through MoUs, pricing commitments with international customers.

items.quote: In the next 18 months, we should be able to convince two out of three or three out of three customers to basically sign up with Neogen and get into long-term agreement for electrolytes.

items.statement: BuLi Chem shipping to Korea and Japan; positive interest from Europe and US; quality improved for semiconductor applications
items.quote: We have already started shipping our products to Korea and Japan, which were the first markets we had identified and we are also seeing positive interest from Europe as well as US.

items.quote: Neogen also forayed into semiconductor material supply chain during the last quarter, developing some specialty gas products as well as liquid products required for semiconductor application.

items.statement: Semiconductor opportunity expected to contribute a few crore to few tens of crore in current financial year
items.value: few crore to few tens of crore
items.quote: Yes. It will be a few crore getting into a few tens of crore in the current financial year.

items.quote: In a boost to Indian battery manufacturers, (the government has) exempted critical minerals, such as, lithium from custom duties. This is expected to help reduce production cost of batteries and consequently the overall price of electric vehicles.

items.statement: Operating cash flow positive in Q1; net working capital on stable and improving trend
items.quote: It has been improving. Overall, we have been operating cash flow positive in the 1st Quarter and as of now. Well, you will get to see more numbers in September, but we are on a stable and improving trend, it is not becoming

items.quote: Depreciation and interest expenses are expected to rise due to accelerated capital expenditure in battery chemicals.

items.quote: Our strategic hiring in battery chemicals is nearly complete and close to 70-80 employees are on board focussing on project execution alongside ongoing phase-I production.

items.statement: EV demand uncertainty (range anxiety, hybrid vs pure EV) may affect pace of capacity expansion beyond FY28
items.quote: Again, for me this is more a question of beyond FY28. What is the demand which we are looking at and how soon we need to increase capacity, depending on how this plays out.

items.statement: Bathware aims to grow 1.25-1.5x market; market expected 8-10% in H2, full-year mid-single digits
items.quote: We maintained our guidance around 1.25 to 1.5x the market. We've always maintained that for a long-term basis.

items.quote: We will definitely grow as per the guidance which we have given earlier, we have grown by 24% year-on-year. But definitely, this complete year we will be growing by around 16% to 18% in volumes.

items.quote: we feel on a medium to long-term range we should continue to grow on an average 15% to 18% on sales, and 20% plus on the EBITDA margin.

items.quote: The construction of our Roorkee facility is progressing as planned, with commercial operations expected to commence by Q3FY25.

items.quote: Our capacity utilization in Q1 FY25 for sanitaryware was about 86%, and for faucet it was about 58.5%.

items.quote: Early market inputs suggest secondary sales have seen noticeable upticks since late June and we anticipate further momentum building up through the festive season.

items.quote: the margin reduction is solely a loss of gross margin because of lower revenue, which we recorded in the quarter 1.

items.quote: We have not degrown, but we are at the same, it's at 6.7%. But as far as the guidance for the whole year is there because Q3 and Q4 for this business are at its peak.

items.quote: Our consumer Appliances business delivered INR111 crore in revenue with an EBITDA of INR3 crore at a 2.7% EBITDA margin reflecting the positive impact of cost optimization and exiting our loss-making retail furniture business.

items.statement: Sales-force consolidation expected to add 100+ bps to Bathware EBITDA margin annually
items.quote: We believe that it is going to help us increase our margins by 100 basis points plus on an annual basis.

items.statement: Bathware premium/economy split shifted to 48% premium / 52% economy in Q1 FY25 vs 53%/47% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: In Q1FY25, it was 52% for economy and 48% for premium. In Q1FY24, it was 47% for economy, and 53% for premium for us.

items.statement: Net debt rose ~Rs 100 cr QoQ due to stuck inventory and Roorkee capex; rights issue proceeds primarily for debt repayment
items.quote: First, I think the main reason debt has increased is, we couldn't reduce the level of working capital because of the slowness in the market and some of the inventories is stuck with us right now.

items.statement: Board approved rights issue up to Rs 205 cr for liquidity and substantial debt repayment
items.quote: the Board has approved the raising of funds through issuance and allotment of equity shares of the Company of face value Rs. 2 each (Rupee Two Only) for an aggregate amount not exceeding Rs. 205 crore on rights issue

items.statement: Bathware sales force reduced ~25% (on-roll and off-roll) in Q1 via faucet-sanitaryware team merger; no further restructuring planned
items.quote: we have impacted nearly 25% of our sales force in this quarter based on our decision to consolidate and synergize between our sanitaryware and faucet verticals

items.statement: July secondary sales positive across market and for company; dealer inventory high, may clear in 2-3 months
items.quote: secondaries sales have been positive in July. We've seen some positive momentum on the secondary basis, yes across the market.

items.statement: Consumer Appliances category review ongoing; may exit loss-making categories eroding kitchen margins
items.quote: we are evaluating the product categories in which we are operating. And we don't foresee any strategic future in terms of the categories, we'll come back to investors and share, if we are making a transition within the organization and evacuating those categories.

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 revenue Rs 600 cr, EBITDA Rs 55 cr, margin 9.2%
items.value: Rs 600 cr revenue, Rs 55 cr EBITDA, 9.2% margin
items.quote: Our consolidated revenue for the quarter reached Rs. 600 crore, EBITDA stood at Rs. 55 crore with margins at 9.2%.

items.statement: China import dependence for Bathware reduced from 17-18% to ~3% over last 2 years via in-sourcing
items.quote: It will be like low-single digits, like 3%. Sandeep Sikka: I mean we started off, this used to be 17% to 18%. And from the last 2 years, we are reducing this

items.quote: We would be talking around 14% to 18% of growth on core revenues, and this excludes sale of compost, RDF because those are something that we will expect a sharp change in the second half of the year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 23% to 24% for FY25
items.quote: And EBITDA margins to be around the levels that we have for Q1, which is around 23% to 24%. That is our planned internal hurdle rate.

items.statement: Capex for vehicle scrapping and tire recycling projects estimated at Rs.20 crores to Rs.28 crores plus incremental Rs.8 crores to scale up
items.quote: The investment will be in line with what we have announced. It would be around Rs.20 crores to Rs.28 crores for both the projects and maybe an incremental Rs.8 crores to scale up the entity.

items.statement: One large C&T contract likely to close in Q2 FY25
items.quote: One of the projects is likely to close in this quarter, at least one large C&T contract is likely to close.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 23.8% in Q1 FY25, with 23% to 24% range as base going forward
items.quote: Over the last 2 quarters, we have demonstrated steady improvement in the reported margin, which now stands at 23.8%. And we believe this range of 23% to 24% will serve as a base going forward.

items.statement: Expect RDF sales growth momentum to continue
items.quote: We expect this growth momentum in RDF sales to continue.

items.quote: In Q1FY25, the total contract revenue amounted to Rs.35 crores, which is down from Rs.49 crores compared to the same period last year and Rs.22 crores in the Q4 of '24.

items.quote: We believe that until time the elected members or the standing committees are formally done, there will be some bit of uncertainty on the funding allowed by the departments.

items.statement: Construction and Debris project in Mumbai launched on 14th August, annualized revenue of Rs.30 crores in first full year
items.quote: So on an annualized basis, in the first full year of operations, we will have a revenue of about Rs.30 crores per year.

items.statement: Vehicle scrapping and tire recycling projects expected EBITDA margin of 8% to 12%
items.quote: Looking at the kind of competition or looking at the kind of margins which the current companies are making, that's in the range of about 8% to 12% of EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Net debt of Rs.308 crores as of June 2024, net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.4x
items.quote: As of June 2024, the group's gross debt stands at ~Rs.389 crores with cash and bank balance of approximately Rs.80 crores, this results in a net debt of around Rs.308 crores.

items.statement: Tax rate of 25% applicable for all companies except one processing company shifting in 2028
items.quote: Now new adjusted tax rate about 25%. So the company has shifted all its historical companies and subsidiaries to new tax regime.

items.statement: C&D waste market opportunity estimated at Rs.5,000 crores in India

items.statement: Expects high-teen to 20% year-on-year revenue growth for FY26 and FY27 based on awarded programs and advanced negotiations
items.quote: down the line, if you ask me, for FY 26, FY 27, definitely we are expecting high teen to 20% growth, year on year.

items.quote: we expect very frankly not expecting much of the recovery in the current quarter that is second quarter. But from the third quarter onwards we expect bit of the recovery and maybe it would be stabilized by the end of the fiscal.

items.quote: Let me tell you one European customer what it was there in FY, last quarter of this one FY 24, it was somewhere about say, 14 crore, of quarterly business. And in this particular quarter, June 24, it has increased to 22 crore, revenue.

items.statement: US-based customer started in May 2024 (delayed from Feb-Mar), expected to pick up in Q2 and Q3 FY25

items.quote: broadly 40% into the passenger segment, 10 to 12% into the EV hybrid and remaining into HCB and commercial industrial applications.

items.statement: Added new auto component customers in Europe and US; domestic bearing ring revenue grew 15-18% QoQ
items.quote: we have added a couple of new customers in Europe and in the US also something what it has been, you know, started to the first quarter

items.quote: by end of this fiscal, we are expecting at least 20% from my, European business

items.statement: Customers deferring shipments 15-45 days due to container shortages and high freight costs
items.quote: customers are also deferring certain you know, these small, lifting maybe a half container load they are waiting that let us have an entire container load. Let's postpone our lifting or shipment maybe for, 15, 30 days, 45 days or something like that.

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs 195-200 crore as of call date; zero long-term debt
items.quote: if you ask me, as on date, I am sitting on a, net cash or you can say, or including all my, this thing is it is touching somewhere about 195 to 200 crores

items.quote: Again, the same matter is there with the bankers and in last consortium meeting with our bankers, they are working on it. They are processing not because there are six nationalized banks. So maybe down the line they have asked maybe 40 to 45 days to again revert.

items.statement: Chinese competition exists but customers prioritize precision, supply chain reliability and one-stop solutions over price
items.quote: our customers, you know, those are very much clear or rather, their requirement of the component is highly precision components. And they are ready to pay the, you know, the, best, competitive price without, compromising on the quality front

items.statement: Sales volume 11,000 MT in Q1 FY25 vs 9,900 MT in Q4 FY24 and 10,000 MT in Q1 FY24; marginal tonnage growth offset by commodity price decline
items.quote: In terms of, you know, let me tell you the quantum of my this one, the sales, what it is there in the first quarter, it is somewhere about 11,000 metric ton what we have sold and which was 9900 metric ton, in the quarter 20, last quarter of FY 24

items.statement: Geopolitical factors and container shortages creating hurdles for European exports for last 15-24 months
items.quote: Demand slowdown, particularly in and apart from that this geopolitical reasons what it is there for last almost 15-18 months or 24 months. That is something creating hurdle.

items.statement: Auto component revenue target 45-50% of total by end of FY25 (from ~54% in Q1) as bearing rings recover in H2
items.quote: broadly, our target auto component business would be touching 45 to 50 percentage something by the end of this current fiscal of our overall contribution.

items.statement: CMC revenue target of INR1,000 crore by FY27 will be surpassed with new LOI and capex
items.quote: Earlier, we had talked about by FY '27, we'll touch INR1,000 crores of revenue. I think we will surpass that. With this new announcement and with the orders and the LOIs we've signed, we'll definitely surpass that number by FY '27. It will be over and above that INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Fifth LOI signed with agrochemical innovator for 5-year advanced intermediate supply
items.quote: We have recently signed a new letter of intent with an agrochemical innovator for an advanced intermediate for a new active ingredient. This LOI covers a period of 5 years.

items.statement: CMC pipeline has 12-15 additional products in development
items.quote: I would guess, at least another 12 to 15 products in the pipeline.

items.quote: The Board has also approved an investment of about INR160 crores to increase the production capacity of the Custom Manufactured Chemicals Division at Berigai.

items.statement: CMC Phase 2 expansion expected to commission by end of Q2 FY25
items.quote: Phase 2 of our CMC expansion is progressing well and is expected to get commissioned by the end of Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Phase 3 CMC civil infrastructure being built to accelerate future capacity addition
items.quote: A portion of this investment will go towards creating the infrastructure for the next multi-purpose production block.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA INR124 crore at 11% margin; gross margin improved QoQ from 31% to 40%
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, we reported an EBITDA of INR124 crores with an EBITDA margin of 11%. Our finance cost for the quarter stood at INR59 crores and the net profit for the quarter was at INR24 crores.

items.quote: The unit contribution in the last quarter, that is in, Q1 paste PVC is around INR21,000 per ton as against the suspension PVC was around INR14,500 per ton.

items.statement: Suspension PVC anti-dumping investigation ongoing against all major exporters; decision expected by Q3 FY25
items.quote: Suspension is in advanced stage. The petition has been filed, investigation initiate d, and we expect that maybe by Q3, we should see a decision on that

items.statement: Domestic PVC demand strong driven by infrastructure and construction; destocking easing in FY25
items.quote: Domestic demand continues to remain strong. India's infrastructure missions to provide access to clean water and improve irrigation are critical projects that are bolstering this growth.

items.statement: Net debt INR560-570 crore with cash balance ~INR800 crore
items.quote: Current net debt is around INR560 crores. We are carrying a cash of around INR800 crores, that is around INR570 crores of net debt.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals volumes up 44% YoY driven by new Paste PVC capacity commissioned in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The Specialty Chemicals Division's volumes increased by 44% on a year-on-year basis, mainly due to the commissioning of the new Paste PVC capacity in the last quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Paste PVC price improvement ~$150/ton seen but partially reversed due to EU imports and freight normalization
items.quote: We have seen an improvement of around $150 or so on prices that did happen. Some part of it would have been due to the container fre ight rate movement as

items.quote: The time period of those are typically anywhere between 3 to 5 years. And it may have a component related to the price structure or price formula. In some cases, there may also be some volume agreements or volume arrangements.

items.statement: LOI 5 adds INR300 crore cumulative revenue potential and INR125 crore annualized at steady state
items.quote: The 5th LOI will add INR300 crores to that. On an annualized basis on a steady state, this LOI still add around INR125 crores.

items.statement: Phase 3 CMC capacity commissioning timeline ~12 months from now, can accelerate based on pipeline
items.quote: I would say maybe another 12 months from where we are now, but we could do it much faster. It all depends on how the pipeline is.

items.quote: While Q1 performance was a positive start to the year, prices of PVC have again dropped in July. While this may impact Q2 performance, we believe that various measures being taken to stem the flow of low-cost imports into India, will bear fruit later in the year.

items.statement: Custom manufacturing currently a drag on EBITDA/kg but will improve as volumes ramp up
items.quote: Definitely, the Custom Manufactured Chemicals Business will move the needle as we go forward, especially given the very exciting growth possibilities that we have. So that is going to weigh in as we move along.

items.statement: Phase 1 and 2 CMC capacities fully utilized based on 5 LOIs; Phase 3 civil works underway for next block

items.statement: Custom manufacturing dispatches now evenly paced vs bunched in Q4 FY24
items.quote: This year, the Custom Manufacturing dispatches are reasonably evenly paced. So that is the difference that we are seeing. It is not a drop.

items.statement: R&D Phase 2 and pilot plant expansion commissioned; dedicated labs for hazardous chemistries added
items.quote: The second phase of the R&D was commissioned a couple of quarters back. And similarly, we have already commissioned the next phase of our pilot plant expansion.

items.statement: Suspension PVC revenue stable YoY, up 8% QoQ; positive profit swing from higher PVC prices and lower feedstock costs
items.quote: Suspension PVC revenue has been stable in Q1 FY '25 as compared to the corresponding period last year, while it has improved by 8% sequentially. We wi tnessed a positive swing in profits in the current quarter on account of both improved prices of suspension PVC and lower feedstock prices

items.statement: Management guides for 25% revenue growth in FY25 and expects to achieve historical pharma EBITDA margin of 23% this financial year.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margin to exceed 20% in Q3 and Q4 FY25, driven by operational leverage and gross margin improvement.

So, that add-up will definitely reach us more than 20% margin in this financial year only, hopefully, we will achieve in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Near finalization of a new CDMO contract with a large European originator for Ankleshwar Blocks 2 and 3; validation batches planned next quarter.
items.quote: We are in an active discussion, I think not active discussion but almost a finalization of signing one more contract as a CDMO with one of big originator based in Europe, samples, everything is done, now validation batches will be planned in next quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 210 bps sequentially to 42.1% in Q1 FY25 as raw material prices stabilized and company moves back to old pricing formula with long-term customers.
items.quote: As expected, RM prices have stabilized, and we are slowly moving back to old pricing formula with most of the long-term customer, and therefore, there was a good expansion of around 210 basis points in gross margin in Q1 FY '25 sequentially.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 16.7% in Q1 FY25 from 22.1% YoY due to lower gross margin YoY, higher employee costs from increments and new hires, and seasonal low revenue quarter.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 29.5 crores at 13.2% decrease year-on-year with EBITDA margin at 16.7% down from 22.1% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Advanced pharmaceutical intermediate business grew 16.6% YoY driven by strong CDMO and core product performance; specialty chemicals grew 10% YoY led by commodity chemicals, partially offset by subdued Baba Fine Chemicals.
items.quote: Our advanced pharmaceutical intermediate business reported revenue of Rs. 135 crores for the quarter, reflecting strong robust 16.6% Y-o-Y growth. This increase was driven by strong performance in both CDMO as well as the core product business.

items.statement: Semiconductor demand weak currently but expected to normalize by end of year; battery chemical sector evolving rapidly with capacity building for electrolyte additives and collaboration with global player for electrolyte solution capacity i
items.quote: In the semiconductor sector, despite the current demand is weak, the discussions with customers suggest that this is a short-term issue and demand is expected to normalize by the end of the year.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 15% YoY driven entirely by 18% volume growth, offset by 3% price decline; Q1 historically lowest quarter with sequential growth expected through Q4.
items.quote: So, we have got this 15% hike completely on a volume side that is 18% growth on volume side.

items.statement: Successfully completed PMDA inspection in Japan with no critical or major observations, potentially the only Indian chemical company with both US FDA and PMDA approvals in intermediates, opening opportunities in Japan.

To our knowledge, we may be the only chemical company in India to have successfully completed both US FDA and PMDA inspection in the Intermediate space.

items.statement: Apixaban orders started gradually across customers with peak sales expected in FY26; Rivaroxaban also expected to peak in FY26.
items.quote: Apixaban, your understanding is correct. Rivaroxaban is still we have to wait because it has still time. But we are moderately selling Rivaroxaban as well, but not at the peak right now.

items.quote: So, asset turn for Ankleshwar unit definitely will be more than 3x. But because of we have some good CDMO contracts already in place, it can go more than 4x also.

items.statement: Freight costs and extended delivery times increased due to geopolitical instability but managed through early booking; no sales lost, only incremental shipment cost impact on margins.
items.quote: It is not that great impact on our sales because we have an order in hand for longer period. So, we planned very strategically about the shipment as well. And accordingly, we booked our containers and all. But yes, it has impacted on the cost of the shipment, it is little bit incremental.

items.statement: All debt retired from QIP proceeds; net cash on hand ~Rs. 385 crores as of June; finance costs expected to decline sharply with significant debt repayment.
items.quote: So, as on June, net cash on hand is around Rs. 385 crores.

items.statement: QIP proceeds used to retire all debt; company now net cash positive.
items.quote: From QIP proceeds we have retired all the debt for the company, right? Abhishek Patel: Yes.

items.statement: Other expenses guided at 15-17% of total sales; expected to improve with operating leverage as revenue grows quarter-on-quarter.
items.quote: So, in this case, our other expenses should be ranging between 15% to 17% of the total sales. And as we grow quarter-on-quarter, with better topline, we will have a better leverage, and we will have a savings in this area.

items.statement: Fermion contract validation batches sent; qualification across 84 countries targeted this year with gradual ramp-up Q2-Q4 FY25 and full ramp-up FY26.
items.quote: We have already sent validation batches for the qualification at customer end. And by starting from Q2, Q3, Q4, it will gradually increasing, and it will fully ramp up in FY26 up to the maximum level.

items.statement: Enchem AMI Organics step-down subsidiary established for electrolyte manufacturing in India exclusively for Korean parent; JV terms finalization ongoing with regulatory complexities.

items.statement: Baba Fine Chemicals revenue ~Rs. 5 crores/quarter impacted by Heraeus customer headwinds and ownership change compliance; recovery expected H2 FY25 with new customer collaborations in Korea and Japan.
items.quote: For the past 2 to 3 quarters, BFC has been operating around Rs. 5 crores revenue per quarter affected by business integration and demand issue from our client side. We expect a recovery to begin in second half of the year.

items.statement: Employee costs increased due to annual increments and new hires for Ankleshwar plant.
items.quote: Second is increase in employee costs, higher expenses this quarter resulted from annual increments and new hires for the Ankleshwar Plant.

items.statement: Chinese oversupply pressures pricing in advanced pharma intermediates and commodity chemicals; specialty players with technology-driven processes less impacted.
items.quote: The competitive threat from China's manufacturing capability remains significant, and I expect certain segments of the chemical sector to stay under pressure. items.statement: Exports face longer lead times and higher freight rates; managed through strategic shipment planning and early container booking; no supply restrictions.
items.quote: Geopolitical instability worldwide has led to extended delivery times and higher freight rates over the past quarter, although input prices have stabilized, they remain low, continuing to exert pressure on the pricing of finished goods.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of ~15% average with blended EBITDA margin of 20-21%
items.quote: We have already given the guidance that the revenue growth should be around 15% on an average with an blended EBITDA margin of about 20% to 21%.

items.statement: Copper and gold outlook positive with projects coming online; market growing 2-3%, liner business ~5%

items.quote: The total group revenues for Q1 of FY 2025 stood at INR352 crores with an EBITDA of INR76 crores, that is at an EBITDA margins of 21%.

items.statement: Group order book INR560 crores at June 2024 end vs INR520 crores June 2023, excluding long-term orders like NMDC
items.quote: We also have a strong order book at a group level of INR560 crores as at June 2024 end, vis -a-vis an order book of INR520 crores as of June 2023, without considering the long term orders like NMDC in Tega McNally.

items.statement: Chile project construction started, commercial production targeted by June 2025; additional 51,000 sqm land acquired for future expansion
items.quote: We intend to start the commercial production for the new facility by June of 2025. The Chile project will assist us in consolidating the existing facilities and adding new capacity.

items.statement: Heightened shipping costs will be passed on to customers in most cases; logistics cost increase minimal due to pass-through
items.quote: The impact of heightened shipping costs will be passed on to the customers in most of the cases.

items.statement: Supply chain more vigilant with better planning for raw materials and customer deliveries; inventory built up
items.quote: Our supply chain is more vigilant with better planning for both raw material, as well as customer deliveries. We have built up the inventory and are in constant communication with all our customers.

items.statement: European order executing well for 6+ months, generating ~INR10 crores monthly cash flow over 5+1 year term
items.quote: This order, particularly on an average, generates about INR10 crores of cash flow per month, which is on a steady state basis and keeps continuing accruing us over the period of five plus one, that is six years.

items.statement: Metso is major global competitor; Tega products equal or superior, leading in DynaPrime; continuous R&D investment to stay ahead
items.quote: Metso is our major competitor globally. And our product, both from quality and other aspects of deliverance of value to the customer is in no way second to anyone, okay? And on some of the fronts, including DynaPrime, we are the leaders in that segment.

items.statement: All regulatory approvals including construction received for Chile project
items.quote: We have received all regulatory approvals including construction for the Chile project and have started the construction activity.

items.statement: 75% revenue from exports, 25% domestic (includes 100% of McNally revenue)
items.quote: 75% is my exports on this thing and 25% is domestic sales. In that domestic sales, McNally is -- the entire McNally 100% revenue is a part of that domestic sales.

items.statement: Logistics cost pass-through to customers with small time lag; no significant increase in logistics cost
items.quote: The logistics cost is basically is -- we do not have too much of increase in the logistics cost because we pass on the logistics cost to our customers because small time lag.

items.statement: Open to acquisitions at right strategic value fitment for capability, technology or geographical expansion
items.quote: We are open for any acquisition which comes, but then it has to be at the right value for us. If it's the right value fitment, we are definitely open and we will explore that if it's a strategic fit for us.

items.statement: Shipping routes via Red Sea remain challenging with port congestion and container delays; proactive measures in place from COVID experience
items.quote: From a logistics point of view, the shipping routes continue to be a challenge with shipping lines evading the conflict stricken Red Sea, congestion at major ports along these alternative routes has escalated, delaying the container turnaround times.

items.statement: High employee engagement drives customer satisfaction; team feels engaged and committed globally
items.quote: I believe that high employee engagement leads to improved customer satisfaction, that in turn leads to bett er business results. Our employees across the globe feel engaged and

items.quote: The equipment business performance was lower in the current quarter due to delay in receipt of payments, inspection reports and certain dispatch clearance certificates fr om few customers, which is expected to be regularized in Q2 of the current financial year

items.statement: Tega McNally consortium won NMDC order: INR872 crores total (INR120 crores Tega McNally share) for 7MTPA iron ore plant over 26 months
items.quote: Tega McNally has formed a consortium for designing and commissioning of a new 7 million ton per annum iron ore scre ening and beneficiation plant at Donimalai for NMDC Limited. items.statement: Solar installations at Samali, Kalyani, Dahej plants totaling 1600-1700 kWh; no specific cost savings quantified yet
items.quote: Totally, if you see it's about 1600 to 1700 kilowatt hours of solar power, what we intend to harness.

items.statement: Tega McNally integration milestones and synergy targets progressing as per plan; 18-24 month integration timeline on track
items.quote: The integration milestones and the synergy targets are progressing as per the integration plan and we are satisfied with the progress made till date.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is INR 45-50 crores
items.quote: Our capex, if I look at the years gone by was focused largely on digitization and innovations. While that continues, we'll also keep investing on areas like R&D, etc. But we expect the year to end somewhere between INR 45 crores to INR 50 crores.

items.statement: Demand sentiment muted due to high food inflation; no material change expected in short term
items.quote: As we look at the period ahead, we do not see the demand sentiment changing materially in the short term. I think the food inflation being persistently high has dampened sentiment, the demand sentiment, consumer sentiment.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin at lifetime high 11.5% in Q1 FY25, up 166 bps YoY
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margins at 11.5% grew 166 basis points year on year.

items.statement: PBT margin pre-ESOP at 9.1%, up 219 bps YoY; PAT margin at 6.8%, up 186 bps YoY
items.quote: PBT margins pre-ESOP grew 219 basis points to 9.1% and PAT margins expanded 186 basis points to 6.8%.

items.statement: Service AMC volumes growing; revenue recognition lags 3-4 quarters due to 18-20 month amortization
items.quote: The second is that, as you can imagine, AMCs have a fairly long tenure. The average tenure is anywhere between 18 to 20 months. So, hence, the amortization happens over a fairly long Q1 FY25 Earnings Conference Call August 09, 2024 period of time. And hence, it will take three to four quarters for this to start getting reflected in the reported

items.statement: Commodity prices (polymers) rose in June; monitoring if trend sustains
items.quote: we've seen in the month of June in particular are in the case of certain commodities like polymers, we've seen prices go up. It's still Q1 FY25 Earnings Conference Call August 09, 2024 at a stage where we are in a bit of a wait-and-watch mode to see whether this sustains or not

items.statement: Vacuum cleaner ASPs rising significantly due to shift to convenient cleaning (robotics, upright) at ~4x conventional ASP
items.quote: And as you can imagine, the convenient cleaning segment comes at almost a 4X ASP higher than the conventional cleaning ASPs. So as the category mix evolves and moves towards convenient cleaning, both robotics and upright vacuum cleaner, we are seeing the ASPs improve.

items.statement: Water purifier ASPs up but range-bound; both premium and economy segments growing
items.quote: Equally, in water, there will be both the bookends growing. We will grow the premium segment through innovations and through point-of-sale innovations and interventions. There will also be a lot of effort in driving penetration. So I would say the ASPs will be, I think, up, but will be range-bound in the case of water.

items.statement: Market share gain in water purifiers vs same time last year, driven by premium segment
items.quote: Yes, pretty static report that we have seen a market share gain in water purifiers versus same time last year. And I think the good news is that we are beginning to see the impact of our premium innovations kick in.

items.statement: All regions grew double-digit; Tier-2/3 towns grew faster than Tier-1 metros
items.quote: is that our revenue growth across regions was in double-digit and all regions grew well. And there was no specific reason that was an outlier when it came to growth. In terms of town-wise growth, again, all town tiers grew, but what was an interesting sort of nuance was that our Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns grew faster than the tier-1 towns in metros

items.statement: >75% of economy water purifier buyers are first-time users
items.quote: And I think the good news and encouraging part is that more than 75% of customers who enter, who buy economy products, are first-time users.

items.statement: Welcomes competition including MNC entrant; believes category needs more innovation to unlock penetration

items.statement: Existing manufacturing capacity adequate for current volume growth; no significant capex needed
items.quote: Even if I look at the volume growth that we've had, it's not required any significant investments on the manufacturing side. Our capacities are adequate to cater to it.

items.statement: Service revenue amortized over 18-20 months; costs incurred upfront causing margin compression in Q2
