Hence, what happens is that the AMC that you sell, for example, in a particular quarter, the revenue of that gets amortized over 18 months to 20 months. However, the cost for acquiring that AMC, that cost entirely comes upfront.

items.statement: Water purifier category penetration only ~6% in India; TAM expected to reach INR 23,000-24,000 crores in 5-6 years
items.quote: The expectation is that the categories in which we operate will anyway be between INR 23,000 to INR 24,000 crores in five to six years' time.

items.statement: RO segment growing faster than UV due to inconsistent source water quality
items.quote: So, Sri, I think clearly given the deteriorating water quality across the country, we are seeing the RO segment grow faster.

items.statement: High food inflation dampening consumer sentiment; demand environment could be brighter
items.quote: I think the food inflation being persistently high has dampened sentiment, the demand sentiment, consumer sentiment. That said, I think we have strong set of plans that we have deployed already.

items.statement: Rental model in pilot phase; not scaled up yet; prioritization decision pending
items.quote: Rental, as we've been saying, in our earlier calls as well, remains an area of opportunity that we are watching closely. And it's an area where we believe we have a right to win. We have not scaled up a rental project yet. It is in pilot, we are looking at it closely.

items.statement: Bundled AMC proportion at sale is very low; customers prefer to defer AMC decision
items.quote: The proportion of bundled AMCs upfront is very, very low. And I think if you think about the point I made earlier that one of the barriers that the customers face very often in the category, especially new entrants, is what they believe is a high cost of product and high cost of service.

items.statement: NPS at lifetime high in Q1; significant complaints closed within one hour
items.quote: Our NPS has never been higher. Our lifetime high NPS is what we reached in Q1 well above what we had in Q1 at the same time last year or indeed above the recent year of Q4, number one. Number two, we are seeing a significant number of complaints getting closed within one hour of either the customer facing the complaint or the customer's desired time of resolution.

items.statement: Management expects volumes to improve from Q1 but will wait another quarter to give proper guidance; growth slightly lower than earlier targets
items.quote: It will definitely be better than Q1, but still because of global uncertainties, demand in US and Europe is still subdued. So, we haven't been able to get a clear picture of how much we will be growing.

items.statement: Rail EBITDA/TEU at Rs 9,400; margin slipped due to lower volumes and double stack percentage down 2%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin has slipped a little bit because of the low volumes and our double stack percentage has gone down by say 2% this quarter so that reflects on the EBITDA margin

items.statement: CFS EBITDA per TEU improved to Rs 1,350-1,375 from Rs 540 last quarter
items.quote: CFS has maintained the same volume. And I mean the margins on CFS, if you compare them from the last quarter, which was from three digits have gone up to Rs.1,350 - Rs.1,375, last quarter it was Rs.540 only.

items.statement: EXIM growth expected to continue but pace uncertain; will clarify by end of quarter whether single or double digit
items.quote: I think the EXIM growth will continue. How much? That is to be seen. We cannot make any forward announcements or looking at what is happening everywhere. We will continue to grow.

items.statement: Overall India EXIM volume expected to grow at 5-6% level
items.quote: Overall, I think India is expected to grow at 5% - 6% level in terms of EXIM volume.

items.statement: Waste paper volumes down 30% at Kashipur and 10% at Ludhiana; bookings improving in July-August
items.value: 30% drop in Kashipur, 10% drop in Ludhiana
items.quote: Kashipur, 85% of the waste paper is import. So, there has been close to 30% drop in Kashipur. And in Ludhiana we have 20% of our import volumes and there has been almost 10% Gateway Distriparks Limited & drop in the import waste

items.statement: Jaipur terminal expected operational in 12-15 months; litigation ongoing but backup plan exists
items.quote: According to our present estimates, we will be operational in about 12-months from now.

items.statement: New northern terminal land identified; will be full-fledged ICD at one of their hubs
items.quote: It will be in north of India. So, it is yet to crystallize, I mean we have identified the land and once we have a deal and we acquire the land that will be the appropriate time to inform the location.

items.statement: Double stack percentage fell from 39% average last year to 33% in Q1; recovery to 40%+ will directly improve EBITDA
items.quote: So, last year we averaged at about 39%, but this quarter, we were at 33%. As and when the volume cut back and the imbalance within the ports also like Mundra, Pipavav, JNPT our volumes, some were import-heavy, some were export-heavy.

items.statement: Road has advantage with 10% busy season surcharge; passed on to customers but hope for revision
items.quote: So, little bit, road does have an advantage with the 10% busy season surcharge that came in. Although we passed it on, w e had no choice but to pass it on to our customers and that's been fully implemented now

items.statement: Lost market share YoY in Uttarakhand (25%) and Ludhiana (22.5% from 28%) due to pricing competition on low-value commodities
items.quote: Between Q4 and Q1, we are at the same market share that we had, but it's on a YoY basis we have lost market share in places like Uttarakhand and Ludhiana which we have mentioned in the last few quarters due to pricing competition.

items.statement: Faridabad double stacking completion in couple of months will help regain volumes lost to competitor
items.quote: One big factor is one location which has been connected on double stack and that's why the leader in our sector is gaining from that. As soon as Faridabad, which we just mentioned, is nearing completion, once that is operational, we will get quite a good s hare back what we have lost because of the double stacking advantage and to our competitor

items.statement: Low-value commodities (waste paper ~20%, scrap ~5%) constitute ~25% of volumes; concentrated in Kashipur (80%) and Ludhiana (20-25%)
items.quote: So, if you look at the low value commodities, we need to see a split into import and export. So, what we are talking about is that due to the dip in imports on the low value, so basically one is waste paper that constitutes about 20% of the overall volumes.

items.statement: DFC western corridor completion guided for December 2025; 93% complete up to Vaitarna
items.quote: DFC is giving us guidance of December 2025. And again, the status is the same that 93% of the total WDFC has completed up to Vaitarna and the last leg of 100 kilometers is still going to take a lot of time.

items.statement: Evaluating sale of all five CFS locations together; not piecemeal; Nhava Sheva property expected to fetch good valuation
items.quote: I don't think it will be a piecemeal affair. We let go all the five locations at a proper valuation.

items.statement: Stake in Snowman increased to 46.4%; can acquire up to 5% per year under creeping acquisition; may cross 50% this FY
items.quote: See, we are all owed to acquire 5% under creeping acquisition rules. So, last year we acquired 5%, this year we have acquired a little over 1% and we are at 46.4% now and if we complete the full 5% acquisition in this financial year, so we should be ending up little over 50

items.statement: Snowman 5PL vertical targets 25%+ YoY growth; new ice cream/dairy client to contribute Rs 15-18 cr/quarter from August
items.quote: So, as we explained last time, we have expectations of more than 25% year-on-year growth on this particular vertical to distribute which is the 5PL vertical.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing business expects 12-15% growth this year with new facilities in Lucknow and Kolkata
items.quote: considering the new facilities which are going to be functional in next month, Lucknow and after that Kolkata, and also some of the lease capacities which we are yet to fully utilize, considering all these, we expect around 12% to 15% growth in warehousing business this year.

items.statement: Snowman Q1 margins impacted by Rs 2-2.5 cr one-off costs; Q4 had provision reversals; underlying margins stable
items.quote: So, there are two reasons. One is, there has been some one -off cost which we accounted in this particular quarter, which were one-time cost and we had to take that in repairs and maintenance and some of the accounting

items.statement: Tax rate to stay at 6-7% for next two years
items.quote: Yes, it will stay like this for the next two years at least.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 245 crores (lowest); gross debt Rs 310 crores; down significantly from Rs 800 crores peak
items.quote: Our debt situation is very good right now. I mean we at our lowest net debt to INR 245 crores compared to which was at one-time INR 800 crores or something and even from last quarter last year, if you see it has come down significantly.

items.statement: Capex this quarter not significant; full year plans include Jaipur and new northern terminal
items.quote: not significant CAPEX this quarter, but for the overall year, we still have plans like we have been announcing for one new terminal is in immediate site, plus some balance on Jaipur land.

items.statement: Kashipur long-term target 5,000-6,000 TEUs/month in 5 years; Jaipur target 3,000 TEUs/month in 3 years
items.quote: longer term what we were saying in five years we should be doing 5,000 - 6,000 from this location that will remain the same.

items.statement: NCR market ~2.9 lakh TEUs/quarter; Ludhiana ~65,000 TEUs/quarter (down from 80,000 Q4); Uttarakhand 20,000-25,000 TEUs/quarter
items.quote: roughly if you look at NCR, it was about 2.9 lakhs for the quarter, this is the whole volume of NCR. And if we look at it Q1 last year, it was a very similar figure. So, less than a pe rcent variance. And Q4 was slightly higher; it was crossing 3 lakhs

items.statement: Global uncertainties (Red Sea, port congestion, US/Europe demand) affecting visibility; election and budget policy changes added to Q1 weakness
items.quote: overall that red sea impact still continues, there has a lot of port congestion at various international ports, vessel schedule has been erratic over the last few months. But slightly we have seen some improvement towards June, July is also looking slightly better.

items.statement: CFS revenue impacted by Rs 8.43 cr accounting change (discounts netted from revenue); no impact on EBITDA/TEU
items.quote: This is basically a business model done with consolidators, but it was discount being passed on was actually earlier being counted in the revenue. But as per the accounting standard now, that comes under gross revenue, but under net revenue we have to remove this discount.

items.statement: Acquired 2.2 acres of land in Mumbai Oshiwara from MHADA for Rs. 125.11 crores to build a ~500 bed super specialty hospital.
items.quote: We are extremely pleased to acquire 2.2 acres of prime land in Mumbai Oshiwara in an auction from Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA). This is an important milestone in Medanta's growth journey, as we plan to establish a state of the art ~500 bed super specialty hospital in Oshiwara.

items.statement: Board approved construction of service apartment guest house at Gurugram campus with investment of approximately Rs. 250 crores.
items.quote: have secured Board approval to construct the service apartment guest house on the Medanta Medicity GurugramGurugram campus. This project, with an investment of approximately Rs. 250 crores, will cater to the growing demand from international as well as out of town domestic patients

items.statement: Added 49 census beds in Gurugram mother and child department and 18 new dialysis beds at Patna unit.
items.quote: We have added 49 census beds in Gurugram in our mother and child department, as Dr. Trehan already mentioned. Furthermore, we have added 18 new dialysis beds at our Patna unit, as the demand for our nephrology services in the region continues to remain strong.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin declined to 23.6% due to employee cost increments and sluggish Lucknow growth; mature hospitals EBITDA grew 11.6%.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 2,082 million, an increase of 4.5% year-on-year basis, with an EBITDA margin of 23.6%. Our margins have declined primarily due to increase in employee cost on account of annual increments and some sluggish growth in our Lucknow unit.

items.statement: Outpatient pharmacy revenue increased 25.6% YoY from Rs. 266 million to Rs. 334 million.
items.quote: Our outpatient pharmacy business revenue increased by 25.6% from Rs. 266 million in Q1 FY24 to Rs. 334 million in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: International patient revenue was Rs. 475 million (~6% of total revenue), flat YoY vs Rs. 477 million.
items.quote: During the quarter, revenue from international patients was Rs. 475 million, compared to Rs. 477 million in the same quarter last year. This accounts for approximately 6% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Started treating Ayushman Bharat patients in Lucknow; applied for CGHS and other government scheme empanelment.
items.quote: indicated in our earlier calls, with the increased bed capacity, we have already signed up and started treating patients in Ayushman Bharat Scheme. Furthermore, we have applied for empanelment with the CGHS and other government schemes

items.statement: Planned equipment investments in Lucknow include new biplane Cath Lab and Da Vinci Xi surgical robot; additional investments in Indore and Ranchi.
items.quote: We will be putting in a new Cath Lab, we already have two Cath Labs, we will be adding in our third Cath Lab, in fact it's a biplane Cath Lab, so it's a pretty high end machine. We will be adding in a Da Vinci Xi surgical robot that should come onboard in next several weeks.

items.statement: Manpower cost increases budgeted for the year due to talent competition; clinical talent additions to continue impacting costs.
items.quote: We do anticipate and have budgeted a certain increase in the manpower cost on an overall basis, as well as some maybe on a percentage of revenue basis, just because we feel that there will be increasing intensity for high quality talent given all the various hospitals and all the excitement and investment going into hospitals and healthcare.

items.statement: Operating leverage expected to improve developing hospital margins as volumes recover; scheme patients viewed as margin-accretive due to low marginal cost.
items.quote: Overall, our belief is that because the marginal cost to serve every incremental patient for us is significantly lower. We generally believe that increased volume, even at lower realizations is margin accretive, and we have seen that play out again and agai n, year-over-year in our GurugramGurugram facility

items.statement: Lucknow performance below expectations; management not satisfied but cautions against using last year's high baseline (seasonal dengue, lower bed count).
items.quote: we are by no means satisfied with this performance. But I would caution if we put a baseline of saying, you will be at 75% let's not forget that we have increased Global Health Limited – Medanta August 09, 2024 bed capacity and some of the performance, which you saw last year were really, really I would say above normal performance

items.statement: No financial guidance provided; management refuses to give specific projections for mature or developing hospitals.
items.quote: As we have stated multiple times, we don't give any future projections or any expectations with respect to the specific numbers on either of our developing or matured hospitals.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue growth guidance 20-25% YoY and EBITDA margin 20-22%
items.quote: We are on the track to achieve FY25 guidance of consolidated revenue growth of 20 %-25% year-on-year and EBITDA margin in the range of 20 %-22%.

items.statement: Block 1 of 2 lakh sq ft commercialized in May 2024; Block 2 of 2 lakh sq ft expected by March 2025
items.value: 5 lakh sq ft total greenfield expansion
items.quote: Block 1 of 2 lakh square feet in May 2024. This is just one part of our overall green field expansion project of 5 lakh square feet. Block 2 of another 2 lakh square feet is expected to be completed by March 2025

items.statement: Block 1 operational for LED home lighting, solar panels, systems and new categories; Block 2 civil construction ongoing
items.value: 2 lakh sq ft operational; 2 lakh sq ft under construction
items.quote: Block one of our new integrated facility, nearly 2 lakh square feet, is commercialized in May 2024. This facility will be used for the manufacturing of LED home lighting, solar panels, systems, and other new categories of products.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 13% impacted by new facility costs, USA subsidiary start-up and higher employee costs; expected to stabilize by H2 FY25
items.quote: The EBITDA margin was at 13%, which was impacted by the higher employee benefit cost, operational cost for the new facility and starting of our USA subsidiary.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue up 17% YoY and 34% QoQ across all three verticals; domestic lighting market flat, Gulf exports aided product display
items.quote: For instance, if you look at our revenues, Q1 FY25, it was up 17% year -on-year and 34% quarter-on-quarter. This was an account of all our three vertical business we are doing.

items.statement: Hearables and Wearables sales commenced in Q1 with prestigious clients onboarded; categorized under product display segment for now
items.quote: Coming to the Hearables and Wearables segment, I am happy to inform you that our sales have commenced in quarter 1 and we have successfully on boarded few prestigious clients in this segment.

items.statement: US subsidiary started ESCO and solar product business; initial orders executed with bought-out items impacting margins
items.quote: Yes, if you talk of the business that has come into the direct, I mean, into the subsidiary that is there in the U.S., which is new. So that is the category that we have started in this subsidiary.

items.statement: Main customer Signify was slow last quarter; now things improved across sectors; RV business turnaround expected by H2 FY25
items.quote: Our main customers, the Signify were a little slow. And the overall business, that was a degrowth. So similarly, in the inshore lighting, the main reliance and others were little, but they were revamping their things. So but now the things are almost improved at all the sectors.

items.statement: Exports from India ~INR 12-13 crore in Q1 FY25 with good jump QoQ; UAE exports started, Saudi market potential
items.quote: And I'm just looking for the number right now, it's somewhere close to around INR12 crores to INR13 crores that we posted in that, the export business from India.

items.statement: Debt-free balance sheet maintained; IPO debt repayment completed immediately after IPO
items.quote: Our financial position continued to remain strong with a debt -free balance sheet, well -funded capex cycle and healthy return ratio.

items.statement: More than half of IPO proceeds deployed; on track to deploy rest within set timeline
items.quote: We have now deployed more than half of the IPO fund and are on course to complete, deploying the rest within the timeline we set for ourselves.

items.statement: Target ROCE 30-35% for Hearables and Wearables business once fully established
items.quote: So in that case if you look at the ROCE going forward once this business is fully established our target is to stay in the range of 30% to 35% when it comes to the return on capital employed and that is what we are targeting with this particular business as well

items.statement: Pre-IPO ROCE consistently 30-35%; FY24 ROCE decline due to capex investments; expected to return to 30-35% as new factories ramp
items.quote: But if you look at pre-IPO proceeds before we started making all these investments, our ROCE has always been consistent in the line of 30% to 35%. And going forward, once the expenditure that we have made in the new factories and the expenses that we are currently doing, it is going to give the returns in the near future.

items.statement: Fine Technologies merged into Royalux Lighting recently
items.quote: Yes. So we've merged Fine Technologies into Royalux Lighting. So that is something that we've done recently.

items.statement: Full backward integration in-house: metal, plastic, CNC, moulds, powder coating, tool designing and tool making
items.quote: Yes. We are doing metal, plastic, even doing CNC, even doing our mo ulds. A month and a half before all that, all the investors they visited our facility, they have seen that everything is somewhere under installation, some machines are already installed, including the powder coating and all, everything we are doing in -house. Even the tool designing, tool making is also we are doing in-house.

items.statement: Standalone margins normalized at current ~11% EBITDA after price corrections last year due to muted demand; Q4 FY24 to Q1 FY25 margins steady and growing
items.quote: So we believe that if you look at the standalone numbers, where we are today, this is the margin range for this business. Because last year due to that, muted supply, there was a lot of panic, I would say in the industry, because the demand certainly, was nose diving.

items.statement: Gross margin volatility 36-46% driven by US subsidiary bought-out items and minimum wage increase; temporary phase expected to normalize
items.quote: This year, first quarter the only reason for this sort of decline is the kind of business that we did in the first quarter in the US subsidiary. Like I told in the previous question also that because of the constraint in time and we wanted to establish that relationship with the client.

items.statement: Consistently ahead of peers due to new product lines and backward integration setup; industry saw big decline in FY24 while IKIO remained consistent
items.quote: Even if you look at last year, if you compare our peers to us, we've sort of much ahead of everyone. Yes, so that was only due to the fact that, we constantly bring in new products, we constantly, work on new product lines, not just the new products, but even product categories or product lines.

items.statement: New verticals require team setup and product development expenditure; shorter timeline due to existing electronics design and manufacturing expertise
items.quote: Initially, the costs are generally very high when it comes to establishing the team, development of the product, the sample, a lot of cost is involved a nd by the time you start reaping the benefits . And for us I think we feel that because the kind of business that we've been doing since a very long time which is into lighting and electronics. So we feel that time for us is going to be fairly sho

items.statement: RV business inventory clearances continuing quarter on quarter in energy solutions segment
items.quote: In the segment of energy solution and others, we are witnessing continued pickup in inventory clearances quarter on quarter.

items.statement: Government sudden minimum wage increase impacted gross margin in last quarter
items.quote: What happened is actually, in the last quarter, the government suddenly increased the minimum wages also but because of that also gross margin.

items.statement: Other income increased YoY due to FD income from unutilized IPO proceeds and forex capital gains
items.quote: So other income is , one is our normal income from FDs of the unutilized proceeds from the IPO. And then there is some forex capital gain also, currency, there is something that also we got.

items.statement: Management expects 30-40% top-line CAGR over the next three years
items.quote: If you want to know, then the company will grow at a pace of 30% to 40% per annum in the next coming three years.

items.statement: Revenue growth of at least 30% expected from new flagship showroom
items.quote: We are expecting revenue growth of at least 30% from the new store.

items.statement: Current capex sufficient for flagship showroom; further capex to be decided later
items.quote: The current capex is whatever the company is holding. It is going to work with the current capex for the next coming up showroom. And the further requirement of capital would be decided by the management on a later scale.

items.statement: New 10,000 sq ft flagship showroom in Sowcarpet opening in 9-12 months (Jan-Apr FY26)
items.quote: We will be recalibrating our revenue distribution, focusing entirely onto the B2C segment in our new showroom to enhance our market position and better serve our customers.

items.statement: Plan to open five to six showrooms in two years after flagship launch
items.quote: Initially, our flagship showroom would be opening in another 9 to 12 months. And further from there for the coming two years, we have an expansion plan of geographical expansion here around five to six showrooms in the coming years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin currently around 5.5%; expected to rise as B2C mix increases (B2B ~4%, B2C ~8-9%)
items.quote: The current EBITDA margin is around 5.5% and it is since we are expanding into the retail segment for the coming years, the margin would be surely increasing because the difference between the B2B and B2C segment the margins are around for B2B segment it is around 4% and for B2C it is around 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Retail (B2C) to contribute ~25% of top line after new showroom opens
items.quote: Among that 25% of the top line would be in retail in the coming years after the opening of showroom.

items.statement: Custom duty cut on gold/silver (15% to 6%) and platinum (12.5% to 6.4%) lowers procurement costs; benefit passed to customers immediately
items.quote: Yes, obviously. It is the price is amended immediately from the time of his amendment, the prices of the gold and silver has been reduced. And from the same period, it has been transferred to the clients also because the prices immediately changes, and it gets affected to the market immediately.

items.statement: Shift to lightweight, budget jewellery due to rising gold prices; new designs added daily
items.quote: Since the gold prices have been appreciating, everybody prefers to buy a lightweight jewellery, a budgeted jewellery. So we have been manufacturing that too. And we are, on a daily basis, making researchers to make products more attractive and more reachable.

items.statement: B2B client base includes major multi-store jewellers and generational jewellers across South India
items.quote: We are working with all the major jewellers who are famous and who are operating in multi-stores. Those players who are having familiar name, Pan India. And a few traditional jewelers who are having a very famous and who have been working with us from past four decades, five decades.

items.statement: No exports currently; working on plans to enter export market
items.quote: The company has been currently we do not engage in exports, but the company has further plans of making. We are working on going expansion towards the export market.

items.statement: Current working capital sufficient for flagship showroom; further funding to be decided later
items.quote: Currently, the current stocks and the current working capital will be enough sufficient for the opening of this initial flagship showroom. On a later scale, when there are further expansions, the management will be deciding on getting the source of funds for expansion.

items.statement: Sanctioned loan limit INR 38 cr; utilisation INR 17-18 cr last quarter
items.value: INR 38 crores sanctioned; INR 17 to INR 18 crores utilised
items.quote: I am sorry. It is a limit that is sanctioned for INR38 crores, but the company has been last quarterly utilizing it to the extent of INR17 to INR18 crores.

items.statement: Focus shifting to high-value temple jewellery, diamond and polki jewellery in new showroom
items.quote: Since we are going to add all the premium products along with the diamond jewellery and polki jewellery of the new showroom, so the margins are going to be higher.

items.statement: Organised sector share rose from 17% (2019) to 34% now; duty cut to accelerate shift
items.quote: If you take a data wise, if you say it was around 17% was with the organized sector in 2019. Now it has been improved to 34%. And after the reduction of duty, it is going to be a very plus point for the organized sector

items.statement: Primary raw material is fine gold; pilferage/wastage 0.8-2% during manufacturing
items.quote: It is around, say, 0.8 to 2%.

items.statement: Artisan relationships span 25-40 years across India; design library >5 lakh unique designs
items.quote: We have been working with artisans who are along with us from last 40 years, 30 years, 25 years, who are working with the company and providing us the best quality craftsmanship for the company and for its customers.

items.statement: No split or bonus decided yet; management will decide later
items.quote: That management has to decide. Till now, nothing of that sort has been decided. Later on, anything which will be decided will be surely posted.

items.statement: Gold price rise seen as positive; no demand concern as gold viewed as investment
items.quote: No, no issue at all. Since the prices have been increasing and it is providing a better return opportunity for all the investors who have invested in gold in regular interval. So, everybody is optimistic about gold in near future also.

items.statement: Targets ~19.5% EBITDA margin for Q2-Q4 FY25
items.quote: However, we remain quite confident in our ability to achieve about 19.5% EBITDA margin mark in the fo llowing three

items.statement: Targets 4.5-5% revenue contribution from steel bottles and houseware in FY25
items.quote: Overall, we are targeting around 4.5% to 5% contribution coming from steel bottles and steel bottles and household as a category both put together around 4.5% to 5% of the overall revenue.

items.statement: Pen demand picked up in second half of Q1 after elections; own brands grew 7% YoY domestically
items.quote: Overall, demand picked up in the second half of quarter post the peak of elections. Despite facing such challenges in the demand environment our own brands grew by 7% year -on-year in the domestic market signifying their resilience and wider market

items.statement: Creative segment grew 21.4% YoY to INR 37 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Creative as a segment increased in Q1 25 by 21.4% year-on-year with the revenue clocking in at INR37 crores.

items.statement: Steel bottles grew 116% YoY to INR 8 crores with growing order book
items.quote: Steel bottles has gathered the momentum registering a 116% year-on-year increase to INR8 crores. Aggressive scaling, robust enquiries and a growing order book in the category provide an exciting outlook for this segment.

items.statement: Overall ASP increased to INR 5.29 in Q1 FY25 from INR 5.27 in Q1 FY24
items.quote: Despite certain challenges, our ASP for the overall business increased from INR 5.27 in Q1 24 and INR 5.17 in Q4 24 to current INR 5.29 in Q1 25, a testament of our focus on premiumization strategy.

items.statement: Own brand sales mix improved to 87% in Q1 FY25 from 83% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: Contribution of our own brand sales to overall mix improved to 87% in Q1 25 from 83% Q124 with overall own brand sales growing by 5% on year-on-year basis to INR215 crores.

items.statement: Export own brand sales declined 9% due to Red Sea freight issues; export OEM grew 10%
items.quote: Persistent geopolitical issues around the Red Sea have raised freight costs and created a shortage of shipping containers, bottlenecking supply to the export markets thus affecting overseas own brand sales although demand remains intact. However, we received a very encouraging update from export OEM segment which is on a gradual, but a definite path of recovery, increasing by 10% in the current qu

items.statement: Domestic OEM demand subdued, expected to remain at Q1 levels; to be offset by own brand growth
items.quote: Domestic OEM face a subdued demand and is expected to remain at current quarterly levels whi ch we propose to make up from our own brand sales in domestic market

items.statement: Capex plans on track; creative manufacturing lines ordered, targeting 75% in-house by end of FY25 or early FY26
items.quote: So, as we mentioned that, the capex plan is already on and, everything is in time as per the schedule. And, once the capex, similarly, even for the creative, all the manufacturing lines have been already ordered and set up. So, I think by the end of t he year or early next year we should be making , up to 75% of our total business. What we get from creative would be manufactured in-house

items.statement: Added 20+ distributors and 15 salesmen for steel bottles; entered Reliance and other modern trade
items.quote: Yes. So, in domestic market for steel bottles, we have already appointed 20 plus distributors and we have also recruited around 15 salesmen. And other than that, we have also set up a separate department to cater to modern trade and we have already, got into Reliance and other departmental stores.

items.statement: GST demands mostly replied/settled; two under appeal but liability not substantial
items.quote: Almost all of the GST demands have been replied to or have been settled. So, we don't see a liability out here at our end because... Vimalchand Rathod: There will be some liability. Because it is an appeal. So, as soon as the appeal is settled, then we will know the exact -- But it will not be

items.statement: Steel sourced from India and importers from Korea, Vietnam, China; BIS standards to reduce imports over time
items.quote: And as BIS standards will become more stringent these imports will reduce going on and on. And also from our part, we are having a combi nation of sourcing from steel from India as well as a couple of importers which import from various countries like Korea, Vietnam and other countries and China for us

items.statement: Alpesh Porwal appointed as new CFO with two decades experience; Mayur Gala ceased as CFO and KMP
items.quote: It gives me immense pleasure to welcome Mr. Alpesh Porwal as the new Chief Financial Officer of the company. He has two decades of experience across various functional areas and will provide us with invaluable insights. Mr. Alpesh Porwal succeeds the outgoing Mr. Mayur Gala, who ceases to be the Chief Financial Officer and KMP.

items.statement: Monthly revenue run rate: April INR 61.57 cr, May INR 93 cr, June INR 98 cr, July similar to June
items.quote: Just to add, on the April number was about INR61.57 crores, which moved to about INR93 crores in May and INR98 crores in June.

items.statement: Red Sea geopolitical issues raising freight costs 3-5x and container shortages impacting export own brand sales
items.quote: Persistent geopolitical issues around the Red Sea have raised freight costs and created a shortage of shipping containers, bottlenecking supply to the export markets thus affecting overseas own brand sales although demand remains intact.

items.statement: Re-entered INR 5 price point using existing moulds/machinery; no significant capex needed
items.quote: we received good initial marke t feedback on the relaunch of INR5 MRP products and we remain intact on focusing on this segment as we can leverage our past investments into moulds and machinery to grow this segment without any significant need of additional capex

items.statement: Zoox premium pen brand currently limited to A-class counters; will expand to B/C class in Q3-Q4
items.quote: So, Zoox purposely we haven't launched pan India. We have launched only in few selected outlets because being a little expensive premium plastic pens. So we were focusing on only A class counters. We haven't reached out to B and C class counters. So maybe going forward, we would be entering into those B and C categories as well.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 12-14% for FY25 maintained
items.quote: We are still, I would say, on track to do a $12%-14% kind of growth number. We did guide for, did not guide for 15%, we guided for 12-14%. We are still on track.

items.statement: Howrah Hospital occupancy tracking above 50% in Q2, confident of annual guidance
items.quote: At this point also in quarter 2 we are tracking a figure of more than 50%. So we are fairly confident that on an overall year-ending basis we will be tracking a guidance figure on this.

items.statement: Raipur hospital commissioning by February 2025 adding 155 beds; Ranchi hospital under construction for next 3 years
items.quote: We are coming up with our fifth hospital in Raipur. This should be commissioned by February of 2025. With this, we will be adding another 155 odd beds to our portfolio. We have also signed the lease agreement for a hospital in Rachi. That is under the construction phase and should be added in the next three years.

items.statement: ARPOB increase sustainable due to case mix change and price corrections in TPA and cash prices
items.quote: Yes, definitely the ARPOB is sustainable. These are ARPOB which have increased due to an effect of the case mix as well as increase in prices of both TPAs and our cash prices.

items.statement: Employee cost up due to annual salary increments; doctor fees up due to case mix shift and robot usage; medicine cost down due to case mix change
items.quote: Yes so the employee cost has gone up due to the annual increase in the salaries for the employees which happens every April. If you see in terms of the cost structure due to the change in case mix, the medicine cost or the cost of material consumed has come down, whereas other expenses have slightly gone up because the doctor expenses has gone up.

items.statement: Q1 seasonally weak and impacted by general elections in Eastern India; July revenue run rate INR37 crores; Q2 expected to be better
items.quote: We are right now on a monthly run rate of almost INR 36-37 crores in terms of revenues in Q2. So, we should be, Q2 would be slightly, would be better than the Q1, obviously.

items.statement: ALOS reduced intentionally in Salt Lake (2.78 days) and Dum Dum (4.74 days) to free beds for higher patient volumes; IP admissions increased or stable YoY
items.quote: We had committed to reducing the length of stay of our Dumdum and our Salt Lake hospitals, our mature hospitals, and we managed to do that. Our length of stay has come down to 2.78 in Salt Lake and almost 4.6 in Dumdum from 5.3.

items.statement: Agartala hospital may see temporary revenue impact from Bangladesh patient disruption (5-8% of Agartala revenue); oncology services starting soon to offset
items.quote: So that can we will have a temporary impact on the revenue because Agartala, the Bangladesh patients contribute to almost 5% to 8% of our revenues in Agartala. Having said that, like we've highlighted in the next couple of months, we expect to start the radiation oncology and the PET CT and the LINAC as well in Agartala.

items.statement: Target to become 1,000-bed hospital chain in 2-3 years; open to organic and inorganic expansion in Eastern India including Northeast, Bihar, UP, MP
items.quote: I am excited to share our ambitious goal of becoming a 1,000-bed hospital chain within the next 2-3 years. This target underscores our commitment to scaling our operations and reaching more communities in need for quality healthcare services.

items.statement: Raipur and Ranchi new hospitals expected ARPOB at 10-15% discount to Calcutta hospitals initially, converging to INR36,000-37,000 by year 3-4; break-even in 15-18 months
items.quote: So, obviously for the new hospitals in the initial phase the ARPOB might be at a 10% to 15% discount compared to our Calcutta hospitals. But as the hospital matures by the third or the fourth year, we hope the ARPOB levels to meet up to our Calcutta standards of around the 36,000-37,000 mark in today's terms.

items.statement: INR45 crores cash and investments available for inorganic acquisitions; targeting deal in next 12-15 months
items.quote: We have almost INR45 crores sitting on the balance sheet in terms of available cash and investments which is targeted towards getting such an opportunity and hopefully, we should be able to crack somewhere in the next 12 months, 12 to 15 months.

items.statement: Lease rental for Raipur and Ranchi hospitals INR3-4 crores per hospital per year with escalation every 3 years
items.quote: Yes, it's per hospital and it's an agreed-upon amount with an increase every three years.

items.statement: Not pursuing separate IVF or diagnostics verticals; diagnostics done in-house; IVF to be part of Raipur hospital services
items.quote: We are not looking at setting up IVF or diagnostics as a separate business vertical. It is a part of our existing business vertical itself. We are doing diagnostics in-house across all our hospitals at an OPD level and IPD level. And IVF is something which we are starting off in Raipur also as a part of our hospital service offerings.

items.statement: Fair value disclosure will be included in the Annual Report as statutorily required
items.quote: Yes, the fair value disclosure will be in our Annual Report, as it is statutorily required to be.

items.statement: Consistent interest seen for relicensing Morgan Stanley space at NKP
items.quote: The Company has seen consistent interest for relicensing the space currently occupied by Morgan Stanley.

items.statement: EBITDA margins approximately 77% for Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margins are approximately 77%.

items.statement: Morgan Stanley to vacate 13,000 sq ft in Q3 FY25 and 122,000 sq ft in Q4 FY25 at NKP
items.quote: Morgan Stanley has given notices at the end of July and in August 2024 to vacate approximately 13,000 square feet in Q3 FY 25, and approximately 122,000 square feet in Quarter 4 FY 25, at NKP, respectively.

items.statement: Current licensing rates just north of Rs. 160 per sq ft per month on 80% efficiency basis with roughly three months rent free
items.value: Rs. 160 per sq ft per month
items.quote: They are just north of approximately Rs. 160 per square foot per month on an 80% efficiency basis, with roughly three months of rent free.

items.statement: Carpet area equivalent rate is Rs. 200 plus CAM plus GST
items.quote: No, that's our chargeable area. The carpet area equivalent is Rs. 200.

items.statement: Current interest rate is 8.54% based on monthly T-bill
items.quote: Current rate is 8.54%.

items.statement: Tax rate applicable from FY25 is 34.94% vs 29.12% earlier due to turnover exceeding Rs. 400 crores in FY23
items.quote: the tax rate applicable from the current year, that is FY 2024-25 will be 34.94% as against 29.12% earlier under the old regime, as the Company's turnover has exceeded Rs. 400 crores in FY 2022-23

items.statement: Discussions and consultations on potential restructuring or value accretive measures continue with concerned parties
items.quote: With reference to the potential restructuring or other possible value accretive measures, discussions and consultations with concerned parties continues.

items.statement: Average occupancy rate stable at 99.8% for Q1 FY25 with NKP at 100% occupancy
items.quote: the average occupancy rate for the Company as a whole, that is Nirlon Knowledge Park and Nirlon House combined was stable at 99.8% for the 1st Quarter, and NKP remained 100% occupied.

items.statement: Nirlon House sale process ongoing with regulatory bodies due to strata ownership structure
items.quote: That is under discussion with various regulatory bodies etc., because of the profile of the ownership and the nature of the ownership, which is basically strata, as well as the ownership within Nirlon.

items.statement: Domestic tire volume expected to grow mid-single digits in FY25; replacement market healthy due to infrastructure investment
items.quote: The domestic tire volume is expected to have a moderate growth of around the mid -single digits in FY'25. The replacement market, which contributes significantly to the tire industry volumes is also anticipated to remain healthy.

items.statement: Selling prices maintained despite aggressive dumping from China; raw material costs expected to give relief in second half of quarter
items.quote: We maintained our pricing. We did not yield to the pressure on pricing. There were some small aberrations in the input cost.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 11% in Q1FY25 from 12.5% in Q4FY24 due to front-loaded employee costs and market conditions; expected to improve with capacity utilization ramp-up
items.quote: EBITDA margins for Q1FY'25 stood at 11% as compared to 12.5% in Q4 FY '24. There is one item called employee expenses, this have increased sequentially largely due to the annual revision in salary along with retiral provisions.

items.statement: Dahej capacity expansion at 10-15% completion; Board approved in March; adding 20% to existing capacity; product split not disclosed
items.quote: So we got the approval from the Board in March and I think if I want to put a percentage, probably 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Current utilization ~70% overall; peak utilization expected in 1-1.5 years; expansion targets products at 90-95% utilization
items.quote: About 70% utilization. Peak utilization is not putting a finger, Aditya, on a specific quarter or a month. But we're quite positive this will keep getting ramped up from quarter-to-quarter.

items.statement: Export volume mix 34% in Q1FY25 (up from 32%); revenue mix 34%; growth from Asia, Europe, and US despite container shortages and freight costs
items.quote: So the export is around 34%. I think if I recall, earlier it was 32%, it's about 34% now. And from a market development point, this growth is coming not only from Asia, but also from Europe also to a certain extent.

items.statement: Green energy (solar, wind, cogeneration) at 60-70% of Dahej power; expected to reach 75%+ at full utilization; turbine commissioned, savings from Q2
items.quote: So if you put both together, we should be in the range of 60% to 70% in Dahej, and this should go up with full utilization. As utilization ramps up, I would expect this to go to at least 75 and more.

items.statement: Value-added portfolio expansion underway; results in medium term; localized an imported accelerator product; more products in pipeline
items.quote: We are building up alternative plans to improve our value-added portfolio. We are working on our growth plans on that also. That's what is going on. The results will not be seen immediately, but in the medium term, you can see those results being getting reflected in the operational performance.

items.statement: Antidumping duty study ongoing; no concrete decision yet; will explore if valid case emerges
items.quote: Study is going on. At this moment, we are evaluating various options. And at an appropriate time if we feel there is a m erit -- there's a valid case in this as per the merits, we may explore that option

items.statement: Manufacturing cost comparable to China Sunsine; their pricing advantage from export subsidies; NOCIL has supply reliability and faster turnaround edge
items.quote: So what we have seen is we're quite comparable as far as our -- if you do a comparison with China Sunsine across the product category, it is largely the delta on the export subsidy that tends to kind of give them that additional pricing power.

items.statement: Sales volume index at 144 (base Q1FY20=100); 4% QoQ volume growth; 8% YoY volume growth
items.quote: On the sales volume front, the volumes for Q1FY '25 is at 144 taking a base of Q1FY '20 as 100.

items.statement: Employee cost front-loading: 65% in Q1, remaining 35% spread over Q2-Q4; actuarial valuation for retiral provisions drives pattern
items.quote: So if you see last year, and the last two years, if you see, 65% gets loaded in the first quarter, then you have 30% or 32% gets distributed over the next three quarters.

items.statement: Chinese domestic demand stable, not improving; European market slight improvement but not significant; geopolitical and container challenges persist
items.quote: Yes, so the Chinese market is kind of -- we don't see any significant improvement kind of like more or less stable is what we see. European market, there has been a slight improvement, but clearly not something significant that to, but there is a slight improvement.

items.statement: Green chemicals pipeline in testing/approval stages; related to rubber applications; lower energy-intensive products
items.quote: Yes. So there are quite a few greener, more lower energy -intensive products that we are continuously working on, there are quite a few in the pipeline, but they take their time and they are in different stages of testing and approvals.

items.statement: Management expects minor sales volume growth for FY25 despite Q1 strength
items.quote: Despite the strong performance in Q1, we are witnessing macro challenges accentuated by recessionary fears in USA, Geopolitical sanctions and inflationary raw material scenario coupled with high freight costs are there. This will result in a tepid demand environment for the remainder of the year. However, we believe we will be able to achieve a minor sales volume growth in this financial year.

items.statement: Demand slowing down in Q1; tepid environment expected for remainder of FY25
items.quote: Yes, we are seeing demand slowing down and that's why we are saying that despite this quarter, by the remainder of the year, we will only be able to get a minor growth.

items.statement: Board approved new capex of up to INR1,300 crores for 35,000 MTPA OTR capacity at Bhuj in phases
items.quote: Accordingly, we are embarking on a new capex spend of up to INR1,300 crores for 35,000 metric ton per annum at Bhuj. This will be executed in various phases.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance of INR600-700 crores; Q1 spend was INR200 crores
items.quote: Full year would be between INR600 crores to INR700 crores.

items.statement: Advanced carbon black project of 30,000 MTPA progressing on schedule for H1 FY25 commissioning
items.quote: We are working on advanced carbon black project with a capacity of 30,000 metric tons. This project is progressing well and is as per schedule.

items.statement: New mould manufacturing plant at Bhuj commenced operations for internal consumption
items.quote: Further, we have commenced the operations of our new mould manufacturing plant at Bhuj. Please note this plant will provide us mould for our internal consumption and help better our quality levels.

items.statement: Channel inventory increasing due to Q1 stocking; OEM demand softer
items.quote: It is increasing. Channel inventory is increasing, and OEMs demand is softer also.

items.statement: Targeting full-year EBITDA margin around 24.8% despite cost pressures
items.quote: Last year, full year, our EBITDA margin was around 24.8%, and we will be striving for the same range for the whole of the year.

items.statement: Raw material costs expected to increase 2-3%; freight costs to rise to 8-9% of revenue in Q2
items.quote: Commodity prices are also going up. So raw material, approximately 2% to 3%, will increase the raw material cost.

items.statement: No price hikes taken yet; weak demand limiting pass-through ability
items.quote: No, till now, we have not been able to take any price hike. Going forward, the market demand is a little weak. Hence, we are trying to see what we can do and what we can pass on. But so far, we have not taken anything.

items.statement: Q1 EUR/INR rate 92; Q2 hedge rate around 92.5
items.quote: So this quarter was INR92 euro and next hedging is around 92.5 we can say for next quarter.

items.statement: Forex gain of INR52 crores on sales; INR11 crores on expenses in Q1
items.quote: On sales it is INR52 crores, which is we have disclosed in our presentation. On other expenses, it is about INR11 crores.

items.statement: India market share in agri estimated at 6-7%; outlook remains positive
items.quote: Very difficult to give you an exact number, but between 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Expect to maintain market share despite demand slowdown
items.quote: No, we will be maintaining.

items.statement: Gross debt INR2,771 crores; cash INR2,946 crores; net cash ~INR175 crores as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: Our gross debt stood at INR2,771 crores at the end of 30th June '24. Our cash and cash equivalents were INR2,946 crores. Accordingly, we have a net cash of approximately INR175 crores.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR4 per equity share declared
items.quote: The Board of Directors has declared an interim dividend of INR4 per equity share.

items.statement: Natural rubber sourced from Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Africa, Vietnam based on best deal
items.quote: Yes. From all Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia as well as African countries, Vietnam. So wherever we get the best deal, we buy from there.

items.statement: Macro challenges: US recession fears, geopolitical sanctions, inflationary raw materials, high freight costs
items.quote: Despite the strong performance in Q1, we are witnessing macro challenges accentuated by recessionary fears in USA, Geopolitical sanctions and inflationary raw material scenario coupled with high freight costs are there.

items.statement: Joined Global Platform for Sustainable Natural Rubber (GPSNR) for EUDR compliance and sustainability reporting
items.quote: Further, in order to promote sustainable practices beyond our manufacturing units, BKT recently announced its membership to the Global Platform for Sustainable Natural Rubber or the GPSNR.

items.statement: Guided mid-double-digit volume growth for FY25 and revenue growth ~300 bps above volume growth
items.quote: Yes. Like we mentioned, mid-double-digit growth is what we are looking at. That is the guidance that we are providing.

items.statement: Expect to become net debt free during FY25, sooner than earlier March 2025 target
items.quote: We are on track. In fact, our earlier commentary suggests that we would have been net debt free by March 2025. But I do expect given the current trajectory, it would be even sooner than that.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin base of 14.5% in Q1 FY25, expected to expand further with volume growth and policy benefits
items.quote: Yes. You should consider the new base, if you ask me, is 14.5%. Right. Adjusted for the subsidy, you're looking at an EBITDA margin of 14.5%. That will be your base.

items.statement: Flandy contribution margins stronger than company weighted average, will drive margin expansion as it grows
items.quote: Given the fact that it is on the premium end of the portfolio of the spectrum, our contribution margins are actually better in Flandy as compared to the weighted average for the company as a whole.

items.statement: Q1 volume growth 0.9% YoY impacted by election disruptions; Southern IMFL industry de-grew 0.1% YoY
items.quote: While volume growth was 0.9% YoY, our EBITDA growth stood at 30.8% YoY. This significant growth in EBITDA has been on account of cost optimization initiatives and increasing share of premium products in the portfolio.

items.statement: Seeing good demand in Q2 post elections; confident of resuming industry-beating growth
items.quote: We are seeing good demand in Q2 and the guidance which we have given for the volume growth which will be in the double-digit volume growth that we are very confident we will be able to achieve.

items.statement: ENA costs reduced ~Rs 2/litre in Q1; glass and packing material costs softened; maintained gross margins QoQ despite NSR reduction
items.quote: Despite the highly volatile and inflationary trends in ENA, we have done a great job in our procurement efforts and have seen ENA costs come down by almost Rs. 2 per litre in Q1.

items.statement: Premium share increasing; 85%+ volumes from Prestige & Above segment; Flandy achieved 20% share of Flandy volumes in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
items.quote: 85% plus of our volumes are actually driven by P&A. From that perspective, it was kind of a similar range in terms of growth for both.

items.statement: Green Apple Flandy launch successful; luxury product launch planned in next couple of months; non-brandy premium pipeline for Pan-India expansion
items.quote: Very soon you should be seeing a luxury product coming out of our stables, over the next couple of months itself.

items.statement: Flandy attracting non-brandy drinkers and women; trials from flavoured spirits consumers; 10% of Mansion House volumes in first year
items.quote: We have approximately 10% of the sales coming of Mansion House Brandy, which is the mother brand, which in the first year of launch, is fairly respectable.

items.statement: Free cash flow from net debt free status to be deployed in strategic initiatives including new products and categories
items.quote: What that will effectively do is that, the company will be generating a significant amount of cash, almost the EBITDA will largely translate into a free cash flow, which then we can prudently deploy into various strategic initiatives.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced Rs 22.3 crore; net debt Rs 42.6 crore; prepaid Rs 20 crore Kotak term loan in Q1
items.quote: On the debt front, we reduced our gross debt by Rs. 22.3 crore and have now brought down our net debt to Rs. 42.6 crore. Furthermore, due to strong cash flows, we prepaid Rs. 20 crore of Kotak term loan in the quarter.

items.statement: Marketing spend cut in Q1 due to election disruption expectations; A&SP spend to increase to 2.5-3% of sales over 2-3 years
items.quote: Our range let's say of 2-3 year perspective would be more in the range of 2.5%-3% of sales.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh excise policy expected effective Oct 1; Telangana policy also awaited; both expected progressive based on CM's prior regime
items.quote: What we have understood from reports is that in Andhra Pradesh, they expect to announce the excise policy to be effective from October 1.

items.statement: Q1 FY25: Revenue growth 3% YoY, NSR Rs 1,252/case, EBITDA Rs 50 crore (highest ever Q1), PAT Rs 40.1 crore, PAT margin 12.7%
items.quote: During the first quarter, we have recorded a revenue growth of 3% YoY, predominantly on account of disruptions due to elections. The NSR per case came in at Rs. 1,252 per case during Q1 2025 relative to Rs. 1,249 in the corresponding period of last year.

items.statement: Rs 200 crore tax credit available at start of FY25; no tax payment expected in FY25; tax incidence from Q1 FY26
items.quote: We had around Rs. 200 crore of tax credit available as at the beginning of the year. We are hopeful that this year we will not need to pay any tax and our tax incidence will start from next year.

items.statement: Flandy competes with flavoured vodka category; priced alongside flavoured vodka; flavoured spirits industry growing overall
items.quote: Usually we are priced along with the flavoured vodka. When we look at our market share or tactical analysis which we do, we look at flavoured vodka category as well.

items.statement: Policy announcements in two key southern states pending; volume growth dependent on favourable excise policies
items.quote: Of course, we are waiting for certain policy decisions as I mentioned in two of the southern states. Once they come, that will also set the direction since they are both important markets for us.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 100 crore buyback of up to 50 lakh shares at Rs 200 per share, record date Aug 13, 2024
items.quote: The Board of Directors have approved a share buyback of Rs.100 crores. This buyback will involve repurchasing up to 50 lakh shares at a price of Rs.200 per share, representing approximately 2.2% of the total paid up equity capital of the company.

items.statement: Export stationery expected to grow double digits on previous year reported numbers
items.quote: No, no, double digit is very sure of, for us, to grow in this year.

items.statement: Domestic stationery internal guidance of 14-15% growth for full financial year
items.quote: So from our internal guidance point of view, we should be growing to around 14% to 15% in the whole financial year.

items.statement: Publication business maximum 5% growth for full year due to no curriculum change and product redesigning
items.quote: Yes, maximum because of no curriculum change and this redesigning of products, maximum we'll be able to see 5%.

items.statement: Stationery EBITDA margin improvement of at least 100 basis points; publishing margins to remain same
items.quote: So having restated earlier years number also, so if you combine both business earlier though, it was a separate activity, and we were merging. So, the number that used to come after merging, the margin will improve a little bit. But because the sales growth is limited, we believe that the inflationary cost pressures would be there. And therefore, the net margin, if you combine both businesses toge

items.statement: Publication volume grew ~2% but realization fell due to curriculum reduction and product redesign
items.quote: So again, in volume wise, we have grown by around hardly, it is a marginal growth of 2% in terms of volume, but realization -wise, it reduced.

items.statement: Domestic stationery volume grew ~4% but realization fell due to raw material price reduction passed to customers
items.quote: In reality, volume-wise, it has increased, but it is so dynamic that because of the raw material prices went down and to be with the market, we had to reduce our price of the products. So realization reduced. So in reality, volume -wise, we have grown by around 4% in first quarter.

items.statement: Paper prices corrected 12-13% from Sep 2023 to Jan 2024, forcing product price reductions
items.quote: So whatever inventory that was manufactured, there the price of paper corrected by almost 12% to 1 3%, and that we had to reduce the final product price to remain in line with the competition.

items.statement: Paper prices stable recently; attempted increase last month failed due to no takers
items.quote: No, no. They did try to increase last month, but there were no takers, so they had to again fall back to the same price.

items.statement: CBSE textbook market opportunity Rs 4,000 crore today, expected to grow to Rs 8,000-9,000 crore in 5-6 years
items.quote: So all put together opportunity for CBSE textbook business only, which is INRs.4,000-odd crores today is likely to grow to Rs.8,000 crores to Rs.9,000 crores in 5 to 6 years.

items.statement: Navneet reaches ~10,000 of 26,000-46,000 CBSE schools; fully penetrated in 38,000-40,000 private schools in Gujarat and Maharashtra
items.quote: Altogether out of 26,000 and 46,000 schools, which are using the CBSE publications, we would be reaching hardly to 10,000-odd.

items.statement: Publication revenue Rs 417 crore: Rs 384 crore supplementary, Rs 26 crore textbooks, Rs 7 crore non-curriculum
items.quote: So as far as out of Rs.417 crores, the non-curriculum is just Rs.7 crores, the balance is all curriculum. And within curriculum, supplementary book products is, to be precise, Rs.384 crores and the non-textbook business is Rs.26 crores.

items.statement: Curriculum change for grades 1-2 in Maharashtra and Gujarat expected next academic year, continuing for 4 years
items.quote: Curriculum, both in Maharashtra and Gujarat, part of the curriculum will start changing for a few of the periods and that will then continue for 4 years.

items.statement: Internal discussion ongoing on merging Indiannica subsidiary into parent; no clear timeline yet
items.quote: Yes, that discussion is on internally, but I do not have clear date or time line to mention that.

items.statement: Sales return provisions: Rs 30 crore publication, Rs 3 crore each for exports and domestic stationery in Q1
items.quote: So we have provided around Rs.30 crores in publication business and around Rs.3 crores each in exports and domestic business -- domestic stationary business.

items.statement: Last year Q1 publication sales return provision Rs 32 crore, actual returns Rs 37 crore received in Q2
items.quote: So provision for Q1 was around Rs.32 crores, and we got the return of around Rs.37 crores.

items.statement: Marketing team of 400+ people across India for school canvassing; segregated teams for SSC vs CBSE/ICSE schools
items.quote: So we have a huge fleet of people, more than 400 across India, including Maharashtra, Gujarat, they visit schools on a day-to-day basis and see to it that our books gets recommended.

items.statement: Navneet CBSE textbook business profitable at Rs 26 crore quarterly due to shared sales force; Indiannica still loss-making at Rs 50-65 crore sales
items.quote: At Navneet, with this Rs.26 crores, then yearly maybe Rs.40-odd crores, it will be profitable, reason beingmost of our present team only is selling these products, so the biggest expenditure in CBSE business has been the sales team, which goes all India. That is not there at Navneet.

items.statement: Curriculum change dependent on government action; risk of delay if new government cancels prepared changes
items.quote: Of course, I can't guarantee, but the preparation at the education department has started. Now suddenly, the new government comes and says, we don't want to replace even though curriculum is ready, then it's not in our hands.

items.statement: SFA edtech investment making losses but building strong foundation; confident of future returns despite possible revaluation
items.quote: we are not really worried for next 1 or 2 years for them to make losses, but they are making their foundation very, very strong. So be cause of the accounting policies and standards, we may had to revalue the assets for some of the other reasons. But I'm personally very, very hopeful -- confident of that business giving us really good returns in the future

items.statement: Export stationery revenue Rs 241 crore vs Rs 214 crore YoY; regained business lost to anti-dumping duties by moving production
items.quote: So as you might have seen, the Q1 '25 revenue is Rs.241 crores compared to Rs.214 crores corresponding period. This performance reflects our strategic efforts to broaden our product portfolio and extend our market reach.

items.statement: No major technology investment in blockchain, metaverse or 3D/4D animation; digital investment as per customer need only
items.quote: New -age, of course, we are adding more and more features in the product by using different, different newer technologies, but that's really not a big investment and particularly the blockchain or 3D or 4D animations, all that is really not required in this.

items.statement: CBSE textbook market dominated by 7-9 large publishers in North India; Navneet has blended print-digital advantage
items.quote: Finally, we have seen that around 7 to 8 publishers only have been doing quite big, good revenue because of the consistent content quality and, therefore, we'll have to fight with these 8, 9 publishers who are quite big enough.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of INR7,000-8,000 crores with 2.5% EBITDA margin; FY26 target INR13,000-14,000 crores; FY27 target INR18,000-20,000 crores
items.quote: So, if you look at FY25, we are looking at around INR7000 to INR8,000 crores of revenue, right, which will translate into like 1.3 million ton of steel business put together. And margin should be around 2.5%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 net profit grew 149% YoY to INR 10.5 crores, PAT margin up 280 bps to 5%

items.statement: Q1 FY25 working capital INR 716 crores vs INR 762 crores in FY24, working capital days 210

items.statement: Q1 FY25 inventory days 159, receivable days 95

items.statement: Company became debt-free net of fixed deposits at end of Q1 FY25

items.statement: No price hike expected for next 2 quarters due to competitive market and stable cotton prices
items.quote: The cotton prices are stable, and market is very competitive now and we don't look -- it doesn't look like for next 2 quarters we'll be having any price hike.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 segment volume growth: economy 16%, mid-premium 1%, premium 8%
items.quote: The economy segment grows at around 16%, mid -premium grows at 1% and the premium segment grows at 8%.

items.statement: Women's segment expected to contribute roughly 9% of total sales in coming quarters
items.quote: In coming quarters it should contribute to the total sales, say, roughly 9% of the total sales.

items.statement: Modern trade margins higher than general trade; X-factor areas 18% and modern trade 8% of revenue in Q1
items.quote: The margins are higher for modern trade compared to GT sales.

items.statement: Subcontracting expenses to rationalize to 20-23% from higher Q1 levels; cutting fully in-house, other processes 50% in-house
items.quote: Going forward it will be rationalized to 20% to 23%.

items.statement: EBO count at 29; 1 closed and 1 opened in Q1; planning 5-6 new EBOs next quarter
items.quote: in next quarter, we are planni ng to have 5 to 6 EBOs.

items.statement: Bangladesh situation may help garment exports from India as orders shift
items.quote: it might help us with our exports, garment exporting shoul d be helpful from India because a lot of orders should come to India.

items.statement: Four independent directors appointed effective September 6, 2024

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents plus arbitrage fund investments total ~INR 36 crores
items.quote: We have cash and cash equivalent, net of debts and all it's around INR11 crores and apart from that we have made an investment out in arbitrage fund of aroun d INR26 crores. So total if we combine cash and cash equivalent with investment is around INR36 crores.

items.statement: Rainwear launch limited to modern trade for testing; GT launch decision after Q2/Q3 based on seasonal response
items.quote: Rainwear is a very seasonal product. So we have not launched in GT. We have just to test market and trade. So this year we will see the response because there are chances of having a lot of dead stock because it all depends upon the seasonal and how the rains and all.

items.statement: Q1 growth below guided 18-20% due to election disturbance; inventory piled up from low sales vs projection
items.quote: first quarter we planned and probably that's why our inventory is a bit high as well and primarily what we feel is a lot of because of an election disturbance and all in quarter 1, that didn't -- couldn't happen to what we wanted.

items.statement: Long-term aspiration of 12-15% CAGR, with opportunity for 15-20% growth through modern trade, LFS, EBOs, exports
items.quote: to grow by 12% to 15% CAGR is basically a company like us will have to look at which we are planning to and aspire to. And we are putting up all the efforts in terms of it is modern trade, LFS, EBOs, export we are building up a strong team. So in terms of opportunity there is enough opportunity to grow by 15%, 20%.

items.statement: Margin improvement to 10-11% driven by operating leverage, thermal/outerwear performance, and ad spend rationalization of 2-3%
items.quote: Operating level also and with the thermals and outerwear things are doing bett er and all. Those things should also do better. Sumit Khowala: Rationalized to 6% to 7%. Vikash Agarwal: Yes. So that's another 2%, 3% is there

items.statement: Consolidated net revenue guided between Rs. 70-80 crores for FY25
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we expect the net revenue to be between Rs. 70 to 80 crores for FY25 with NFL and Superscan contributing the best.

items.statement: iServeU net revenue guided between Rs. 35-45 crores for FY25
items.quote: Given our performance of this quarter, we expect ISU to close net revenue between Rs. 35 to 45 crores by end of '25.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA guided between Rs. 20-30 crores for FY25, revised down from Rs. 45-50 crores
items.quote: We think we will probably do between Rs. 20 to 30 crores of EBITDA this year instead of the Rs. 45 to 50 crores that we had guided earlier.

items.statement: Lending book target of Rs. 418 crores for FY25
items.quote: I think our target for this year is Rs. 418 to be exact. That's what we are trying to achieve for this financial year in terms of the loan book.

items.statement: Lending book leverage target of 1 to 1.5X on consolidated network basis by FY25 end
items.quote: We expect our lending book to be levered 1 to 1.5X on a consolidated network basis by FY25 end.

items.statement: Distribution income expected to double to Rs. 8-10 crores in FY25 from Rs. 4 crores last year
items.quote: Typically, we make between 2% to 3% on that. So, I think we are thinking that on the distribution side, on a gross income basis, anywhere between Rs. 8 to 10 crores of income will come in this financial year.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs. 6.6 crores in Q1 FY25 vs positive EBITDA in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA loss for the quarter is Rs.6.6 crores. The loss expanded on account of two factors.

items.statement: Net yields on lending book improved to 18% and expected to be sustainable
items.quote: I am also happy to report that our net yields on our lending book have improved to 18%. We expect this yield to be sustainable going forward.

items.statement: Sound Box contract fulfillment commenced with 35,000+ devices delivered in June-July, run rate of 50,000-60,000 per quarter
items.quote: On the iServeU front, I am pleased to report that we have commenced the fulfillment of the Sound Box contract and have delivered more than 35,000 devices across June and July. We expect to have a delivery run rate of about 50,000 to 60,000 sound boxes per quarter.

items.statement: AUM including FLDG exposure at Rs. 208.5 crores, up 78% YoY

items.statement: Monthly loan origination throughput of almost Rs. 170 crores with 160 financial partners
items.quote: Additionally, we have 160 financial partners this quarter and have raised a monthly origination throughput of almost 170 crores.

However, we have witnessed normalization in June and growth in July thereafter.

items.statement: Added new distribution partner Ninjacart, expected to scale up in Q2
items.quote: This quarter we added a new partner Ninjacart and we expect this partnership to start scaling up in Q2.

items.statement: Secured contracts with top insurance companies for Superscan, advanced talks with large BFSI players
items.quote: We have also secured contracts with some of the top insurance companies. As we start to implement these contracts, this will lead to significant incremental revenues. We are now focused on expanding both our product stack and client base to ensure the comm ercial success of Superscan

items.statement: iServeU reorganized into four verticals: Financial Inclusion, Merchant Acquiring, SaaS, Program Management; expect 45% of ISU net revenue from SaaS and Program Management by FY25
items.quote: Consequently, we expect 45% of the net revenue of ISU by FY25 will come from the SaaS and the Program Management verticals.

items.statement: Superscan OCR toolkit implemented internally with 100% of internal case volumes routed through it
items.quote: We have implemented Superscan in our own proposition leading to 100% of internal cases volumes now being routed through Superscan.

items.statement: No significant incremental CAPEX expected; basic build complete, focus on monetization

items.statement: Total debt drawn in NFL standalone at Rs. 52.5 crores at end of Q1 FY25
items.quote: We have drawn a total debt of Rs.52.5 crores in NFL on a standalone basis at the end of Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Warrant subscription of balance 80% expected by February 2025; evaluating bolt-on acquisitions of Rs. 50-150 crores that may require incremental equity
items.quote: Firstly, there is a certain equity infusion that is expected this year, right? We have got the warrants issued last August. Only about 20% of those warrants have been subscribed as per the law of the country, right? So, the balance 80% is expected to come in before February of '25, which means this financial year.

items.statement: Targeting bolt-on tech acquisitions (51-100% stake) with profitability or near-profitability, not book value businesses
items.quote: We are not looking at book value businesses right now. I can tell you what we are having right now in terms of conversation, but it's a moving target. Right now, we are not talking to anyone where there's a book value jump. So, I am not looking to acquire a lending business where we are just acquiring a book.

items.statement: ECL provisions of Rs. 2 crores in Q1 FY25, total provisions at Rs. 10 crores; incremental provisioning for one old supply chain financing account
items.quote: The ECL provisions on loans in Q1 FY25 was Rs.2 crores, taking the total p rovision to Rs.10

items.statement: Loss rates on new loans over last 18 months under 1%; recovering ~Rs. 1 crore/quarter on old stressed account
items.quote: If I look at all the new loans that have been done over the last 18 months, I think our loss amounts are sitting at less than 1% on the entire loan book that has been generated over the last 18 months. But there are some older positions that we are just trying to chop away with. And so that's what it's really. So, again it's not symptomatic of a problem, it is an old problem that we need to figure

items.statement: Consolidated cash and cash equivalents at Rs. 104.5 crores as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: Our consolidated cash and cash equivalents stood at Rs. 104.5 crores as on 30th June 2024.

items.quote: Our finance professional network increased by 15% YoY and stood at 6,044 as of 30th June 2024. We further processed 51,816 loans through our network in Q1 of FY25 and reported an increase of 307% YoY and 8%.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA loss driven by election impact on financial inclusion and lending provisions; issues deemed transitory with Q2 expected to return to profitability path
items.quote: The current quarter has presented some challenges which are transitory in nature. The underlying fundamentals of our businesses remain strong. We are committed to overcoming these short-term challenges and resume our trajectory of profitable growth.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin expected at 19-20% for existing business excluding Vizag acquisition
items.quote: Between 19% and 20% is what we expect.

items.statement: Established centers revenue growth expected at 13-15% for full year
items.quote: I think the growth trajectory will continue as it is which was established around 13% to 15%.
