items.quote: And that should result into 14%-15% growth which we just mentioned in.

items.statement: ETR expected to be 30-32% for rest of FY25
items.quote: We expect ETR from here onwards to be in the range of 30% to 32% for the rest of the year.

items.statement: CAPEX expected at Rs. 80 crore per quarter for FY25
items.quote: For the current quarter, we did a CAPEX of about Rs. 80 crores. And for this particular year, we will maintain a similar range in the current year for the rest of the quarters also.

items.quote: CAPEX for the quarter was Rs. 80 crores and we expect the CA PEX to be in the same range including investments in the new facilities like Whitefield, North Bangalore during the year

items.statement: Vizag acquisition to increase debt by Rs. 200 crore initially and Rs. 150 crore after 18 months

items.quote: Our Adj. EBITDA for Q1 FY25 was Rs. 93 crores compared to Rs. 77 crores in Q1 of FY24, marking a 21% growth.

items.quote: Our revenue for Q1 FY25 is all time high at Rs. 526 crore, reflecting a growth of 17% adjusted for discontinued centers at MSR in Bangalore.

items.quote: We achieved a 17% year-on-year growth in chemotherapy sessions, a critical metric for our medical oncology offerings.

items.quote: We have already moved our OPD services to that hospital towards the end of 1st Quarter. We have moved out daycare services. Very soon, we will be moving our inpatient services.

items.statement: ARPOB increased 12% YoY to Rs. 44,340 driven by lower ALOS and better realization
items.quote: Some of the other highlights during the quarter include an ARPOB of 44,340, reflecting a 12% increase year-on-year.

items.statement: Government removed clinical investigation requirement for new drugs approved in US, UK, Japan, Australia, Canada

items.quote: In the 1st Quarter of rollout, we have been able to extend cancer care through our app to almost 8,000 unique patient IDs. We have been able to service 28,000 plus orders on e-pharmacy platform.

items.statement: Established centers grew 14% YoY; emerging centers grew 33% YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Regarding the performance of our established and emerging centers, they continue to deliver market-beating growth with established centres growing by 14% and emerging centres by 33% year-on-year for the quarter.

items.statement: PAT grew 59% YoY to Rs. 12 crore in Q1 FY25

items.statement: No immediate inorganic opportunities mature; evaluating strategically

items.quote: In India in Q1 FY25 , as per the SIAM data, the 2W industry sales grew by 19.8% compared to Q1 of the previous financial year. Scooters grew by 27.9% and Motorcycles grew by 16.5%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 14.3% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA margin was at 14.3%.

items.quote: Standalone EBITDA grew by 19.7% from Rs. 2,409 million in Q1 FY24 to Rs. 2,884 million in Q1 FY25, with EBITDA margin of 13.5%.

items.statement: European EBITDA margin was 16.6% in Q1 FY25

items.statement: Rs 17,705 million of RFQs from OEMs in India
items.quote: I would like to mention that we have Rs. 17,705 million worth of requests for quotes from OEMs.

items.quote: Since FY21 in India, Rs. 36,774 million of business has been won, out of which Rs. 28,364 million is new business and replacement business is Rs. 8,410 million. items.statement: Total EV business wins Rs 8,421 million till date; Maxwell subsidiary Rs 4,242 million

items.statement: Europe won €3.1 million orders in FY25 YTD including first VW hybrid plastic component
items.quote: In FY25 till date, our Europe business has won orders of €3.1 million, including the first V olkswagen business win for a specialty plastic component for a hybrid vehicle.

items.quote: In the last nine quarters, out of €118 million order s won, €61 million orders are for the battery EV business and €37 million is for the hybrid business.

items.statement: Europe investing €50 million per year
items.quote: We are doing €50 million investments per year.

items.statement: 2W disc brake assembly capacity 6.2 million per annum; brake discs 8.1 million; 3W brake assemblies 1 million
items.quote: With this new plant, our 2W disc brake assembly volumes have increased to 6.2 million numbers per annum and brake discs to 8.1 million numbers per annum . Also, for three wheeler brake assemblies, we have increased to 1 million numbers per annum.

items.statement: ABS assembly capacity scaled to 640,000 per annum; target 1.2 million by 2026
items.quote: We are further planning to increase these volumes to 1.2 million single and dual channe l ABS assemblies by 2026.

items.statement: Aluminum alloy wheel capacity expanding to 5.5 million per annum run rate from Q1 FY25
items.quote: we are now at our plants at Chakan expanding to supply at a run rate of 5.5 million wheels per annum from this quarter onwards.

items.statement: Target 4W share of consolidated business from 25% to 45% by FY30
items.quote: To increase our 4W share of consolidated business from 25% to 45% by FY30.

items.statement: Europe Q1 FY25 turnover €80.3 million, up 16.8% YoY; EBITDA €13.3 million, up 20.2%; net profit €4.9 million, up 15.7%

items.statement: Expect margin improvement as supply normalizes, more visible in Q3 FY25

items.statement: US demand improving for holiday season orders; EU demand growing for Ready-to-Cook

items.statement: EBITDA margin 6% in Q1 FY25, improved YoY and QoQ; freight costs up 60-70% pressuring margins

items.quote: Coming to the shrimp volumes sold by our company, it stood at 2,571 metric tons in Q1 of FY '25 as against 2,302 metric tons in Q4 FY '24 and 3,447 metric tons in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Discontinued operations PAT Rs 4.2 cr in Q1 FY25; expected to decline further.

items.statement: Expect 13% to 15% EBITDA margin in near future

items.quote: The prices are already bottom ed out and we are getting regular order at certain prices of ibuprofen. So, we do not fear any more reduction of prices in Ibuprofen

items.statement: Ibuprofen capacity utilization at 80% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Capacity utilization of ibuprofen presently around 80% and for non-ibuprofen it has started increasing which was earlier ranging from 40% to 70%.

items.statement: Expect non-ibuprofen capacity utilization to reach optimum level within 2 years
items.quote: We are expecting a ramp up of our capacity utilization at an optimum level within next 2 years.

items.statement: No immediate capacity expansion planned in chemical segment

items.statement: Added paracetamol and acetic anhydride manufacturing in last 2 years
items.quote: Also we have added projects manufacturing of paracetamol and acetic anhydride in the last 2 years.

items.statement: Set up new large capacity ETP plant at same location
items.quote: We have ETP plant which is around 10 years old, but we have set up another ETP plant in the location itself with a large capacity.

items.statement: Paracetamol prices fell over 40%, Metformin 15-20% in last year

items.statement: Ibuprofen prices stable at $9-10 vs $12 four years ago
items.quote: Earlier around 4 years back the prices of ibuprofen was ranging around $12, now we are getting the average realization of $9 to $10.

items.statement: Power, fuel and freight costs decreased, lowering other expenses
items.quote: Actually, in last year, our power and fuel expenses are on high side due to coal prices which are now stable and decreased somehow and freight part is also on decreasing side.

items.statement: Agrochemical segment benefited from normal monsoon with good volume growth
items.quote: Normal monsoon and onset of timely rains has benefited Agrochemical Segment with good volume growth.

items.statement: Specialty chemical faces volume and pricing pressure from high channel inventory and China dumping
items.quote: In regard to Speciality Chemical, high channel inventory and destocking has led to continued volume and pricing pressure on the industry. In addition to this continuous dumping by China and lower prices a re hurting profitability

items.statement: Export queries and trial orders increasing from regulated markets
items.quote: has also increased. Various technical people of respective clients of competitors who have had quality issuesare coming for audit purpose and we are getting some trial orders or samples

items.statement: Export contribution started increasing with CEP approvals

items.statement: SI Group reportedly exiting ibuprofen with 4,500-5,000 tonne capacity
items.quote: We have heard from the newspapers that they are exiting, but as per our internal sources, their capacity is around 4500 to 5000 tonnes.

items.statement: Largest ibuprofen player for over a decade, backward integrated advantage
items.quote: We are the largest player of ibuprofen since last more than a decade and we are concentrating only on our clients, our regulatory approvals, our qualities and other after sales services.

items.statement: Export share stable at 30% of revenue in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In this quarter we have 30% export and 70% domestic turnover, which is similar to the last years export and domestic sales.

items.statement: Inventory increased due to new products (paracetamol, acetic anhydride) and bulk alcohol order
items.quote: As we have added new products in the market . So, the inventory has been increased accordingly for the new product s like P aracetamol and acetic anhydride. That may be the reason to increase level of inventories in our finished product and for raw material we have got a good order from one vendor on

items.statement: Net cash of Rs 190 crore as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: That is around Rs. 190 crore in the bank.

items.statement: No buyback planned; cash reserved for organic growth and opportunities
items.quote: Our priority as of now is to enhance the business, increase the capacities of the various products and the cash is there for grabbing any good opportunity in the market.

items.statement: May consider acquisitions if good opportunity arises at proper valuation
items.quote: If any good opportunity, which is benefic ial for the company ’s shareholder or any business comes in the market with a proper valuation, we may consider that , but as of now, our first priority is to go organically

items.statement: No decision on bonus, split or buyback; board to discuss
items.quote: So, bonus and the split, we can discuss this in the board, and board will take decision on it, but as of now, there has not been any decision.

items.statement: R&D team continuously working on new non-ibuprofen products
items.quote: We are having various products in the pipeline and our R&D team is continuously working on those such products.

items.statement: Peak revenue potential at current rates estimated at Rs 2,400-2,500 crore
items.quote: At the current rate, it may be around Rs. 2400 to 2500 crore.

items.statement: Freight rates surge and logistics cost pain expected ahead
items.quote: Freight rates surge continues, imports/exports, logistics cost pain is expected going ahead.

items.statement: Formed 50-50 JV with UPL named Augene Chemical Private Limited for downstream amine derivatives

items.quote: Both the companies are expected to invest about Rs. 150 crore each into this JV over the next two years. The commercial supplies are expected to begin by Q1 FY27, targeting peak annual revenue potential of Rs. 400-500 crore within the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Suyog Kotecha joined as Executive Director and CEO on June 17, 2024
items.quote: I am delighted to have Mr. Suyog Kotecha joining in as Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of Aarti Industries Ltd. Suyog joined our team on June 17th, 2024 bringing with him extensive expertise in strategy, innovation, and business transformation.

items.statement: Target 20-30% YoY volume growth for FY25; EBITDA guidance withdrawn due to margin volatility
items.quote: I think on demand front, we are pretty confident of delivering growth in the range of 20% to 30% and this is coming with a combination of commissioning of some of the new projects as well as better capacity utilization in some of the existing product chains.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg down vs pre-COVID levels; margin recovery expected to be long-haul due to Chinese competition
items.quote: On a broader level, yes, EBITDA at a rupees per Kg level for many of the products is not equivalent to where it was three, four years back and that's also reflected in our EBITDA margin percentages.

items.statement: FY25 capex Rs. 1,500-1,800 crore; Rs. 270 crore spent in Q1; bulk of remaining spend on Zone-IV Chlorotoluene project
items.quote: From an overall capital expenditure point of view, we had projected Rs.1,500 crore to Rs. 1,800 crore in the financial year and in Q1 we have already spent Rs. 270 crore.

items.statement: Nitrotoluene capacity expanding from 30,000 to 45,000 tons; Ethylation capacity 3x from 8,000-10,000 to ~25,000 tons; commissioning end of Q2 FY25
items.quote: Currently, the capacity is around 30,000 tons and we are looking to ramp it up to around 45,000 tons. And for Ethylation, we have a capacity of around 8,000 tons to 10,000 tons and it is expected to go by around 3x maybe around 25,000 tons roughly around that magnitude.

items.statement: Positive demand momentum in pharma, polymers, additives, dyes, pigments; green shoots in agrochemicals
items.quote: We have been witnessing positive demand momentum in key end use applications like pharma, polymers, additives, dyes and pigments. Even in agrochemicals, there are small green shoots of demand recovery.

items.statement: Chinese pricing pressure across portfolio, most acute in agrochemicals; 70-80% of product basket faces Chinese competition
items.quote: I think the pressure on pricing from Chinese capacity is across the board. It is much more aggravated in the Agchem chain from an application standpoint. But the pressure is there even in other segments.

items.statement: Energy application now significant share (~60% exports in Q1); fuel additive demand linked to gasoline/naphtha cracks
items.quote: Energy as an application has become a relatively large application for us, which is bringing additional volatility to the business performance as it is linked to external factors like crude, gasoline cracks, naphtha cracks which have their own element of volatility.

items.statement: Other expenses fell QoQ due to absence of annual employee benefit costs and lower freight from Middle East/Asia mix shift
items.quote: Some of the annual costs which were there in Q4 related to employee benefits and other stuff would not be there in Q1. So, that is some component and in some pockets the freight has been lower.

items.statement: Current debt ~Rs. 3,300 crore; expected to rise to Rs. 3,500-3,800 crore in FY25 due to capex and working capital
items.quote: So, as regards this year, I expect it to be anywhere between Rs. 3,500 to 3,800 crore. It depends on how the raw material prices and the working capital play, around that.

items.statement: Prioritizing Tier-1 customers as demand recovers; still tactically using Tier-2/3 in some chains including China
items.quote: Yes, broadly speaking, as we see demand recovery on many of the end use markets, we prioritize our sort of Tier-1 customers in those chains. There are some chains where tactically we may still have to go back to Tier-2, Tier-3 customers, sometimes including that in China.

items.statement: No new Chinese capacity seen recently in Ethylation/Chlorotoluene; but broader value chain substitution risk exists
items.quote: No, not at this stage. We haven't seen any new capacity coming in China in the recent times. But what we need to understand is ultimately it's a value chain, right?

items.statement: No direct exposure to Bangladesh (<1% of portfolio); monitoring indirect impact on dyes/textile customers
items.quote: We don't have direct exposure to Bangladesh or any significant exposure to Bangladesh. So, right now we are not seeing any risk from the particular events happening in Bangladesh. And I think the exposure is less than 1% of total business portfolio.

items.statement: Margin volatility from energy application seasonality and Chinese dumping; EBITDA guidance withdrawn until better visibility
items.quote: I think the pressure from China is actually not sort of going away and we have seen that across broader product portfolio, not in a specific chain, but across broader product portfolio, the pressure on margin is still very intense.

items.statement: Target 20-25% EBITDA CAGR over 5 years (~2.5-3x EBITDA); three themes: project execution, R&D in sunrise sectors, culture retention
items.quote: Our goal as stated earlier is to deliver 20% to 25% CAGR growth in EBITDA, which if we take a five-year view, then it is almost 2.5x-3x growth in EBITDA.

items.statement: Nitrotoluene + Ethylation expansion capex ~Rs. 400-500 crore; Zone-IV Chlorotoluene project bulk of remaining FY25 spend
items.quote: It would be in the magnitude of around Rs. 400 crore to 500 crore.

items.statement: Target 50% utilization of new Nitrotoluene/Ethylation capacity in FY25; 60-80% in FY26
items.quote: We are expecting somewhere in the range of targeting up to 50% capacity utilization within this financial year and then taking it all the way up to 60% to 80% capacity utilization level in the next financial year.

items.statement: Benzene and aniline prices rose QoQ/YoY in Q1; some softening seen in current quarter
items.quote: On benzene, we have seen sort of a sequential increase in prices going up to Q1 FY25 level. But in the current quarter, we have started to see some softening in the benzene prices. I think aniline has remained quite volatile.

items.statement: Export share rose to ~60% in Q1 FY25 from ~52% due to energy application mix
items.quote: I think energy application which has now become significant part, their larger share comes from export and that's why you will see compared to last year average where I think our overall share of export was, I think roughly 52%-odd has gone up to 60% now in the Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Long-term contracts (SABIC, other) on track; SABIC plant running at full capacity; revenue/volume trajectory as expected
items.quote: I think both these contracts continue to do very well. In fact, the contract with SABIC has ramped up quite significantly. I think indication of demand from their side, start of this calendar year versus now there has been significant improvement.

items.statement: Zone-IV Chlorotoluene value chain to add 40 downstream specialty products; commissioning phased from FY26
items.quote: We have a portfolio of 40 different products as part of that investment and we will go significantly downstream into specialty derivatives, right? We will not stop at sort of the first two levels of derivatives.

items.statement: PDA production ~206 tons/month in Q1 FY25 vs 135 tons/month YoY
items.quote: The PDA number is roughly around 206 tons per month for the current quarter against last year same quarter this number was 135 tons per month.

items.statement: Pass-through pricing works on benzene downstream; aniline downstream partly exposed to market pricing causing volatility
items.quote: On benzene downstream we have decent amount of portfolio where we have a pass-through pricing mechanism, and we are able to retain that. On Aniline downstream product portfolio, I think some part of it is linked to raw material, some part of it is not directly linked to raw material where we take market exposure.

items.statement: FY25 capex peaks; FY26 capex expected significantly lower
items.quote: No, I think it's only for this FY'25. In fact, I think from a annual CAPEX point of view, we will peak in this financial year. I thin k our CAPEX for the next financial year is expected to be significantly lower compared to current levels

items.statement: Non-MMA volume growth ~5-6% QoQ; YoY growth skewed by energy application scale-up
items.quote: So, if you are talking about QoQ volume growth, then actually the volume growth is quite consistent even in non-MMA portfolio; it still remains in the range of 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Fuel additive demand optimistic long-term despite EV trend; product more sustainable than metal-based alternatives
items.quote: We think from an absolute volume point of view still ICE engine rate capacity remains in the market. This fuel additive is actually much more sustainable compared to other options available today in the market, right.

items.statement: Expects ~12,000 metric tons recycling volume linked to Rs 30-35 crore profit for FY25
items.quote: as I envisaged, about 12,000 metric tons, which I will link with the profitability of about Rs. 30 crores plus, or even Rs. 35 crores is what we envisage out of 12,000 metric tons.

items.quote: we have invested by 30th June entirely Rs. 50 crores in the plant and machinery and the land building.

items.statement: Total capacity expanded to 25,200 metric tons per annum across two facilities in Vasai East
items.quote: Ecoreco has already expanded its capacity to 25,200 metric tons per annum.

items.quote: it was a very nominal utilization during the June quarter because on 5th June only we formally inaugurated it.

items.quote: EBITDA margin improving by 298 basis points to 76.12%. The consolidated PAT for the quarter rose by 73.04% to Rs. 8.15 crores, reflecting a PAT margin enhancement of 125 basis points to 60.64%.

items.quote: we insist our suppliers, particularly the producers, that if they are following certain practices in the world, in the developed countries, they should follow over here too, like giving the material at a nominal price, bearing other expenses, and all other things put together, we always focus on reducing the cost of acquisition of the waste.

items.quote: CPCB is particularly with the Ministry of Environment, is working on the mechanism of giving us a higher EPR fees, suggesting or mandating v ery shortly that higher EPR fees should be charged by the formal sector so that they can bridge the gap of price difference between formal and informal

items.quote: I am very, very positive about the kind of strictness the CPCB is now demonstrating and using that, rather asking producers to work on the lines of the rules. It's much higher than all the lines strictly, I am very positive.

items.statement: 100% procurement directly from end-users and producers (MNCs, Class A); no imports or market purchases
items.quote: We don't import anything, ne. We don't procure from the market, two. But we directly take it from our end user, which are inclusive of the multinational Company's user admin and the producer board.

items.quote: revenue from operations, it includes both, or rather 3, recycled material, refurbished, EPR fees, and of course, the data restriction service charges. So, it's a combination of all four.

items.quote: we are accumulating cash and we will assess the requirement of further investment in plant machineries and the capacity, which will be sometime in September 25, we will evaluate based on the performance of March '25 and half of the year of the next year.

items.quote: Now we have about 50. And with the capacity as utilization increases, more number will be added according to the requirement.

items.quote: Obviously, we have learned from that mistake of our shortfall, whatever we noted and have been correctly implemented in the old one also and in the new one also.

items.quote: the generation level of e-waste is very, very high in India. It's close to about 4 to 5 million metric tons.

items.statement: Differentiates via full compliance focus vs formality; premium services command higher fees from MNCs
items.quote: we do take care that we provide, we take care of the compliances of the clients in its totality, as against considering them as a formality under the rules. This is the difference what we always follow.

items.quote: whatever the purchases we have made is not necessarily that everything gets consumed within the same quarter itself. It might be old inventories, because it all relates to what you accumulate and what kind of batch you make out of that to generate which kind of metals.

items.statement: TERRA partnership (120 global members) expanding client access and business gradually
items.quote: the addition with the TERRA and TERRA's other members is expanding our wings and is adding to gradually the business.

items.statement: No current plans to monetize proprietary technology; focus remains on core recycling operations
items.quote: one more addition of Ecoreco and deviating from the core action of recycling is not right now on the consideration.

items.quote: those expenses are purely incurred by another Company of mine personally, but not from the Eco Recycling Limited because it's not profitable for Eco Recycling to do that.

items.quote: The stand -alone AUM stands at INR31,035 crores, gr owing by 20.6% year-on-year. With a consolidated AUM of INR44,932 crores, it is an increase of 21% over the same quarter last year.

items.quote: Up to INR1 lakh, 42%; INR1 lakh to INR2 lakh, 23%; above INR2 lakh, 35%.

items.statement: Competitor ban impact not significant, business distributed among many players including banks

items.statement: Import duty on gold cut from 15% to 6% in Union Budget, may moderate domestic gold prices

items.statement: Raised US$300 million from dollar bonds in May 2024 for business growth

items.quote: With regard to liquidity, cash and cas h equivalents was at INR5,383 crores on a consolidated basis and undrawn bank line was INR3,530 crores as on 30th September.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR1 per share declared for Q1
items.quote: Considering the consistent earnings, Board has declared an interim dividend of INR1 for this quarter.

items.quote: There are some challenges in collections because of farmer agitation in Punjab, general election, etc. And connected with that, there were some rumors spread about non-waivers. items.quote: New product development accounted for 32% of the total sales in this last quarter.

items.quote: The overall weighted average gas cost in Q1 was at INR 31.64 as against INR 33.91 in Q1 FY24 which is significantly lower as compared to the industry standards.

items.statement: Dividend trend of healthy payouts to continue; FY24 dividend INR 60 per share amounting to INR 78 crore

items.statement: B2C sales 64% of revenue, B2B projects 36%; project mix slightly up from 35%
items.quote: As of now, the total project to retail ratio, 64:36. It was earlier something like 65:35.

items.statement: Tier 3 cities lead with 43% of sales, Tier 1 35%, Tier 2 22% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Regarding sales distribution, Tier 1 cities accounted for 35% of total sales, Tier 2 cities for 22%, and Tier 3 cities led with 43% of total sales.

items.statement: Organized sector estimated at INR 5,000 crore sanitaryware and INR 8,000 crore faucetware; unorganized at INR 4,000 crore and INR 6,000 crore respectively

items.quote: Also because of the fact that the pollution board has started becoming more and more strict in respect of the kind of emissions and effluents which are being discharged.

items.statement: Retailer loyalty program enrolled over 20,000 retailers with 3 lakh+ invoices; 37% of INR 217 crore retail sales eligible for rewards
items.quote: Since launching the Retailer Loyalty Program in FY 2022-2023, we have enrolled over 20,000 retailers and accumulated more than 3 lakh invoices on the application.

items.statement: Advertising spend INR 11.5 crore in Q1 FY25 vs INR 11 crore in Q1 FY24, in line with FY25 projection
items.quote: In Q1 FY25, we have spent INR 11.5 crore as compared with INR 11 crore in Q1 of FY24 towards publicity, which is in line with our projected spending for FY25.

items.statement: Demand softness expected to continue in Q2 FY25; recovery anticipated from Q3 FY25
items.quote: We anticipate that the improvement in the demand condition will start from the second half of the year.

items.statement: Consolidated double-digit revenue growth expected for FY25; organic single-digit growth
items.quote: With our growth levers in pace and despite a muted Q1, we anticipate improved consumer sentiments in second half of the year. This will drive positive growth for FY '25 with an overall consolidated growth expected to be in double digits.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 estimated flattish; Q3 and Q4 expected to show growth
items.period: Q2 FY25, Q3 FY25, Q4 FY25
items.quote: On the organic level, we'll be growing, okay, since quarter 1 was muted. Quarter 2, we estimate it would be flattish. In quarter 3 and quarter 4, we are expecting there will be a growth perspective.

items.statement: Operating profit margin sustainable at 18-19% for FY25
items.quote: Operating profit looks sustainable at 18% to 19%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin range 14-15%
items.quote: We work on a 15%, 14% to 15% EBITDA.

items.statement: Acquired 50% stake in Kraus Casuals; now a subsidiary

Pursuant to this acquisition, Kraus h as become a subsidiary of our

items.statement: Net addition of 17 EBOs in Q1 FY25; total 505 EBOs including 350+ Killer EBOs
items.quote: As of 30 June 2024, there has been a net addition of 17 EBOs in quarter 1 of FY '25, bringing the total to 505 EBOs, including over 350-plus Killer EBOs.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 muted due to consumer sentiment slowdown, heatwave, fewer weddings
items.quote: Financial year '25 started on a muted note with sales of INR151 crores and an EBITDA of around INR28 crores. The performance was primarily impacted due to the continued slowdown in the consumer sentiments. The same got aggravated due to prolonged heatwave conditions, particularly in the North India, leading to a lower footfall during the period. The lower number of weddings also impacted the perfo

items.statement: Expect consumer sentiment improvement from current month; Q3 and Q4 better
items.quote: I expect that, okay, the consumer sentiment will improve from this month itself, okay? But we are looking forward that, okay, quarter 3 and quarter 4 would be better.

items.statement: Spring/Summer '25 trade show response encouraging across Killer, Easies, Kraus, Junior Killer
items.quote: With an encouraging response to our July '24 trade show for Spring/Summer '25 collection, including Killer, Easies, Kraus and Junior Killer, we are confident in achieving the robust growth in the coming months.

items.statement: Non-apparel (accessories) share up 6.4% to 9.4%; apparel volume share up 60% to 70%
items.quote: Yes, other would be non-apparels.

items.statement: Denim revenue flattish YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: On the revenue front, denim has performed absolutely flattish.

items.statement: Retail SSG negative ~10% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: On the retail level, on the tertiary level, it has been negative close to around minus 10.

items.statement: Retail channel 45%, non-retail 55% of Q1 FY25 sales
items.quote: Quarter 1 FY '25 retail was 45%, non-retail was around 55%.

items.statement: Junior Kidswear launch experimental; testing 3-4 stores, need 2-3 seasons to set goals
items.quote: We are just initially starting, that we will try out 3-4 stores first, because we don't know, Kids is very new for us also. We will try out 3-4 stores, but we cannot say that we will be able to take a call after that that how many stores we will open. Like I told you last time that at least we need 3 seasons to set the new theme.

items.statement: Junior Killer positioned premium vs US Polo Kids; vacuum in premium kids segment
items.quote: I think Tejas there is still a vacuum for premiumization in this category structure. Our competition is not with unorganized sector. or I would say it's more with competition like U.S. Polo Kids. Your price in that category, I think there is still vacuum for a lot many brands to enter that price bracket.

items.statement: Junior Killer price points: T-shirts INR799-1,599, Jeans INR1,699-2,299, Cargos INR1,899-2,299
items.quote: T-shirts started from INR799 onwards, INR799 to maximum INR1,499 or INR1,599. Jeans we started from INR1,699 to INR2,299 and cargos started from same INR1,899 to INR2,299.

items.statement: LCL volumes up 6% QoQ; FCL volumes up 9% YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: For the quarter gone by, we saw the LCL business increased by almost 6% compared to the previous quarter. We also witnessed the FCL business up 9% as compared to the last year.

items.statement: Container utilization improved 4% YoY; 40-feet container share increased ~9%
items.quote: So, we have on the utilization index, we have each container utilized 4% better as compared to last year. We have also been able to increase the share of 40 -feet container by almost 9%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA up 34% QoQ on 13% revenue growth in Q1 FY25
items.quote: all these things combined have allowed us to improve the margins in the business and therefore that has contributed to the positive growth in EBITDA, which on a consolidated basis is about 34% compared to the previous quarter on the back of 13% expansion in the consolidated revenue.

items.statement: July-August volumes stronger; sustained recovery expected through September-October and end of year
items.quote: We have been noticing that for the month of July as well as August, the volumes have been stronger and we see a similar demand outlook for September and October, and therefore our general belief is that market should see continued sustained recovery in trade volumes until the end of the year.

items.statement: Express business EBITDA up 33% QoQ; operational efficiencies sustained
items.quote: On the Express business, we have seen that operational efficiencies which had been achieved in early part of this calendar year have sustained and that has allowed us to continually improve the operating margins in the express business, and as an outcome of t hat, the EBITDA for the quarter is almost 33% higher than the previous quarter.

items.statement: Contract Logistics revenue up 13% QoQ and 22% YoY; business diversified across chemical, e-commerce, auto
items.quote: we have increased almost 13% as compared to the previous quarter, we have increased almost 22% compared to the previous year, and this is primarily on the back of renewed contracts and now we are expanding in other domains.

items.statement: Expect sequential improvement to continue for remaining quarters of FY25; no specific volume guidance given
items.quote: we have seen sequential improvement, and we expect the same sequential improvements to continue for the remainder of the year on quarterly basis.

items.statement: Target to grow faster than market in both LCL and FCL for FY25
items.quote: we would continue to expand market share, which means that we would grow faster than the market in both LCL and FCL business for FY25.

items.quote: Apart from that in Allcargo ECU we do not have any large CAPEX requirements, only maintenance CAPEX, etc., which is expected. So, the summary is we expect the debt to go down from here, not go up.

items.statement: Working capital expanded due to higher freight rates; DSOs range-bound and controlled

But typically, around the Chinese New Year around February, there is then a little bit of a slackness, there could be some decline as well.

items.statement: Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay volumes could double in 9-12 months after new leadership appointment
items.quote: we appointed a new leadership team in Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. Three markets where we felt we were underrepresented and now we have a very strong commercial team which has come onboard toge ther as one team, and we expect that the volumes in these three countries could potentially double from the current levels in next nine to 12 months.

items.quote: We have achieved lot of cost savings as discussed in the past calls through standardization and then outsourcing of operations from the United States into Mex ico, and we continue to evaluate other such opportunities on how we could standardize operations and then outsource to reduce costs. And the second opportunity in that category is to continue to drive automation, because standardization also

items.quote: Sandeep joined us as Chief Operating Officer last year in the GATI business and there is clearly bee n a strong outcome. items.statement: Contract Logistics margin profile sustainable for 2-3 years; transport revenue may dilute margin % but grow absolute margin
items.quote: We don't see a si gnificant upward or downward revision in the margin profile. It should sustain from a two to three-year horizon. items.quote: the biggest challenge is on the supply side, with the whole red sea crisis, the additional turnaround transit time, also the US ports have been congested. So, all these factors have been leading to a bit of a supply shortage as well and we cannot really comment about the geopolitical situation but at least the immediate future, we don't see things changing rapidly.

items.statement: LCL yield (gross profit per CBM) range-bound; FCL yield (gross profit per TEU) volatile with freight rates
items.quote: LCL yield is gross profit per cubic meter, and the FCL yield is gross profit per TEU. Now, of course this is on an index that we share, but one could clearly see for instance the LCL yield is more range-bound and now on the back of increased utilization, w e believe we should get back to where we were 12 months ago and then possibly imp rove from there on.

items.statement: Revenue CAGR guidance of 12-14% over three years to FY28 with double-digit EBITDA margin by FY28
items.quote: we would like to keep our guidance of 12 % to 14% CAGR in revenue growth and EBITDA of 10% to 12% by FY28 if we will -- we are optimistic about achieving that.

items.statement: Expects double-digit adjusted EBITDA margin by end of FY25 and sustained in FY26
items.quote: I think as we go into summer and spring season, we are optimistic about hitting a double digit EBITDA, I guess by the end of th is year, and the next year should be in line with those double digit as well.

items.statement: Order flow much greater than last year; growth plan on track across US, UK, Europe, Australia, Japan

items.statement: Order book is as per plan and thoroughly on track
items.quote: Order book is as per our plan. I think we are on track, thoroughly on track.

items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA witnessed a decline of 34.3% year -on-year to INR13.3 crores in Quarter 1 FY25 with adjusted EBITDA margin at 4.8%.

items.quote: Woven 58%, knit 42% in Quarter 1 FY25 compared to woven 73%, knit 27% in Quarter 1 FY24.

items.quote: FY25, see our plan was, is, one is in India, we are adding capacity in Bihar, and the second is in Orissa, in partnership factory, in collaboration with the existing factory, which is infrastructure, which is existing there. The second is, you know, in terms of adding capacity, it will be in Bangladesh, and India also, in Madhya Pradesh.

items.quote: Overall, we are looking at almost 3,000 machines getting added in India in the plan which we have discussed. I think a number of this is a calculation we can share with you later in case you would like to know more details.

items.quote: Between Bangladesh and India are our major contribution as of now. In India we realize that we are in places which are more expensive. So we have to move some of our factory or add factories in the lower cost region. So that's definitely would be an important part of the capex.

items.statement: Finance cost ~2.2% of sales; absolute cost may rise with receivables financing but could fall with interest rate cuts; repaid INR15 crores high-cost long-term loan

items.statement: Raised INR149.5 crores via Qualified Institutional Placement from marquee investors

items.quote: So one of them has touched 100. The second one is about to touch 100. The third one is crossing at this point of time, maybe around 55-60 mark move towards 100.

items.statement: Bangladesh consolidation accelerating; smaller players may exit, stronger players gain share; India needs ecosystem development to compete

items.statement: Bangladesh LDC tariff benefit for EU/UK expected till 2029; extension chances may improve with current situation
items.quote: Bangladesh has got LDC status and because of which they have a GST benefit for the European countries and UK. So, that benefit they would have till 2029, if nothing changes.

items.statement: Raw material prices stable except linen fibre which remains inflationary
items.quote: Overall, the raw material prices remain stable for now with exception of the linen fibre which continues to be an inflationary trend.

items.statement: Overseas revenue grew 22% YoY; India revenue grew 7.3%; all shipments under FOB terms so Red Sea crisis not impacting costs
items.quote: Overseas revenue increased by almost 22% and India revenue increased by 7.3%.

items.quote: India this quarter experienced a higher percentage of absenteeism and attrition at our factory levels and this has been due to the prolonged election and the very high temperatures that India experienced this summer.

items.quote: So, volume growth is 35% is what we have seen here, and I think we mentioned that as a part of our three-year strategy, much of the growth in revenue will be driven largely from the volume growth.

items.quote: So, partnership factories are contributing around 21% in Q1 and 79% in house. So, this is in terms of the volume.

items.statement: Top line dipped 3.7% YoY due to subdued rural economy and adverse climatic conditions including heat waves and early monsoon
items.quote: During the quarter gone by, our top line dipped by 3.7% on a Y-o-Y basis. The decline is primarily attributed towards subdued rural economy.

items.statement: Unable to take price hikes and pass on to consumers due to sluggish demand
items.quote: Furthermore, the company is not able to take price hike on its product and pass on to the consumer on the back of sluggish demand which leads to additional pressure on the performance.

items.quote: The overall capacity utilization stood at 89% in Q1 FY '25. I am pleased to share that the company has also reduced debt by INR 31 crores during the quarter which brings our debt-to-equity ratio at comfortable levels.

items.statement: Lab grown diamonds account for 55% of D2C business and 15% of studded jewellery revenue

items.quote: Under the asset-light model, we disbursed Rs. 2,058 crores which is we did transactions of about Rs. 2,058 crores. Presently, the Company has nine partnerships. We have inked in other partnership in quarter one and gotten a letter of approval in quarter two from another public sector bank. By the end of this quarter, we should be at about 10 functional partnerships.

items.statement: Net interest income Rs 927 crores in Q1 FY25 vs Rs 562 crores in Q1 FY24; ROA 1.8% vs 1.7%
items.quote: has come in at Rs. 927 crores this quarter versus Rs. 562 crores quarter one of last year. Profit after tax for quarter one Fiscal ‘25 was Rs. 327 crores versus Rs. 296 crores in quarter one Fiscal ‘24. Gearing is moderate 1.9 x. Our target is to maintain it between 2 to 2.5x. Return on assets for the quarter for the overall book was 1.8% versus 1.7% in quarter

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.68%, Net NPA 1.52% at end June 2024; lowest in 16 quarters; imputed provisions 11.6% of loan book
items.quote: As at the end of June '24, our gross NPA stood at Rs. 1,782 crores translating to 2.68%, net NPA is at 1.52%. NPAs are at a stable level of 16 quarters. As we have been sharing, the Company carries imputed provisions of 11.6% of the loan book.

items.statement: Raised ~Rs 24,000 crores since April 2023 across diverse sources: equity Rs 3,700 cr, bank term loans Rs 5,000 cr, retail bonds Rs 834 cr, private placement Rs 3,000 cr, co-lending Rs 11,617 cr
items.quote: If you refer to Slide #16, you would notice that we have since April ‘23, which is the last fiv e quarters raised close to about Rs. 24,000 crores, of which we start practically, each and every source of capital available to us

items.statement: Pre-funded 75% of FCCB maturity proceeds due September 2024; setting aside 25% per quarter since Feb 2024
items.quote: Since February of 24, the Company has been setting aside 25% of the payable monies every quarter. This is now built up to 75% of the maturity proceeds. And these will be duly paid on whenever the put option is maturing.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds for 80% asset-light portion ~8.5%; balance sheet borrowings ~9.5%; cost decline expected in 6-12 months
items.quote: One is what is the cost of capital which is coming to fund the 80% of what we are funding, that number today would be in the handle of 8.5%. And then there is the cost of capital for the residual 20% that we are funding and holding on our balance sheet. For the balance sheet borrowings, we would be borrowing at about 9.5% today.

items.statement: Long-term dividend policy: 30-40% of profits
items.quote: The long-term dividend policy of the Company would be to keep dividends between 30% and 40% of profits.

items.statement: Heavy investments in technology; onboarded advisor from RBI's core group on IT innovation; upgrading technology backbone and risk modules
items.quote: Lastly, in order to remain competitive, as well as to further the cause of compliance and risk management, we are making heavy investments in technology. We have also just onboarded an advisor who is part of the RBI's core group towards IT innovation.

items.statement: Merging six smaller subsidiaries; identifying fee-based businesses; new corporate structure to be unveiled with Q2 FY25 results
items.quote: We would also like to unveil a completely new corporate structure they have as part of the Board outcome gathered that we are merging six of our smaller subsidiaries. We have also lined up the identification process of a couple of fee based businesses.

items.statement: Rights issue call money window open Aug 8-22, 2024; expects Rs 2,462 crores to be received; net worth to rise from Rs 20,269 crores
items.quote: The net worth of our Company as of June end stood at Rs. 20,269. As most of you would be aware, the final call monies were called and the window to pay up the call money opened on 8th of August and will close on the 22nd of August 2024. When this money is with the Company, the net worth would rise by a further Rs. 2,462 crores.

items.statement: Regulatory environment demanding compliance, risk management, liquidity management at center; company focusing on benign ALM with no month borrowing more than few hundred crores
items.quote: Having come through this six -month detailed review process, before we were granted the fresh certifi cate of registration and keeping in mind the current regulatory environment , we are not only is one classified as an upper layer, non -bank finance Company, but what one is witnessing that the regulator is expecting regulated entities to keep compliance, risk management, liquidity management, etc

items.statement: Co-lending/assignment/securitization at Rs 11,617 crores; 16 banks/FIs for sell-down; total ~26 partners
items.quote: We also do sell down transactions with 16 banks and financial institutions. So, in total, we'll have close to about 26 partners with whom we are doing business.

items.statement: 25th year of operations; rebranding from Indiabulls Housing to Sammaan Capital underway across branches and channels
items.quote: This is also the 25th year of our operations. The erstwhile Indiabulls from which the Company originates, was incorporated in the year 2000. Our rebranding exercise around the new brand and our 25 years of operations is underway across var ious channels and our branches and points of presence

items.statement: Monthly disbursement run rate of Rs. 120-130 crore expected to continue
items.quote: the run rate that we are running at is between Rs. 120 crores to Rs. 130 crores on average of monthly disbursements, and the endeavor is to continue running at that pace

items.statement: Long-term co-lending AUM target of 35-45% of total AUM
items.quote: it will hover between 35% to 45% over the long term, which is where it is, given there is also a certain amount of cyclicality associated with this business

items.statement: Target leverage of 2x to 4x over long term
items.quote: Our endeavor is to run leverage between 2x to 3.5x or 2x to at most 4x, is where the leverage will be

items.statement: Target ROA above 3% and ROE of 15% over long term
items.quote: the goal is to generate a 3+ percentage ROA and get to a 15% ROE

items.statement: Target NIM of up to 8% over time
items.quote: the goal is to get back to up to an 8% net interest margin, which will happen over a period of time

items.statement: NIM rose to 6.7% in Q1 FY25 from 6.1% a year ago
items.quote: we have seen an increase in our net interest margin, which rose from 6.1% to 6.7%, given higher yields from increasing business with these co-lending partners

items.statement: Gold loan NIM ~6%, business loan NIM ~7.5%
items.quote: net interest margin for the gold loan product is close to about 6%. And the net interest margin for the business loan product is higher at about 7.5%

items.statement: AUM grew to Rs. 11.6 billion, up from Rs. 6.6 billion a year ago
items.quote: Our AUM, which includes on-balance sheet and off-balance sheet loans, originated with co-lending partners, has grown to Rs. 11.6 billion, up from Rs. 6.6 billion a year ago

items.statement: Disbursements of Rs. 3.8 billion in Q1 FY25, up from Rs. 2.7 billion
items.quote: Our disbursements for the quarter stood at Rs. 3.8 billion, up from Rs. 2.7 billion in June 2023

items.statement: Gold loans 66% of AUM, MSME business loans 33%, others <1%
items.quote: 66% of our AUM comprises of gold loans, 33% in MSME business loans and less than 1% in loans against property and personal loans, which are in run-off mode

items.statement: Co-lending AUM at 41% of total AUM
items.quote: Lending as a Service today comprises about 41% of our total AUM

items.statement: Gold loan GNPA 12 bps, business loan GNPA 3.7%
items.quote: Gross NPAs in the gold-backed business loan product are 12 basis points, 0.12%. The gross NPAs in the business loan product are 3.7%

items.statement: Gold loan auction recovery >109% of principal and interest
items.quote: we have recovered more than 109% of principal and interest due on gold loans which were sold in auction and therefore, we have refunded excess amounts to borrowers

items.statement: Collection efficiency 480% including prepayments on gold loans
items.quote: Collection efficiency, including prepayments and repayments on gold loans, which is a regular feature in the business, was 480% in the quarter

items.statement: SIDBI BC book: 8% bounce rate, 100% bounce collection, 0% net bounce rate
items.quote: on a low 8% bounce rate in this book, we have collected 100% of these bounces with a 0% net bounce rate since we started originating these loans for SIDBI

items.statement: Branch network stabilized at ~125 branches, adding 1-2 per quarter in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra
items.quote: Our goal was always to get to about 125 branches, which is where we are at. At the margin, we will add probably one to two more branches, if at all, on a quarterly basis in three geographies pred ominantly, which is Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra

items.statement: Branch breakeven period 10-14 months on average
items.quote: Usually 10 to 14 months is the breakeven period for the branch, depending on the geography

items.statement: Opex as % of AUM for gold loan branches below 7.5%, down from >8% in FY24
items.quote: Op ex as a percentage of AUM for the gold loan branches has decreased to below 7.5%, down from over 8% in all of fiscal '24

items.statement: Opex expected to decline further in FY25 and FY26
items.quote: We anticipate this percentage to decline further in coming quarters of fiscal '25 and '26

items.statement: Cost of funds hovering at 13%, up from ~11.83% pre-rate hikes
items.quote: Our cost of funds are still hovering in the 13% range, which has been high. Recall, prior to the RBI raising rates by 250 basis points a few years ago, they were well below 12%. It was about 11.83% at that point in time

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio at ~24%, to increase with warrant infusion
items.quote: We are at about 24% on capital adequacy. And once the entire money for the warrant infusion comes in which is the balance Rs. 66 crores that we expect over the next 15 months, this number will inch up

items.statement: Warrant issuances of Rs. 880 million announced, Rs. 220 million received, Rs. 660 million expected over 15 months
items.quote: In the last two quarters, the Company has announced warrant issuances of Rs. 880 million, of which Rs. 220 million has been received. Over the course of the next 15 months, we expect to receive the remaining Rs. 660 million

items.statement: Gold loan: 55,000+ active borrowers, avg ticket Rs. 1.3 lakh, tenure 12 months origination
items.quote: The gold loan business has an active borrower base of more than 55,000 customers and an average ticket size of Rs. 0.13 million. The tenure of these loans at origination is usually 12 months

items.statement: Business loan: 43,000+ active borrowers, avg ticket Rs. 1 lakh, tenure 1.5 years
items.quote: In the business loan product, we have an active borrower base of over 43,000 customers and an average ticket size of Rs. 0.1 million. These loans have an average tenure of one and a half years

items.statement: Average household income Rs. 3-4 lakh, 32% new-to-credit customers
items.quote: The average household income is between Rs. 3 lakhs to Rs. 4 lakhs, again, that's the average. And the new to credit customer base is about 32%

items.statement: Green energy finance for 3-wheelers: Rs. 11.5 crore book, 0% GNPA, avg ticket Rs. 1.6 lakh, tenure 18-24 months
items.quote: We have a book of about R s. 11.5 crores. And at this point in time, there are no gross NPAs on the book. It's only been about seven months. But so far the product has performed fairly well

items.statement: Daily gross disbursement Rs. 4.5-5 crore
items.quote: the daily disbursement on a gross basis was closer to between Rs. 4.5 crores to Rs. 5 crores

items.statement: 85% of branches in Tier 2/3/4 locations, 66 profitable in Q1 FY25
items.quote: With over 85% of our branches situated in Tier 2, Tier 3 and Tier 4 locations, 66 branches were profitable in 1Q '25

items.statement: Gold price increases make lending cautious due to mark-to-market risk if prices fall
items.quote: When gold prices go up in the manner in which they have gone up, that usually makes us a little nervous about wanting to lend more. The reason being that it also exposes you to a risk, god forbid there is a fluctuation in gold prices going downwards

items.statement: RBI requirement for BC gold loans: gold must be kept with capital provider, causing Shivalik BC slowdown
items.quote: there is a requirement from the RBI that in a BC relationship with gold, the gold gets kept with the capital provider, which is Shivalik. So, for us, in a co-lending or a BC relationship, it's not possible for us to transport the gold or keep the gold with the partner

items.statement: Differentiation through customer service and product variances
items.quote: the most important feature on how one could stand out, at least we try and make an effort to stand out in our customer service. It's a very easily used term but very hard to do

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 25% YoY for FY25, with 25% CAGR targeted for next 3 years from FY24 base
items.quote: So '25, we have already given a guidance of 25%. Fi rst quarter has happened and has panned out quite well. We see that, this will continue for the remaining of the financial year. So 25% minimum improvement year-on-year is given

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of plus or minus 1% around current levels for full year FY25
items.quote: So there is no reason why these margins plus or minus 1% should be achievable for the full year, if not better

items.statement: Order inflow target of INR3,000 crores for FY25 excluding MHADA BDD project additions
items.quote: we do hope to achieve the target of INR3,000 crores in the current fiscal, if not more. This INR3,000 crores is excluding the fronts open up from BDD project of MHADA

items.statement: Net working capital cycle reduction target of 20 more days by March 2025, total 37 days reduction for FY25
items.quote: I do believe that ther e are more scope for 20 days till 31st March 2025. Now that means an overall reduction of 37 day s is what we are committed to do in the current financial year

items.statement: Capex target restricted to INR65 crores for full year FY25
items.quote: we do expect to restrict this figure to about INR65 crores for the full financial year

items.statement: Standalone order book at INR8,828 crores as of June 30, 2024, plus INR1,000 crores additional MHADA BDD work front
items.quote: Our order book on a standalo ne basis as on 30th June 24, stood at INR8,828 crores. Further, the work front for additional INR1,000 crores has been made available by MHADA for our BDD project

items.statement: Public sector 72%, private sector 28% of order book; target to maintain 70-75% public, 25-30% private mix
items.quote: Public sector accounts for 72% while private sector accounts for 28% of the total order book.

items.statement: Margin expansion from higher EPC project revenue share; cost of materials and construction services falling as percentage of revenue
items.quote: Secondly, you will see that the cost of consumptio n of material and construction services has also following in proportion as a percentage of the top line

items.statement: Strong bidding pipeline across public and private sectors; expect >INR2,000 crores monthly bidding opportunities in coming months
items.quote: I think we are not anything more than two or three months away from th ere. Where at least you would have an opportunity to choose and bid for more than INR2,000 crores per month

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex of INR28 crores including office purchase; core asset addition only INR18 crores
items.quote: The overall, the total additions to our -- was about INR28 crores in Q1, a ll right? And we do expect to restrict this figure to about INR65 crores for the full financial year

items.statement: Gift City project in full flow, expected completion by January 2025; actively bidding for more projects in Gift City area
items.quote: Gift City project is in full flow. We expect to com plete that by January of current financial year. We continue to bid. As we speak, we are bidding for certain more projects in Gift City area

items.statement: Net working capital cycle reduced by 17 days in Q1 FY25 vs Q4 FY24; driven by INR100+ crores retention collection, surety bond access, debtor days reduction, IGMS recovery, and real estate asset monetization
items.quote: Our efforts towards improving the net working capi tal cycle has translated into a reduction of 17 days in Q1 FY '25 over Q4 FY '24

items.statement: Expect INR60-70 crores cash flow from real estate asset disposal in remainder of FY25
items.quote: And we do expect about INR60 crores to INR70 crores o f cash flows coming in from there in the remainder of the current financial year

items.statement: Gross debt INR336 crores, net debt INR94 crores as of June 30, 2024; gross debt-to-equity 0.21x, net debt-to-equity 0.06x
items.quote: Gross debt stood at INR336 crores as on June 30, '24 as c ompared to INR326 crores as on March 31, 2024, with gross debt-to-equity at 0.21. Net debt s tood at INR94 crores with net debt to equity at 0.06x

items.statement: Interest cost includes mobilization advance interest, LC discount charges, and bank guarantee commissions on ~INR1,500 crores BG limits, not just borrowings
items.quote: This includes discount charges paid on LC for purchase of material and it is not necessarily attributable to only the CC limit or the gross borrowing, which you see of INR330 crores.

items.statement: Top private clients: Raymond (INR1,500+ crores order book), Godrej, SBUT, Lodha (4th repeat order), M3M, Oberoi, DLF, Piramal, Prestige, Phoenix, Raheja; government: MHADA, CIDCO, MCGM, BSNL, PWD, IOCL, Gift City
items.quote: So the top clients at the moment from an order book perspective, would start with Raymond. The entire Thane project current order book profile is more than INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Competing with L&T, Shapoorji, Ahluwalia in EPC building segment; mature competition reflected in profit margins; private sector on invitation basis with repeat orders
items.quote: We are one of the prominent players and being EPC c ompany and competing with likes of L&T, Shapoorji, Ahluwalia. I believe that all these are mature

items.statement: MHADA BDD project: executed INR134 crores in Q1 (INR100 crores certified, INR34 crores ARPU); expect INR140+ crores monthly from Dec/Jan with price variation
items.quote: The company has executed in Q1 approximately INR134 crores of work. Out of this INR100 crores is certified sales and INR34 crores is ARPU sales approval.

items.statement: CIDCO project: INR64+ crores certified sales in Q1; expect ~INR100 crores in Q2, >INR150 crores from Q3 onwards, improving in Q4
items.quote: Similarly, on CIDCO front, the company has done certified sales in excess of INR64 crores. We believe that the momentum of CIDCO will be exponential.

items.statement: Hospital sector targeting 15-17% of overall outlook; executing 3 hospitals, completed Varanasi AIIMS (fastest in country), bidding for more
items.quote: So that sector will definitely be at least 15% to 17% of our overall outlook.

items.statement: Maharashtra state elections to cause 60-day public sector bidding lull; central PSU and other state projects to continue unhindered
items.quote: So yes, there will be no bidding 40 days prior to t he election dates and I do not know what election dates whether they have been announced or not. So you will have a 60-day lull in the public sector in Maharashtra

items.statement: Labor availability remains industry-wide challenge; mitigated by 15-day payment cycle (from monthly) and higher EPC revenue reducing labor intensity
items.quote: So we have addressed a certain part of that. And I' d like to speak to you today, we are in 90% manned across projects, manned as the sense, the la bor force

items.statement: Depreciation on site establishment (temp structures) falling from INR265 crores (Apr 2022) to ~INR100 crores now; balance to be written off over next 4 quarters
items.quote: So it's very clear that the site establishment, which was INR265 crores as on first of April 22 stand's at close to INR100 crores as on today. So you have already written off depreciation of INR165 crores

items.statement: Actively bidding for CPWD, AIIMS, central PSU projects; JICA/ADB funded projects in Bihar, Andhra Pradesh with central government guarantee
items.quote: we are working for today. We ar e very eager to add CPWD and we are very eager to add those projects which the central government has funded, whether it is through PSUs or for that matter, projects, which may come up in the state of Bihar all state of Andhra

items.statement: Bank guarantee limits of INR250 crores pre-approved, expect overall INR350 crores availability excluding CIDCO/MHADA; BGs recycled quarterly as advances recovered
items.quote: So we are already armed with pre limits of INR250 c rores available with us, okay? And that is good enough to take care of the next quarters. Further, you have to remember that bank guarantee were issued and they are received back also

items.statement: Private sector margin profile maintained; no compromise on margins; developers accepting higher rates for quality; Raymond and M3M projects with no performance/advance guarantees
items.quote: That we will work with our margin profile. There is no need for the company to compromise on its margin pr ofile. Given our order book and also the fact that nearly INR3,500 crores is yet to get added on MHADA project

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting to EPC public projects (70%+); EPC projects have 40% RCC vs 60% finishes/MEP/BM, improving revenue per labor cost
items.quote: In a pure shell and core business fo r the private sector, the labor requirement is much higher. It's a normal thing because you're doing only the RCC works. As opposed to this, when you go to government, a contract is only 40

items.statement: Maintains FY25 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs. 2,000 crores
items.quote: We are not changing our guidance at all. We absolutely stand by the Rs. 2,000 crore guidance that we have and we will be on track to achieve the number.

items.statement: Guides FY25 consolidated EBITDA north of Rs. 400 crores
items.quote: So, our guidance on the consolidated EBITDA will be north of Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: Expects EPC EBITDA margins in 15% range for FY25
items.quote: we expect our EBITDA margins to be in the 15% range. So, good healthy EPC EBITDA margins is what we will continue to get.

items.statement: BESS projects carry 90%-95% EBITDA margins over 12-year tenure
items.quote: For doing this, GUVNL will pay us a monthly capacity charge. We expect that the monthly capacity charge from the two projects that we have, is going to be approximately close to Rs. 260 crores a year and this is of course going to be a pretty high EBITDA business. This is going to be something like a 90%-95% EBITDA business for us.

items.statement: Solar order book including BESS stands at Rs. 4,700 crores as of July 31, 2024
items.quote: Our solar order book including BESS project wins stands at Rs. 4,700 crores as of July 31, 2024 with the bid pipeline that significantly exceed this figure.

items.statement: BESS order book at Rs. 3,200 crores; active bid pipeline of Rs. 6,000-7,000 crores
items.quote: We have Rs. 3,200 crores of order book and about as we speak we have bid for about between close to Rs. 6,000-Rs. 7,000 crores of more bids we have placed on the BESS projects.

items.statement: Expects Rs. 15,000-20,000 crores of BESS bids in market over next year
items.quote: I expect that the market will see at least in the next about 365 days in one year, we will see about Rs. 15,000-Rs. 20,000 crores of BESS bid pipeline, which will get shaped up based on the conversations that we are having with various state and central utilities.

items.statement: Chakan EV plant has 30,000 units annual capacity; first year production target 7,000 units
items.quote: It will be manufactured at our Greenfield plant in Chakan, Pune with an annual capacity of 30,000 units per annum.

items.statement: BESS order book of Rs. 3,200 crores requires ~Rs. 300 crores equity; additional Rs. 6,000 crores wins would need ~Rs. 500 crores more equity
items.quote: for a Rs. 3,200 crores order book, we will need approximately equity of about close to Rs. 300 crores is what we will need. So, approximately let us say, the Rs. 3,200 crore order book is going to be built on asset base of about Rs. 1,200-Rs. 1,300 crores and at a 20% equity requirement we will need between Rs. 250 and Rs. 300 crores of equity for the current BESS pipeline that we have.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced by Rs. 33 crores in Q1 FY25 to Rs. 1,363 crores
items.quote: our gross closing debt for the quarter actually reduced by Rs. 33 crores to Rs. 1,363 crores. So, there has been a reduction of debt, which has happened in this quarter by about Rs. 33 crores over the March 2024 closing of Rs. 1,397 crores, which reduced to Rs. 1,363 crores.

items.statement: QIP proceeds allocated to debt reduction and BESS/IPP project development
items.quote: a portion of the funds will go into debt reduction and building the order book that we have around energy storage and the projects that we have recently won. So, these will be the two major allocation of funds which is going to be there, both portion of it around debt reduction and a portion of it around the development business which is BESS and the IPP projects that we have.

items.statement: Warrant round closed at 60 lakh warrants (~Rs. 538 crores); board approved fresh Rs. 500 crore fundraise
items.quote: the previous fundraise that we announced in the month of March closed at 60 lakh warrants at an average price of Rs. 871 which is approximately Rs. 538 crores of capital.

items.statement: EPC net working capital cycle ~40-45 days; Rs. 2,000 crore revenue needs ~Rs. 600 crores working capital (Rs. 250 cr fund, Rs. 350 cr non-fund)
items.quote: So, I think for the business of approximately Rs. 2,000 crores that we will do, we will need approximately close to Rs. 600 crores of working capital. But this includes both fund and non-fund limits which are there. Approximately, about Rs. 250 odd crores might be through fund limits and rest Rs. 350 crores will be through non-fund limits.

items.statement: EV manufacturing breakeven at 12,000 units; expects to reach BEP in FY27
items.quote: Our breakeven point for this plant is at about 12,000 vehicles.

items.statement: EV launch delayed to April 2025 for extended testing; first year production 7,000 units
items.quote: As of now, we hope that our on-road sales will start by about April of next year. So, that is when we will start the commercial sales of the vehicle.

items.statement: EV manufacturing initially B2B only (fleet/cargo); no distribution channel needed for FY25-26
items.quote: So, this is going to be primarily a B2B product in the first few years. So, we are only going to sell it to business customers. And for the fleet variant and for the cargo variant, we will only have business customers and fleet customers. So, for that, we do not need to set up a distribution channel.

items.statement: EV leasing AUM at Rs. 600 crores; scalable to Rs. 3,000 crores with same team
items.quote: This team is today doing an AUM of Rs. 600 crores. This team can also do AUM of Rs. 3,000 crores.

items.statement: BESS projects bid at ~15% EBITDA margin; better procurement can improve margins
items.quote: when we are bidding, we are bidding at about 15% EBITDA margin and if we are able to do better procurement, then we are able to increase our margins.

items.statement: Share pledge tied to IREDA/PFC debt for EV leasing; expected to taper over 3-4 years as debt reduces
items.quote: the share pledge is given as a collateral against the long term debt that we have received from IREDA and PFC for the leasing business. So, we expect that will taper down over the 3-4 year time period.

items.statement: Claims largest standalone BESS portfolio in India; strong bid pipeline validates leadership
items.quote: I think Gensol has the largest portfolio of standalone BESS projects in the country. The bid pipeline that we have is also extremely strong. So, we will continue to maintain a significant leadership position in the BESS domain.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 consolidated revenue Rs. 297 crores (105% YoY), EBITDA Rs. 89 crores (30% margin), PAT Rs. 15 crores (50% YoY)
items.quote: Our consolidated total revenue has increased from Rs. 145 crores in Quarter 1 FY24 to Rs. 297 crores in Quarter 1 FY25, reflecting 105% growth. The consolidated EBITDA increased to Rs. 89 crores with a 30% margin in Quarter 1 FY25, representing a remarkable increase from a figure of Rs. 37 crores and a 25% margin last year.

items.statement: Transmission corridor development beyond 2030 dependent on government investment; no near-term headwinds seen
items.quote: Beyond 5 years, we are all dependent on how the Government of India shapes up transmission corridors across the country and I am sure if you look at the budget this year, there h as been significant allocation which has gone to development of transmission

items.statement: Raised Rs 150 crore via QIP at Rs 318 per share on June 25, 2024
items.quote: During the quarter ended June 30, 2024, the Company raised Rs. 150 crores by way of QIP and allotted 47,16,981 equity shares of face value, Rs. 1, each to eligible qualified institutional buyers at an issue price of Rs. 318 per share, which includes a premium of R s. 317 per share

items.statement: Utilised Rs 60 crore of QIP proceeds for working capital loan repayment in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Out of the net proceeds of the issue, during the quarter the Company has utilized Rs. 60 crores towards repayment of working capital loans, and the balance amounts are invested in high credit quality short-term money market instruments.

items.statement: Net debt stood at Rs 57.8 crore as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: As on 30 June 2024, the Company had a net debt of Rs. 57.8 crores.

items.statement: Expect net debt to become zero with surplus by end of FY25 after QIP deployment
items.quote: Borosil balance sheet will be, overall, the net debt will be zero and there will be some surplus, at the end of the financial year

items.statement: Term loan of Rs 125 crore and working capital loan of Rs 7-8 crore outstanding as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: our term-loan at the moment as of 30 June is about Rs. 125 crores, and maybe a small working capital of about Rs. 7 crores, Rs. 8 crores.

items.statement: Rs 90 crore payable to Borosil Scientific remains outstanding
