items.quote: Europe achieved revenue of INR1,571 million, reflecting a 34% year-on-year increase or growth

items.statement: Emerging markets formulation revenue grew 36% YoY in constant currency led by Turkey price actions
items.quote: Emerging markets reported revenue of INR1,187 million, marking a 36% year-on-year growth in constant currency terms

items.statement: Operating expenses reduced 1.1% YoY despite global inflationary pressures
items.quote: We have managed to achieve a 1.1% reduction in our opex on a Y-o-Y basis. That is INR1,291 million in Q1 financial year '24 to million in Q1 financial year '25

items.statement: Formulation growth driven 1/3 volume, 1/3 pricing, 1/3 new products; Turkey growth mostly price-led, Europe ~3-4% price rest volume
items.quote: About 1/3 on volume, about 1/3 on pricing and about 1/3 coming from new products and launches. That's a good sort of mix which we would expect for this kind of a business going ahead in the future

items.statement: Started distributing vaccines for a European partner in Belgium and Netherlands; not manufacturing vaccines
items.quote: we're not in the manufacturing of vaccines. But because we have a very strong presence in market in the front end in many countries, we are looking at vaccines as being an interesting area to distribute

items.statement: Zoetis product supply expected to resume in second half of FY25 (previously indicated August)
items.quote: We expect it on the second half of the year to come back. I had indicated August. It could spill into the second half of the year

items.statement: Capex for FY25 guided at INR 50-60 crore, subdued after prior years' investments
items.quote: the capex for the current year is going to be subdued, but it's supposed to be around INR50 crores to INR60 crores for the current financial year across the board

items.statement: Turkey facility received EU GMP certification enabling exports to EU and reactivation of discontinued German plant products
items.quote: our plant is now certified EU GMP, which means it's end-supply from our Turkish facility to the European Union as well

items.statement: Turkey exports to Middle East/North Africa doubled in Q1; target to match import value in 12-18 months for natural FX hedge
items.quote: we, today, export about 50% of what we import equivalent value, and that is something we intend to neutralize and make our exports equal to imports in the next 12 to 18 months

items.statement: Term loan restructuring completed: single global bank, simplified covenants, additional lines created; net debt down ~INR 12 crore QoQ
items.quote: We also successfully completed our term loan restructuring process, moving away from multi-geography multibank structure. This restructuring has resulted in simplifying our borrowing structure and covenant

items.statement: Interest cost up slightly due to restructuring; floating rate debt so cost to decline as rates fall over next few quarters
items.quote: interest has slightly gone up because of that. And this is a short-term phenomenon. I think the interest rate increase, which you have seen will remain so of that amount will remain for this next few quarters, and then it will start going down

items.statement: Actively pursuing bolt-on acquisitions/partnerships in companion animal formulations and API R&D/scale; not large M&A due to balance sheet discipline
items.quote: We look both for -- on the formulation side, we would be focusing on opportunities which may be there on companion animals largely. The kind of transactions, which are, right now, possible on the formulation side, would not be full-fledged companies, but it could be assets which are around brands, which could be around licensing

items.statement: Working capital days at 110-120 range due to geographic spread, logistics delays; target to gradually reduce as situation eases
items.quote: we must resume the working capital to be range bound. I'm going down gradually as the situation improves or eases

items.statement: India formulation business at INR 120-140 crore annualized; team expanded 40%, targeting acceleration in 12-18 months
items.quote: The India formulation business today, which is run at an annualized sales of around INR120 crores to INR140 crores, we expect that this should definitely accelerate in another 12 to 18 months

items.statement: Companion animal share <5% of business; target 15% over 3-5 years
items.quote: That is not yet fully developed. It is less than 5% of our business at this point of time. And we would like that to grow substantially to at least, as I have indicated in the past, coming to 15% over a 3- to 5-year period

items.statement: Vizag API facility received positive EIR review; preliminary Japan certification; pursuing WHO prequalification
items.quote: The Vizag A PI facility has received a positive reviews at the EIR, which is We've also received preliminary certification from new markets like Japan. And we are in the process of finalizing prequalification registrations for supply for WHO products

items.statement: Turkey market still not steady despite stabilization; monitoring quarter-to-quarter; geopolitical and disease intensity variability
items.quote: it is not a steady market yet. But it's a high opportunity market. It is amongst the largest in the world, and we are also very strong over there. So we have to learn to create, in an agile manner, in that market

items.statement: India formulation team expanded ~40% in Q4 FY24; further expansion planned by end of FY25
items.quote: we have expanded our team by almost 40%, and we will follow this up with more expansions towards the end of this year

items.statement: US FDA project on hold for next 12-24 months; lower priority vs other growing markets
items.quote: from a short-term point of view, which I would say is the next 12 to 24 months, it's unlikely that we will do any kind of acceleration on the U.S. project

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance revised to 15-20% for FY25 from earlier 20-25%
items.quote: No. So, I think the guidance, which I would have, is probably more like 15% to 20% on a top line growth.

items.statement: Expects double-digit EBITDA margins by late H2 FY25, sustainable 11-13% in 3 years
items.quote: As I said before, I think we definitely continue to hold our guidance in the same spread that we will get into double-digit EBITDA margins.

items.statement: 3-year revenue CAGR ~15%, targeting ~INR5,000 crores by FY28
items.quote: So, I would give a guidance of anywhere between around, let's say, 15% over the next 3 years. And if I were to work on that 15% CAGR mark, I would expect revenues maybe around INR5,000-odd crores by FY '28.

items.statement: 40-50% of order book to convert in FY25 (mostly H2), 40% in FY26, 10% in FY27
items.quote: So, I would say that in FY '25, we will see almost close to 40% to 50% of this, and most of this will come in H2. Another 40-odd percent will be pushed to next year, FY '26, and maybe about 10-odd percent will come in FY '27.

items.statement: FY25 capex INR200-250 crores (Chakan Phase 2, Sanand EV readiness); maintenance INR80-100 crores
items.quote: For the full year FY '25, we are looking at anywhere between INR 200 crores to INR250 crores capex. A large part of it would be under the new Chakan Phase 2 expansion and also the Sanand, Gujarat readiness for the EV model of Maruti Suzuki.

items.statement: No capex for PCB localization; will switch suppliers instead
items.quote: So, for the localization, we will not be investing. It will be simply a supplier, which is an importer to a localized supplier. So, we would not necessarily be incurring any capex on account of the localization of these electronic components.

items.statement: Chakan Phase 1 utilization ~55-60% in Q1; target 80-85% by Q4 FY25 via Thar 5-door and Scorpio shift
items.quote: So, by quarter four, we do expect this to be around 80% to 85%. Primarily a couple of reasons. I think there are certain new programs of Mahindra & Mahindra, the most -- the next one being the Thar five doors, which will get into production.

items.statement: Chakan Phase 2 on track for Q1 FY26 commissioning; timeline unchanged but capex may be pruned
items.quote: So, the Phase 2 expansion in terms of a timeline continues to be on track because these are for certain models of OEMs, like Volkswagen and Tata Motors, and the model launches have not been delayed.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 9.1% (+40bps YoY); normalized EBITDA 7-8.2% range; manufacturing EBITDA fell from 10.4% (Q4) to 8.4% (Q1)
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q1 FY '25 stood at 9.1%, a growth of 40 basis points Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Material margin under pressure from higher LED mix (high import content) and plastic price escalations; OEM pass-through lag 3-6 months
items.quote: since the penetration of LED has increased to 45% now compared to, let's say, 39% in the last year, the gross margin or the material margin also is under a bit of a pressure because of high import content still on the LED aspect

items.statement: Fixed costs up from new Chakan plant; XUV700 volumes halved vs plan (7-8k to 4-4.5k/month) causing under-absorption
items.quote: Our major expenses on the fixed costs were increased due to the new Chakan facility, whic h went online in November 2023. However, unfortunately, the volumes for some of the critical models, for which the new investment was made has actually declined since that time period, specifically on the XUV700

items.statement: ~25% of total buying value still imported (electronics: PCB, connectors, capacitors, LED modules); PCB board localization in progress, SMT already local
items.quote: So as of now, this in terms of the value, I will have to -- so about 25% of the total buying value would still be imported, which would again be largely driven by the electronic category.

items.statement: PCB localization benefits expected FY26 after validation and inventory exhaustion; no capex required
items.quote: The benefit of that, I would say, it will only accrue sometime in FY '26 because these electronic parts also have a very long lead time. So, we would exhaust all the imported inventory in the pipeline and only then move to localization.

items.statement: Passenger vehicle industry growth seen at 3-5% FY25; inventory buildup at retail; Q2 demand similar to Q1 (weak)
items.quote: I think most analysts have predicted that their forecast for FY '25 for the passenger vehicle space continues to be in low single digits, anywhere between 3% to 5%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 outlook similar to Q1 with continued demand headwinds; recovery expected H2 post festive
items.quote: No, Q2 is similar as Q1. We are not seeing any strong offtake in demand from the OEM. Q2 would be pretty similar in line with Q1.

items.statement: LED share of lighting revenue 45% in Q1 (up from 35% YoY); target higher in FY25; 2-wheeler LED penetration ~50%, 4-wheeler ~55%
items.quote: With respect to segment mix, Q1 FY '25 as a percentage of revenue, 65% from passenger vehicle, 29% from 2-wheelers and 6% from commercial vehicles.

items.statement: 2-wheeler revenue share ~30% currently; expected to stay ~1/3 of total; order book 30% 2-wheeler, 70% PV+CV
items.quote: I think our 2-wheeler share is now almost close to 30%. I think going forward, again, with a higher penetration of LED, so thereby increasing the value per vehicle, the 2-wheeler share, I would expect it to be around 1/3 of the total pie.

items.statement: Maruti: Q1 growth 11% YoY; full year revised to 15-20% (from 20%); single-source on new Swift and first EV (EV launch FY26)
items.quote: We had originally anticipated maybe close to a 20% growth. Maybe that growth gets certainly revised to maybe around 15% to 20% in light of certain headwinds in the passenger vehicle segment.

items.statement: M&M: Q1 volumes +15%, wallet share +57%; expected 30-35% growth FY25; Thar 5-door and Scorpio shift to Chakan key
items.quote: So, we do expect Mahindra to be one of the significant growth contributors for the full year, perhaps growing at maybe close to 30-odd per cent on a year-on-year basis, 30% -35% growth coming from Mahindra.

items.statement: Mould revenue Q1 high; full year estimate INR220-250 crores
items.quote: Going forward, I think for the full year, our estimation is anywhere between INR 220 crores to INR250 crores of revenue from moulds revenues for the full year.

items.statement: Sanand plant subsidy INR10 crores/year until FY28 (10 years); Maharashtra (Chakan) eligibility pending
items.quote: Sanand concerned the per month subsidy, i.e., the per annum subsidy is around INR10 crores. Pratik Kothari: This is for how long? Sanjay Mehta: It is up to '27- '28 financial year. It is for 10 years

items.statement: CEO Raju Ketkale driving manufacturing efficiency, productivity, capex reduction, fixed cost optimization; benefits expected H2 FY25
items.quote: We are now in very big way taken the activity for improving. One is very clearly now we have some manufacturing efficiency improvement opportunities are available. So very clearly. Then also, we have opportunity for the productivity improvement, okay?

items.statement: XUV700 volume drop 50% vs plan major risk to Chakan utilization and margins; PV demand slowdown risk to revenue guidance
items.quote: XUV700 used to be at 7,000 to 8,000 a month production rate. Now it has fallen down to close to around 4,000, 4,500. So almost half of what we had anticipated.

items.statement: Exports not part of strategy; focus on domestic market; logistics and geographic restrictions (Stanley presence) limit exports
items.quote: Exports are right now not a part of our strategy from a product exports. Also, some of our lighting products are not very friendly logistically to be exported. And then again, certain geographic restrictions also are there when we look at Stanley's own presence in other Southeast Asian markets.

items.statement: Raw material escalation claims from OEMs have 3-6 month lag; expect compensation from Q2 onwards
items.quote: We are under discussions with the OEMs to get compensated. But as you know, this is a lag of about 3 months to 6 months. So, we do expect in the subsequent quarters, the OEMs to be compensating us from the raw material escalation.

items.statement: Capex guidance maintained at Rs 5,000 crore plus/minus 10% for FY25, under reassessment due to closed acquisitions
items.quote: Our CAPEX guidance remains the same at Rs. 5,000 crores plus minus 10%. However, with all the acquisitions closed and in light of the increased business parameter that we have with these new businesses, we are reassessing this.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex was Rs 1,078 crore; 18 greenfield plants announced, 2 operationalized in India and China, 1 new in Mexico, 7 for non-auto
items.quote: Our CAPEX for the quarter was Rs. 1,078 crores. As announced earlier, we are setting up new plants to support growth coming out of emergi ng markets. Out of the 18 Greenfields we have announced earlier, two have been operationalized and commenced production in India and China respectively. Additionally, we are adding one new plant in

items.statement: Consumer electronics JV with BIEL Crystal: Rs 2,600 crore investment, 130,000+ sqm facility, production start Sep-Oct, ramp-up over next year
items.quote: This new vertical, we envisage that will require investments of around Rs. 2,600 crores over a period of time. We are setting up state -of-the-art facilities with an estimated area of more than 130,000 square meters for this project. We expect start of production around September- October, with subsequent ramp up in production over the next year.

items.statement: Consolidated ROCE annualized at 18% in Q1 FY25, target 40% by end of five-year plan (FY25)
items.quote: And I would like to report that the consolidated ROCE based on Q1FY25 annualized basis is now sitting at 18%. While we have a bit to go towards 40%, we will surely make more progress on this number in coming quarters.

items.statement: Global light vehicle production flat YoY; India and China growth offset by Europe softness; industry forecasts flat or slight de-growth in FY25
items.quote: On the vehicle production side, I want to highlight that the light vehicle production remained largely flat on a year-on-year basis. Significant amounts of growth coming out of India and China is being offset by softness of demand in the developed markets, especially Europe.

items.statement: Copper prices inflated during quarter but now softening; logistics costs up significantly due to Red Sea crisis and Asian port congestion
items.quote: certain pockets of challenges still remain, such as commodities like copper remain inflated during the quarter and is now showing signs of softening. The logistic costs creeped up significantly due to the Red Sea crisis and congestion at the Asian ports, which resulted in longer lead times and hence higher inventories

items.statement: Net debt increased Rs 3,000 crore due to M&A closures and higher working capital from Red Sea crisis and volatile customer schedules; expected to normalize in H2 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, net debt increased by Rs. 3,000 crores. This is primarily attributed to the M&A closures and increased working capital requirements due to the Red Sea crisis and volatility in customer schedules. The increased working capital expected to normalize in the second half of FY 2025.

items.statement: All announced M&As closed (Yachiyo, Lumen, ADI Industries); acquired assets margin-accretive; synergies early days; new JV with Sojitz stake purchase (Rs 230-240 crore payout in Q2)
items.quote: All the M&As announced over the past many quarters have been successfully closed in SAMIL. And SAM IL is now a more diversified and robust platform of growth for all stakeholders. It is important to highlight that all acquired assets together have been margin-accretive. And as synergies start to unfold, things should improve even further.

items.statement: Revenue Rs 28,900 crore (+29% YoY), EBITDA Rs 2,785 crore (+44%), PAT Rs 994 crore (+65%) in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The Company reported quarterly revenues of approximately Rs. 28,900 crores, which is up 29% EBITDA of Rs. 2,785 crores, which is up 44%; and PAT of Rs. 994 crores, which is up 65% compared to the same quarter last year.

items.statement: 3CX10 diversification principle: no customer, country, or component >10% of business (except India); diversification helps overcome regional slowdowns
items.quote: I think the thing that Motherson is always focused on is 3CX10. No customer, no country, no component to be more than 10% of our business. I think obviously for the countryside, India is the largest one that crosses that threshold, but otherwise most of the other customers and the country that we are present in is much below that threshold.

items.statement: Board congratulated team on successful Q1; no management changes mentioned
items.quote: The board congratulated the team on a very successful quarter one. And as you will all agree, with a tough background, we have really done our best here and provided the best result possible with all the efforts of the teams.

items.statement: Management does not know if INR 4,000 crore FY25 revenue target will be met due to commodity inflation/deflation uncertainty
items.quote: The reason why we've stayed away from mentioning about INR 4,000 crores is -- the actual answer is, we don't know.

items.statement: Board authorized up to INR 50 crore investment in KNS Shoe Tech subsidiary via rights issue
items.quote: As a sign of our commitment towards the shoe business, the Board has authorized an investment up to INR50 crores in the wholly owned subsidiary, KNS Shoe Tec h by way of subscribing to the rights issue

items.statement: Baddi healthcare plant hit highest production in July 2024; most regulatory approvals received, exports resumed to UAE, Australia, Africa; Russian FDA approval pending ~1 year
items.quote: I'm pleased to inform you that the integration of health care and wellness plant in Baddi is progressing and has clocked the highest production in July '24, last month.

items.statement: North shoe factory integration expected to complete by Q2 FY25; South sports shoe line started, targeting full capacity by Q3 FY25
items.quote: Additionally, the integ ration of the North shoe factory is prog ressing, and we expect it to be completed by the next quarter. In the meantime, we have started operations in the new sports shoe line that are in the south and are confident of ramping them to the full capacity by

items.statement: Ice cream factory relocated from Kundli, Haryana to Nashik due to CWC Act permitting processing not manufacturing; production expected by March 2025
items.quote: the new ice cream factory that was being set up in n Kundli, Haryana has been transferred to Nashik due to certain operational issues, and this has led to some delay in the proje ct. Production is expected to commence by March '25, that is the next

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA grew 47% YoY but PBT only 23% due to higher depreciation and finance costs from Baddi and shoe businesses not fully ramped
items.quote: The continuing integration of Baddi factory and the shoe units which have led to the higher growth in our EBITDA numbers, a growth of 47%, then the PBT num bers, which is -- which was up only 23% in comparison since we were not able to complet ely absorb the additional depreciation and finance costs of these businesses

items.statement: Effective tax rate increased to ~25% from 20% last year; expected to remain ~25% going forward
items.quote: The effective tax rate is increased to around 25% as compared to 20% in last quarter -- l ast year. We believe that the effective tax rate will be around 25% hereon

items.statement: Seeing volume growth recovery but too early to judge if structural consumption revival or temporary election/base effect; cautiously optimistic
items.quote: It's a little early to judge whether this is a revival of the consumption demand, or a temporary dip caused by the elections and a base effect of the previous year. Suffice to say that we are cautiously optimistic about the future.

items.statement: Private label business remains very small vs large FMCG brands but customer count increased significantly; started supplying shoes to online/offline retailers
items.quote: However, the number of customers in private label has increased tremendously over the last few quarters, including a bunch of B2C brands and online as well as offline retailers.

items.statement: BIS norms for footwear implemented August 2024; domestic manufacturing capacity insufficient to meet demand, benefiting contract manufacturers like HFL
items.quote: August is the date from when BIS has been implemented. People have stocked up on their imports in view of this because we do not have the capacity as a country to actually fulfil the demand that th e shoes sector has in the country

items.statement: Baddi OTC pharma plant has anchor tenant covering 60-65% capacity; July 2024 highest production in ~2 years; Russian FDA approval for 1 of ~20 products pending
items.quote: From a volume perspective, I think we mentioned this earlier th at we have an anchor tenant agreement with our customer there, where nearly 60%, 65% of the capacity has been underwritten by our main

items.statement: Finance cost and depreciation ~INR 20 crore each in Q1 FY25; expected to be mostly steady state now
items.quote: Both the finance cost and the depreciation is INR20 crores, INR 20 crores for this quarter. And still we do the round of investment. This will be mostly steady-state now.

items.statement: Warrant proceeds of INR 70-75 crore still in FDs depressing ROE; capex deployment spread over next 12-18 months
items.quote: Even today, in spite of having deferred that money, we have INR 70 crores -- INR70 crores or INR75 crores laying in FDs which has actually depressed our ROE numbers for this quarter.

items.statement: Vanity Case Nasik operating asset merger application to be filed with SEBI/Stock Exchanges in September 2024; NCLT process expected to complete by September 2025
items.quote: We will file the application to SEBI and Stock Exchanges in the month of September. And we expect that NCLT process will take another year to complete. So, we are hoping by September '25, the entire process will be completed.

items.statement: Employee benefit expense increased majorly due to ~4,500 people added from shoe business acquisition; cost base to continue in coming quarters
items.quote: The employee benefit expense is increased majorly because of t he shoe business. As we have mentioned last -- I think in the last interaction of investor c all, we have told that we are taking around 4,500 people with the business

items.statement: Top line is complete pass-through of raw/packing material prices; bottom line should not be affected by inflation/deflation
items.quote: our top line is a complete pass-through especially as far as ra w materials and packing materials is concerned. So, from that perspective, if most of our prices go up, volume, even if the same volume will end up showing a higher turnover, it may not affect our bottom

items.statement: Q1 FY25 consolidated revenue INR 670.9 crore (+40.4% YoY), PBT INR 36.2 crore, PAT INR 27.2 crore (+16.5% YoY)
items.quote: We achieved the high est quarterly turnover on a consolidated basis at INR 670.9 crores, having grown at 40.4

items.statement: Existing shoe business capacities expected to reach steady state by Q4 FY25; management hopes to allocate more capital to expand footwear capacity by then
items.quote: I would say, at the end of Q4 is when our existing capaciti es will reach a steady-state performance. Having said that, given that we are extremely bull ish about this segment, I'm hoping that by Q4, we would have allocated some more capital to expand capacity in this segment

items.statement: Ice cream factory delay of 2 months not expected to materially impact FY25 revenue; bigger risk is commodity inflation/deflation impact on top line
items.quote: I frankly am not sure that it would make such a large bend or it will make such a circular difference for this financial year gi ven that now that ramp-up period will happen between March and April, definitely it will make a difference of 1 month, 1.5 or 2 months, but that's during the ramp-up phase

items.statement: No new customers expected at Baddi OTC pharma plant in FY25 due to 8-12 month regulatory gestation; any additions would be a bonus
items.quote: So I don't see us being able to sign on any new customers in th is financial year, and that's what we are building even in our numbers, that we do not expect any new customers to come in, in this financial

items.statement: EBITDA margin ~8% last 5 quarters driven by commodity deflation and higher-margin new businesses (shoes); deflation not yet seen as sustainable
items.quote: So, the deflation is still there. We are not seeing that it is sustainable yet. So, the margins are better because of deflation. And also the shoe business and the new businesses which we are in are better in terms of margins.

items.statement: Baddi plant resumed exports to UAE, Australia, Africa; Russian FDA approval for one high-value product pending ~1 year
items.quote: have received most of the regulatory approvals and have resumed exports to UAE, Australia, Africa and in addition to the dom estic business. The only appro val that is pending from the Russian FDA that is expected to take another year, thereby dela ying exports to Russia

items.statement: Warrant structure chosen to avoid ROE depression from undeployed capex funds; INR 70-75 crore currently in FDs
items.quote: The primary transactions was done in the form of warrants because we were not sure of being able to deploy the entire sum of money right away, and we didn't want our ROEs to be depressed in the meantime.

items.statement: Brownfield expansions at Hyderabad, Silvassa, Lucknow progressing well
items.quote: All the previously announced brownfield expansions at various sites, including Hyderabad, Silvassa, Lucknow are progressing quite well.

items.statement: Maintain FY25 pre-sales guidance of INR 2,000 crores
items.quote: We continue to maintain our guidance of INR 2,000 crores of pre-sales in FY '25.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 area booked 4.43 lakh sq ft valued at INR 235.32 crores
items.quote: Area booked was 4.43 lakh s square feet in first quarter of FY '25 vis -à-vis 10.60 lakhs square feet in the last quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 PAT negative INR 5.45 crores due to lower-margin deliveries and one-off costs
items.quote: PAT for Q1 FY '25 recorded a negative at INR 5.45 crores, vis-a-vis positive INR 10.87 crores in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Expect losses in Q2 FY25 due to lower deliveries; H2 FY25 expected healthy with full-year profit
items.quote: We anticipate reporting of losses in second quarter of the current year as well due to lower deliveries planned. However, second half of the current financial year is expected to be healthy in terms of deliveries, leading to reported profits for full year FY '25.

items.statement: HSIIDC land parcel launch slipped to Q1 FY26 due to approval delays
items.quote: Prem, we are a little off track. I think it will slip to the first quarter of the next financial year. We've been stuck in a bit of approval there. So I think it will go to the Q1 of next financial year i.e. FY'26.

items.statement: Input costs not down; land prices stabilizing after significant increases
items.quote: Sir, our input costs are not down but they have not increased substantially in the construction end. The thing that is there the input cost that had gone up the most was land. So for new projects that was becoming a little bit of a challenge and and is a little bit of a challenge right now. But I see land prices now stabilizing.

items.statement: Pivoting business development towards senior living as less cyclical segment
items.quote: Other piece is also that we are pivoting more and more towards senior living as a segment. I think more and more Business Development (BD) will happen in senior living.

items.statement: High end-user and repeat customer base leveraged through service and referrals
items.quote: We continue to do what we do. We service them well and hope for them to give us references. I think that's the basic thing we have been doing. Just continue to do the same.

items.statement: Launch pipeline: Amarah Phase 4, Malhar Phase 3, ONE44 Phase 2 in Q2; Swarang and Ekansh Phase 4 in Q3
items.quote: So this quarter, we are launching Ashiana Amarah Phase 4, Ashiana Malhar Phase 3 and ONE44 Phase 2. Next quarter, we hope to launch Ashiana Swarang as a new project completely and also Ashiana Ekansh Phase 4.

items.statement: Aspirational target to launch 84-85 lakh sq ft and sell 14 lakh sq ft unsold inventory over 5-6 years
items.quote: What we have if I exclude Milakpur, have about 84 - 85 lakhs square foot to launch, about 14 lakh s square foot to sell in unsold area today, operating some more 3 lakhs in a quarter in completed stock, and that's about a crore square foot. Aspirationally, we would like to complete this cycle in 5 financial years starting the first April of this year, i.e. FY'25 and outside can go to 6 financial y

items.statement: Amarah Phase 4 realization ~25% higher than Phase 3; willing to accept lower velocity for higher pricing
items.quote: The realization would be about 25% higher than phase 3 as well. Now with most of the projects sold out, we are gunning for higher realizations. We'll be willing to live with a little lower velocity as compared to previous phases and look to maximize pricing as we go forward in this project.

items.statement: Pre-tax operating cash flow INR 74.92 crores in Q1 FY25 vs INR 83.15 crores in Q1 FY24
items.quote: Further pre -tax operating cash flow recorded at INR 74.92 crores in the last quarter vis -a-vis INR 83.15 crores in Q1 FY '24, and INR 92.9 crores in Q4 FY '24.

items.statement: Comfortable taking slightly more leverage given INR 1,700 crores collectible from ongoing projects; will remain conservative vs peers
items.quote: The comfort on taking more debt is basically coming from the fact that we have about INR 1,700 crores to collect from ongoing projects itself. And only 35 lakh s square foot of construction to do, plus 14 lakhs square foot of unsold area in the launch pipeline itself only to sell. All of that gives us good visibility of cash flows over the next 3 years. Since we have good visibility of cash flows

items.statement: No QIP needed currently; comfortable with debt position

And because the sales have been quite robust, the community continues to be PBT and cash positive with the overall cash surplus of about INR 120 crores as of June '24.

items.statement: Noida Phase 2 launch delayed due to RERA rejection; appeal pending with appellate tribunal.
items.quote: This could lead to a delay in launch, but we have a healthy pipeline, and we are confident we will be able to mitigate the impact of this delay to realization.

items.statement: Employee cost increase due to annual increments, variable pay payout, new geography launches, AGEasy growth, and ESOP expense.
items.quote: So, if you are comparing from 31st March to 30th of June, there is an impact of the annual increments what we have given to employees and fortunately, our MOSs were above expectation for 31st March '24. And hence, there was a variable pay payout also.

items.statement: Care Home pricing varies by market; Bangalore pricing above Gurugram due to mature market and higher acceptability.
items.quote: The Bangalore pricing is a little above the Gurugram pricing. So, it depends on market to market, what we see as a good product market fit, we decide the pricing accordingly because Bangalore is a more mature market.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA loss contained at INR 21.5 crores in Q1 FY25 vs INR 16 crores loss in Q4 FY24; net worth INR 466 crores.
items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA loss has been contained in line with our expectations, it's a loss of about INR 21.5 crores versus a loss of INR 16 crores in Q4 FY '24, primarily on account of no inventory to sell the residences vertical.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 40,400 crore as of the call date
items.quote: With regard to your second query regarding the order book, the order book as of today, I am not giving as on 30th of June, it is slightly dated, as on today, the order book is 40,400 odd crores.

items.statement: Targeting revenue higher than previous year, numbers to be firmed up after Q2
items.quote: As far as the revenue for the current year is concerned, we are targeting may be some increase over next year, over previous year, still to firm up the numbers. As we move ahead, the clarity would be available may be after second quarter.

items.statement: Planning Rs 4,000-5,000 crore capex over next 4-5 years; Rs 800 crore already spent on land acquisition
items.quote: See currently, we are expecting an expenditure of INR 4,000 crores to INR 5,000 crores over the next four to five years. And recently incurred around INR800 crores in acquisition of land on long-term lease basis and settlement of our existing long-term lease.

items.statement: Current capacity handles 10 warships and 11 submarines; new graving docks will enable larger vessels and US Navy repair work
items.quote: Currently, we have like an installed capacity for handling 10 warships, capital warships and 11 submarines. Now, the facility which we are augmenting, infrastructure augmentation in two places. One is adjacent to our existing facility here in Dockyard as well as in Nhava yard. We are planning for bigger dry docks where we will be able to build as well as repair.

items.statement: Targeting three deliveries in FY25: one destroyer ahead of schedule, one frigate on schedule, sixth submarine
items.quote: As far as deliveries are concerned, yes, we are targeting three deliveries. One for destroyer, which we plan before the contractual delivery schedule. One frigate, which we are targeting to meet the delivery schedule, because this is the first frigate of the project

items.statement: FY26 deliveries: two frigates, one merchant vessel, one fast patrol vessel
items.quote: For '26, we are planning to deliver the third frigate. And then we have -- in case second is not happening this year, then second and third. In case second is not happening this financial year, in the financial year '25- '26, we will have to deliver two frigates. Then we have also one delivery in financial year '26 for the merchant ship. So, then there is also delivery of the fast patrol vessels.

items.statement: Nomination-basis contracts carry ~8% PBT margin; efficiencies and early delivery boost actual margins
items.quote: As far as our normal sustainable margins are concerned, these orders are on nomination basis, where the margins are around 8%. items.statement: Employee cost % of sales to decline as revenue grows; no substantial manpower increase planned
items.quote: As a percentage of sales in case the sales are going up, this percentage would come down because we do not intend to increase the manpower in a substantial manner.

items.statement: Navratna status grants higher board powers: capex decisions without ministry reference, JV/collaboration up to Rs 1,000 crore each
items.quote: company, it provides a significant advantage to the company as significantly higher powers are available with the board. Capex decisions can be taken without any kind of a restriction or without any reference to the ministry, which facilitates quicker decisions. With respect to joint ventures and collaborations also, compared to the,…as a non-Navratna company and a Navratna company, we can collabo

items.statement: Prioritizing capex/infrastructure over higher dividend payout; current yield low at market price
items.quote: In fact, we are looking for substantial capex and infrastructure augmentation. So I believe that also the growth of the company should be more important than distribution of profits by way of dividend. In any case, considering the share market price today, our dividend, the company declares, would be, in terms of percentage terms it would be a very paltry amount.

items.statement: Working capital profile stable for next 3 years based on current order book and payment terms
items.quote: Definitely dependent on the order profile and the customer profile and the payment terms. So as of now, I can only say with respect to the orders which are available in hand. We don't see any change in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Submarine business offers recurring refit revenue vs ships where Navy handles major refits internally
items.quote: So this gives the Company a continuous business cycle over a very long horizon. Which isn't case with respect to ship building. Major substantial refits with respect to ships they are handled by the Navy themselves. Because they have the dedicated naval dockyards.

items.statement: P75I AON value Rs 43,000 crore (2018); bid submitted, awaiting evaluation
items.quote: AON value as of 2018 is 43,000 crores. We have submitted our bid. As and when it is evaluated and discussed the numbers would be out and we will be declaring it to the market.

items.statement: Refit margins negotiated case-by-case; can be higher or lower than original construction margins
items.quote: Refits are negotiated prices. So this can have higher, this can have lower depending upon the assessment and negotiation at that point of time.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at 30-35% YoY with 22% EBITDA margin (+/-100 bps)
items.quote: Also, as guided earlier, we are still maintaining a 22% EBITDA margin for the year with plus-minus 100 basis points and with a revenue growth of 30-35% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue guided at INR 200+ crores with EBITDA margin 20% (+/-100 bps)
items.quote: We estimate that the highest ever revenues to be around INR 200 crores plus with an EBITDA margin of 20% plus -minus 100 basis points.

items.quote: We expect to execute around Rs.104 crores of orders in Q2 and INR323 crores for FY25 in this sector.

items.quote: Another positive sign is the cash flow from operations stood at INR 24 crores positive as compared to FY24 full year Rs 57.4 crores. The company will be achieving an improvement in cash flows by end of FY25 compared to FY24.

And the second half is also going to be very strong for MTAR based on the kind of work

items.statement: Average order-to-delivery timeline reduced 45% from ~4 days in FY21 to 2.2 days currently across 19,000 pincodes.
items.quote: So in FY '21, on average, our order to delivery timelines are close to four days. Today, we have reduced that drastically, whereby the average order to delivery time line on our platform across all 19,000 pincodes across the length and breadth of India is now 2.2 days. So a 45% red uction in our O2Ds in the past three years

items.statement: GMV grew 25% YoY in Q1 FY25 with Beauty at 28% and Fashion at 15%

items.statement: Overall gross margins improved 48 bps YoY; Fashion gross margins up 360 bps driven by higher marketing and servicing income
items.quote: So as we can see on an overall basis, our gross margins improved by 48 basis points Y-o-Y. While gross margins in BPC remained largely steady. Our fashion gross margins in Q1 improved by 360 basis points on a Y-o-Y basis, primarily driven by higher marketing and servicing income.

items.quote: So as we can see, whether it is in terms of fixed assets turnover ratio, which has improved from 9.1x last year to 10.3x in the first quarter this year.

items.quote: In the quarter 1 of FY25, if you were to analyze the GMV comes out at INR 55 crores.

items.quote: So what we have been driving for last, I think, 6 - 7 quarters is that a lot of our outer packaging, we are reusing recycling materials for the brand boxes. So that really reduces our cost quite a bit.

items.quote: The e-commerce business, yes, it does have some levers for us to improve the margins, but we already feel like it's operating in a very, very healthy EBITDA margin.
