items.statement: Coimbatore regional hub (~130 beds) project started, expected completion in 24 months
items.quote: The project work for the regional hub hospital in Coimbatore (~ 130 beds) has just started and is expected to complete in 24 months' time.

items.statement: Gurugram land parcels registered at sector 44 and 56, building sanction approvals submitted for sector 44
items.quote: We have registered the land parcels in G urugram at sector 44 and 56. For sector 44, we have submitted the drawings to HSVP for building sanction approvals. Further, for the sector 56, we will be submitting the drawings to HSVP in the coming week

items.statement: EBITDA margin 28.4% in Q1 FY25, matured hospitals operating leverage improves margins with revenue growth
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the first quarter amounted to INR 93.7 Crores marking a 6.9% growth compared to the same period last year with an EBITDA margin of 28.4%.

items.statement: New hospitals EBITDA breakeven at ~35% occupancy, Hyderabad within 12 months, Bangalore 12-15 months, Chennai 15-18 months
items.quote: Usually about 35% occupancy we break even. And a t a place like Bangalore, it will take about 12 to 15 months time. Chennai might take about 15 to 18 months

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue grew 15% to INR 330.2 crores, outpatient footfalls up 12%, inpatient admissions up 10%, deliveries up 10% YoY
items.quote: For the Q1 FY25, our re venue registered a growth of 15%, amounting to INR 330.2 crores. Similarly, our EBITDA increased by 7%, reaching to INR 93.7 crores, while the PAT was down by 4.2% to INR39.7 crores due to higher depreciation and finance

items.statement: Matured hospitals revenue growth 7-8% YoY in Q1, expected to accelerate to double digits in season
items.quote: On the matured units the revenue growth has been healthy. It has been at around 7% to 8% growth year-on-year basis and we expect this growth to go further up as we enter into the season.

items.statement: IVF program expanded to 11 centers, all commissioned with embryology services started, early footfalls impressive and organic
items.quote: Now we've got to about 11 total. Now I think all of them are commissioned, all the embryology services have started, the doctors have been recruited, the business plan is laid out. And I think whatever the early footfalls that we are seeing are pretty impres sive and are pretty organic

items.statement: New hospitals price attractively initially, insurance tie-ups take 6-9 months impacting ARPOB
items.quote: Generally, in a new hospital, people see how expensive it is. First thing is you don't want to get that in major name. So, you will definitely price it attractively in the beginning. Second important thing is, you may not have the insurance to solve those things.

items.statement: Outstanding from trust unchanged from March, expect INR 3-4 crores reduction as year progresses
items.quote: It remains same from the March what ever we have seen. It is same. So as the year progresses we expect that the INR3 crores to INR4 crores to further come down Alankar.

items.statement: Net cash position INR 518 crores as of June 30, 2024, confident to fund all planned capex through internal accruals without debt
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong with a net cash position of INR518 crores as of June 30, 2024 which will support our ongoing capital expenditure plans. Given our current cash flow and anticipated internal accruals in the coming years, we are confident in our ability to complete all planned capital expenditures through internal accruals without acquiring debt financing.

items.statement: AGM conducted July 30, 2024, all resolutions passed, dividend paid same day
items.quote: I am happy to share that we successfully conducted our AGM on July 30, 2024, with all the resolutions passed by the shareholders and the company has paid the dividend on the same day.

items.statement: Competition in Hyderabad not new, brand drives business not individuals, not impacted long-term
items.quote: Rainbow is very large and has strong forte. I mean, I don't think we will not be kind of impacted directly through the loss of clinical talent because the brand drives the business here and not individuals.

items.statement: Occupancy 42.4% overall, matured hospitals 50%, new hospitals 27.6% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our overall occupancy rate fo r the quarter was 42.4%, with the matured hospitals achieving 50% occupancy, and the new hospitals, including the recently commissioned hospitals, recording a 27.6% occupancy rate

items.statement: ARPP (average revenue per patient) grew 6-7% YoY and QoQ to INR 1,07,000
items.quote: If you see that, that has gone up. That shows that we are getting the high-end complex cases at our hospital. And that has gone up on year-on-year basis by 6% and quarter-on-quarter basis also. So, I think 1,07,000 is ARPP, which has gone up by 7%.

items.statement: Gurugram approvals delayed due to HSVP bureaucracy between Gurugram and Panchkula offices, land registered, permissions applied
items.quote: I think, it's just a phase of government nothing else, actually. W e know the CEO and despite knowing the CEO of HSVP , it still takes that much time becau se this how the systems work . Also, for Haryana, it has got two offices, one is in Gurugram and other is in Panchkula. Between these two offices it takes its own time

items.statement: Insurance tie-ups for new hospitals take 6-9 months, impacting patient inflows initially
items.quote: we will take at least ~ 6 months to get all the insurance s sorted out (when we start a hospital). So that's again, they're (Insurance Companies / TPAs) are not going to give you the insurance approval as soon as you start the hospital. It's always challenging.

items.statement: Pay mix 52% insurance, 48% cash; international business 2.9% of revenue (INR 9.4 crores) in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our pay mix continues to be robust and balanced with 52% of the revenue coming from the insurance segment and the remaining 48% from the cash patients. Additionally, our international business accounted for 2.9% of our total revenue for the first quarter amounting to INR 9.4 crores.

items.statement: Exploring acquisition opportunities philosophically aligned, optimistic about potential deals
items.quote: And als o, the opportunities we're looking at seriously are acquisitions, which we are quite optimistic about. If something comes which is philosophically aligned to us, we'll definitely go for it

items.statement: New hospitals recruit full-time doctors, medical teams need time to settle for organic growth
items.quote: These are organic businesses. These are not aggregation businesses like multi-specialties, like a lot of sales driven, those things. These services will take its own time because we do recruit doctors on a full-time basis.

items.statement: Launched Adult Vaccination Outreach Program (AVON) pilot with top 5 vaccine manufacturers covering Influenza, HPV, Pneumococcal, Shingles
items.quote: During the quarter, we have launched a pilot project, A dult Vaccination Outreach Program (AVON), with the top five vaccine manufacturing companies to cater to the immunization needs of the families. AVON initiative will cover vaccines inclu ding Influenza, HPV, Pneumococcal and Shingles

items.statement: Management guides for 18-20% top-line growth and 15-18% bottom-line growth for FY25, down from original 18-20% PAT guidance due to duty cut impact
items.quote: our guidance on 18%-20% growth on top line will continue, our guidance on 18%-20% growth on bottom line. Ideally, post the duty impact should be muted in the sense that there might be a rather than a growth of 18%-20%, we should look at a growth of 15%-18%

items.statement: Management targets 12.5-13% studded ratio for FY25, confident of reaching at least 12%
items.quote: We are sure that we will achieve the 12.5% to 13% this year. But surely, we will touch 12%.

items.statement: Management expects SSSG of 13-14% for FY25, contributing major portion of 18-20% total growth
items.quote: SSSG will be around 1 3% to 14%. When we say 18 to 20 b etween 13 to 14 SSSG. The major contribution anyway comes from the SSSG stores only

items.statement: Management guides gross margin of 14-15% and EBITDA margin of 7-8% for FY25, subject to customs duty impact
items.quote: We have said 14% 14.5% to 15% and EBITDA we have said 7% to 8%. And this is subject to this custom duty impact.

items.statement: Opened 6 stores in Q1 FY25 (4 COCO, 2 franchisee, including 1 in Dubai); targeting 18-20 stores for full year
items.quote: in that particular quarter, we added 6 stores, out of which 4 were company owned, company- operated, and 2 were franchisees. So that's what it was, we have been planning and aiming to open about 18 to 20 stores for the whole financial year

items.statement: Q1 retail sales grew 11% (standalone 9%), highest ever Q1 sales; SSSG 4% due to post-Akshaya Tritiya slowdown from elections, heatwaves, gold price volatility
items.quote: In terms of the retail sales, we have seen 11% growth, and the same store sales growth was about 4%.

items.statement: Post duty cut, footfalls and sales increased significantly in last 15 days; Q2 YTD growth tracking 25-30%, supporting 18-20% full-year guidance
items.quote: we are growing around 25% to 30% YTD, sorry, in the in the 2nd quarter, till the end of now, so that gives around 18% to 20% YTD growth

items.statement: Studded ratio fell to 9.6-9.7% in Q1 from 11.5% FY24 average due to weak diamond sales; diamond inventory Rs 450-500 crore out of Rs 2,593 crore total
items.quote: In Q1, the studded ratio, sir, came down. Last year, on an average, the studded ratio was about 11.5%. But in Q1, the studded ratio was around 9.6%~9.7%.

items.statement: Wedding jewellery contributes ~40-45% of sales; Q1 saw stronger wedding/high-ticket sales, weaker small-ticket items
items.quote: it's usually around 40% ~ 45% is what we assume the wedding jewellery share is.

items.statement: Opened first international store in Dubai targeting Indian diaspora and broader Middle East/Africa markets for handcrafted Calcutta jewellery; calibrated expansion approach
items.quote: out of that one store in Dubai. So that was also a journey that we began to establish ourselves, our brand, with a global presence, reaching out to customers, not only from the Indian diaspora

items.statement: Franchisee stores growing faster than COCO, indicating tier 3/4 demand recovery; franchisee SSSG improved significantly
items.quote: Higher growth is happening in the franchise e stores over the last year. So which clearly indicates that the tier three and tier four town demand is coming

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond pilot in 3-4 stores, not yet breakeven; FY25 contribution Rs 50-100 crore; seen as fashion/daily wear segment, not replacing natural diamonds for weddings
items.quote: in the current year, in 24 -25, when we talk about the Sennes segment, which consists of lab -grown perfume and the leather bags, the contribution is not likely to be more than Rs 100 crores

items.statement: FY28 revenue aspiration of Rs 2000 crore if roads and building segments expand
items.quote: And if we increase the building a little and increase the road, if we go to the highway, then it will be 2000 plus, very easily.

items.statement: Order book stands at over Rs 1800 crore unexecuted work
items.quote: Sir, in excess of 1800 crores unexecuted work is with us.

items.statement: Bid pipeline exceeds Rs 4000 crore with 10-15% expected conversion in 1-2 months
items.quote: The bid pipeline is more than Rs. 4000 crores, where we have participated and the maximum result should be within one to two months.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 24-26% considered sustainable for current and new projects including HAM roads
items.quote: Yes, sir, these are all projects with the same margins.

items.statement: Significant increase in water sector works expected from government entities post-budget
items.quote: I think there's going to be a significant increase in the water sector works that are going to come out of the government entities.

items.statement: Order book split 75% water segment, 25% other segments
items.quote: 75% water segment, 25% from other.

items.statement: Acquired manufacturing property in Fatehpur, UP for Rs 50-60 crore to use as bank collateral for BG facilities
items.quote: We have acquired a manufacturing entity in Fatehpur, UP. We have told in our board meeting that our plan is to shut down by December. Ultimately, we will use that property as collateral which we need for banking facilities.

items.statement: No long-term borrowings except minor vehicle loans; company operates debt-free
items.quote: I think there must be some misunderstanding because currently we do not have any long-term borrowings. Maybe there are one or two odd vehicle loans. Apart from that, there are no long-term borrowings.

items.statement: Trade receivables of Rs 250 crore at March end; Rs 125-150 crore collected in Q1 FY25
items.quote: It will be around Rs. 125-150 crores.

items.statement: Three-month payment cycle with 10-15% retention money; no payment delays as projects funded by World Bank, ADB or central government
items.quote: We are not facing any payment delay issues. The nature of the business is such that we almost 10% to 15% of the amount gets withheld by the department in shape of retention money that is released after commissioning of the project.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue expected at 30-40% of annual, H2 at 60-70% due to seasonality
items.quote: So I think it would be anywhere around for H1 it would be based on year-to-year 30% to 40% and for H2 it would be 60% to 70%.

items.statement: Permanent headcount 250-300 employees; salary cost clarification: Rs 23.78 crore total, Rs 13.76 crore to KMP, rest to other staff
items.quote: the salaries portion for the previous year was around 23.78 crores, out of which only 13.76 crores goes to KMP and the rest is for salaries to the other staff.

items.statement: Competitors include LC Infra, DR Agarwal, Infracon, Khilari Infrastructure, Mega Engineering, NCC, L&T, Shapoorji Pallonji; larger players less active lately
items.quote: If you were to consider players similar to our size, then I think there's a few companies based out of Gujarat, LC Infra, DR Agarwal, Infrac on. Then there are some companies in Mumbai, Khilari infrastructure is one of them. And then some companies based out of Andhra, Mega engineering, NCC and L&T, Shapoorji, Pallonji also used to participate in these kind of works, but lately we haven't been see

items.statement: Will not compromise margins for higher win rate; will increase tender participation instead
items.quote: No, sir, we will not compromise on the margin. But we will increase the number of tenders in which it participates. So the quantum of the order we will increase.

items.statement: Order book executable in 2-2.5 years
items.quote: Two years. It will be executed in two to two and a half years.

items.statement: Acquired 75% stake in Brijbihari Pulp & Paper for Rs 60 crore; 25% held by Chairman Ramveer Singh; transaction not yet completed, Rs 5-7 crore advance indicated
items.quote: We have considered it just now, that's why we have decided to acquire it. In that, maybe Rs. 5 crores-7 crores advance to be given, we have intimated it, that too has not gone.

items.statement: Executing Rs 325 crore government housing project for RBI in Mumbai under joint development model
items.quote: We are currently doing a project with the government in Mumbai. It is about 325 crores. We are developing housing colonies for RBI.

items.statement: Real estate joint development on fixed per sq ft rate with margins maintained at current levels
items.quote: Our rates will be fixed on per square foot basis which will be entered into a contract by us, keeping the margins constant as in our books right now.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations negative due to 15% retention money and 3-month payment cycle scaling with 30% revenue growth; expected to improve
items.quote: No, it will improve. It's still there. Till now, if we don't need money, we don't have any loan, that is how we are running the system.

items.statement: Group revenue growth guidance of 15-17% for FY25
items.quote: the previous year, we grew as a company, not service alone . I'm saying as an organization, as a group, we grew by 15% on the top line, which continues to be our guidance for this year.

items.statement: Service business revenue growth target of 20-25% for FY25
items.quote: Service business, we target to grow by approximately 20% to 25%, and that will be the guidance for the year also.

items.statement: Q1 volume flat YoY due to elections, heat waves and floods
items.quote: Q1 is always our weakest quarter, and this year there has been more impact on back of both the central elections and the macro-climatic factors like heat waves and floods that have happened across the regions that we ope rate in.

items.statement: EV two-wheeler slowdown due to Ather model transition; recovery expected from August
items.quote: Growth has been slowing fo r the past two quarters, primarily due to lower supplies from our two-wheeler supplier Ather and this is expected to turn around with their new model launch which has happened in the beginning of July and numbers shall start showing up in the later half of August and September.

items.statement: Q2 bookings nearly double July daily average ahead of Onam festival
items.quote: in the last four-five days, we are seeing that the bookings are almost double of what has been the July daily average.

items.statement: EBITDA fell 3.4% YoY to INR 52 cr; margin 4% due to weak service revenue
items.quote: EBITDA was INR 52 crores versus INR 53.8 crores in Q1 FY '24, a decrease of 3.4% Y-o-Y. EBITDA margin stands at 4% for Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Service revenue grew 4.5% YoY but volume flat; service drives EBITDA margin
items.quote: Total income from vehicle service and repair business stood at INR 217 crores, up 4.5% from INR 208 crores in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: New vehicle sales down 2% YoY to 9,676 units; revenue up 10.4% to INR 931 cr
items.quote: the company sold about 9,676 new vehicles versus 9,874 in similar quarter previous year, showing a 2% Y-o-Y degrowth. Total income from new vehicles sold was INR 931 crores, up by 10.4% from INR 843 crores in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Pre-owned sales down 9.3% YoY to 2,472 units; revenue down 7.2% to INR 85 cr
items.quote: the company sold about 2 ,472 pre-owned vehicles versus 2,724 in a similar quarter of the previous year, which shows a 9.3% Y -o-Y degrowth. Total income from pre-owned vehicles sold was INR 85 crores, which is down 7.2% from the INR 91 crores that we sold in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: EV revenue down 39.5% YoY to INR 13.6 cr; Ather down 41%, Piaggio down 72%
items.quote: EV revenue was INR 13.6 crores versus INR 22.4 crores in Q1 FY '24, a decrease of 39.5% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Added 3 sales outlets in Kerala and 1 in Tamil Nadu for Tata Motors division
items.quote: We added about three sales outlets and booking offices in Kerala, and one sales outlet and booking office in Tamil Nadu for our Tata Motors division.

items.statement: Seven new service centers added last year; another seven planned this year
items.quote: last year we have built about seven new service centers. And I mean, like I said, this year too, we have another seven centers coming up.

items.statement: JLR inventory robust for July and August with 30-35 promised vehicles
items.quote: as on June 30 th, we were carrying a robust inventory for the next entire July sales, and for July 30th also we had inventory for August with a promised order intake of probably approximately 35, 30 vehicles.

items.statement: Average selling price up across segments: PV +12.7%, Pre-owned +2.3%, Service +4.9%
items.quote: We have seen an uptrend in our average selling price, increased from INR 8,54,057 to INR 9,62,403.

items.statement: Honda ASP up 12% YoY; revenue up 8% despite 2% volume growth
items.quote: Honda ASP has gone up by 12%. So overall the revenue of Honda actually grew up by 8% in Q1 compared to previous year.
State-wise, Q1 FY '25 revenue breakup, Kerala is 60%, Tamil Nadu 26%, Karnataka 9%, and Maharashtra 5%.

items.statement: Maruti volume +1%, Honda -1%, JLR +40%; Tata CV +9%, Bharat Benz +28%
items.quote: In terms of Maruti per se, year on year we have grown by about 1% in terms of volume. In terms of Maruti, in Honda, it is about minus 1%. In JL R, we have a growth of about 40%. And in terms of commercial vehicles, there has been a 9% growth in Tata commercial vehicles and about 28% growth in Bharat Benz.

items.statement: Inventory normalization expected by end-August with Onam festival deliveries
items.quote: So, definitely the inventory levels will come down drastically from a week onwards.

items.statement: Total debt INR 420 cr as of 30 June 2024; INR 192 cr IPO proceeds repaid by 31 March
items.quote: The total debt on 30th June is about INR 420 crores.

items.statement: Working capital funding deployed INR 650 cr for inventory and debtors
items.quote: as the inventory levels have gone up, that was basically deployed for our inventory funding. So technically, you can say about INR 650 crores is our funding that has gone for inventory. Inventory and debtors, sorry, working capital.

items.statement: Two subsidiaries received double-notch credit rating upgrades: Popular Auto Works BBB- to BBB+, Prabal Motors BBB to A-
items.quote: Popular Auto Works Private Limited, got double notch credit rating upgradation from BBB - to BBB+. Whereas the other subsidiar y, Prabal Motors Private Limited, also got a double notch rating upgradation from BBB to A-.

items.statement: Appointed Chief Risk Officer (Jarly, Head Finance) effective 13 August 2024
items.quote: We are pleased t o announce the appointment of our Chief Risk Officer with effect from 13th August, that is yesterday. So Jarly, who is the Head Finance of our Pop ular Vehicles and Services division, has been given the additional responsibility of CRO.

items.statement: Piaggio EV three-wheeler volumes down 30-40% due to CNG competition; may exit if no improvement
items.quote: overall, EV volumes in three-wheelers have gone down by about 30 %-40% on the back of CNG and other alternate fuels being available. So that is the segment that we are watching. If Popular Vehicles and we see further drop or if we do not see any action happening on that front, then we will take a call on Piaggio at that point of time

items.statement: Won FADA Dealer Excellence Award 2024 (Big Dealer) and MSIL Platinum Band achievements
items.quote: Our Group has won the FADA Dealer Excellence Award for 2024 in the Big Dealer category and also our subsidiary, Popular Auto Dealers, has received the two topmost Platinum Band Achievements from MSIL.

items.statement: Annual EBITDA margin guidance of around 18% and PAT margin of 11-12%
items.quote: In the past also, we have given a guidance of 18% EBITDA and around 11% to 12% of PAT. And that's how historically our margin profile has been.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 25-30% year-on-year for next couple of years
items.quote: From the revenue perspective, we are definitely looking at around 25 to 30% increase year on year. That is what has happened in the last year as well. And we should be able to exceed that in the next couple of years as well.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs. 12,461 million with 91% domestic, 9% international; 95% heating equipment, 5% waste gas handling
items.quote: Our order book remains strong, standing at Rs. 12,461 million with a well-diversified composition. Geographically, 91% of our current order book is driven by the Indian customer requirement and 9% orders coming from the international markets. Product-wise, heating equipment amounts to 95% of our current order book and 5% from the waste gas handling equipments like flares and incinerators.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline: complete Rs. 1,246 crores to be executed in FY25 and FY26
items.quote: So, just to answer your question in short, the complete Rs. 1,246 crores order book should ideally get executed in this year and next year.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of roughly Rs. 4,000 crores with Rs. 1,000-1,500 crores domestic and Rs. 2,000-2,500 crores export
items.quote: So, basically, the bid pipeline roughly stands at something like Rs. 4,000 crore, wherein maybe about Rs. 1,000-1,500 crores is for domestic and Rs. 2,000-2,500 crores is for exports.

items.statement: Q1FY25 EBITDA margin 13.4% down from prior year due to lower revenue vs expenses, ESOP provision of Rs. 54.6 million, and revenue mix
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin has gone down as compared to the same period last year. This is mainly due to the increased operational cost as we scale up our business and invest in future growth. Also, the creation of ESOP reserves to the tune of Rs. 54.6 million for the employee benefit.

items.statement: ESOP provision of Rs. 5.46 crores in Q1FY25; similar provisions expected each quarter based on share price
items.quote: Yes, Sagar, this provision is made for this quarter and every quarter there will be a provision, and that provision corresponds to the market value at the end of the quarter.

items.statement: No additional capex needed for Reliance cracking furnace order; existing Mundra facility sufficient
items.quote: And we don't need any additional capex to execute this project. Whatever the existing facilities we have, that is sufficient. We might have to create some facilities at the site to execute the job.

items.statement: Mundra SEZ facility enables complete modular construction for export orders; logistics cost lower than site fabrication
items.quote: So, they prefer a complete modular construction which we do at our shop in Mundra. That was the basic purpose of having a large shop in Mundra at SEZ so that we are able to completely build them and ship them.

items.statement: No price escalation clauses; raw material ~10% of order value; critical materials procured immediately or back-to-back with suppliers
items.quote: Generally, we do not have the price escalation clause in the purchase orders, but what happens is that the raw material purchased by us from a percentage perspective is quite low. It is, not even maybe 10% of the order value.

items.statement: Secured significant new orders from Reliance Industries (cracking furnace) and Indian Oil Corporation (incinerator) in Q1FY25
items.quote: JNK India was also successful in securing significant new orders from industry leaders such as Reliance Industries and Indian Oil Corporation, and also for the new product lines.

items.statement: Order book end-user mix: petrochemicals 55%, refining 33%, steel 12%
items.quote: End-user-wise, the petrochemicals sector currently contributes almost 55% of our order book, followed by the refining at 33% and the steel at 12%.

items.statement: Export order book 9%; bid pipeline includes Rs. 2,000-2,500 crores export opportunities; first US order received in Q1FY25
items.quote: Geographically, 91% of our current order book is driven by the Indian customer requirement and 9% orders coming from the international markets.

items.statement: JNK Global partnership provides access to global vendor lists and inquiries; engineering and manufacturing done at JNK India Mundra facility
items.quote: So, automatically, they give the engineering and manufacturing opportunity to JNK India, and all the engineering and manufacturing is done from JNK India. So, that's how we benefit out of this collaboration.

items.statement: Revenue run rate historically: Q1+Q2 ~1/3 of annual, Q3+Q4 ~2/3 of annual
items.quote: Historically, what has been the case is whatever we had done in Q1 and Q2, almost double we have done in Q3 and Q4. That has been the historical trend.

items.statement: Developing capabilities in hydrogen, renewable energy systems, flares, and waste gas handling; first green hydrogen project commissioned at IOCL Faridabad
items.quote: We have already executed a green hydrogen project in IOCL Faridabad, so the hydrogen fuel station is ready. It is from basically CBG, from the compressed biogas to hydrogen.

items.statement: Order finalization delays possible for large capex projects (domestic and export); CPCL project may spill to FY26
items.quote: It might get spilled over as well, because they are now speaking of reviving the project. So, they'll have to start sending the inquiries again, and then, start getting the proposals and finalization.

items.statement: IPO raised Rs. 300 crores primary capital in April 2024; funds strengthening balance sheet for working capital and growth
items.quote: The past year has been particularly noteworthy for us, culminating in our IPO which has raised Rs. 300 crores in primary capital.

items.statement: IPO funds significantly strengthened balance sheet providing support for working capital and future growth
items.quote: From a capital structure perspective, the funds raised from our IPO have significantly strengthened our balance sheet, providing the support necessary for our working capital and future growth.

items.statement: Targets Rs 900-1,000 crore revenue in 3-4 years with parallel bottom-line growth
items.quote: That's the target. That's a very clear target, primarily. And more than the top line also, we are focused on making sure that we're able to get our bottom line also growing parallelly.

items.statement: Plans 11 new stores across three formats in FY25, on track for execution
items.quote: We are planning 11 stores this financial year. We are more or less on track for that.

items.statement: Adequate manufacturing capacity for B2B growth; only manpower additions needed
items.quote: Capacity as far as the missionary as well as the plant is concerned, there is no challenge. We'll need to probably only, include more manpower as we go forward.

items.statement: ~30,000 premium units (>Rs 3 cr) sold in top 5 cities over past 4 years, 85% delayed, handover expected from H2 FY25
items.quote: Broadly, our data shows that close to about 30,000 units have been sold above RS. 3 crores in the past four years, of which I think almost 85% of the projects have been delayed.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 gross margin 53.2% vs 56.5% in Q4 FY24 due to sea freight, airlift costs, forex, and one bulk sale at lower margin
items.quote: On gross margin, Q4, gross margins were 56.5% and current Q1 is about 53.2%. What really impacted was because of sea shipment, which is we import leather from sea, because of the sea freight going up and also the delays in arrivals of these shipments, we had to airlift a lot of leather or a lot of imported goods for our supply chain.

items.statement: Expects gross margin to return to ~56% range from Q2 FY25 via price hike, freight stabilization, localization, and operating efficiency
items.quote: What we believe is from Q2 onwards, we should come back to our 56% range I mean, you know, like all the scenarios and those one-time bulk sale that we had in Q1. Without that, we should go back broadly to our Q4 margins.

items.statement: Leather localization at ~30-33% currently; targets 75% in 18-24 months for ~20-22% overall cost savings
items.quote: Currently, around 30 %, 33% of our leather has been localized. My target is to get to a point of 75% localization in the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: KCD (kitchen) pilot in Bangalore: 150 projects booked, 100 executed; plans pan-India rollout in ~1.5 years
items.quote: While we have successfully launched our KCD in Bangalore only Bangalore last year in September and we have done the pilot marketing here, we are happy to say that we have taken close to about 150 projects and executed close to 100 projects in Bangalore.

items.statement: Stanley Level Next grew ~35% YoY in Q1; Stanley Boutique and Sofas & More flat to -5% due to renovations and format challenges
items.quote: Of all the three formats, Stanley Level Next has reported a growth of from Q1 to Q1 almost 35% and Stanley Boutique and Sofas and More have almost been flattish to negative to almost like negative 5% growth in other two segments.

items.statement: Mature Level Next stores (>2 yrs) show 20-25% SSSG driven by full-home solutions including kitchen/wardrobes; Boutique negative SSSG; Sofas & More 5-7% SSSG
items.quote: Stanley Level Next , which is my luxury format store this more than two years store format is showing an average growth of 20% to 25%. Again to understand here, this growth is coming in mainly because we have pivoted to a more complete home solution offering

items.statement: New homeowners drive 65-70% of B2C revenue; renovation significant only in mature markets like Mumbai
items.quote: As of now, we could say that depending on the market 65% to 70% comes from new home makers as far as our business is concerned.

items.statement: Added Steelcase as new B2B client; existing global clients face headwinds but exports continue to Europe, US, Middle East
items.quote: Having said that, yes, we have added a new customer in the form of Steelcase, which is an American company for their domestic manufacturing. We have signed up a contract with them.

items.statement: BIS certification for furniture imports expected to expand in 12-24 months; PLI scheme for manufacturers also progressing — both positive for organized players
items.quote: So, we believe that while this process of what you call as blocking free import has already started, it will definitely come into full play probably 12-24 months from now. The government also is working very clearly with the lobby of furniture manufacturers to give PLI to manufacturers.

items.statement: BIS certification currently for seating components; scope expected to expand to full furniture category
items.quote: So right now, they have implemented BIS certifications for some components which are used in seating solutions. Slowly they will, we are expecting what we understand is this should get the scope of this should get expanded and include furniture as a category also.

items.statement: Net cash Rs 199.5 cr post-IPO; IPO proceeds allocated to store expansion, renovation, backward integration (metal processing, leather sourcing)
items.quote: Regarding the IPO proceeds, we have strategically allocated the funds to expand our retail network, open new stores and renovate existing locations.

items.statement: Store maturity curve: Year 1 ~60%, Year 2 ~70-75%, Year 3 ~85%, Year 4 full maturity; cannibalization offset by market share gains
items.quote: The trend we have been observing is that the store usually gives us about 60% of business the first year, about 70%-75% the second year and about 85% the third year and then at fourth year we call it as a full matured store.

items.statement: Advertising spend reduced to 3.4% of revenue in Q1 due to subdued markets
items.quote: In fact, I think we have been restrictive and reduced our advertisement spend in Q1 considering that markets were fairly subdued and we didn't get initial response. So, I think we have ended up spending 3.4%

items.statement: Premium/luxury housing demand strong but delayed 18-24 months due to COVID and RERA extensions; elections temporarily slowed high-value purchases; traction picked up post-elections
items.quote: While premium and luxury housing has been witnessing tremendous demand, there has been an averag e 18 months to 24-month delay in handover of projects sold in the past 3 years to 4 years due to disruption caused over COVID years and RERA has extended the delivery deadlines to builders across the country

items.statement: Expects solid housing delivery from H2 FY25; strong pipeline for next 2 years
items.quote: So, we are expecting solid delivery to start happening perhaps by H2. And most of the projects that were delayed are now coming almost into completion stage. And we expect a very good housing handover to happen in H2, starting from H2 of this year. And there's a lot of pipeline for the next two years.

items.statement: Targets ~100 stores in 3-4 years (from 61 currently); cautious expansion due to real estate challenges and metro disruption risks
items.quote: So, in my mind, it is planned in such a way that we plan to get to about 100 stores in the next three to four years and a very meaningful growth without losing any stores for lack of business due to bad location.

items.statement: In-house manufacturing share: Level Next ~95%, Boutique ~85-90%, Sofas & More ~65%; targets full self-sufficiency in 12-18 months
items.quote: As of now, Level Next almost 95% of the furniture is fully made in -house. Perhaps only the lighting and certain accessories we are importing. Stanley Boutique almost 85 %-90% is fully made. And again, maybe 10%-15% is imported like carpets and accessories. Sofas & More, 65% is produced by us about 35% is imported and sold.

items.statement: B2C 78%, B2B 22% in Q1 FY25; expects 80:20 ratio to persist
items.quote: 78 and 22, that's been the trend for FY 24 as well. And as far as what we anticipate is both the segments will continue growth and will maintain a ratio of 80, 20 between B2C and B2B going forward.

items.statement: Store opening delays due to construction labour shortage; 3 mature stores relocated due to metro disruption and fire incident
items.quote: We encountered delays in opening of new stores due to non-availability of construction labour and we had to relocate three ma tured stores due to disruption caused by metro lines and a fire incident in one of the stores

items.statement: Revenue Rs 100.7 cr (+5% YoY), EBITDA Rs 20.1 cr (+25.6%, 20% margin), PAT Rs 3.8 cr (+8.6%) in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In Q1 FY25, I am pleased to report we delivered revenues of operations of RS. 100.7 crores, reflecting a 5% increase compared to the same period last year. Our EBITDA grew by 25.6% to RS. 20.1 crores achieving a margin of 20% and PAT increased to 8.6% to RS. 3.8 crores.

items.statement: Geographic revenue: South India ~83% of total; expects moderation as pan-India expansion progresses
items.quote: Geographically, our business in South India accounts for around 83% of our total revenue which will continue to moderate in the near term.

items.statement: Store format: 61 stores across 25 cities (37 COCO, 24 FOFO); anchor store pilot (all 3 formats) near Bangalore airport successful
items.quote: We currently operate 61 stores spread across 25 cities among all the three formats of which 37 are company-owned and company-operated and 24 are franchisee-owned and franchisee-operated.

items.statement: Production guidance of 50 million tons for FY25 maintained despite 1 million ton shortfall in Q1
items.quote: Number two, of course, we still keep a guidance of around 50 million tons. I know we are running about 1 million tons plus on shortfall as compared to last year because of 2 reasons.

items.statement: NSL monthly breakeven targeted by end of Q2 FY25, quarterly breakeven in Q3 FY25, annual breakeven in FY25
items.quote: Once the 5-kilometer electrification is done by the end of next month, we will be able to dispatch 2 rigs daily against the 1 rig currently and we label -- hopefully by the end of this current quarter in Q2. On a monthly basis, we'll be able to break even. Quarterly breakeven will come, of course, in Q3 and annual breakeven will come in this financial year.

items.statement: Capex spend of INR384-400 crores up to August against annual target of INR2,200 crores; expect to exceed target by substantial margin
items.quote: Up to August spend, we have spent around INR384 crores or almost INR400 crores in NMDC for against an annual target of around INR2,200 crores. So our capex is going on full stream and the two major projects that were basically, we were asked -- in fact, we decided to keep on hold and redraw the entire thing to our pellet plant and our beneficiation plant, we wanted to make common facilities so tha

items.statement: Slurry pipeline, beneficiation and pellet plant system expected operational by mid-calendar 2026
items.quote: For the entire system, it will get operational, I think the latest time is, I think it was December '25, just let me have a look or I think it is March -- around March '26 what we expect that all the three packages will be up and running. And the entire system will run around somewhere around mid-calendar year '26.

items.statement: Lump demand expected to decline to 20-25% of volumes in 5-7 years as larger blast furnaces increase pellet usage; expansion plans factor this shift
items.quote: Strategically, there are reports we have done some market survey for this. We expect that in 5 to 7 years especially around '31, '32 or maybe somewhere around '35 with the bigger blast furnaces coming in which has higher capacity of pellets, the lump demand itself might go down to around 20% to 22% or 25%. And we are in our expansion plan, we have factored that in. So we'll have to keep flexible f

items.statement: Average sales realization was INR5,304/t in Q1; expected to fall to ~INR4,304/t after two INR500/t price cuts, in line with market trends
items.quote: Our prices, we have taken 2 price cuts in the last 2 times. That's about INR500 and INR500, about a INR1,000, we have taken a price cut. And that is why our average sales realization which was Q1, it was around INR5,304. Now it should come down to around INR4,304 but that has been the general trend of the market.

items.statement: Pricing terms exclude all taxes and duties beyond royalty, DMF and annuity; any new levies recovered separately from customers
items.quote: Yes, it is excluding all the taxes and duties. Even now when we have the consolidated pricing it is inclusive of royalty, DMF and annuity and additional royalty. Any new taxes and duties are always in addition to that.

items.quote: So far as Chhattisgarh is concerned, we are already recovering it and -- from our customers and paying it. So there will be hardly any retrospective effect. There was some about INR144 crores old demand which we have paid in cash, but under -- if such a demand now fructifies in a related case remember this is not one of these 81 cases. Then if there is a judgment which is akin to this one, then ab

items.quote: About INR2,900 crores was due from the Monitoring Committee of which we have already received about INR1,000 crores, INR995 crores or INR993 crores last year which was there in the year before last. items.quote: This is a pre-demerger expenses at INR2,500 crores. items.statement: Royalty expense booked on production basis (not sales); Q1 royalty down 13% YoY matching 14% production decline

items.statement: Per-ton cost highly sensitive to production volumes due to 90% fixed cost structure; 1 million ton production drop increases per-ton cost by INR150-200
items.quote: Per ton cost you see this is a fixed cost industry. So if your production goes down, your per ton cost goes up, even if we have production for a unit goes down by 1 million tons, the per ton cost goes up by about more than INR150, INR200 simply because 90% of my cost is fixed cost and only 10% of my cost is variable cost.

items.statement: No provision made for potential Karnataka/Chhattisgarh liabilities as they are in parallel cases not covered by current SC judgment; recovery expected via 12 installments from existing customers
items.quote: No, not yet because as I have said, most of my 2 big cases at Chhattisgarh and Karnataka are not in one of these -- not in these 81 cases. They are related cases. Section 4 is already complete. Section 7 notification for Rohne has already come a

items.quote: Yes. So we lost some money in Panna. Paloncha is a non-working unit as we know that we have some fixed costs there, which we basically watch in award functions and other fixed costs. We lost some money in the pellet plant as well. But pellet plant, we are trying to give a new eye on that. So we lost around INR12 crores in pellet plant, in Panna, we lost about INR21 crores. And in the sponge iron,

items.statement: EC extension applications for 5-star mines under automatic route without public hearing; 4 mines recently received 5-star rating; approvals expected this financial year
items.quote: These are our 5-star mines will get automatic route which is without local hearing etc. We have applied for that, 3 of our mines are 5-star of our mines as you know, in fact, 4 of our mines are 5-star mines. It was recently given in the -- I think last week, we got the 5-star rating by the IBM in terms of the minister. So those things we would be getting done

items.statement: Management guides for FY25 exit EBITDA margin of 9% and remains confident of meeting revenue, EBITDA and PAT guidance for the year
items.quote: We are further marching towards FY25 exit at 9% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Order book stands at $475 million as of June 30, 2024 with robust pipeline particularly in data center solutions
items.quote: Our backlog stands steady at $475 million as of June 30, 2024, bolstered by a robust pipeline, particularly in data center solutions.

items.statement: INR410 crores equity raise via preferential warrants to fund data center expansion, network infrastructure advancement, innovation in cloud/cybersecurity/AI/IoT, and go-to-market expansion in North America and emerging markets
items.quote: We're excited to report a significant funding boost of INR410 crores to drive growth in key focus areas within the digital infrastructure sector.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA grew 28% YoY to INR115 crores with margins expanding 240 bps to 8.1% from 5.7% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: For quarter one FY25, EBITDA margins increased to 8.1%, which is a growth of 240 basis points year -on-year compared to EBITDA margins of 5.7% in quarter one of FY24.

items.statement: Revenue declined 9% YoY to INR1,423 crores due to strategic exit from low-value customers, delayed project execution, and muted demand from federal partners
items.quote: revenues for the quarter were lower by 9% year-on-year and stood at INR1,423 crores in quarter one of FY25. The top line is affected due to our strategic exit from low -value, non -accretive customers coupled with some delay in decision-making leading to delayed project execution and with muted demand for our product business from some federal partners during the quarter.

items.statement: Strategic exit from low-value long-tail customers; 90% of business from top 250-300 customers; focus on deepening relationships with Fortune 500 clients
items.quote: We have instituted a strategic program to assess our customer base. 90% of our business comes from top 250-odd customers who are large multinationals. We see a lot of scope in going deeper than going wider with a long tail.

items.statement: Data center solutions revenue was ~$175 million annually; Q1 FY25 estimated at $40-45 million
items.quote: this quarter it should be around $40 million or $45 million, but yes, we don't have the exact numbers but yes, it should be around $40 million , $45 million.

items.statement: Data center expansion focused on India and North America; serving hyperscalers like Meta, Amazon, Microsoft; India data center pipeline forecast to grow from 1,300 MW to 3,000+ MW
items.quote: So, I think we are looking at two specific geographies in that space and both are hyper India and North America. We do serve customers in the European market as well. Many of them are North American customers, but we see hyper growth in the data center, specifically in India where we are constructing our strategy and plan to be a significant player.

items.statement: Debt ~INR400 crores at SOFR+250bps; $100M AR securitization facility off-balance sheet; interest cost INR140 crores includes securitization cost; comfortable with debt levels but will reduce if no growth opportunities
items.quote: So on a INR400 crores we have the interest, which is basically in the range of SOFR plus 250 basis point. And then we have a $100 million of the AR securitization facility, which is an off -balance sheet non-recourse facility.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY25 significantly better than H1; Q2-Q4 revenue additions from focus accounts to exceed long-tail exits; confident of meeting full-year revenue, EBITDA and PAT guidance
items.quote: We expect our second half of the year to be significantly better than the first half. We are still guiding within our revenue guidance range for the year. We are confident of meeting our EBITDA and PAT norms for the year that we've had before.

items.statement: Hired seasoned sales and solution architects with industry-specific expertise; organized North America into 5 verticals and worldwide into 5 horizontals with leaders in place
items.quote: We have divided our North American business, which are largest businesses, into five verticals and worldwide into five horizontals. All the vertical leaders are in place. All the horizontal leaders are in place at this time.

items.statement: No significant inorganic acquisitions in past year (~$4M only); current focus on organic growth to $1.2-1.3B; inorganic opportunity-based for $2B target over 4 years
items.quote: We haven't done any inorganic in the past year or so. So, barring a small $4 million or so that we did, this is largely organic. Going forward, as you said, in two parts, we expect our current focus is on organic growth, double-digit taking us from a current $800 million kind of a run rate going to $1.2 billion to $1.3 billion.

items.statement: Project delays due to customer site readiness, third-party vendor supply issues, and macro uncertainty around Fed rates; expect improvement when Fed cuts rates (anticipated September)
items.quote: In our project business, it's important for us that the site is ready for our engineers to run the projects. So if there is a delay, there could be a mismatch of revenues in a certain quarter. It's not a standard trend, but it does happen once in a while. And we saw some dip of our revenues getting backlogged because we couldn't complete certain projects largely from a customer interest point of v

items.statement: Technology Products segment breakeven at $20M revenue; gross margins north of 40%; shifting focus to IP-led products (Black Box Emerald brand) with R&D in Ireland and Bangalore; expect TPS to be accretive to 9% EBITDA target
items.quote: Our business technology products breaks even at about $20 million. So every dollar outside of that is highly accretive. As we move forward, we plan to grow the business in this current year over 20-odd percent. So if you look at the current fiscal year, it will be equal accretive or more from our 9% guidance perspective that Deepak called out that will end the current year time.

items.statement: AR securitization facility of $100M funds working capital; cost ~INR70 crores included in interest expense; trade-off between debt reduction and deploying capital for growth at 8% cost
items.quote: Because basically our business is a -- we need a working capital to run the business. And for that working capital is funded through AR securitization. So the AR securitization facility cost goes into the interest rate.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY25 higher than H1 due to budget utilization patterns: India fiscal year-end (Jan-Mar) and US calendar year-end (Q3) drive capital-intensive project execution
items.quote: So I think from our perspective, we expect that H2 to be higher than H1. There is an element of seasonality to an extent that there is a budget and a fiscal year norm. In India largely, the fiscal year ends in March. So, therefore, if you have an India-specific business, people want to utilize their budget in the Jan, Feb, March period, specifically if they're doing capital -intensive work.

items.statement: Gradually increasing prices to low-end customers or exiting if no value seen; focus on profitable growth with top customers
items.quote: And we made a call saying we'll focus on our top customers to go deeper because their ability to spend is very, very high. A nd to that extent, we have been gradually increasing prices to our low end customers or exiting if we don't see value

items.quote: We just expanded the R&D in Bangalore. We expect the percentage of own IP products to increase significantly quarter after quarter going forward and therefore be accretive for us as we grow that business as well.

So when you say about the market dynamics, it's not a particular customer, which we continue to serve Facebook, we expect large orders from them over the next couple of months.

items.statement: Average project execution ~9 months; order book mix of projects (6-18 months), annuity contracts (1 year), product sales (point of sale), services (P&L basis); target order book 25% above revenue plan; expect to consume 60-70% of current $4
items.quote: Our average project size are nine months. Some of them are six months, some of them are 18 months, some of them could be longer. So the average size of our projects is about nine months. We do have annu ity contracts that last for a year. We do also serve a lot of customers on demand that are practically revenue at the point of sale

items.statement: India data center market at 1,300 MW currently, forecast to double to 3,000+ MW; per MW build-out cost nearly half of US due to lower labor costs; global players driving demand
items.quote: I think over the last couple of months, I think the total number of projects in India on the ground for data centers specifically was about 1,300 megawatts. It is now forecasted to double, more than double to 3,000 megawatts.

items.statement: INR410 crores raised via preferential warrants to existing promoters, marquee investors, and KMPs; wide participation; capital to be deployed prudently for growth and return on capital employed
items.quote: As Sanjeev mentioned, we have secured INR410 crores equity raise earlier in this month in the form of issuance of preferential warrants to existing promoters, marquee investors, and KMPs. We have seen wide participation and interest from various investors.

items.statement: PAT grew 55% YoY to INR37 crores; PAT margin 2.6% (+110 bps YoY); exceptional items INR15 crores from severance costs; EPS INR2.21 vs INR1.43
items.quote: Coming to profit after tax, we have reported a robust 55% growth year-on-year at INR37 crores as compared to INR 24 crores for quarter 1 FY24. PAT margins stood at 2.6%, growth of 110 basis points year -on-year.

items.statement: Organic growth target: double-digit growth to reach $1.2-1.3B from current ~$800M run rate; $2B target over 4 years includes inorganic element; investments in go-to-market, vertical/horizontal structure, high-value business developers
items.quote: We are currently at a range of $800-odd million. We are expecting organically to take this business to $1.2 billion, $1.3 billion with a double-digit growth going forward for the next several years. And yes, we will be looking at, to be able to go to 2 billion, we will have to look at inorganic growth.

items.statement: Agnostic to industry verticals; well-positioned for digital infrastructure decade with data center build-out, semiconductor, AI-led infrastructure; some headwinds in banking, federal sectors
items.quote: We are agnostic to industry. We are, of course, lucky from that perspective that this is a digital infrastructure decade. There are a lot of data centers getting built. And therefore, we have taken a call to make significant investments. Some investments take time. These are large customers. The selling cycle sometimes are 6 months, 9 months. But once you're in, you're in for a long haul.

items.statement: Management reiterates guidance to retain high single-digit profitability margins in UCP segment
items.quote: whatever we have always been giving guidance that we will retain - the high single-digit profitability % which we have been ensuring all along. And our endeavour going forward also will be to retain that high single-digit profitability.

items.statement: Management maintains guidance of high single-digit profit margins overall
items.quote: We maintain our guidance or indication of overall single-digit -- high single-digit profitable margins -- profit margins. And that kind of remain.

items.quote: Our quarter 4 FY '24 growth story continued in quarter 1 FY '25 with a whopping 67% volume growth in Unitary Cooling Products, as compared to the corresponding previous quarter.

items.quote: Like RAC and CR, the performance of the air cooler vertical added extra flavo ur to the milestones of the company in the current quarter with a staggering 170% volume growth over corresponding previous quarter.

items.statement: CAC margins moderated due to lower retrofit job margins but expected to improve in coming months
items.quote: Unlike product sales in the current quarter, margins from retrofit jobs were lower, which moderated the overall EBIT performance for the vertical for the quarter. This, however, will improve over the next few months.

items.statement: Domestic Projects order book stands at Rs 4,769 crores; International Projects order book at Rs 2,734 crores; total segment order book Rs 7,503 crores as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: the quarter. The car ry forward order book for international business as of 30 June 2024 stood at Rs 2,734 crores, largely in UAE and Saudi Arabia region. The total carry forward order book of the segment stood at INR7,503 crores as of 30 June 2024

items.statement: Domestic Projects order booking subdued due to elections; pickup expected in H2 FY25

items.statement: Earmarked Rs 800-1,000 crores capex for factories; ramping up production and investing in plant and machinery
items.quote: Each, we have earmarked large sums of capex, almost Rs 800 crores to Rs 1,000 crores which we have earmarked for our factories. All the factories are going in the full swing. We're ramping up production. We are investing into plant and machinery.

items.statement: Chennai RAC factory (1 million capacity) and Waghodia water dispenser line (3.5 lakh capacity) started commercial operations
items.quote: we have started commercial operations in our RAC factory in Chennai, with a capacity of 1 million and water dispenser line with a capacity of around 3.5 lakhs in Waghodia.

items.statement: Chennai plant production commenced in current month after receiving commercial license
items.quote: Yes, Chennai plant is fully ready to start production. Production has begun in this month. We were waiting for the commercial certificate or licensing to be approved by the government, which we've received. So production has commenced.

items.statement: Premium 5-star AC sales mix improved; strong demand for advanced features and energy savings
items.quote: Strong demand for premium category of products, i.e. 5-star rated products, continued. And overall sales mix for these products has also improved for Voltas.
