items.statement: 10 acquisitions announced in CY2024 contributing Rs 830 cr revenue; 5 closed (Rs 315 cr), 4 expected to close in Q2 FY25 (Rs 433 cr), 1 may spill to Q3 (Rs 82 cr)
items.quote: Till date in calendar year 2024, we have announced 10 acquisitions contributing Rs. 830 crores in revenue, of which 5 acquisitions generating Rs. 315 crores in revenue have already been closed. The remaining acquisition of 4 entities contributing Rs. 433 crores in revenue are expected to close in quarter 2 FY '25, while the closing of one acquisition with revenue of Rs. 82 crores might spill over

items.statement: Acquisitions split: 31% consolidation in existing geographies, 32% new geographies, 37% new product portfolio
items.quote: So far, the 10 acquisitions announced strategically cater to three objectives, consolidation in existing geographies, which is representing 31% of revenue acquisition, adoption of new or addition of new geographies, which is 32% and new product portfolio, which is 37%.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin of announced acquisitions expected at 6-8%
items.quote: These acquisitions are margin-accretive with a blended EBITDA margin in the range of 6% to 8%, which would further enhance our profitability.

items.statement: Acquisition valuations at mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA multiples (5-8x)
items.quote: If you have to take a number, as we told you, that in mid-to-high single-digit is what we are paying. So, you can take it between 5 to 8 times of EBITDA multiples.

items.statement: Net investment value of Rs 350 cr for 830 cr revenue acquisitions; 77% equity ownership, 100% revenue ownership
items.quote: Yes, this is including what we have paid and what we will paying. CV Ram: Yes, upon closing

items.statement: Call options to acquire remaining stake at predetermined valuations over 1-3 years
items.quote: No, so for all the remaining stake, we always have a call option. So, it is up to us. We have a time frame to exercise the call option. Sometimes it is for part of the stake it is after one year, part of the stake it is after 3 years, right.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 gross margin 9.1% vs 8.8% YoY (+27 bps) driven by procurement efficiencies and product mix
items.quote: We recorded a gross profit of 9.1% in Q1 FY '25 vis-à-vis 8.8% last year, an improvement of 27 basis points. As Prabhat mentioned, this is primarily driven by gross margin expansion, driven by procurement efficiencies and an optimized product mix.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 2.8% (Rs 30 cr) moderated by acquisition-related one-time costs and HR investments
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at 30 crores with a growth of 17% on year-on-year basis. EBITDA margin stood at 2.8%. We have initiated and undertaken several acquisitions in Q1 FY '25. However, these acquisitions come with associated costs, particularly few one-time expenses, including due diligence expenses.

items.statement: Pro forma EBITDA margin 3.5% and ROCE 14% after full integration of announced acquisitions (excluding organic improvements)
items.quote: With the contributions from recent acquisitions on pro forma basis, EBITDA margin to improve from 2.8% to 3.5% and ROCE to improve from 9.2% to 14%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 consolidated revenue Rs 1,097 cr, up 22% YoY vs Indian Pharma Market growth of 9%
items.quote: We have once again delivered industry leading growth with consolidated revenues of Rs. 1,097 crores representing a 22% year-on-year increase from Rs. 899 crores in quarter 1 FY '24. This growth is significantly higher than the Indian Pharmaceutical Market growth rate of 9% during the same period.

items.statement: Organic revenue growth 16% YoY in Q1 FY25 (2x industry growth target)
items.quote: See, we have always maintained this kind of a guidance that we are targeting to grow 2x of the industry growth rate, right. So, this quarter, the industry grew by 9%, right. And we grew by 16

items.statement: IPO proceeds of Rs 1,000 cr sufficient for 2-3 years of acquisitions; internal accruals to fund marginal acquisitions thereafter
items.quote: So, we have raised 1,000 crores through IPO, right. That is sufficient for us for next 2, 3 years acquisition targets, right? Beyond that the company will start generating enough internal accruals to do marginal acquisitions.

items.statement: Peerless Biotech acquisition adds medical devices and diagnostic equipment/consumables portfolio
items.quote: With the acquisition of Peerless Biotech, we have also expanded our product portfolio into synergistic product segments like medical devices and diagnostic equipments and consumables.

items.statement: SKU coverage at ~65,000 across India (pharma market has 150,000+ SKUs)
items.quote: See, now we are doing almost 65,000 SKUs. In India, more than 150,000 SKUs are available in pharma alone, right.

items.statement: Retail customer base ~86,000+ annually (~10% of India's retail customer base)
items.quote: On an annual basis, if you look at last year, we had around 86,000 plus retail customers. That's almost 10% of India's customer base.

items.statement: Employee cost increased to Rs 43 cr in Q1 FY25 from Rs 37 cr QoQ due to inorganic acquisitions and annual salary increments
items.quote: Yes, it includes inorganic acquisitions and also if you are comparing with last year, sorry, previous quarter, then there is, in the first quarter, there will be salary cost increments also in the Q1.

items.statement: No plans to raise capital for next 2-3 years; IPO proceeds sufficient for acquisition targets
items.quote: We don't see any reason to hit the capital markets again in next 2, 3 years' time frame.

items.statement: Organic cash flows expected to turn positive from FY26 onwards
items.quote: Yes, definitely, I think by next year, organics should start delivering positive cash flows, organic division from FY '26 onwards.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue growth guidance of 30% on FY24 base of INR850 crores
items.quote: The overall guidance that we had given was that we will grow from about INR850-odd crores that we did for the full fiscal '24 by 30%. So, that guidance continues to remain.

items.statement: FY25 seat addition guidance of 40,000 seats to reach 135,000 total seats
items.quote: We had, last earnings call, we had given a capacity addition of 40,000 seats. We had ended the year at 95,000 seats. We are looking to add about 40,000 additional to reach 1,35,000 seats total.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin improvement guidance of 1.5 percentage points maintained
items.quote: That said, we stick to our guidance of 1.5% for the year because we will keep on adding new centers and cities to our portfolio. And hence, there could be a short-term impact. But however, we continue with our guidance of 1.5% for the year as a whole.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance similar to FY24 at around INR142 crores
items.quote: We had given a similar guidance on the capex as was last year. So last year was around in INR142 crores. We gave a similar guidance on the capex for current year.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex cash outflow of INR35 crores
items.quote: On the capex side, we have done an operating cash outflow of around INR35 crores on the capex.

items.statement: Operational seats reached 100,398 across 169 centers as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: As of June 30, 2024, our total operational seats stand at 100,398 and we have 169 operational centers.

items.statement: Pipeline of 11,640 seats under fit-out and 15,688 seats under LOI for total visibility of 127,726 seats
items.quote: Currently, we have 11,640 seats under fit-out and letter of intent in place for 15,688 additional seats, providing us with strong visibility on achieving our growth targets.

items.statement: Construction and fit-out segment revenue grew 55% YoY to INR67 crores with healthy order pipeline
items.quote: Our construction and fit-out projects, which encompasses our design and build business, have shown remarkable performance with a growth rate of 55%, culminating in a revenue of INR67 crores. This segment is gaining significant traction, buoyed by a healthy order pipe line and favourable market outlook

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin improved 1.8% QoQ to 30.7% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: As you can see, our EBITDA margin has improved from 28.9% to around 30.7%, which in itself is a 1.8% improvement quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: IGAAP equivalent EBITDA margin at 11.5% in Q1 FY25, up 249% YoY
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA on IGAAP Equivalent basis stood at INR30 crores, which is showing a robust growth of 249% year-on-year. Our margins are at 11.5%.

items.statement: Construction and fit-out gross margin improved to 16% from 15.5%
items.quote: In fact, we have slightly improved our margins on construction business at the gross level. So it was around 15.5%, and now has increased to 16% and thereabouts.

items.statement: New seats sold at 3-5% YoY escalation; existing portfolio sees 3-8% annual escalation based on cohort size
items.quote: The new seats which are being sold are being sold at 3% to 5% year-on-year escalation as compared to the earlier seats. Similarly, what we see is annual escalation, which in our case ranges from about - on average about 5% for smaller cohorts between 5% to 8% and for larger cohorts between 3% to 5%.

items.statement: Signed demand contracts for 11,000 new seats in Q1 FY25, exceeding supply additions
items.quote: On the demand side, we signed demand contracts for 11,000 new seats in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Exit month blended occupancy at 71%; mature centers (>12 months) at 84% occupancy
items.quote: Our exit month occupancy rate was 71%, indicating strong demand for flexible workspaces, aligned with our supply additions. It is important to note that this is a blended occupancy level. Occupancy typically increases as new centers mature. For centers older than 12 months, the occupancy rate stands at 84%.

items.statement: Client base: 65% large corporates/MNCs, 22% SMEs, 13% startups; 36% multi-center clients; 56% revenue from 100+ seat cohorts
items.quote: In terms of occupied seats, approximately 65% of our client base consists of large corporates or MNCs, 22% are SMEs, 13% are startups and the remainder are freelancers. In our portfolio, we have 36% multi -centre clients. The contribution of 100 -plus seat c ohorts to our total cohort remains robust at 56

items.statement: Average client tenure 34 months with 24-month lock-in; 100+ seat cohorts average 46 months tenure with 36-month lock-in
items.quote: The total average client tenure in our portfolio is 34 months, with a lock-in period of 24 months. For greater than 100-seat cohorts, the average tenure is 46 months, with a lock-in tenure of 34 months.

items.statement: Gross debt INR30 crores, debt-to-equity 0.08, net debt-to-equity negative 0.41 as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: As of 30th June, our liquidity position stood at a very comfortable INR185 crores. The gross debt at consolidated level stood at INR30 crores. As a result, our debt-to-equity is INR0.08, which was INR0.20 in Q1 of FY '24. And our net debt-to-equity stood at negative INR0.41, which was negative INR0.13 in Q1 of last fiscal.

items.statement: ROCE improved from 43% in FY24 to 68% annualised in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our ROCE has improved from 43% in FY'24 to 68% (on an annualised basis) for Q1 of the current financial year.

items.statement: Managed aggregation model at 67% of seats; target 65-68% MA vs SL mix for FY25
items.quote: Out of the new seats added or under-fit out, 79% were under our asset-light managed aggregation model, reinforcing our commitment to this effective business model. We continue to maintain a strong portfolio of 67% seats under this risk-averse model.

items.statement: Differentiated strategy focusing on sub-500 seat cohorts (30-54% CAGR 2020-22) with mid-size centers creating operational moat
items.quote: According to a CBRE report, the demand for flexible workspaces across these sub-500 seat cohorts, which is 1 to 50, 51 to 100 and 100 to 500 seats had been growing consistently with a CAGR of almost about 30%, 41% and 54% between 2020 and 2022. Why we get excited about this cohort is because this cohort helps us with better price realization. Then we are able to manage it's a manageable churn and

items.statement: New seat additions (20,000 in last 6 months) temporarily impact profitability until seats mature and fill up
items.quote: We have added around 20,000 seats in the last six months. The seats typically get filled up over a period. So we are seeing some impact maybe in the current quarter. And as I mentioned in my opening remarks that it has to be seen over a longer period. The quarter may not reflect the numbers.

items.statement: Focus on leadership and talent development through learning and development initiatives
items.quote: Some other exciting things on the anvil for Awfis include a more enhanced user experience incenters and online with mobile app and website revamp, more focus on leadership and talent development through learning and development initiatives.

items.statement: Targets double-digit volume growth for FY25 with Mass Premium at mid-to-high single digit and P&A at mid-double digit
items.quote: Our outlook for a double-digit growth for the Financial Year FY25, we are of the view that we are on the right track.

items.statement: Expects to exit FY25 with EBITDA margin better than Q1's 10%, targeting early double digits
items.quote: Our outlook is that we should exit the year better than the Q1 EBITDA, maybe early double digits.

items.statement: Maintenance CAPEX guided at Rs 15 crore annually for Telangana distillery; growth CAPEX of ~Rs 450 crore for two 150 KLPD distilleries to achieve near 100% captive ENA
items.quote: Our CAPEX guidance is largely in form of our strategy CAPEX for our distillery in the state of Telangana which is about 15 crores on annualized basis.

items.statement: Backward integration CAPEX of ~Rs 450 crore for two 150 KLPD distilleries expected to yield 450 bps gross margin improvement; benefits likely from FY27
items.quote: The capital required for this is we believe that what we need are two distillers of 150 KLPD each and the capital required for this will be roughly Rs. 450 crores.

items.statement: ICONiQ White annual run rate at ~4 million cases in Q1 FY25, up from 2.3 million cases in FY24; expects to double FY24 volume
items.quote: Currently the annual run rate for ICONiQ White is between 4 to 5 million cases and is expected to double its volume from last year's base of 2.3 million cases.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 10% vs 6.5% in Q1 FY24; gross margin improved to 38.7% from 34.5% YoY driven by packaging savings and price hikes
items.quote: We also delivered a double-digit EBITDA margin at 10% in Q1 FY25 as compared to 6.5% EBITDA margin in Q1 of FY24.

items.statement: Gross margin expansion in Q1 FY25: ~3.1% from price increases, ~1% from COGS savings after netting incremental costs
items.quote: It's around 3.1% on the price and around (+1%) on the overall COGS after netting off the incremental cost.

items.statement: Annualized price hike benefit ~Rs 40 crore; Q1 FY25 benefit Rs 18-20 crore vs Q1 FY24; further hikes expected in Telangana, West Bengal, Himachal
items.quote: The total aggregate price increase on an annualized basis, Ramki can I leave on you if my number is off, but I think it's just about Rs. 40 crores on an annualized basis.

items.statement: ENA prices range-bound at Q4 FY24 exit levels, marginally lower; 30% captive from 60M LTR Telangana distillery at 100% utilisation; need 300 KLPD more for ~100% captive
items.quote: As we shared earlier , our outlook was that the ENA prices for FY25 would be range bound. This is the exit price of Q 4 of FY24 which is the last Financial Year and so far, the prices are holding on to that level, maybe marginally lower

items.statement: Packaging savings: mono-carton removal on Sterling B7, OC Blue, ICONiQ; PET conversion on Officer's Choice in 6 states; market bottle utilisation target 20% vs 12-13% last year; glass/PET light-weighting
items.quote: We are this year planning our market bottle utilization at about 20% which was about 12%-13% last year. So, that's about a 7% increase in our market bottle utilization.

items.statement: P&A volume salience rose to 36.9% in Q1 FY25 from 33.5% in Q1 FY24; value salience rose to 46.1% from 43.2%
items.quote: Our P &A volume salien ce has increased to 36.9% in Q1 of FY25 as compared to 33.5% in Q1 of FY24. That is an increase of roughly 3.5% and the value salience has increased to 46 .1% in Q1 of FY25 as compared to 43.2% in Q1 of FY24

items.statement: Q1 FY25 industry growth ~2-3%; early signs of recovery in July; rural consumption improving with normal monsoon; Mass Premium segment saw low single-digit degrowth
items.quote: The overall industry growth was about 2% or 3%. We are seeing some sign of recovery in early July. So, that's a good sign for us.

items.statement: Telangana overdue receivables ~Rs 384 crore as of June 30; expect resolution over next quarter with improvement from September; working capital access improved post-IPO
items.quote: The total receivables from Telangana outstanding as on 30th June is around Rs. 384 crores which is overdue.

items.statement: Repaid ~Rs 800 crore gross debt from IPO proceeds; zero long-term debt; fresh working capital debt of Rs 325 crore at 8.5% vs prior 10-10.5%; annual interest cost to fall ~50%
items.quote: We repaid around Rs. 800 crores of gross debt which was there from the IPO proceeds. As on date we have around Rs. 325 crores of working capital debt which is a fresh debt after repayment of all the debt.

items.statement: IPO completed July 2024; proceeds used to repay Rs 720 crore bank debt and clear all VAT overdues; now raising low-cost working capital facilities for growth
items.quote: With the successful completion of the IPO process in July '24 in line with the main purpose of use of the IPO proceed being repayment of debt amounting to Rs. 720 crores. Accordingly, all the bank debt has been repaid.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh new excise policy expected Oct 1; includes retail privatization and national brand entry, enabling ICONiQ launch; currently ~1.9M cases sold in AP
items.quote: Andhra Pradesh policies yet to be out . A s and when it is announced it will be effective 1 st October. But from what we understand there are three important elements of the policy. The first element is privatization of retail which is a positive for a Company like ABD

items.statement: India-UK FTA still under discussion; no firm timeline; closure would significantly reduce bulk scotch cost as India's largest user after Pernod and Diageo
items.quote: India-UK FTA is still at a discussion stage. Of course, the new prime minister of UK has made a positive statement about the FTA but timelines are not yet formed.

items.statement: Launched Zoya luxury gin in Maharashtra (Mumbai, Thane, Pune, Nashik, Nagpur); ICONiQ White expanded to Madhya Pradesh, Meghalaya, Chandigarh and paramilitary channel; launched 180ml PET Hippy pack in UP, Maharashtra, Daman
items.quote: We successfully launched Zoya ABD's first luxury gin and the inaugural product in our Prem brand portfolio which focuses only on the premium and the luxury portfolio in the state of Maharashtra.

items.statement: Partnership model (not distribution) for premium/luxury brands with global companies; seeking partners with serious India intent, pan-India distribution access, and co-investment in brand building
items.quote: We have maintained a position that we are looking for a partnership model and not a distribution model. In the partnership model we are looking at global companies which have serious intent about India as a territory.

items.statement: Increased employee cost due to new hiring for premium/luxury vertical (Prem brand division) and general overhead increases
items.quote: Controlled advertising and marketing A&P spend which was largely offset by increased employee cost on account of new hiring mainly on account of setting up the vertical catering to our premium brand, focused on premium and luxury portfolio.

items.statement: Adopted new 25% tax regime; effective rate marginally higher in first year due to deferred tax; 25% from March 2026
items.quote: We have opted for the new regime of taxation which is 25%. So, the first year of shift there will be some deferred tax. So, it could be marginally higher by a percent. But after that from March '26 onwards it will be 25%.

items.statement: Telangana receivables delay impacted Q1 volume; if resolved, Q1 would have shown double-digit growth; expect resolution over next quarter
items.quote: If you have the right working capital access in Q1 which of course has been resolved post the IPO, we should have been in a double-digit growth. We should have been able to post a double-digit growth.

items.statement: LST division revenue growth expected at 5-8% for FY25; Chemical division revenue growth targeted at 8-10% for FY25
items.quote: For LST, since the capacities are always as of now, maxed out, anywhere our expectation is that it will be between 5% to 8%. And even for Chemical that we will try to get closer to 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA expected to grow 7-8% to around INR120 crores in FY25 from INR110 crores last year
items.quote: Last year, we made an EBITDA of INR110 crores consolidated. So obviously, you can take a growth of 7% to 8%. So, of that, it comes to around INR120 crores.

items.statement: Chemical division EBITDA margin target raised to 8-9% from current 5-6%; PAT margin target around 6%
items.quote: Last year, we are making an EBITDA of around 5% to 6% in Chemical division, but our forecast for the coming years is to make EBITDA of around 8% to 9% in Chemical division. And PAT is around 6%.

items.statement: LST rental business maintains steady EBITDA margin of 48-52%
items.quote: In rental business in LST, we are constantly keeping an EBITDA of around 48% to 52%, between 40% to 52%.

items.statement: LPG terminal capex estimated at INR700-750 crores for 64,000 ton capacity at JNPT
items.quote: So, it's around INR700 crores -- INR700 crores to INR750 crores, that is the capex required for building that 64,000 capacity of LPG.

items.statement: 18,000 KL capacity addition at JNPT fully utilized at 100%
items.quote: And this result also include your 18,000 KL capacity which has already come into the existence. So, there is a 100% capacity utilization there? Rishi Pilani: Yes

items.statement: LPG terminal capacity tied up with BW LPG and CPIL; orders for such tanks typically roll in near completion
items.quote: So, see, we already have a certain capacity that is tied up with BW LPG and CPIL. And generally, the orders for such type of LPG tanks start rolling in once they come nearer to completion.

items.statement: Chemical division focusing on niche products like food preservatives and lube oil additives; pursuing FDA and REACH certifications for export expansion
items.quote: The product mix we have is a very niche product mix, like food preservatives, the lube oil additives, where the custom -- and what we are doing is we are also getting new certifications, like FDA and REACH and all we are in the process of that, so that we can maximize the sale of the products to not only within the domestic region, but also export it.

items.statement: Exploring new products including methyl benzoate and lube oil additive derivatives; details proprietary
items.quote: See, we are exploring a lot of other products like methyl benzoate and we are also looking at some derivatives of the lube oil additives.

items.statement: Raw material purchasing system modified to achieve better pricing benefits in Chemical division
items.quote: The raw material purchasing has been also modified the system of purchasing to give us benefits of better pricing in raw material purchasing.

items.statement: Chemical division demand remained intact in Q1 FY25; volume and margin growth expected from Q3 FY25
items.quote: Chemical division demand remained intact. So, you can see there is a June to June, Chemical division has performed steadily. And overall EBITDA, you're talking, yes, you can take INR500 crores revenue and EBITDA of INR100 crores, so 20%, 23%.

items.statement: LST growth limited to 5-7% range until new LPG terminal commissioned; Goa terminal not at full capacity but capturing available market share
items.quote: In JNPT and Cochin also, we are now -- the tank capacities are fully utilized. So, for us to expect that we can get step jumps even by doing changes in products and all is not really tactical beyond the 5% to 7% range.

items.statement: New JNPT capacities not competing for A/B/C class high-margin products; new berths reduce vessel waiting time benefiting JNPT attractiveness
items.quote: Currently, the capacities that are coming up in JNPT, none of them are of the same class as us. So, they are not there to handle the A class, B class and the C class products, which are the high revenue margin products.

items.statement: Chinese competition exists but quality preference and established customer base provide protection
items.quote: Yes. So, we always keep facing competition. But like I said, that in terms of quality, we are being favoured by our customers. So, we are -- so though China is giving us competition but we have our own customer base, and we are growing that.

items.statement: Chemical division capacity utilization increased steadily over 5-7 years without fresh working capital infusion
items.quote: If you see year-over-year basis for the last 5 to 7 years, the capacity utilization has steadily gone up without any infusion of fresh working capital into the company.

items.statement: No fresh debt or equity needed for capex; LPG equity contribution already secured; internal resources sufficient for tank additions
items.quote: It can be easily funded through internal resources. And thirdly is the LPG capex, which we are working on, for which we have already secured the -- whatever is the equity contribution that is required from GBL has been already secured by us.

items.statement: Legal steps ongoing against NBFC lenders; one lender dropped recovery; discussions with another lender progressing
items.quote: We are continuously taking all the legal steps to make sure that there is no impact on the company. And so far, we've not seen any impact. You must have seen that actually one of the lenders has dropped all its -- recover money from the company.

items.statement: Demerger of Chemical and Tank divisions pending court judgment; hearings not controlled by company timeline
items.quote: There is a legal issue with this diversification. We are waiting to get the court judgment in this matter. And we are -- unfortunately, the hearings are happening in a space that is not controlled by us in terms of time.

items.statement: Wharfage revenue decline due to jetty repair for 3 months (dredging during JM Baxi handover); one-in-a-decade event with no financial loss as pass-through
items.quote: This is like probably once -in-like-a-decade event. What happened is JNPT handed over the operations to of the jetty to JM Baxi and as per the handover clause, JNPT had to complete some maintenance, dredging and et c etc, on the jetty, which is like a part of the handover process

items.statement: EPC business being transferred to subsidiary; no fresh EPC projects until transfer complete; EPC not viewed as profit centre
items.quote: we are doing is slowly, slowly, we are transferring the entire EPC business into our EPC subsidiary. So, because of that, we are not taking any fresh projects into the EPC until this transfer is getting over

items.statement: Standalone PAT up 14% YoY to INR157 million; Consolidated PAT up 6% YoY to INR164 million in Q1 FY25
items.quote: During the Q1 of FY '25 on a stand-alone basis, profit after tax is 157 million as against 138 million for Q1 of financial year '24 with an increase of 14% Y-to-Y. And for consolidated basis during the quarter 1 of FY '25, profit after tax is 164 million as against 155 million for Q1 of financial year '24 with an increase of 6% Y-to-Y.

items.statement: Expects booking value growth of at least 20% annually, historically growing 30-35%
items.quote: We have been growing very significantly and we expect the growth to continue at least 20% and generally we have been growing at 30%, 35%.

items.statement: Plans to launch 5.8 lakh sq ft carpet area across Bhandup, Monte South, and Nexzone in next four quarters with GDV of INR1,300 crores
items.quote: So, this, in the next four quarters we intend to launch something in Bhandup around 1.5 lakh square feet carpet area. Monte South around 2 lakh square feet carpet area. Nextzone around 2.5 lakh square feet carpet area. The totalling figure comes, the GDP of the whole becomes around INR1,300 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 area sold 72,912 sq ft, booking value INR158 crores, collections INR186 crores
items.quote: Area sold stood at 72,912 square feet, booking value stood at INR158 crores, collection stood at INR186 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA INR69 crores at 40% margin, PBT INR44 crores, PAT INR38 crores
items.quote: Consolidated Q1 FY25 financial performance, total revenue stood at INR173 crores. EBITDA stood at INR69 crores which translates at 40% margin. Profit before tax stood at INR44 crores. Profit after tax stood at INR38 crores.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR718 crores as on 30 June 2024 from INR751 crores at end of FY24
items.quote: The net debt position — net debt has reduced to INR718 crores as on 30th June 2024, as against INR751 crores as at the end of FY24.

items.statement: Enabling resolution for INR500 crores fundraise via QIP or other routes; proceeds for debt repayment, asset acquisition, and new projects
items.quote: currently, the enabling resolution has been cleared. It is to raise funds, not necessarily through QIP route, but any QIP and other possible options are open. So, that is how enabling resolution has been made. Our committee has also formed on that and we are exploring all the possibilities. Once the money is raised the ultimate use is going to be one to repay a little bit of debt, one to acquire n

items.statement: Potential equity dilution of ~15% if INR500 crores raised at INR3,000 crores market cap
items.quote: Well, if you consider the enabling resolution of INR500 crores, that percentage will come to around 15% if you consider INR3000 crores as a market gap, but it will exactly, exact number will depend on when it is happening and how much it is happening.

items.statement: Process ongoing to merge private company assets/projects into listed entity; will follow QIP process
items.quote: So, we are in the process of consulting with our consultants and legal lawyers and others on how to go about bringing some of the assets from the outside listed company into the listed company. So, that process is going on. We will come back with all those announcements very soon. First, the process is going to be the QIP process. Then there is going to be a process which will immediately follow o

items.statement: Bhandup prices increased ~5% YoY historically; plan to continue at least that pace without hampering sales
items.quote: In the past, we have increased about 5% year-on-year, which is exactly not hampering the sales at all. So, we want to continue at least that pace.

items.statement: Realisation trend likely to continue in FY25 but at slower pace across projects due to OC readiness and market demand
items.quote: The trend is likely to continue. It may be at a slower pace, but still the price are likely to rise.

items.statement: Panvel demand booming due to Mumbai Trans Harbour Link and airport nearing completion; sustained sales despite township competition
items.quote: Nexzone as an area, Panvel is just booming. Hence the market is actually accepting the price hike. Bhandup as an area we are very confident of this area as per sales. So, we have been pushing the rates higher.

items.statement: Bhandup seen as goldmine with GMLR road widening and infrastructure growth attracting premium players; company dominating with NeoHomes

items.statement: QIP proceeds (Rs 100 Crores) for 3 Mumbai redevelopment projects; GMP sale proceeds (Rs 100-110 Crores) for growth capital, Baner-Pashan project, and EPC working capital collateral

And that QIP specifically for these three projects and apart from that, what is the sale of GMP that is meant for the -- you need some kind of capital infusion in Baner Pashan Link Road in coming days also.

items.statement: Ticket size qualification increasing; Raipur project completion will enable bidding for Rs 700+ Crore projects; targeting Rs 600-800 Crore projects
items.quote: We are in the process of almost finishing the Raipur, Chhattisgarh project, which will give us a single certificate of upwards of Rs 500 Crores which therefore will enable us to start bidding for projects upwards of Rs 700 Crores going forward.

items.quote: We are currently at 80% government. We would like to hopefully be at 70% government, 30% private or 65% government, 30%, 35% private. We do want to have private exposure. We do not want to be exposed only to government.

items.statement: Strategy to avoid projects in states with elections due in 12-18 months; prefer hospital projects in non-metro locations to reduce political risk
items.quote: And the second thing we also do is the elections are due for the last 12 months to 15 months, 18 months, we do not bag any order in that state because that is where time where people are busy with elections, and then there are risks.

items.statement: Net debt risen to Rs 38 Crores due to real estate JV investments; bridge loan of ~Rs 40 Crores taken for project launches pending QIP/GMP proceeds
items.quote: This fiscal year, we have seen our total debt go up because we are involved in new real estate joint ventures. As a result, our net debt has risen to Rs 38 Crores over the past last year.

items.statement: GMP divestment to Shinryo for Rs 155-157 Crores (net Rs 100-110 Crores) expected to close by end of month/early September; QIP approved, 6 months validity remaining

items.statement: Real estate sales booking Q1 FY25: 12,244 sq ft, Rs 7 Crores sale value, Rs 11 Crores collections
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, we achieved new sales booking totalling 12,244 Square Feet, generating a sale value of Rs 7 Crores and a total collection of Rs 11 Crores.

items.statement: Labor availability shrinking; mitigating via design-build EPC (60-80% of projects) to improve labor efficiency 15-20% at drawing board level
items.quote: And the only other thing in our industry that is pulling us back is the availability of labor which is shrinking regularly. And so therefore, to counter that, we are focusing 60 % - 70% - 80% of our projects on design and build EPC mode.

items.statement: Political risk mitigated by avoiding orders in election-bound states 12-18 months prior; hospital projects in non-metro areas less prone to political interference
items.quote: What happens is these projects are generally not in the radar of politicians. The fund is allocated by the departments in their health care projects, there is very little risk of them being stalled or cancelled if there is any political change in the state.

items.statement: Promoter holding at 31%; company prioritizes growth over maintaining promoter stake percentage; promoter may or may not participate in fund raises
items.quote: See when the company needs capital to grow and if it has to come from beyond the promoter and if it means there is a plus minus some dilution to the promoter stake, I think we, as a firm, are ready to face that because I think the company is a bit more important than the exact ratio of the promoter holding in the company.

items.statement: No significant legal cases with material financial liability; routine contingencies only
items.quote: We don't envisag e any that kind of payment or something is coming up in the system. We can -- it is a normal routine kind of thing. So, we still hope to cross the Rs1,000 Crores mark. So, in fact it's the Rs1,100 Crores mark this year with EPC and real estate alone without GMP.

items.statement: Air freight volumes grew 60% quarter-on-quarter in Q1 FY25, supported by IATA accreditation received last year.

So there has been a good 60% growth in the overall air freight sector on quarter-to-quarter basis.

items.statement: Management expects growth to continue in Q2 FY25 and coming quarters due to a good pipeline and tailwinds.

items.statement: Revenue was ₹102.8 crore in Q1 FY25, up 9.1% quarter-on-quarter and 2.4 times year-on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA increased 10.6% quarter-on-quarter and nearly doubled year-on-year in Q1 FY25.

items.quote: we are not present in the LCL segment as of now. I think that is the only segment which is not there with us, but we are looking at organic growth through that segment, maybe through if we can work closely, you know in some acquisition and all.

items.statement: Strategy includes regular roadshows in US and LatAm countries to acquire overseas clients and agents for export business growth.

Similar activity we keep on doing for LatAm countries also and that is going to continue for us.

items.quote: So, Maheshji as we have already started our commercial production with introduction of 3,000 metric tons of capacity at New Anjar facility and with effect from 1st October, we shall be rolling out another 9,000 metric tons of capacity.

items.quote: With a strong order book outlook, coupled with our strategy to capitalize on the increasing capex by our customer segments, we expect strong top-line as well as bottom-line growth in near-medium term.

items.statement: Power sector orders expected earlier, possibly Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26, driven by 80 GW thermal expansion
items.quote: Now, we are expecting it to get those orders much earlier maybe in the last quarter of this fiscal or maybe the first quarter of the next fiscal.

items.statement: Fully qualified for supercritical power plants with BHEL and NTPC, approved by NPCIL for nuclear, pursuing overseas nuclear opportunities
items.quote: We are qualified with BHL. We are qualified with NTPC. We are qualified as any other player in the Indian power sector market, who shall be putting up these supercritical power plants.

items.statement: Advanced discussions with global EPC player for step-two agreement, may formalize in weeks, discussing 2-3 large jobs
items.quote: We are in very, very advanced stage of discussion for that particular matter. We are calling that as step two. In that step two, we shall be formalizing all of our agreements and that is very much on the pipeline.

items.statement: 40-45% of business from exports, orders on FOB basis so freight cost impact not borne by company
items.quote: So, as far as our orders are concerned, our orders are FOB basis. So, the impact of the cost increase in terms of freight cost does not come to us

items.statement: IPO proceeds Rs 3,250 million, utilized Rs 935.32 million so far: Rs 179.82 million working capital, Rs 755.50 million debt repayment
items.quote: Of the total IPO proceeds of 3,250 million, we have already utilized 935.32 million so far, towards 179.82 million towards working capital needs and 755.50 million towards repayment of debts.

items.statement: Full Rs 175 crore debt repayment completed before 10 July 2024, though only Rs 75.5 crore reflected as of 30 June
items.quote: We had already made a payment of INR175 crores towards repayment of working capital. However, the amount of working capital demand loan, which were actually paid out post-30th June, that is why this amount is shown as INR75.5 crores.

items.statement: Full-year revenue, margin and order inflow guidance to be provided in about a month after Anjar capacity rollout and customer approvals
items.quote: So, in a month's time, we will make sure to give you a good guidance in this respect

items.statement: Revenue: piping division 81.3% (13.2% YoY growth), heavy fabrication 7.4% (295.2% YoY growth)
items.quote: Revenue from piping division saw a 13.2% year -over-year growth, contributing 81.3% over revenue, whereas heavy fabrication division saw a year -on-year growth of 295.2% with sales contribution of 7.4% of the growth.

items.statement: Heavy fabrication unit fully occupied, no order booking challenges
items.quote: our heavy fabrication unit is also fully occupied. So, we do not have any challeng e as far as the order booking is concerned for that particular unit

items.statement: Not pursuing Indian nuclear sector aggressively due to long project durations, focusing on overseas nuclear opportunities
items.quote: However, since the jobs which come from the nuclear sector, particularly from Indian customers, they run for years and years together. So, we are not very keen to go full blast, particularly for the nuclear sector in India.

items.statement: Revenue potential from existing capacities guided at Rs 1,600-1,800 crore over next couple of years, subject to raw material prices
items.quote: we had guided to around Rs. 1,600 crores to Rs. 1,800 crores of sales. The only caveat there is the raw material prices, because whatever we are trying to give you as numbers is based on an assumption of the raw material prices.

items.statement: Mango order book 80% confirmed and booked, 20-25% under negotiation; order book higher than FY24 but may not translate to higher sales due to limited production capability
items.quote: almost 80% of the order already confirmed and booked, and another 20%, 25% order what is targeted during the season is under negotiation.

items.statement: Domestic volume growth only 5-6% vs targeted 20% due to key brand facility breakdown (7-8 days lost) and local brand deferring tomato dispatch to July
items.quote: we have landed around 5%, 6% growth in the domestic market. The reason behind that, in the month of, I mean, from June second week onwards, whatever target volume have been given to us by the brands where we supply the major volume, we can see a downfall in the volume.

items.statement: Export shipments deferred due to container unavailability and high freight costs; Rs 10.76 crore DDP/CFR shipments not recognized in Q1, plus Rs 10-12 crore lost shipments; vessels skipping India for China due to higher rates
items.quote: the value of that container is around Rs. 11-odd crores. I think we have given that number in the Investor Presentation as well. 10 point something, Rs. 10.7 crores or Rs. 10.8 crores to be precise.

items.statement: Tomato processing capacity more than doubled, to be commissioned in October; pastry line expansion of 2 lines (Rs 3-4 crore) planned for immediate future, targeting 10 lines total
items.quote: We have now more than doubled our tomato processing capabilities. Last year we had a Rs. 150 crore order which we could have possibly taken. We could not take that order, because we did not have the capacity. That capacity will be commissioned in October this year

items.statement: Totapuri mango raw material prices almost double FY24; Alphonso slightly cheaper; mango processing lower by 25% due to lower crop availability in South India
items.quote: Processing of mangoes was lower by around 25% in FY'25 due to lower crop availability in South India. Totapuri raw material prices were almost double of what we procured in FY'24 and Alphonso was slightly cheaper than what we actually procured in FY'24.

items.statement: Blended realization Rs 88/kg in Q1 FY25 vs Rs 105/kg in Q1 FY24 due to product mix change (no tomato/guava sales); business model is complete pass-through of raw material prices
items.quote: the average realization for this quarter was around Rs. 88 kg. All put together, the export and domestic put together. But I am sure you will not get much of a sense with respect to this, because our product mix keeps on changing.

items.statement: Key brand facility breakdown caused 7-8 day shutdown during peak season; local brand deferred tomato dispatch from June to July; Hong Kong branded portfolio (Greentop) getting repeat orders
items.quote: One of the big brands who consume a huge volume from us, a couple of their facility docketing line, there is some breakdown. And due to that, they have to shut down the facility for six to seven days.

items.statement: India tomato lycopene/color value poorer than global standards; less than 1% of tomatoes processed; tied up with seed companies to develop export-quality varieties for contract farming
items.quote: the lycopene value and the color value of tomatoes in India is actually poorer because of which the export markets do not consume that in large numbers. So, India is the largest producer of tomatoes, but less than 1% actually gets processed.

items.statement: Income recognition deferred for Rs 10.76 crore DDP/CFR shipments per ICAI accounting standards; vessel must reach destination port before revenue recognition
items.quote: income recognition standards actually say that if it's a DDP shipment or a CFR shipment, unless the vessel actually reaches the port of the customer, you cannot, I mean, recognize the income in your P&L statement.

items.statement: Lower mango production (25% less) reduces inventory blockage and working capital requirement, which will automatically reduce debt; Totapuri price increase would increase inventory blockage but lower production offsets
items.quote: we have actually produced less, 25% less with respect to mango this particular season because of unavailability of good quality of processing variety mangoes. So, to that extent, the working capital requirement will come down, which will automatically reduce the debt.

items.statement: Endeavor to reduce debt from Rs 469 crore (FY24), but depends on business growth; lower mango production reduces working capital need and debt
items.quote: the endeavor is to actually reduce the debt, but it also depends upon whether we increase the business or not. So, this year, as we explained, the raw material prices for Totapuri has gone up.

items.statement: Open offer closed with 500,212 shares (under 1%) tendered; voluntary offer triggered by Ray Simkins joining as promoter for B2C global expansion; enables creeping acquisitions up to 5% annually after crossing 25% threshold
items.quote: While I did mention in my opening remarks, but it's a public knowledge and I have no hesitation in confirming with you that I got 500,212 shares to be precise.

items.statement: Export logistics risk: vessels skipping India for China due to freight rate disparity ($15-20k vs $5-6k per container); shipping normalization expected post-September, backlog of 30-40 containers
items.quote: most of the vessels are skipping and going to China due to the Christmas demand in U.S. So, apart from the Rs. 10.76 crores, which we were able to make the shipment, but could not recognize. We have also lost another Rs. 10 crores, Rs. 12 crores of shipments.

items.statement: Pectin project trial runs done; commercial production starting late August (22-26 Aug); customer audits take minimum 6 months, revenue generation expected early 2025
items.quote: in our pectin project, our main raw material is dried peel. So, during mango season, we have already dried whatever peel wastage was there. Now it will be converted into pectin. So, I think around fourth week, 26th of August or maybe 22nd or 23rd of August, the process will start to produce pectin.

items.statement: Tetra Recart concrete numbers expected by end of FY25 (March 2025); product development and testing with brands ongoing, shelf-life testing (6-12 months) delaying orders
items.quote: With respect to what numbers, we can actually guide you with, for Tetra Recart, we would request you to give us time till the end of FY'25 to give you concrete numbers on the same.

items.statement: Tomato capacity expansion done outside PLI scheme as PLI commitments already overshot
items.quote: So, we have actually done it outside the PLI, because whatever we had committed under the PLI, we had already overshot that. So, the expansion of tomato is outside PLI.

items.statement: Frozen category seeing huge surge in demand globally post-COVID; business development with big brands in US, UK, Europe, Gulf takes minimum 8 months; spray dried powder seasoning business flat for 1-1.5 years
items.quote: across the world we are seeing a huge surge in demand for frozen categories, especially post-COVID, we would like to enter. But for business development and I mean the start of business, there's a huge time requirement.

items.statement: Exploring new geographies: Russia (banana/pulp opportunity from Ecuador political tension), Sri Lanka, UK, Spain (sold tomato pulp to Spain in FY23)
items.quote: Russia is one of the markets that we are actually exploring. Sri Lanka is another market that we are exploring. The UK is another market that we are actually exploring for tomatoes. In FY'23, we even sold to Spain.

items.statement: Alphonso realization 2.5x Totapuri per metric tonne; portfolio has more Totapuri as it sells globally; farmer relations provide procurement price advantage (x-1 vs industry 1x)
items.quote: If realization per metric tonne for Totapuri is 1x, then realization per metric tonne for Alphonso will be 2.5x. This depends on the raw material price.

items.statement: Pastry line business: first container exported to UK; 2 more lines by Oct-Nov, 5 more to follow; targets 10 lines generating >Rs 100 crore business; good EBITDA margins, in-house consumption advantage
items.quote: I believe that if we are able to put these 10 lines, this can generate more than 100 per business. We did see, in the pulping business, this year around or this quarter around that the prices of Totapuri were slightly higher and almost double.

items.statement: Total export shipment deferment approximately Rs 25 crore (Rs 10.76 crore accounting deferment + Rs 9.8-10 crore lost shipments due to vessel unavailability)
items.quote: Approximately Rs. 25 crores. All put together, as in, all put together including the Rs. 11 crores would have been around Rs. 25 crores.

items.statement: Tomato and guava expected to drive volume growth in FY25 due to good monsoon and doubled tomato capacity; mango sales volume similar to FY24 despite 25% lower processing
items.quote: Because of a good monsoon this year we are expecting tomatoes to be good and since we have also more than doubled our capacity in tomato, I think that should help us push through.

items.statement: Revenue CAGR of around 20% over next three years driven by ATBS, antioxidants and VOPL products
items.quote: We expect our revenue to have a CAGR of around 20% over the next three years, which will be mainly driven by ATBS, antioxidants, and other products from VOPL.

items.statement: On track for 20% CAGR revenue guidance over three years
items.quote: Yes, I think we are on track for that one. We have basically guided for a 20% CAGR over a period of three years.

items.statement: Overall FY25 capex approximately INR570 crores including VOPL and ATBS expansion
items.quote: The overall capex to be spent in FY '25 would be approximately INR570 crores. This includes VOPL.

items.statement: VOPL capex plan exceeding INR500 crores for MEHQ, Guaiacol, anisole, 4-meth and Iso Amylene derivatives
items.quote: VOPL has outlined a capital expenditure plan exceeding INR500 crores, focusing on production of MEHQ, Guaiacol, anisole, 4-meth, and other Iso Amylene derivatives.

items.statement: ATBS expanded capacity to come into play from FY26
items.quote: The expanded capacity for ATBS will come into play from FY'26, and this will aid further growth in ATBS.

items.statement: MEHQ plant meaningful revenue contributions expected from FY26 onwards
items.quote: Meaningful revenue contributions from the MEHQ plant can be expected from FY26 onwards.

items.statement: Remaining VOPL products scheduled for commissioning in second half of FY25
items.quote: Additionally, the remaining products under capex are scheduled for commissioning in the second half of FY '25.

items.statement: Antioxidant capacity utilization expected to reach 50% in FY25
items.quote: Secondly as far as 50% capacity utilization, yes, for FY25 I think we should be coming closer to that one year.

items.statement: ATBS witnessing robust growth in FY25 with demand exceeding supply for high-grade ATBS
items.quote: ATBS, which is our largest product, is witnessing a robust growth in FY '25.

items.statement: Butylphenol and IB derivatives performing well with sustained growth expected
items.quote: The butylphenol business, along with other IB derivatives like PTBBA, Ester, continues to perform well, and we expect the growth to be sustained going ahead as well.

items.statement: Antioxidant sales showing good growth in FY25 despite weak global demand
items.quote: In antioxidants, we had recorded approx. INR130 crores of sales in FY24, and even though the overall global demand for antioxidants is going through a weak period, we are seeing a good growth in our AO sales in FY '25.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margins of 26% to 27% expected on sustainable basis from Q2 onwards
items.quote: I think one can expect normalized EBITDA margins of 26% to 27% on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Q1 margin dip due to raw material price increases, logistics issues, inventory in transit, and missing high-margin customized products
items.quote: The raw material prices increased during Q1. So you will see some price increase happening in Q2. Secondly, there were a lot of logistics issues in Q1, a lot of delays, unavailability of tankers. So we had a lot of inventory in transit, which actually reflect a sale in Q2. Then, of course, other than the regular shutdowns that Kaviraj mentioned, we also have some customized products, which are qui

items.statement: Prices stabilized with raw material cost changes passed through contracts
items.quote: Prices are presently stabilized. It's not, there is not much of a moment as such, because anyway, we have our, you know, contracts in place. So whatever price change that happens in terms of the raw materials, that is passed on.

items.statement: Freight costs increased but passed on to customers; lead times increased
items.quote: Well, one, the lead times have increased. One has to keep that in mind. So the delivery time has increased. Secondly, while the freight costs have gone up, we are thankfully in a position to pass on most of that to our customers.

items.statement: Electricity cost up ~10% per unit; coal prices also risen; renewables cover 40-50% of energy
items.quote: One is the electricity cost itself has gone up because there is a raise in prices that has happened in electricity. So that's almost like a 10% kind of a raise that has happened on a unit basis. Secondly, there is also some rise in coal prices which is there, which is seen and that's essentially why the...

items.statement: High-grade ATBS constitutes over 70% of ATBS volumes; margin difference minimal due to higher production cost
items.quote: So, yes, 70% and 70% more than 70% is the high-grade ATBS because that is essentially what is being now asked by the customers.

items.statement: IBB, IB, HPMTBE and customized products revenue expected to remain steady in FY25
items.quote: The revenues from IBB, IB, HPMTBE, and customized products is expected to remain steady during FY'25.

items.statement: ATBS 90-95% export; domestic growing as customers realize benefit of local ATBS production
items.quote: ATBS, well, it's 90% - 95% export, but domestic is also growing because our customers are realizing since the ATBS producer is in India, it makes sense to make the ATBS polymer in India also.

items.statement: MEHQ main demand in China; Guaiacol demand in India and export; sampling through traders for exports
items.quote: Well, the main demand is in China for MEHQ. Guaiacol there is demand in India as well. So it does cater to local as well as export. We have started sampling through traders, which will be used in export sales.

items.statement: ATBS demand exceeds supply; high-grade quality requirement limits production capacity
items.quote: See, in ATBS right now, the demand exceeds the supply. Because the demand, which is there, it's for a very, very high grade ATBS quality, which restricts our production capacity.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 net income INR533.98 crores (19% YoY), EBIT INR114.8 crores (23% YoY), PAT INR86 crores (24% YoY)
items.quote: On a standalone, Y-on-Y basis, the net income for quarter ended 30th June, 2024 is INR533.98 crores as against INR448.5 crores, registering a 19% growth. The EBIT increased by 23% to INR114.8 crores as against INR93.44 crores, and the PAT increased by 24% from INR69.42 crores to INR86 crores on a Y-on-Y basis.

items.statement: Product revenue mix: ATBS 33%, butylphenol/IB derivatives 21%, IBB 15%, IB/HPMTBE 12%, AO 8%, customized 4%
items.quote: ATBS is roughly around 33%, IBB is around 15% odd, butylphenol and IB derivatives is roughly around 21%. The customized products is around 4% and IB & HPMTBE those products are around 12%. AO is around 8% and rest is others.

items.statement: VOPL established as 100% owned subsidiary for niche specialty chemicals manufacturing
items.quote: Vinati Organics Limited has established a 100% owned subsidiary Veeral Organics Private Limited (VOPL), dedicated to the manufacturing of niche speciality chemicals.

items.statement: New antioxidant product timeline uncertain; typical new project gestation 12-18 months
items.quote: Very difficult to answer this as of now without knowing what kind of AOs would be getting added to the entire lineup. But typically, the range is around 12 to 18 months is essentially what happens with any new project.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY25 is north of 15%
items.quote: Our revenue guidance for the year though still remains at north of 15%.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to improve YoY for next 2-3 years
items.quote: I think an improving trend is what we should expect YoY for the next 3 odd financial years.

items.statement: Total capex commitment of Rs 30 crore for capacity expansion and brand building, Rs 5 crore for cultivation expansion, Rs 45-50 crore for hospitality over next 2 years
items.value: Rs. 30 odd crore... Rs. 5 odd crore... Rs. 45 crore - Rs. 50 crore
items.quote: In our CAPEX outlay for the next 2 years, all of it will get committed in this financial year, but some will get spend this year and some in the year after. But we expect to spend about Rs. 30 odd crore in capacity expansion and brand b uilding. We are expecting to spend ~Rs. 5 odd crore in expanding area under cultivation. I mentioned already about Rs. 45 crore - Rs. 50 crore in building the hosp

items.statement: Current capacity 4.5 million liters, expanding by ~25% to north of 5.6 million liters by end of FY25, commercialization by December 2024
items.value: 4.5 million liters to north of 5.6 million liters
items.quote: Our existing capacity at the moment is roughly 4.5 million liters. This year we are looking to expand that by approximately 25% and that will be north of 5.6 million liters by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Current utilization disproportionately high, above healthy 80-85% range, capacity constraint held back growth last 6-9 months
items.quote: Our utilization right now is disproportionately high. Normally, in a wine business about 80%-85% capacity utilization is considered very healthy. We are actually operating at higher than that, which is not ideal and we are adding capacity so that we do not feel the capacity constraint that we are feeling today.

items.statement: Sales volume ~4.2 million liters in FY24, volume CAGR ~30% from FY21-24
items.quote: Our sales in million liter s for last year was approximately 4.2 million liters. And our sales approximately as I mentioned earlier, have grown at about 30% at a CAGR level over the last three odd financial years

items.statement: EBITDA margin ~13.5% in FY24, improving trend for 3 years, gross margins maintained strong momentum in Q1 FY25 despite election disruptions
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the last financial year was ~13.5% and like I said earlier, it has been an improving trend from the last 3 years.

items.statement: Gross margins for Wine-in-Can slightly better than bottles by a couple of percentage points due to lower packaging cost
items.value: a couple of percentage points better
items.quote: On a gross margin level, it is fairly consistent with bottles as well, slightly better. You can say a couple of percentage points due to the lower packaging cost which is there in Cans.

items.statement: Premium and Luxury segments contribute 73% of revenue in FY24 (up from 70% in FY21), Super Premium + Luxury above Rs 1,200 contribute 14-15%, Premium Rs 600-1,200 contributes 55-60%, Value Rs 250-550 contributes 20-25%, Cans contribute ~5%
items.quote: If you look at our numbers for FY21, we had 70% contribution from the premium and super premium segments, and this has risen to 73% in FY24 on an expanded operating base.

items.statement: Top brands: Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc-Shiraz each contribute 8-8.5%, Sparkling Noi contributes 5.5-6%, portfolio has 7-8 major brands each contributing 5-7%
items.quote: brands in the Red Wine segment, one with Cabernet Sauvignon a nd the other being Cabernet Franc-Shiraz both contribute roughly 8%-8.5% to our overall business. And then we have a bunch of other brands which are also contributing roughly 5%-6%, one being, for example, our Sparkling brand Noi, which is approximately number 3, which is also contributing about 5.5%-6% for us

items.statement: Geographic revenue split: South, West, North each 25-30%, East fourth; Top 6 states: Maharashtra, Karnataka, Delhi, Telangana, West Bengal, Goa
items.quote: The South, the West and the North regions contribute handsomely of course to our overall topline. And they are all within the range of 25%-30%. And then of course, that is followed by the East region in number 4.

items.statement: Channel split: 75% retail (off-trade), 25% HoReCa (on-trade); HoReCa share increasing over last 3 years; HoReCa leadership in Delhi, West Bengal, Karnataka, Odisha
items.quote: Currently as of last year, the split is roughly 75-25 with 75% coming from retail and 25% coming from HoReCa.

items.statement: 22,000 touch points pan India including Army Canteen; exclusive brands for Taj (Svara), ITC (Ghungroo), Living Liquidz (Amaris)
items.quote: We have now over 15 years developed a skill to build good, powerf ul brands and become a pan India business. Our deep relationships in the HoReCa segment are our key advantage that we have on our side and that has now resulted in us having 22,000 touch points pan India including the Army Canteen and leadership in certain states like Delhi etc

items.statement: Beneficiary of Maharashtra WIPS scheme, received Rs 14 crore in FY24
items.quote: Yes, we are availing WIPS scheme in Maharashtra like other wineries are and last year we received around Rs. 14 crore in FY24.

items.statement: Total debt ~Rs 90 crore (Rs 15 crore long-term, balance working capital); may add Rs 10-15 crore long-term debt for planned capex
items.quote: At this point of time, we have roughly Rs. 90 crore of debt in our balance sheet. About Rs. 15 crore is long term debt, and the balance is working capital. We may take an additional Rs. 10 crore - Rs. 15 crore of long-term debt going forward to complete all the CAPEX that we have planned over this year and the next year.

items.statement: Trading business contributed ~Rs 100 crore revenue in Q1 FY25, will reduce dramatically in Q2, shut down completely in Q3
items.quote: While in Q1, the trading business of the listed entity contributed approximately Rs. 100 crore in reve nue, t his will reduce dramatically in Q2 and will completely shut down in Q3

items.statement: S&D spend at ~30% of revenue, trending 28-30% over last 3-4 years; efforts underway to reduce S&D spend
items.quote: Basically we are at below 30% in the S&D trends and basically if you see from last 3-4 financial years, we are between 28% and 30%.

items.statement: 95% of packaging material procured domestically, improving trend over last few years
items.quote: 95% of all our packaging material at the moment is procured domestically and that has been an improving trend for the last few financial years.

items.statement: Imported and adapted ~12 varietals from best wine regions, successfully cloned; process of identifying new varietals ongoing; recently imported new varietals yet to be planted
items.quote: We have imported now and adapted approximately 12 varietals from the best wine growing regions in the world and have successfully cloned them as well. The process of identifying and incorporating new varietals is still ongoing.

items.statement: CAGR FY21-24: Net revenue ~25%, Gross profit ~26%, EBITDA ~100%, PAT ~300%
items.quote: Our net revenue as you can see has grown at a CAGR of ~25%, our gross profit at a CAGR of 26%, our EBITDA at a CAGR of 100% and PAT which is almost 300%.

items.statement: Crop failure risk from natural calamities mitigated by geographic diversification of vineyards (new 150-acre parcel 200km away)
items.quote: Something we have done recently and we will continue to do more of is that we have recently taken a new parcel of 150 acres of land under active farming which is approximately 200 kilometers away from our winery. Now, what that does is that it slightly derisks us from an agro-climate risk perspective.

items.statement: Vineyard tourism: Phase 1 - 40-key property on 170 acres at Akluj, capex within Rs 50 crore, ARR Rs 20,000-25,000, occupancy 40% first 3 years then 60-70%; city-based outlets planned for wine tasting and D2C
items.quote: We are expecting to build a 40 key property in Phase-1 at our location. We expect our ARRs to be around Rs. 20,000 - Rs. 25,000 per room night. In terms of occupancy rates, I think first maybe up to 3 years, it may be around 40% odd, but after 3 years it will pick up to about 60%-70% is our expectation.

items.statement: Wine-in-Can (TiLT) grew 30% YoY in Q1 FY25, record quarter; >90% retail channel; gross margins slightly better than bottles; major focus for future growth
items.quote: On the Cans currently, if we look at our business model, firstly we are very happy with our Can performance in quarter 1 of this year as we recorded a 30% growth over Q1 of last year. It was a record Q1 for us in terms of Cans.

items.statement: Investing in brand development and augmenting middle management, reflected in current EBITDA margins
items.quote: We are continuously investing towards brand development and augmenting middle management, and this is getting reflected in our EBITDA margins at the moment.

items.statement: Kolkata plant for pulses and grains to be commissioned in February 2025
items.quote: we plan to commercialize our new plant in Kolkata, dedicated to pulses and grains. Within, I think, it will be commissioned in the month of Feb 25.

items.statement: Surat plant land acquired, commissioning expected next financial year
items.quote: Additionally, we are also trying to launch a new plant in Surat, for which we have already acquired land and it will be commissioned in the next financial year.

items.statement: Kolkata plant capacity 100,000 tons per year for Masoor; edible oil capacity 50,000 tons per year
items.quote: Like we are already trying to install, we are installing 100,000 tons per year of Masoor. And around, edible is around 50,000 tons per year.

items.statement: Surat plant to process lentils, channa, and matar pulses
items.quote: We are putting for pulses. Like we can process three types of pulses in that unit. One is lentils. One is channa. And the third one will be matar.

items.statement: Edible oil refining operating margin targeted at 2% to 2.5% on processing only
items.quote: So, our operating margin will be around 2% to 2.5%. We will be just trying to have that on processing thing only.

items.statement: Processing margins expected to increase profit by 1.5% to 2% of revenue once plants operational
items.quote: So, we think our profit may increase like 1.5%, 2% of the revenue. It may increase.

items.statement: Domestic demand for food grains and pulses increasing enormously, driving shift from exports
items.quote: our domestic demands have increased very much enormously. You can say like, yes, our domestic demands have increased very much.

items.statement: Government prohibiting sugar and rice exports, encouraging ethanol production from grains, discouraging agri-commodity exports
items.quote: government prohibited the export of Sugar. If you see the results of March ending 23, the major revenue was from sugar exports. So, we were not mentally ready, to, like, the government will prohibit the export of Sugar and Rice from India.

items.statement: Shifting from exports (22% of Q1 FY24 revenue) to imports and domestic processing, developing own brand for retail
items.quote: reducing our Reliance on exports, which accounted for approximately 22% of our revenue in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Top five export markets identified as Bangladesh, Iraq, Dubai, Saudi Arabia, Egypt
items.quote: Bangladesh, we have been doing tenders. So, like, if we export, the number one country is Bangladesh. Iraq is buying international tenders. We can go to -- we can supply to Iraq. Then Dubai, Saudi Arabia, Egypt.

items.statement: Surat plant located 18 km from Hazira port at Navsari Surat Road industrial park for logistics advantage
items.quote: Navsari Surat Road is 18 kilometers from Vesu. There is an industrial park coming up, green industrial park. So, we have taken land over there.

items.statement: Will not exit quota-dependent sugar/rice export business but will wait for government quota opportunities
items.quote: We are not going to shut down our old business. We are not going to go away from that business because that is already there. That is already established. So, we are not going to switch off anything which we are having.

items.statement: Entering edible oil refining as related agri-commodity with ready market and conversion margin from crude to refined
items.quote: this edible oil is also something related to this agri-commodity which is used for consumers -- which are used by consumers. So, the trade is same and there is always margin of conversion from crude to refine.

items.statement: Textile brand Pakhi Commercial (Youmaa) and Luma brand showing good demand, repeat orders from MBOs, expansion plans underway
items.quote: In the initial stages, like, in Pakhi, they have launched the product somewhere in March or April. So, they are doing good. As for the results, I have seen on June and like, they are doing good. There is good demand coming, repeat orders coming from various MBOs, and we are doing very good on the other fronts also.

items.statement: Plan to add another processing unit in Bombay after Kolkata and Surat plants commission
items.quote: We plan to increase our processing units. One, after this two commissioning, we'll be planning to have one more unit at Bombay.

items.statement: Management reiterated prior full-year guidance; Q1 on track with confidence in market tailwinds for remainder of year
items.quote: I think we will stay with the guidance we provided last time. There is nothing that requires a review at this stage. Q1, w e have largely stayed on track with that projection, and we expect with some, and there is strong confidence that there will be market-related tailwinds to help in achieving whatever minor deficit that might be there

items.statement: Double-digit EBITDA margin targeted over two years, not in FY25, due to continued investments in brands, people and marketing
items.quote: the double digit is about a two-year journey. And so, it was not for this year. Bear in mind, again, I am saying that there are, the reason why it's a two-year journey because in these two years, we are also investing on brands and promotions and advertisement. We are investing in people ahead of the curve.

items.statement: India demand modest-to-sluggish in Q1 due to elections and weather; bounce-back expected from September driven by government infrastructure and housing spend
items.quote: Looking ahead in Quarter 2, we expect the demand scenario to be moderate in India and challenges on pricing to continue. However, we expect a bounce back from September onwards driven by government spends on infrastructure and housing, and this will all have a positive impact overall when we assess the full financial year in March-April.

items.statement: B2G pipe segment revenue at only 30% of normal in Q1 due to election-related fund delays; 50% budget increase for Jal Jeevan Mission expected to drive catch-up from September
items.quote: Overall, what we estimate is, and Ajay, you can help me, I think from steady state, the revenue was only about 30% of normal. So, the erosion was to the extent of 70%. It is something that we are reliably told that was experienced by other players also in the industry.

items.statement: Parador order bookings remain strong; third straight quarter of positive momentum on billings and order bookings
items.quote: Despite ongoing market sluggishness, Parador's order bookings remain strong. We have also introduced several new products ac ross categories to capture a larger market share

items.statement: Contribution margins improved across most segments despite price realization drops: Blocks +220 bps, Boards +170 bps, Putty +90 bps, Construction Chemicals +1000+ bps, Parador +370 bps YoY
items.quote: In Blocks, we improved our contribution margin by 220 basis points, in Boards by 170 basis points, in Putty by 90 basis points, in Construction Chemicals by over 1,000 basis points. And at Parador, the contribution margin improved by 370 basis points. All of these are in comparison with the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin down ~290 bps YoY due to strategic investments in product mix shift, manpower, technology and marketing; other costs reduced ~100 bps
items.quote: Overall, the drop in EBITDA level, nearly about 290 basis points compared to last year, is attributed to strategic investments for the future. Essentially three categories, there is a shift in product mix, manpower costs, while we have already shaved off nearly 100 basis points on other costs, we have sufficient line of sight to guide this EBITDA percentage beyond 10% plus over the next couple of

items.statement: Price realizations fell across categories: Pipes -12%, Putty -6%, Parador -5.7%, Blocks -3%, Panels -3.5% YoY due to aggressive competitor pricing and sluggish demand
items.quote: In Blocks, the price realization dropped by about 3%, for Panels by about 3.5%, in Putty by nearly 6%, in P ipes and Fittings by about 12%, and in Parador by about 5.7%. This is largely attributed to aggressive price play by industry players in wake of sluggish demand and increased competitive activity

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted ~5% away from Roofing strategically; Pipes & Fittings crossed Rs 150 cr quarterly revenue for first time (78% YoY growth); Construction Chemicals grew 35% YoY with Tiling ~100%
items.quote: Significantly, in this quarter, we at HIL have made a nearly 5% swing away from Roofing in our overall revenue mix. It's a metric that we had highlighted we want to strategically shift, and the first signs of those impacts are now visible.

items.statement: Chennai AAC block plant commissioning in H2 FY25 adding 2 lakh tons (phase 1) with capacity for another 2 lakh tons; aims to be India's largest single-location AAC plant
items.quote: The Chennai plant that will get commissione d in the second half of this year, we are adding 2 lakh tons in the first wave of that expansion, and we have capacity for another 2 lakh tons after that, which can be quickly switched on. That site is being prepared with the view that it will be India's largest single location AAC block plant anywhere in the country by any player

items.statement: Pipes & Fittings capacity sufficient to reach Rs 800-1,000 cr revenue; further expansion planned to achieve Rs 1,500 cr milestone; capacity investments on drawing board
items.quote: See, we have shared that the aspiration for us is, first milestone on the Pipes and Fitting segment is to get near the Rs. 1,500 crore mark. At the moment, we feel we have the capacity which will take us to 800 to 1,000 with small incremental, but after that we need to put capacity. We are already on the drawing board to plan for those capacity expansion.

items.statement: Building Solutions serviced 1,500+ projects in Q1; Parador gained significant market share in Engineered Wood, Resilient Flooring, DIY and commercial channels across Germany, Nordics, Spain, North America, Middle East, China
items.quote: We have significantl y grown our customer base, having serviced over 1,500 plus projects in this period

items.statement: Pipes & Fittings volume grew 103% YoY (43% standalone excl. Crestia) vs industry 10-20%; Roofing maintained 25% market share with highest Q1 sales and price premium; Parador gained share in declining European markets
items.quote: This business, Pipes and Fittings, crossed the Rs. 150-crore quarterly revenue mark for the first time. It represents a 78% growth year-on-year on revenue. The business has grown twice as much in volume terms over last year to cross the 10,000 metric ton in sales for this quarter. You would recognize and appreciate that this growth rate is significantly higher than the overall industry growth and

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission budget hiked ~50% to Rs 75,000 cr for FY25; AMRUT 2.0, gram panchayat broadband, piped gas expansion create new B2G pipe opportunities
items.quote: If you recall, in this year's budget, the allocation, budgetary allocation for Jal Jeevan Mission has been hiked up by nearly 50%. So, last year, the government spent about Rs. 50,000 crore. The allocation this year is about Rs. 75,000 crore.

items.statement: Key hires: Manish Khandelwal as Head of Putty & Construction Chemicals (20+ yrs exp, grown businesses 0-1,000 cr); Pranav Desai as Head of Innovation; dedicated B2G sales organization built; ranked #12 Great Place to Work 2024, #1 in manufa
items.quote: I am happy to share that we have recently onboarded Mr. Manish Khandelwal as the new head of our Putty and Construction Chemical business. With that dedicated bandwidth and the strong experience of over 20 years that he brings in, in the home and Building segment, and having grown businesses from 0 to 1,000 crore, we feel the Construction Chemical and Putty business is poised for strong growth in

items.statement: Crestia acquisition integrated successfully; Topline (Crestia) contributed Rs 45 cr revenue in Q1; retail sales accelerated to highest ever in June
